Passenger trains operate according to a  scheduled timetable. Despite the 
operational constraints, including those mentioned above, Indian Railways 
makes every effort to operate trains as per their schedule and maintain 
punctuality. Efforts are also made to minimise the impact of train regulation 
on passengers by disseminating timely information well in advance, thereby 
reducing inconvenience to the travelling public. 
Despite above constraints, during 2025-26, approximately 95% of scheduled 
trains (Mail/Express and Passenger trains) were operated  in Bilaspur 

 
Page 3 of 9 
division which includes 96 % scheduled trains on their designated routes 
over the Bilaspur Division. Similarly, over 98% of scheduled trains were 
operated in Raipur division which includes 97% scheduled trains on 
designated routes ran over the Raipur Division. 
Steps taken to improve punctuality on Indian Railways: 
Punctuality is accorded high priority on Indian Railways (IR) and all possible 
efforts are made to run trains on time. However, on Indian Railways, several 
factors affect punctuality which include foggy weather, path 
constraints/congestion, asset maintenance and other issues, alarm chain 
pulling, agitations, cattle run over and other unforeseen circumstances.  
The steps taken to improve punctuality of train services include: 
● Regular, continuous and real-time monitoring of punctuality of trains using 
technological tools and IT systems. 
● Use of an integrated digital platform for monitoring of train operations 
comprising Integrated Coaching Management System (ICMS) and Control 
Office Application (COA) which are integrated with National Train Enquiry 
System (NTES). 
● Progressive advancement for automatic uptake of timings by the train 
movement itself, is being achieved through GPS devices fitted locomotives 
{Real-Time Train Information System (RTIS) and Remote Monitoring and 
Management of Locomotives and Trains (REMMLOT)} and Data loggers 
integrated with the station signaling system.  
● Data loggers ensure real time and realistic reporting of arrival / departure 
of passenger trains at stations. 
● IR has been replacing conventional coaches (ICF coaches) by modern light 
weight LHB coaches having state -of-the art technology. The Production 
units of Indian Railways are producing only LHB coaches from April 2018 
onwards. The production of LHB coaches has continually increased during 
the years and about 50,000 LHB coaches have been turned out since 2014. 

 
Page 4 of 9 
IR has also been proliferating Vande Bharat, Namo Bharat Rapid Rail and 
Amrit Bharat trains, for quick acceleration and deceleration. 
● To improve punctuality, IR also undertakes rationalisation of time tables. 
One such exercise, in a scientific manner, was undertaken with the 
assistance of IIT- Mumbai using their traffic simulator. The exercise also 
aimed at provisioning of fixed  Integrated Maintenance block s on all 
sections to minimise detention and improve punctuality. 
● New generation High  capacity Locomotives are being utilised for Right 
powering of trains. 
● Further, with a view to minimise and mitigate the effect of fog and to assist 
the Loco Pilots run the train during foggy weather conditions the following 
steps have been taken by Indian Railways: 
(i)   GPS based FOG SAFE DEVICE – A Global Positioning System (GPS) 
based portable 'Fog Safe Device' (FSD) is being provided to Loco Pilots, 
which displays upcom ing critical landmarks such as approaching 
signal, level crossing gates, permanent speed restrictions etc. in 
advance during poor visibility conditions like fog. This device is used 
for safe train operation especially during winter season and to help 
reduce stress on Loco Pilots while running in poor visibility 
conditions.  As on 31.05.2026, there are 33,624 Fog Safe devices 
available over Indian Railways. 
(ii)   Modified Semi-Automatic Stop Signal (MASS) System : MASS has 
been introduced on the Automatic Signalling territory during abnormal 
conditions like Fog & Bad Weather impairing visibility. The system 
helps minimise delay in train operation during foggy weather 
conditions.  
Train operation during fog and poor visibility conditions is an essential 
component of the training curriculum and the same has already been 
incorporated in the Transportation Module and Technical Module of the 

 
Page 5 of 9 
prescribed training syllabus for Loco Pilots (LPs) and Assistant Loco 
Pilots (ALPs). 
● Modernisation of Signalling infrastructure: Indian Railways is modernising 
the signalling infrastructure for enhanced reliability & safety. It is using 
reliable digital technology by provision of electronic interlocking systems 
with adequate redundancy (in power supply & transmission media), dua l 
detection systems for train vehicle verification and replacement of 
electromechanical installations. Several improvement measures have 
been taken such as: 
a) Provision of Electrical/Electronic Interlocking Systems with 
centralized operation of points and signals in place of old 
mechanical signalling. It has been provided at 6671 stations as on 
30.06.2026, out of which Electronic Interlocking have been 
provided at 3954 stations. 
b) Complete Track Circuiting of stations to enhance safety for 
verification of tra ck occupancy by electrical means has been 
provided at 6671 stations upto 30.06.2026. 
c) Axle counters for automatic clearance of Block Section, BPAC 
(Block Proving Axle Counter) are provided to ensure complete 
arrival of train without manual intervention befo re granting line 
clear to receive next train and to reduce human element. These 
systems have been provided on 6085 Block Sections up to 
30.06.2026. 
d) Signalling assets maintenance are planned & under taken during 
Rolling Block introduced in Indian Railways ( Open Lines) General 
Rules vide Gazette notification dated 30.11.2023, wherein work of 
integrated maintenance/repair/replacement of assets is planned 
in advance on rolling basis and executed. 
 
 

 
Page 6 of 9

Improving of speed potential: 
 
Strengthening, upgradation, modernisation and improvement of track 
infrastructure is a continuous and ongoing process over Indian Railways. 
The following measures are being taken by Indian Railways, including 
SECR, to upgrade railway tracks: 
  i.   Modern track structure consisting of 60kg, 90 Ultimate Tensile 
Strength (UTS) rails, Wider and heavier Pre -stressed Concrete 
Sleepers (PSC) with elastic fastening, fan-shaped layout turnout on 

 
Page 8 of 9 
PSC sleepers and H -beam Sleepers on girder bridges are being 
used while carrying out primary track renewals.  
ii. The Thick Web Switches and Weldable CMS Crossings are being 
used in turnout renewal works. 
iii.   Supply of 260m long rail panels have been increased to avoid 
welding of joints,  thereby improving safety and riding quality. 
iv.     Thick Web Switch Expansion Joints are being used in place of earlier 
Conventional/Improved SEJs. 
      v.  Adoption of better welding technology for rails i.e. Flash Butt                 
Welding. 
vi.  Adoption of mechanized system for track maintenance using high 
output plain tampers and points & crossing tampers for improved 
maintainability & reliability of track.  
vii. Deployment of state -of-the-art modern machines including Rail 
Grinding Machines to further improve asset reliability. 
     viii. Mechanisation of track laying activities through use of track 
machines like PQRS, TRT, T-28 etc. 
ix.  Interlocking of Level Crossing (LC) Gates for enhancing safety at LC 
gates. 
 x. Use of advanced Phased Array technology of testing of rail and 
welds. 
xi. Deployment of Integrated Track Monitoring Systems (ITMS) and 
Oscillation Monitoring System (OMS) for comprehensive h ealth 
assessment to ascertain optimal maintenance requirements. 
xii. Adoption of portable Track Measuring Trolley for continuous 
recording of track parameters in yards. 
xiii. Using web enabled Track Management System (TMS) for integration 
and data analytics of the track inspection records received through 
various sources to enable precise maintenance inputs.

STATEMENT TO BE LAID ON THE TABLE OF LOK SABHA IN RESPECT OF PARTS 
(a) TO (e) OF THE LOK SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. 251 FOR 05TH AUGUST, 2026 
REGARDING “BROADBAND CONNECTIVITY UNDER BHARATNET IN 
TELANGANA” ASKED BY SHRI RAMASAHAYAM RAGHURAM REDDY.  
 
(a) The BharatNet Project has been approved for provision of broadband connectivity in a phased 
manner to all Gram Panchayats (GPs) in the country, including in the State of Telangana. Further, 
the Government has approved the Amended BharatNet Program (ABP) under a design, built, operate 
and maintain model to upgrade the existing network created under Phase-I and Phase-II of the 
BharatNet Project and to create incremental network for new GPs, its operation and maintenance and 
provision of 1.5 crore fiber-based internet connections. As on 30.6.2026, 10,833 GPs had been 
connected in Telangana under BharatNet project.  
(b) In the State of Telangana 10,022 villages have mobile coverage, out of which 9,929 villages 
are covered with 4G/5G connectivity. District-wise details are at Annexure I. 
(c) to (e) Government of India through Digital Bharat Nidhi (DBN) has undertaken several 
projects for improvement of telecom connectivity in tribal and remote areas of Telangana, as well as 
for establishment of telecom infrastructure in aspirational and rural areas in the State of Telangana, 
such as Left Wing Extremism (LWE) Phase-I Upgradation, LWE Phase-II Project and 4G Saturation 
Project for provision of mobile connectivity and BharatNet Project for provision of broadband 
connectivity. Complaints/grievances regarding poor telecom connectivity are addressed in 
coordination with Telecom Service Providers (TSPs).  
 As on 30.06.2026, 412 mobile towers have been commissioned in the State of Telangana 
under DBN funded projects, covering 493 villages. The Government of India has approved the 
proposal of the Government of Telangana for implementation of ABP in the State and communicated 
in-principle approval to the State Government.  
 The Department of Posts has undertaken several measures to improve postal infrastructure in 
Telangana. Advanced Postal Technology (APT) has been rolled out in all the Post Offices in 
Telangana Circle. 5,427 Branch Post Offices have been equipped with mobile devices, providing a 
unified digital platform for postal, banking, insurance and citizen centric services. Post Office 
Savings Bank has been fully computerized on a Core Banking Solution platform offering modern 
digital services, including ATM access, DBT payment, internet banking, mobile banking, 
NEFT/RTGS, e-Passbook and e-KYC. Additionally, UPI services are also being provided through 
India Post Payments Bank -Post Office Savings Account linkage, in all Post Offices in the State of 
Telangana. Further, 24/48 Speed Post services have been launched in six metro cities, including 
Hyderabad.

“Online Assurance Monitoring System (OAMS)” 
 
252.  Shri Satish Kumar Gautam: 
Shri Rahul Singh Lodhi: 
 
 Will the Minister of Parliamentary Affairs be pleased to state:- 
(a) the status of the initiatives launched through the Online Assurance Monitoring 
System to track, evaluate and guarantee the expeditious execution of formal Assurances 
given by the Ministers in both Houses of Parliament;  
(b) the d etails of features introduced for documentation, alerts and monitoring of 
pending Assurances;   
(c) whether the said digital architecture enable the Committee on Government 
Assurances in real-time monitoring of pending Assurances given by the Minister in both 
Houses of Parliament and if so, the details thereof; and  
(d) the specific interventions introduced to reduce delays in implementation and 
increase the accountability of various Ministries to their legislative obligations? 
 
Answer 
Minister of Parliamentary Affairs; and Minister of Minority Affairs 
(Shri Kiren Rijiju) 
(a) to (d) A statement is laid on the Table of the House. 
***** 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 
Statement referred to in reply to parts (a) to (d) of Lok Sabha Starred Question No. 252 
for answer on Wednesday, the 05th, August, 2026 regarding “Online Assurance 
Monitoring System (OAMS).” 
 
(a) to (d ):- The Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs has developed the Online Assurance 
Monitoring System (OAMS), a centralized web -based platform for end -to-end digita l 
processing and monitoring of Government Assurances given by Ministers on the floor of both 
Houses of Parliament. The system facilitates efficient processing and monitoring of 
Government Assurances while promoting transparency, accountability and effectiv e 
coordination among the Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs, the Committees on Government 
Assurances of both Houses and the concerned Ministries/Departments. 
  The OAMS provides a workflow -based platform for creation and processing of 
Government Assurances,  online submission of Implementation Reports by the concerned 
Ministries/Departments, maintenance of digital records, online status tracking, and electronic 
submission and processing of related documents. It also generates automated monthly 
reminders for timely submission of Implementation Reports.  
 The OAMS enables the Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs and the Committees on 
Government Assurances of both Houses to monitor implementation of Government 
Assurances in a transparent and time -bound manner. It fa cilitates review of pending 
assurances by providing updated status and related records, and where necessary, supports 
calling representatives of the concerned Ministries/Departments to tender oral evidence 
before the Committees. OAMS also enables online su bmission and examination of proposals 
for extension of time and dropping of assurances, allowing seamless electronic coordination 
among all stakeholders.  
 
 To ensure expeditious implementation, the Ministry regularly monitors pending 
Government Assurances through OAMS, which is available in the public domain through the 
OAMS portal (https://oams.nic.in). It examines Implementation Reports submitted by the 
concerned Ministries/Departments, processes proposals for extension of time and dropping of 
assurances for consideration by the Committees on Government Assurances, and processes 
accepted Implementation Reports for laying before the respective Houses of Parliament. The 
digital platform has strengthened monitoring, record management, transparency, coordinat ion 
and timely implementation of Government Assurances, while enhancing the accountability of 
the concerned Ministries/Departments towards their legislative obligations. The Ministry also 
periodically reviews OAMS and introduces necessary improvements, as required, to further 
enhance its effectiveness in the monitoring and management of Government Assurances.

FINANCIAL ALLOCATION FOR PM-SGMBY 
 
*253. SHRI RAVINDRA DATTARAM WAIKAR 
        DR. SHRIKANT EKNATH SHINDE 
 
Will the Minister of NEW AND RENEWABLE ENERGY be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether renewable energy financial allocation has been increased in the Budget 2026-27 with 
relation specifically for Pradhan Mantri-Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana (PM-SGMBY) 
representing solar budget and if so, the details of the strategic priorities driving this allocation; 
(b) the number of rooftop installations have added in systems demonstrating accelerating 
adoption along with the details of Government target for the financial year 2026-27; 
(c) whether subsidies per household for systems with collateral-free loans through a national 
digital portal have democratized access to solar power and if so, the details of registration and 
installation completion rates; 
(d) whether duty exemptions on battery storage capital goods and solar glass inputs alongside tax 
incentives for domestic manufacturing aim to build an atmanirbhar solar ecosystem and if so, the 
details thereof; and 
(e)   whether PM-SGMBY transforms consumers into prosumers generating their own electricity 
while reducing distribution losses and supporting the non-fossil fuel capacity target by year 2030 
and if so, the details thereof? 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF NEW & RENEWABLE ENERGY, CONSUMER AFFAIRS & FOOD AND 
PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION AND EDUCATION. 
 
(SHRI PRALHAD JOSHI) 
 
(a) to (e): A statement is laid on the table of the house. 
 
***** 
  

STATEMENT 
A statement referred to in reply of parts (a) to (e) of Lok Sabha Starred Question No. 253 to 
be answered on 05.08.2026 regarding Financial Allocation for PM-SGMBY 
 
(a) to (c):  The budget of Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE) has been increased 
from Rs. 25,301.22 Cr at Revised Budget stage in 2025-26 to Rs. 32,914.67 Cr at Budget Estimate 
stage in 2026 -27 and the corresponding increase in the budget for PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli 
Yojana (PMSG: MBY) is from Rs. 17,000 Cr at Revised Budget stage in 2025 -26 to Rs. 22,000 
Cr at Budget Estimate stage in 2026-27. The increase in the budget of PMSG: MBY is mainly on 
account of accelerated adoption of RTS systems installations by residential households under  the 
scheme. 
As a result of various steps taken by the MNRE, including timely disbursement of subsidies and 
facilitating timely sanction of collateral-free loans through digital portal s, the rate of installation 
of RTS systems which was few months for coverage of one lakh households during the initial 
phase of implementation of the scheme has now reached to around 6 days for covering one lakh 
households.    
Under the PMSG: MBY, which is a demand driven scheme launched in February 2024, a total of 
77,44,376 applications have been received, with a cumulative installed capacity of 14.8 GW have 
been installed, benefitting o ver 50 lakh households, with ₹28,024 crore as Central Financial 
Assistance (CFA) across the country, as on 04.08.2026. 
 
(d): To promote domestic manufacturing of solar glass, the Government has waived off Basic 
Customs Duty (BCD) on import of sodium antimonate for use in manufacture of solar glass. 
Additionally, t o promote indigenous manufacturing capabilities and develop an Aatmanirbhar  
ecosystem for battery storage in the country, exemption from BCD has been provided on specified 
capital goods, machinery and equipment required for the manufacture of lithium -ion cells for 
batteries used in electric vehicles and Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS).  
 
(e): Households with rooftop solar systems, generat e their own electricity for self-consumption 
and may export surplus power to the grid , as per prevailing State/UT regulations . Since, RTS 
systems are installed at the consumption end or tail end of distribution network, therefore, it  
reduces distribution losses. Under the PMSG: MBY, solar power generation capacity of over 14.65 
GW has been added till 31.7.2026, contributing to the non-fossil fuel capacity target of 500 GW 
by year 2030.

QUESTION NO.256 TO BE ANSWERED ON 05.08.2026 IN LOK SABHA 
(a) to (c): Indian Railways serve about 58 cr meals every year on an 
average. About only 0.0008% food quality related complaints are received 
on average. Based on complaints during the last three years, appropriate 
penal actions have been taken by IRCTC. Such actions include imposition 
of fines amounting to ₹5.13 crore, issuance of 54 show-cause notices, 06 
termination of contracts and debarment of  licensees for food quality and 
hygiene violations. The list of debarred licensees is published on the 
IRCTC’s website.  
Regular and surprise inspections are conducted by Railway/IRCTC officials, 
including Food Safety Officers, to ensure quality, hygiene, safety and 
regulatory compliance. These inspections cover key aspects such as food 
safety, staff deployment, equipment maintenance, cleanliness and 
adherence to prescribed standards while promoting best practices in food 
handling, storage and preparation.  
Indian Railways continuously endeavour to provide good quality and 
hygienic food items to the travelling passengers as per the prescribed 
norms. Necessary steps are accordingly taken by Indian Railways from 
time to time to ensure the same. The following measures have been taken 
to improve quality, hygiene and food safety: 
 Supply of meals from designated Base Kitchens. 
 Commissioning of modern Base Kitchens at identified locations. 
 Installation of CCTV Cameras in Base Kitchens for real time and 
better monitoring  of food preparation. 
 Shortlisting and use of popular and branded raw materials for food 
production. 
 Deployment of Food Safety Supervisors at Base Kitchens to monitor 
food safety and hygienic practices. 

 
Page 2 of 2 
 Deployment of on-board IRCTC supervisors on trains. 
 Introduction of QR codes on meal packets supplied in trains to 
enhance food safety, transparency and passenger awareness. The QR 
code provides details regarding date of packing, name of the licensee 
and FSSAI license number, for information of passengers. 
 Regular deep cleaning and periodical pest control in Base Kitchens 
and Pantry Cars. 
 Mandatory Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) 
certification to ensure compliance with Food Safety Norms. 
 Regular food sampling as a part of the monitoring mechanism to 
ensure quality of food on trains. 
 Regular training is conducted by IRCTC to enhance the skills of 
catering staff, focusing on customer service areas, i.e., 
communication, courteous behaviour, service standards, personal 
grooming, and hygiene. 
 Third Party Audit is done to examine hygiene and quality of food in 
Pantry Cars and Base Kitchens. Customer satisfaction survey is also 
conducted. 
 Regular and surprise inspections by Railway/ IRCTC officials, 
including Food Safety Officers.

Will the Minister of MINORITY AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether any assessment has been undertaken regarding the status of traditional artisan

and if so, the details thereof; 
(b) whether any schemes or programmes are being implemented for preservation, promotion 
and market access of products produced by such artisan communities and if so, the details 
thereof; 
(c) whether any challenges relating to declining incomes, market access and continuity of 
traditional skills among such communities have been identified and if so, the details thereof; 
and 
(d) the measures taken by the Government to promote sustainable livelihoods and  
preservation of traditional artisan skills among minority communities including those residing 
in Barmer district of Rajasthan? 
 
ANSWER  
 
MINISTER OF MINORITY AFFAIRS  
(SHRI KIREN RIJIJU) 
 
(a) to (d) A Statement is laid on the table of the House. 
 
  

STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS ( A) TO ( D) OF LOK SABHA 
STARRED QUESTION NO. 257 TO BE ANSWERED ON 05.08.2026 ASKED BY 
HON’BLE MEMBER OF PARLIAMENT SHRI UMMEDA RAM BENIWAL 
REGARDING “STATUS OF TRADITIONAL ARTISANS LIVELIHOODS AMONG 
MINORITY COMMUNITIES”. 
 
(a) The Ministry of Minority Affairs had conducted the impact assessment of the erstwhile 
Upgrading the Skills and Training in Traditional Arts/Crafts for Development (USTTAD) 
Scheme in 2015 -16 through Management Development Institute (MDI) . The evaluation 
examined the implementation and outcomes of the scheme and recommended, inter alia, 
spreading wider awareness of scheme through social media and mobile outreach, strengthening 
the capacity of master artisans, improving training quality through local -language and digital 
content, promoting entrepreneurship, Self -Help Groups (SHGs), bank linkages and market 
access, creation of a Project Management Unit (PMU) for better coordination and monitoring, 
periodic skill -gap assessments, enhanc ing opportunities for marketing and credit linkages . 
USTTAD scheme subsequently merged into the Pradhan Mantri Virasat Ka Samvardhan 
(PM VIKAS) Scheme in 2021-22. 
(b)        Under the Traditional Skilling component of the PM VIKAS Scheme, interventions 
are undertaken to preserve and promote traditional arts and crafts while enhancing livelihood 
opportunities for artisans belonging to the six notified minority communities. For promotion 
and market access, the Ministry had organized artisan marketing events like Hunar Haat, which  
has been rechristened as 'Lok Samvardhan Parv'  under PM VIKAS scheme. These events 
provide artisans and culinary experts from minority communities a platform to exhibit and sell 
their handicrafts, handloom products, indigenous products and traditional cuisines, besides 
facilitating buyer-seller interaction and market linka ges. So far, 41 Hunar Haat  and 6 Lok 
Samvardhan Parv have been organized at various locations across the country. 
 
(c)  to (d ) The  challenges faced by traditional artisans include limited market access, 
competition from mass -produced products, inadequate access to credit, changing consumer 
preferences and declining interest among younger generations in pursuing traditional 
occupations.  The PM VIKAS scheme focus on skill upgradation, entrepreneurship 
development, design and technology support, market linkages, branding, exhibitions, and 
digital marketing. The scheme also promotes capacity building, institutional support, and 
enhanced livelihood opportunities for artisans and craftsmen. These interventions aim to 
preserve traditional arts and crafts while improving their economic viability and ensuring 
sustainable livelihoods for the artisan communities. 
Government has taken several measures , including capacity building and marketing

Implementation of Kavach:- 
 
1. Kavach is an indigenously developed Automatic Train Protection (ATP) 
system. Kavach is a highly technology intensive system, which requires 
safety certification of highest order (SIL-4). 
2. Kavach aids the Loco Pilot in running of trains within specified speed 
limits by automatic application of brakes in case Loco Pilot fails to do 
so and also helps the trains to run safely during inclement weather. 
3. The first field trials on the pas senger trains were started in February

Assessment of the system by Independent Safety Assessor (ISA), three

Morena Incident:- 
Trains are provided with a number of safety features. One of these safety 
features is the Passenger Emergency Alarm Chain. Pulling this alarm chain 
leads to brakes being applied in the train and it also alerts the loco pilot and 
the train manager of possib le an emergency situation that these staff then 
verify and attend. The passenger emergency alarm chain must be used only 
in cases of genuine emergencies and not misused for personal conveniences 
like stopping the train at a convenient stop for detraining. Pulling of 
Emergency Alarm Chain, without reasonable and sufficient cause is a 
punishable offence under Section 141 of Indian Railways Act, 1989 and can 
lead to penalty of imprisonment/fine.  
On 14.06.2026, after Train No. 19665 (KURJ -UDZ) Express passed H etampur 
Station in Jhansi Division of North Central Railway, there was a case of 
alarm chain pulling in the General Coach No. 235816/C of the train, second 
from the Train Engine, which led to the train stopping mid -section 
(Hetampur-Dholpur) at about 16.22  hours at km 1279/28 -14. When the train 
stopped, some passengers got down from this coach and trespassed on to 
the other running lines. The loco pilot of the oncoming train No. 20424 (FZR -
SEY) Patalkot Express, observed trespassing passengers, immediately 
sounded continuous warning horns and applied emergency brakes on 
perceiving risk. 
While most of the people trespassing on to the running lines dispersed, 4 of 
them failed to clear the tracks on time and were run over under the Train No. 
20424 (FZR-SEY) Patalkot Express, before it could come to a stop. 
A detailed examination of the coach no. 235816/C and adjoining coaches 
was carried out. There was no evidence of fire, smoke or electrical defect in 
any of these coaches, nor was any other emergency situation that could 
have warranted pulling of the emergency alarm chain. 

 
Page 10 of 11 
 A further detailed examination also found no evidence of any burn marks, 
flash marks, overheating, insulation damage, smoke residue, electrical short 
circuit, equipment failure or any other f ire-related clue in these coaches. 
Electrical fittings, switches and under -gear equipment were found normal 
and intact. 
In this case, cause of the chain pulling was for reason other than any 
genuine emergency. 
Measures to Prevent Fire Incidents in Running Train Coaches:- 
Fire safety in trains of Indian Railways encompasses all phases of design, 
manufacturing, maintenance and operation of trains in Indian Railways. To 
ensure that incidents of fire do not occur on trains of Indian Railways, a 
large number of steps have been taken, the more important of which are as 
follows: 
1. Provision of Minimum two Fire Extinguishers in all coaches over Indian 
Railways. 
2. Fire Detection & Suppression System has been provided in fire prone 
areas of Power cars and Pantry cars. 
3. Fire and smoke Detection system has been provided in coaches as per 
extant guidelines. 
4. Water mist type fire extinguishers are being provided on pantry cars and 
power cars in phased manner. 
5. Provision of emergency windows in coaches for evacuation in case of 
fire. 
6. Use of fire -retardant material as per global fire -retardant norms in 
coaches for seats/berths, panels, flooring, insulation, toilets etc 
forimproved fire safety. 
7. Use of fire-retardant E-beam cable in coaches. 

 
Page 11 of 11 
8. Use of different levels of protection in th e form of fuses, Miniature 
Circuit breaker (MCBs) and Motor protection Circuit Breakers (MPCBs) 
in the electrical circuits to prevent the damage from electrical 
faults/surges. 
9. Provision of Aerosol based fire suppression system in electrical 
cabinets. 
10. Further, up -gradation of material in line with global standards is 
regularly being carried out with fitment of new generation material in 
Amrit Bharat & Vande Bharat Sleeper trains. 
11. Display of “Fire Notices” for widespread information in all coaches to 
inform and alert passengers regarding various “Do’s” and “Don’ts” to 
prevent fire. These include messages regarding not to carry any 
inflammable material, explosives, prohibition of smoking inside the 
coaches and penalties etc. 
12. Prohibition of flame based cooking in coaches. 
13. There is a provision of 4 Emergency Talk Back Units in every coach of 
Vande Bharat. This facilitates communications of passenger with Train 
Manager/Loco-pilots in case of exigencies.Passenger Emergency Alarm 
Buttons have been provided in th e Vande Bharat Train. Each coach has 
been provisioned with 4 such push buttons for emergency usage. 
14. There is an integrated help line called Rail Madad which can be 
accessed by users through the number 139 for seeking help during 
emergencies.

(d) The Government has already established several National Scientific 
Research Institutions in Kerala across different scientific and research 
domains with varied mandates. The detail s of such institutions are given in

(e) Apart from establishing several Scientific Institutions, the Government 
has taken several measures to strengthen scientific research, innovation 
and technology development in Kerala. Significant initi atives are given 
below: 
 
o The Department of Science and Technology (DST) is strengthening 
Kerala's scientific ecosystem through targeted grants, infrastructure 
funding, and intellectual property support. Key measures include funding 
the Kerala State Council  for Science, Technology and Environment 
(KSCSTE) through the State S&T Programme, establishing a Patent 
Information Centre to drive IPR awareness and patent filings, and backing 
student innovation projects. The INSPIRE Scheme supports research and 
innovation by funding doctoral studies, offering postdoctoral tracks, and 
building local STEM talent pools. Technology Translation and Innovation 
Division is funding proof -of-concept development, nurturing local start -
ups through translational programs, and bridging academia-industry gaps. 
It converts early -stage research into market -ready prototypes while 
supporting regional S&T initiatives. Under FIST Scheme, during the last 
five years, 9 STEM departments at various academic 
institutions/universities and 12 PG C olleges, were supported in Kerala for 
augmenting basic infrastructural facilities for conducting quality research 
in basic and applied sciences. 2 Sophisticated Analytical Instrument 
Facilities (SAIF) were established in the State of Kerala (Mahatma Gandhi 
University, Kottayam and Cochin University of Science and Technology, 
Kochi) to provide the facilities of sophisticated analytical instruments to 
the researchers to pursue advanced R&D activities.  Under the Promotion 
of University Research and Scientific  Excellence (PURSE), University of 
Calicut, Thrissur has been supported to strengthen the Research and 
Development (R&D) infrastructure to conduct mission -oriented research 
in various areas of Science and Technology (S&T) aligned with national 
priorities. The Technical Research Centre (TRC) at Sree Chitra Tirunal 
Institute for Medical Sciences and Technology (SCTIMST) is conducting 
mission-mode R&D in critical medical devices, supporting regulatory 
compliance, and fostering industry partnerships. 
o One of the  constituent laboratories of the Council of Scientific and 
Industrial Research (CSIR), namely National Institute for Interdisciplinary 
Science & Technology (NIIST), Thiruvananthapuram has established 
research programmes to promote fundamental science and f oster high -

strong scientific and translational potential. These initiatives are 
intended to accelerate the progression of basic research into 
technologies and solutions that address n ational priorities and societal 
needs.  
o Department of Biotechnology (DBT) is supporting R&D projects through 
its Central sector BioRIDE scheme in the state of Kerala. To boost 
research ecosystem, DBT has sanctioned three projects under the 
Research Resourc e Service Facility and Platform (RRSFP) focusing on 
building institutional capacity by upgrading postgraduate teaching and 
research laboratories and enhancing access to high end scientific 
equipment. To strengthen innovation and technology development, BIRAC 
(Biotechnology Industry Research Assistance Council), PSU of DBT has 
established two incubation centres in Kerala which provide startups and 
innovators with access to advanced lab infrastructure and industry 
linkages. BIRAC has enabled industry academia  collaboration for 
technology and product development through PACE (Promoting Academic 
Research Conversion to Enterprise), BIPP (Biotechnology Industry 
Partnership Programme) and SBIRI (Small Business Innovation Research 
Initiative) programs in Kerala.  
o Several broad -based programs like Advanced Research Grant (ARG), 
Prime Minister Early Career Research Grant (PMECRG), Inclusivity 
Research Grant  (IRG) launched by Anusandhan National Research 
Foundation (ANRF)  provide financial assistance to researchers and 
scientists in academic institutions in order to create supportive 
environment for doing research in frontier areas of science and 
engineering across the country, including Kerala. 
o The Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) has undertaken 
several in itiatives to strengthen scientific research, innovation and 
technology development in Kerala through its research institutes, All 
India Coordinated Research Projects (AICRPs), National Innovations on 
Climate Resilient Agriculture (NICRA), Krishi Vigyan Ken dras (KVKs) and 
other research and extension programmes.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS 
LOK SABHA 
STARRED QUESTION NO. 261 
TO BE ANSWERED ON AUGUST 06, 2026 
 
ASSESSMENT OF HOUSING SHORTAGE 
 
NO. 261 SHRI K GOPINATH: 
 
Will the Minister of HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the details of the latest assessment of the housing shortage in urban 
areas of the country; 
(b) the total number of houses sanctioned and completed under Pradhan 
Mantri Awas Yojana- Urban (PMAY -U) 2.0 as on date and the total 
amount of Central assistance released for the purpose, State/UT -
wise; 
(c) whether there is a gap between the assessed shortage and the 
houses sanctioned so far and if so, the reasons therefor; and 
(d) the measures being taken to bridge this gap within the 'Housing for 
All' mission period? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS 
(SHRI MANOHAR LAL) 
 
(a) to (d): A statement is laid on the Table of the House.  
  

 
STATEMENT REFERRED IN REPLY TO LOK  SABHA STARRED QUESTION 
NO. 261 * FOR 06.08.2026 REGARDING ‘ ASSESSMENT OF HOUSING 
SHORTAGE’.  
 
(a): ‘Land’ and ‘C olonisation’ are State subjects and schemes relating to 
housing for their citizens, including Economically Weaker Sections (EWS), 
Low Income Groups (LIG), migrant workers and semi -urban households is 
domain of the respective State/  Union Territory (UT) Governments. Data 
regarding homelessness, availability and quality of housing is captured 
during regular census exercise. As per census 2011, out of total urban 
population of 37.7 crores, 9,38,348 persons were homeless  and 17.4 % 
urban population was living in slums.  
 
Thereafter, Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (erstwhile Ministry of 
Housing and Urban Poverty Alleviation) constituted a Technical Group 
(TG-12) on estimation of urban housing shortage of the country for the 
Twelfth Five-Year Plan (2012-17). As per the Report of this Committee, the 
total housing shortage at the beginning of the 12th Plan period i.e. in 
2012, was 187.8 lakh. It was also assessed that housing shortage was 
more in Economically Weaker Section (EWS)/ Lower Income Group (LIG) 
segment which are focused beneficiaries in PMAY-U and PMAY-U 2.0. 
 
(b): Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA) has been implementing 
Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana -  Urban (PMAY -U) since 25.06.2015 to 
provide all weather pucca houses with basic civic amenities to eligible 
urban beneficiaries across the country. Based on the learnings from the 
experiences of implementation of PMAY -U, MoHUA has revamped the 
scheme and launched PMAY -U 2.0 ‘Housing for  All’ Mission with effect 
from 01.09.2024 for implementation in urban areas across the country to 
support 1 crore additional eligible beneficiaries in next five years. PMAY-U 
2.0 is implemented through four verticals i.e., Beneficiary Led 
Construction (BLC), Affordable Housing in Partnership (AHP), Affordable 
Rental Housing (ARH) and Interest Subsidy Scheme (ISS). The Scheme 
Guidelines may be accessed at  https://pmay-
urban.gov.in/uploads/guidelines/Operational-Guidelines-of-PMAY-U-2.pdf.  
 
Housing demand being dynamic in nature, under PMAY -U, 111.48 lakh 
houses and under PMAY -U 2.0, 16.20 lakh houses have been 
sanctioned. The State/UT -wise details of houses sanctioned, grounded 
and completed/delivered along with Central assistance approved and 
released under PMAY -U & PMAY -U 2.0 is at Annexure.  The progress of 
the scheme can also be accessed on the PMAY -U dashboard 
(https://dashboard.pmay-urban.gov.in). 
 

(c) and (d): PMAY-U adopted a demand driven approach and there were 
no fixed State/UT-wise targets. States/UTs were requested to undertake 
demand survey for assessing demand of housing in urban areas through 
their Urban Local Bodies (ULBs)/  Implementing Agencies. The assessed 
demand reported by States/ UTs in 2017- 18 was around 112 lakh. 
Housing demand being dynamic in nature, sanctioning of houses is 
continuous activity based on proposals received from State /UTs.  
Under PMAY-U, 111.48 lakh houses and under PMAY -U 2.0, 16.20 lakh 
houses have been sanctioned.  PMAY-U and PMAY-U 2.0 taken together, 
more than 2 crore houses are expected to be sanctioned, which is more 
than assessed demand.  
 
To improve targeting, eligible citizens are also allowed to apply through 
Unified Web Portal of PMAY -U 2.0 with all details on the portal. 
States/UTs/ULBs validate the beneficiaries as per the eligibility criteria 
of the scheme guidelines and selection/  scrutiny of beneficiary lists are 
done by the States/  UTs. The Unified Web Portal for submitting the 
online applications may be accessed through https://pmay-urban.gov.in.

IMPLEMENTATION OF PMAY-U 2.0 IN TAMIL NADU 
 
NO. 262  SHRI C N ANNADURAI: 
DR. RANI SRIKUMAR:    
 
Will the Minister of HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government is implementing Pradhan Mantri Awas 
Yojana-Urban (PMAY-U) 2.0 in Tamil Nadu to provide affordable housing 
to Economically Weaker Section (EWS), Low -Income Group (LIG) and 
Middle-Income Group (MIG) families through financial assistance and 
interest subsidy and if so, the details thereof; 
(b) the number of beneficiaries identified, houses sanctioned and 
financial assistance approved in Tamil Nadu under PMAY -U 2.0 
including the number of beneficiaries covered under EWS, LIG and MIG 
categories, district-wise; 
(c) the details of Central assistance released, interest subsidy 
sanctioned and dwelling units proposed for construction in Tamil Nadu 
since the launch of PMAY-U 2.0; and 
(d) whether the Government proposes to expedite approvals, fund 
releases and implementation to ensure timely completion of affordable 
housing projects across Urban Local Bodies in Tamil Nadu and if so, the 
details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS 
 (SHRI MANOHAR LAL) 
 
 
(a) to (d): A statement is laid on the Table of the House. 
 
 
 

STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN THE LOK SABHA STARRED QUESTION 
NO. *262 (2nd POSITION) DUE FOR ANSWER ON 06.08.2026 REGARDING 
IMPLEMENTATION OF PMAY-U 2.0 IN TAMIL NADU 
(a): Based on the learnings from the experiences of implementation of 
PMAY-U, Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs ( MoHUA) has launched 
PMAY-U 2.0 ‘Housing for All’ Mission with effect from 01.09.2024 for 1  
crore additional eligible beneficiaries belonging to Economically 
Weaker Section (EWS)/ Low Income Group (LIG)/ Middle Income Group 
(MIG) segments. PMAY-U 2.0 is implemented through four verticals i.e., 
Beneficiary Led Construction (BLC), Affordable Housing in Partnership 
(AHP), Affordable Rental Housing (ARH) and Interest Subsidy Scheme 
(ISS). 
 
The scheme guidelines can be accessed at https://pmay -
urban.gov.in/uploads/guidelines/Operational-Guidelines-of-PMAY-U-2.pdf 
 
(b)& (c): Based on the project proposal submitted by State of the Tamil 
Nadu, a total of 18,577 houses under PMAY -U 2.0, have been 
sanctioned by the Ministry. Out of which, 7,083 houses are grounded 
and 2,334 houses are completed/delivered, as on 13.07.2026. A total 
Central Assistance of ₹251.44 crore has been sanctioned, of which 
₹54.61 crore has been released to the State of Tamil Nadu under PMAY-
U 2.0, so far. A total of ₹7.44 crore Interest subsidy has been released 
to 2,310 beneficiaries under ISS vertical of PMAY -U 2.0 in the state of 
Tamil Nadu. There are 1,552 LIG and 539 MIG beneficiaries under ISS 
vertical, all other sanctioned beneficiaries belong to EWS category. The 
district-wise physical and financial progress under PMAY -U 2.0 in the 
State of Tamil Nadu is annexed. 
 
(d): PMAY-U & PMAY -U 2.0 are demand- driven schemes. Based on the 
applications and beneficiary selection, project proposals are approved 
by the State Level Sanctioning and Monitoring Committee (SLSMC) and 
thereafter considered by the Central Sanctioning and Monitoring 
Committee (CSMC) for release of Central Assistance. Sanctioning of 
houses is continuous activity based on proposals received from States 
/UTs. Proposals received from States/UTs are examined and approved 
expeditiously, subject to their conformity with the Scheme Guidelines 
and fulfilment of the prescribed eligibility conditions. Release of Central 
Assistance is made in accordance with the prescribed compliances 
under the scheme as Mother Sanction through SNA-SPARSH.

MINISTRY OF JAL SHAKTI

IMPLEMENTATION OF JJM 2.0 
 
*265.  SHRI MITESHBHAI RAMESHBHAI PATEL:  
SMT. D K ARUNA:  
 
Will the Minister of JAL SHAKTI be pleased to state:  
(a) the key features of Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) 2.0 including the implementation framework 
and funding pattern along with the major changes introduced in JJM 2.0 in comparison to the 
first phase in the country including Telangana;  
(b) the reforms proposed to ensure long -term sustainability of water sources, operation and 
maintenance of rural drinking water supply systems and strengthen community participation in 
the country;  
(c) the details of the fun ds allocated and released under JJM 2.0 during 2026 -27, State-wise 
including Telangana;  
(d) the timeline and targets set for achieving universal and sustainable rural domestic tap water 
supply under JJM 2.0 across the country;  
(e) the details of the fund s sanctioned, released and utilised under JJM since 2019, year and 
State-wise;  
(f) the number of sanctioned and functional household tap water connections under JJM since 
2019, year and State-wise including district-wise for Andhra Pradesh; and  
(g) the measures taken to prevent groundwater contamination and over-exploitation under JJM 
2.0? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF JAL SHAKTI  
(SHRI C R PATIL)  
 
(a) to (g) A Statement is laid on the Table of the House.  
 
  

Page 2 of 6 
 
Statement referred to in reply to parts (a) to (g) of Lok Sabha Starred Question No. *265 
answered on 06.08.2026 regarding “ Implementation of JJM 2.0 ” asked by Shri 
Miteshbhai Rameshbhai Patel & Smt. D K Aruna 
 
(a) to ( e) Drinking Water is a ‘State’ subject, and hence, under JJM, the responsibility of 
planning, approval, implementation, operation & maintenance of drinking water supply 
schemes lies with State/UT Governments. The Government of India supports the States by 
providing technical and financial assistance.  
To make provision of tap water supply to every rural household across the country, 
Government of India, in partnership with States, has been implementing Jal Jeevan Mission 
(JJM), since August 2019. The Jal Jeevan Mission has transformed rural drinking water supply 
across the country, with more t han 82%  of rural households now reported receiving water 
through functional tap connections. 
In March, 2026, Union Cabinet has approved the extension of JJM period up to December 2028 
with enhanced outlay and restructured implementation focusing on structu ral reforms in rural 
drinking water supply sector under JJM 2.0. The focus under JJM 2.0 has shifted from creation 
of infrastructure to long-term functionality, citizen-centric, water quality, source sustainability 
and assured service delivery. 
Further, JJM 2.0 also focuses on the quality of infrastructure and operation and maintenance 
(O&M) of rural piped water supply schemes through Jan Bhagidhari  by restructuring and 
reorienting the implementation of the JJM from infrastructure creation to a service delivery, 
supported by drinking water governance and institutional ecosystem for sustainable rural piped 
potable water supply. Separate MoUs are signe d with States/ UTs, to ensure adherence to 
timelines, sustainability and citizen-centric water service delivery. Every State / UT including 
Telangana has to comply with the guidelines issued under JJM 2.0. 
Under JJM 2.0, a uniform national digital framewor k, namely “Sujalam Bharat” has been 
created under which every rural village is assigned a unique Sujal Gaon ID, for digitally 
mapping the complete drinking water supply system from source to tap. Gram Panchayats 
(GPs) and Village Water  and Sanitation Commi ttee (VWSCs) have been involved in the 
commissioning and formal handover of schemes through “Jal Arpan” for ensuring transparency 
and accountability. A Gram Panchayat certif ies completion of works and declares itself “Har 
Ghar Jal” only upon confirmation t hat adequate in -village operation and maintenance 
mechanisms have been established. “Jal Utsav” is conducted as a community-led maintenance 
and review event, integrating local cultural ethos while reinforcing collective responsibility for 
drinking water secure future. 
JJM is a centrally sponsored programme  and the fund sharing pattern between Centre and 
States / UTs is 100% for Union Territories without legislature, 90:10 for North Eastern & 
Himalayan States and UTs with legislature and 50:50 for rest of th e States. Moreover, under 
Support and Water Quality Monitoring and Surveillance (WQM &S) activities the funding 
pattern is 100% for Union Territories, 90:10 for Himalayan, North Eastern States and UTs with 
legislature and 60:40 for other States.  
No new piped water supply scheme shall be taken up under JJM 2.0 except the schemes in   
Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan ( PM-JANMAN) and Dharti Aaba 
Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan (DA-JGUA) areas as per extant guidelines. Further, no central 

Page 3 of 6 
 
assistance shall be provided for retrofitting schemes and any pending liabilities under such 
schemes to be met from the State Government's financial resources. 
Presently, the State-wise central allocation and fund drawn by the States including Telangana 
so far in FY 2026-27 is at Annexure – I.  
Moreover, Year-wise and State/ UT-wise details of financial progress under the Mission is in 
public domain and is accessible at:  
https://ejalshakti.gov.in/JJM/JJMReports/Financial/JJMRep_StatewiseAllocationReleaseExp
enditure.aspx  
(f) Significant progress has been made in the country since the launch of Jal Jeevan Mission, 
towards enhancing access to tap water to rural households. At the start of Jal Jeevan Mission 
in August 2019, only 3.23 crore (16.72%) rural households were reported to have tap water 
connections. As on 04.08.2026, out of 19.36 crore rural households in the country, more than 
15.90 crore (82.19%) households are reported to have tap water connections in their homes. 
The present status of implementation, indicating the number and percentage of rural households 
reported with Functional Household Tap Connections, State-wise under the Jal Jeevan Mission 
(JJM) are available on JJM Dashboard, as updated by State/UTs. The link for same is as below:  
https://ejalshakti.gov.in/jjmreport/jjmindia.aspx 
The district -wise details of functional households tap connections in Andhra Pradesh is at 
Annexure – II. 
(g) The measures taken to prevent groundwater contamination and over-exploitation under JJM 
2.0 are as under: -  
(i) To prevent over extraction of groundwater and hydraulic interference between wells, 
installation of additional tubewells or borewells within the prescribed safe distance 
from an existing drinking water source are reviewed in accordance with Central Public 
Health and Environmental Engineering Organisation (CPHEEO), Central Ground 
Water Board (CGWB) and Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) technical standards. 
(ii) District Administrations and Gram Panchayats to utilize geospatial information and 
datasets available through the Decision Support System (DSS) and other digital 
platforms to Map drinking water source locations; Monitor surrounding land use 
patterns; Identify potential contamination risks; Support plan ning and implementation 
of appropriate source protection measures. 
(iii) Appropriate minimum sanitary protection distances to be maintained around drinking 
water sources such as tube wells and borewells to minimize the risk of contamination 
from anthropogenic activities. 
(iv) States/ UTs to undertake source protection and contamination prevention measures in 
compliance with the relevant guidelines and standards issued by the CPHEEO, CGWB 
and BIS.  
(v) All water quality test results are linked to the national Water Quality  Management 
Information System (WQMIS) for near real-time tracking, early contamination alerts, 
and public access. 

Page 4 of 6 
 
(vi) Avoid construction of soak pits, leach pits, septic tanks, magic pits or other waste 
disposal structures within the sanitary protection radiu s of drinking water sources. 
Where such structures cannot be avoided due to site/ area constraints, appropriate 
protective and mitigation measures are adopted to prevent contamination of the 
drinking water source.

2026 ASKED BY SHRI KODIKUNNIL SURE SH REGARDING 
„UPPGRADATION OF EXIS TING ROADS AS NATION AL HIGHWAYS IN

(a) to (e) The Government  in Ministry of Road Transport  and Highways 
receives proposals from State Governments  and Union Territory 
Administrations including the  State of Kerala fr om time to time for 
declaration of State roads, as new National Highways. 
 
State roads are declared as National Highways (NHs) from time to 
time on the basis of well-established broad principles, including: - 
 
i. Connecting adjacent countries, National Capital with State 
Capitals / one State Capital to another State Capital, major 
ports and ports prioritised for development by the Ministry 
of Ports, Shipping & Waterways, large industrial centers or 
tourist centers. 
ii. Roads having important strategic requirements. 
iii. Arterial roads which enable sizeable reduction in travel 
distance and achieve substantial economic growth. 
iv. Roads which help in opening up large tracts of backward 
area and hilly region. 
v. Synergy with PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan (NMP). 
  
 Length of NH network in the State of Kerala is about 1,858 km at 
present. Government has notified 76 km of State Roads / greenfield 
stretches as NHs in the  State of Kerala during the last five years and 
current year. The Government has received a list of 27 State Roads for  
declaration as National Highway, from the State Government of Kerala 
during the  last five years. However, currently these are not under 
consideration.  
 
Besides there are 10 Greenfield projects envisaged for implementation 
by the National  Highways Authority of India (NHAI),which will form 
part of the NH network  in the State  on their approval.  Details of

Statement referred to in reply to parts (a) to (d) of Lok Sabha Starred Question No. *267 
answered on 0 6.08.2026 regarding “Central Assistance for the Godavari Water  Grid

(a) to (d) Since August 2019, Government of India, in partnership with States, is implementing 
Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) -Har Ghar Jal to enable every rural househo ld including Andhra

Cabinet has approved extension of the Jal Jeevan Mission, with an enhanced outlay and a 
restructured reform in the rural drinking water supply sector under JJM 2.0.

At the start of the Mission, only 30.74 lakh (32.18%) rural households were reported to have

rural households have been provide d tap water connection including Kakinada and other 
districts of the Godavari region.

STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (A) TO (D) IN RESPECT OF LOK 
SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. *268 FOR REPLY ON 06.08.2026 REGARDING 
IMPLEMENTATION OF SATAT SCHEME ASKED BY SMT. SHOBHANABEN 
MAHENDRASINH BARAIYA AND SHRI KRISHNA PRASAD TENNETI 
(a) to (d) The Government launched the “Sustainable Alternative Towards Affordable Transportation 
(SATAT)” initiative on 1st October, 2018 to establish an ecosystem for production of Compressed 
Bio-Gas (CBG) from various waste and biomass sources and to promote its use along with natural gas. 
Under the initiative, Oil and Gas Marketing Companies (OGMCs) invite Expressions of Interest 
(EOIs) to procure CBG from potential entrepreneurs. CBG plants are established by entrepreneurs, 
public-sector enterprises and other entities based on their techno-commercial assessment. 
Government have adopted a “Whole-of-Government” approach for development of CBG projects 
under the Galvanizing Organic Bio-Agro Resources Dhan (GOBARdhan) initiative across the country. 
Multiple Ministries and Departments have introduced enabling measures for growth of the CBG 
sector. 
Progress of CBG initiatives, including SATAT, is reviewed by the Inter-Ministerial Task Force on 
GOBARdhan, comprising representatives of stakeholder Ministries and Departments. The Ministry 
also periodically reviews implementation in consultation with OGMCs, CBG producers and other 
stakeholders. 
As per information compiled from the GOBARdhan Portal, 217 CBG plants, with an aggregate 
production capacity of approximately 1,773 tonnes per day, were functional as on 31st July, 2026, 
including 180 CBG plants under SATAT and CBG-CGD Synchronisation Scheme. 
Government have taken several measures to strengthen CBG offtake and facilitate its integration with 
City Gas Distribution (CGD) and natural-gas pipeline networks. These include: 
(i)   A Scheme for Development of Pipeline Infrastructure (DPI) for facilitation of CBG offtake, with a 
total financial outlay of Rs. 994.50 crore for the period FY 2023-24 to FY 2028-29, provides 
financial assistance for laying pipelines connecting CBG plants or clusters with CGD and natural-
gas pipeline networks. So far, 19 CBG plants have been connected through pipelines under the 
Scheme. 
(ii)  Extension of the CBG-CGD Synchronisation Scheme, where GAIL, through a tripartite 
agreement ensures offtake of CBG to the concerned CGD entity, up to 31st December, 2047 and 
expansion of its scope to include injection of CBG into natural-gas pipeline networks. 

(iii) Introduction of phased mandatory sale of CBG in the CNG (Transport) and PNG (Domestic) 
segments of CGD networks, prescribed at 1% for FY 2025-26, 3% for FY 2026-27, 4% for FY 
2027-28 and 5% from FY 2028-29 onwards. During FY 2025-26, CBG sales in the CNG (T) and 
PNG (D) segments reached 1.05% against the target of 1%. 
During FY 2025-26, OGMCs procured approximately 96.5 thousand tonnes of CBG, more than twice 
the quantity procured during FY 2024-25. The extent of substitution of fossil-fuel imports depends on 
the quantity of CBG produced and consumed in place of conventional natural gas and other fossil 
fuels. With commissioning of additional CBG capacity and increased utilisation of CBG, its 
contribution to substitution of imported natural gas is expected to increase further. CBG plants support 
clean-energy production by converting agricultural residue, cattle dung, press mud, municipal solid 
waste and other organic waste into renewable fuel. This contributes to improved waste management, 
reduction in stubble burning and greenhouse-gas emissions, production of organic manure, 
improvement in soil health and promotion of a circular economy. CBG plants also support the rural 
economy through direct and indirect employment, additional income opportunities for farmers, 
development of feedstock and organic-manure supply chains, promotion of organic farming, creation 
of local infrastructure and enhancement of energy security.

(a) to (e):  The National Air Sport Guidelines (NASG, 2023) aims to promote 
safe, affordable and sustainable air sports in the country. These guidelines 
superseded the earlier National Air Sports Policy (NASP) 2022. The guideli nes 
establishes a national framework for air sports through the Air Sports 
Federation of India (ASFI). NASG outlines the governance structure, safety, 
security, registration, flight permission along with provisions of penalty, 
suspension and cancellation for non-compliances in Air Sports activities. Given 
the evolving nature of air sports, the guidelines are dynamic and are reviewed 
from time to time.  
 
Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) oversees the safety requirements 
and licensing for DGCA-regulated categories such as gliders, micro-lights, light 
sports aircraft (LSA), gyroplanes, balloons, powered hang gliders, in 
accordance with the Aircraft Rules, 1937 and DGCA Civil Aviation 
Requirements issued thereunder. The list of operators operating Ho t Air 
Balloons (HAB), Motor Gliders and Aircraft for skydiving is at Annexure I. 
DGCA has issued twelve (12) Special Certificates of Airworthiness (Special C 
of A)/Airworthiness Review Certificates (ARC) for aircraft engaged in Air 
Sports operations. Furth er, as part of DGCA's continued safety oversight 
programme, three (3) safety audits and one (1) surveillance have been 
conducted during 2025-26.

STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (A) TO (D) IN RESPECT 
OF LOK SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. 271 FOR ANSWER ON 
06.08.2026 REGARDING "IMPLEMENTATION OF MODIF IED UDAN 
SCHEME" ASKED BY SHRI BIBHU PRASAD TARAI AND SHRI 
JANARDAN MISHRA.   
 
(a) & (b): The next phase of the UDAN Scheme has been launched on 04.07.2026 
to promote regional air connectivity in Tier -2 and Tier-3 cities and remote regions 
across the country, targeting 120 new destinations and 4 crore passengers over the 
next 10 years. The Scheme is being implemented from F.Y. 2026 -27 to F.Y. 2035-
36 with an outlay of Rs. 28,840 crore, including development of 100 airports from 
existing unserved airstrips w ith an outlay of Rs. 12,159 crore and Rs. 3,661 crore 
for development of 200 heliports in Hilly, North -Eastern and Aspirational 
(HINER) areas.  
The Scheme provides a Challenge Mode framework under which State 
Governments may nominate aerodromes and helipad s for development. Proposals 
are evaluated based on availability of encumbrance -free land, infrastructure 
readiness, technical and operational feasibility, traffic potential, statutory 
clearances and support of the State Governments.  
 
(c): The Union Cabinet has approved the next phase of UDAN scheme, which 
includes the proposal for procurement of two HAL Dhruv helicopters and two 
HAL Dornier aircraft for operation of regional air services, particularly in remote 
and difficult -terrain ar eas, to augment the availability of small aircraft and 
helicopters for regional connectivity and promote the domestic aerospace sector 
under the Atmanirbhar Bharat initiative. 
 
(d): To strengthen the operational viability of regional routes and promote 
sustainable passenger traffic, the Scheme incorporates a longer VGF mechanism 
extending up to five years, progressively tapered to enable airlines to transition 
towards commercially sustainable operations. 
 
Further, the State Governments/Union Territory Admin istrations may identify and 
propose their priority routes for inclusion in the bidding process in accordance with 
the provisions of the Scheme.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIATION 
LOK SABHA 
STARRED QUESTION NO. : 273 
 ( TO BE ANSWERED ON THE  6th August 2026 )  
EXPANSION OF DIGI YATRA PLATFORM 
273.    SHRI RAHUL SINGH LODHI                   
             SHRI KHAGEN MURMU                        
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION 
be pleased to state:- 
(a) whether the Government has undertaken measures to expand the Digi Yatra platform 
across additional airports in the country and if so, the details thereof; 
 
(b) the measures undertaken to enhance the accessibility of the platform including support for 
regional languages and other passenger-friendly features; 
 
(c) whether the Government has undertaken any assessment regarding the impact of Digi 
Yatra on passenger facilitation and airport operations and if so, the details thereof; and 
 
(d) the measures adopted to strengthen data privacy, cybersecurity and secure biometric 
authentication under the Digi Yatra ecosystem? 
ANSWER 
Minister of CIVIL AVIATION      (Shri Kinjarapu Rammohan Naidu) 
(a) to (d): A statement is laid on the table of the house. 
****** 
  

STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (A) TO (D) IN 
RESPECT OF LOK SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. 273 FOR REPLY 
ON 06.08.2026 REGARDING EXPANSION OF D IGI YATRA PLATFORM 
ASKED BY SHRI RAHUL SINGH LODHI AND SHRI KHAGEN MURMU  
 
(a) to (d):  The Government has undertaken  a phased expansion of the Digi 
Yatra ecosystem. Starting with 3 airports in December 2022, Digi Yatra is 
now available at 39 airports. Digi Yatra has been designed as a citizen-centric 
platform focusing on accessibility, inclusivity and ease of use. Several 
passenger-friendly features are available in Digi Yatra, including, Driving 
Licence-based enrolment through DigiLocker and multilingual support. Apart 
from English, 11 Indian languages namely Hindi, Tamil, Bengali, Marathi, 
Kannada, Telugu, Gujarati, Odia, Assamese, Sanskrit and Malayalam are 
supported in Digi Yatra app. Further, the Digi Yatra ecosystem is 
continuously improved based on  passenger feedback received through 
customer support channels and airport interactions.  
 
Digi Yatra provides seamless, hassle -free and faster passenger processing, 
saving approximately 50% of the passenger's time at different checkpoints at 
the airport s, as compared to manual validation, which helps in addressing 
congestion at the airports. Since launch, Digi Yatra app has been downloaded 
over 2.5 Crore times and it has been used more than 10.75 Crore times by 
passengers to travel through Digi Yatra enabled airports.  
 
The Digi Yatra Central Ecosystem (DYCE) is built on the fundamental tenets 
of privacy. Digi Yatra app is built on privacy by design and there is no central 
storage of passenger's Personally Identifiable Information (PII) data, thereby 
mitigating issues of data loss, theft and leakage. All the passenger data is 
encrypted and stored in the passenger's smartphone wallet and shared only for 
a limited time duration with the origin airport, where the passenger's ID needs 
to be validated. The data  is purged from the system within 24 hours of the 
scheduled departure time of the flight. 
 
 Digi Yatra complies with the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 and 
the Rules made thereunder. Regular security assessments, vulnerability 
assessments and a udits are undertaken to strengthen the overall security 
posture of the platform. These measures ensure that Digi Yatra remains a 
secure, privacy-preserving and trusted digital identity platform for seamless 
passenger processing.

LOK SABHA 
STARRED QUESTION NO. 274 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 06th AUGUST, 2026 
 
Crude Oil Production 
 
*274: Ms. Mahua Moitra: 
 
पेटŌोिलयम एवं Ůाक ृ ितक गैस मंũी 
 
Will the Minister of PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the details of the domestic production of crude oil both from offshore and onshore fields 
during the last three years, year-wise;  
(b) whether there has been a decline in production from major mature fields of Oil and Natural Gas 
Corporation (ONGC) and Oil India Limited (OIL) during the said period, if so, the details 
thereof; 
(c) whether the Government has proposed for Enhanced Oil Recovery (EOR) and Improved Oil 
Recovery (IOR) projects, including polymer flooding and microbial EOR, if so, the details 
thereof and if not, the reasons therefor; 
(d) whether the Government has undertaken reservoir re-evaluation using advanced seismic imaging 
and digital oilfield technologies, if so, the details thereof; and 
(e) the details of the projected contribution of EOR to domestic crude oil production by the 
year 2030? 
 
ANSWER 
 
पेटŌोिलयम एवं Ůाक ृ ितक गैस मंũी 
(ŵी हरदीप िसंह पुरी) 
 
MINISTER OF PETROELUM AND NATURAL GAS 
(SHRI HARDEEP SINGH PURI) 
 
(a) to (e): A statement is laid on the Table of the House. 
  

 
STATEMENT REFFERED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (a) TO (e) OF LOK SABHA 
STARRED QUESTION NO. *274 BY MS. MAHUA MOITRA TO BE ANSWERED ON 06TH 
AUGUST, 2026 REGARDING ‘CRUDE OIL PRODUCTION’ 
 
(a) The domestic production of crude oil from Offshore and Onshore fields during the last three 
years is tabulated below: 
OIL (Million Metric Tonnes, 
MMT) 2023-24 2024-25 2025-26 
OFFSHORE 15.03 15.09 14.83 
ONSHORE 14.33 13.61 13.13 
Grand Total 29.36 28.70 27.96 
 
(b)  The domestic oil production over the last three years has shown slight decline primarily owing 
to natural decline in mature and ageing oil and gas fields, as per details given below:- 
OIL (MMT) 2023-24 2024-25 2025-26 
ONGC (Nomination) 19.21 18.47 17.80 
OIL (Nomination) 3.34 3.44 3.43 
Total 22.56 21.91 21.23 
 
During this period, the National Oil Companies (NOCs) namely Oil and Natural Gas Corporation 
(ONGC) Limited and Oil India Limited (OIL) have consistently sustained their production levels. 
The NOCs have been able to contain the annual decline rate to around 2% since 2014-15, which is 3 
times superior to the global average decline rate of 6% for mature fields (as per International Energy 
Agency). 
 
(c) & (d): The Government does not directly implement field-level projects for Enhanced Oil 
Recovery (EOR), Improved Oil Recovery (IOR), or reservoir re-evaluation. The responsibility for 
reservoir management and selection of suitable recovery techniques rests with the exploration and 
production (E&P) operators. Such projects function within the statutory and regulatory framework 
established under the Oilfields (Regulation and Development) Act, 1948 and the Petroleum and 
Natural Gas Rules, 2025, which provide for the systematic and efficient development of petroleum 
resources.  
 
The Government supports these efforts through policy incentives, basin-level studies and technical 
oversight. For better understanding of hydrocarbon resource potential at the basin level, the 
Government has funded Hydrocarbon Resource Assessment Study (HRAS) through which 
comprehensive re-assessment of India's sedimentary basins was carried out in the year 2017.  

 
Details of EOR/IOR and reservoir re-evaluation initiatives undertaken by E&P operators are in 
Annexure-I. 
 
Further, the 'Samudra Manthan' - National Offshore Exploration Scheme has been approved by 
theUnion Cabinet on 31.07.2026 for large-scale acquisition, processing and interpretation of high-
quality seismic data, accelerated exploratory drilling in deepwater and ultra-deepwater areas, along 
with development of common infrastructure and oil & gas manufacturing zone. Details of the 
scheme are in Annexure-II. 
 
(e): EOR is not a centrally executed production programme and its contribution is, therefore, not 
projected as a single separate national target for the year 2030. EOR projects are planned and 
implemented field-wise by individual E&P operator on the basis of reservoir characteristics, 
technical feasibility and economic viability. The incremental production expected from such projects 
forms part of the respective field development and production plans and is periodically revised in 
light of pilot results, actual reservoir response, project implementation schedules and prevailing 
techno-economic conditions. Accordingly, the contribution of EOR to domestic crude oil production 
by 2030 will be the aggregate of incremental production realised from the various projects 
implemented by the Lessees. 
***** 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 
  

 
ANNEXURE-I 
ANNEXURE REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (C) TO (D) IN RESPECT OF LOK 
SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. *274 BY MS. MAHUA MOITRA TO BE ANSWERED 
ON 06TH AUGUST, 2026 REGARDING ‘CRUDE OIL PRODUCTION’ 
A. Details of Major EOR/IOR Initiatives 
 
1. Oil and Natural Gas Corporation (ONGC) Limited 
a) ONGC has been a pioneer in the implementation of Enhanced Oil Recovery (EOR) methods 
since 1987, having successfully executed over 22 pilot and commercial projects to date.  
b) Currently, implementation of a comprehensive portfolio of EOR technologies has been 
undertaken across fields in Gujarat, Assam, and Mumbai High.  
c) These include in-situ combustion, polymer flooding, alkaline-surfactant-polymer (ASP) 
flooding, low-salinity water flooding, microbial EOR, miscible gas injection, and immiscible 
gas injection.  
d) These measures form part of ONGC's continuing programme to moderate natural decline in 
mature reservoirs and enhance recovery from existing fields. 
e) ONGC also carries out IOR through work-over, well stimulation, development drilling, 
installation of artificial lift, and reservoir pressure maintenance. 
2. Oil India Limited (OIL) 
a) Implementation of Low-Salinity Water Injection has been undertaken in 17 reservoirs of the 
Upper Assam Basin  
b) For heavy-oil recovery, Cyclic Steam Stimulation has been successfully implemented in the 
Baghewala field of Rajasthan since 2018 
c) In addition, OIL regularly undertakes field-specific IOR measures such as work-over, well 
stimulation, development drilling, installation of artificial lift, and reservoir pressure 
maintenance. 
3. Vedanta Limited 
a) Vedanta has successfully implemented chemical Enhanced Oil Recovery (EOR) techniques 
in its fields within Block RJ-ON-90/1 in the state of Rajasthan.  
b) Full-field Polymer flood has been implemented across all major producing fields, namely 
Mangala, Bhagyam, Aishwariya, and NE.  
c) A significant expansion of this initiative has been undertaken with Alkali-Surfactant-Polymer 
(ASP) flooding implementation in the Mangala field.  
d) These measures form part of Vedanta's ongoing programme to enhance recovery from its 
producing assets and maximise hydrocarbon production from existing fields. 
 
B. Details of reservoir re-evaluation and digital oilfield initiatives 
 
a) A range of advanced geoscientific and digital technologies is being deployed by operators to 
enhance reservoir characterisation and unlock the full potential of hydrocarbon resources. 

 
These include advanced seismic imaging, AI/ML-driven interpretation workflows, 3D 
seismic data re-processing, digital reservoir modelling and simulation and advanced well 
logging.  
b) Operators are also leveraging digital oilfield technologies, including sensors, SCADA 
systems, IoT, AI, and advanced analytics, across their E&P operations to enable data-driven 
decision-making.  
c) Reservoir evaluation forms an integral part of regular field-level reserves assessment and 
management activities. Operators periodically re-evaluate reservoirs using updated 
geological interpretation, well results, production performance, pressure data, and reservoir 
modelling.  
  

 
ANNEXURE-II 
ANNEXURE REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (C) TO (D) IN RESPECT OF LOK 
SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. *274 BY MS. MAHUA MOITRA TO BE ANSWERED 
ON 06TH AUGUST, 2026 REGARDING ‘CRUDE OIL PRODUCTION’ 
Brief of "Samudra Manthan" – National Offshore Exploration Scheme 
1. The Union Cabinet approved 'Samudra Manthan' – the National Offshore Exploration Scheme on 
31.07.2026 with an outlay of Rs.84,084 crore for implementation up to FY 2030-31. 
2. The Scheme envisages strengthening India's energy security through accelerated offshore oil and 
gas exploration and production, technological capability enhancement, and alignment with the vision 
of Viksit Bharat. 
3. The Scheme includes a component for large-scale acquisition, processing and interpretation of 
high-quality seismic data to improve understanding of offshore hydrocarbon potential. 
4. The Scheme envisages accelerated exploratory drilling in deepwater and ultra-deepwater areas. 
5. The Scheme includes a component for: 
a) Development of common offshore production and evacuation infrastructure. 
b) Establishment of an Oil & Gas Manufacturing and Services Zone, in line with the Make in 
India initiative. 
6. The Scheme document includes provisions relating to digital programme management, capacity 
building, technology adoption, stakeholder engagement and international outreach. 
7. The Scheme is envisaged to contribute to improved offshore resource assessment, increased 
exploration activity, employment generation, investment and strengthening of the offshore 
exploration ecosystem.

IMPLEMENTATION OF SBM-U 
 
NO. 275 SHRI JUGAL KISHORE: 
     SHRI RAJKUMAR CHAHAR: 
 
Will the Minister of HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government has undertaken a review of the implementation 
of the Swachh Bharat Mission-Urban (SBM-U) in the Urban Local Bodies 
(ULBs) and if so, the details and the key findings thereof along with the 
details of the work undertaken so far across  the country, ULB and 
State/UT-wise including Jammu; 
(b) the progress made so far in scientific processing of municipal solid 
waste, waste segregation at source, treatment and restoration of legacy 
dump sites along with the details of the funds sanctioned, released and 
utilised for the same across the country, U LB and State/UT - wise 
including Jammu; 
(c)whether the Government has taken any specific measures to strengthen 
the effective implementation of the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026 
by the ULBs across the country and if so, the details thereof along with 
the details of the financial and technical assistance provided thereunder, 
ULB and State/UT-wise including Jammu; 
(d) the observed impact of these initiatives on achieving garbage-free cities 
across the country; 
(e) the details of waste processing capacity created during the last three 
years, city-wise; and 
(f) the measures proposed to be taken to improve waste management and 
reduce landfill dependency across the country? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS 
(SHRI MANOHAR LAL) 
 
(a) to (f): A statement is laid on the Table of the House. 

STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO LOK SABHA STARRED QUESTION 
NO. 275 FOR 06.08.2026 REGARDING “IMPLEMENTATION OF SBM-U” 
(a): Sanitation is a State subject. State/ULBs are responsible for planning, 
designing, executing, operating and reviewing sanitation projects including 
Urban Waste Management (UWM) and Sewage Treatment Plant (STP) 
facilities in the urban areas of the country.  
The Government of India launched the Swachh Bharat Mission-Urban (SBM-
U) on 2 October 2014 to achieve Open Defecation Free (ODF) status, 
scientific solid waste management, and sustained behaviour change, 
followed by SBM-U 2.0, launched on 1 October 2021, with the aim of making 
all cities Garbage Free,  through scientific waste processing, legacy 
dumpsite remediation, and Used Water Management (UWM) in urban areas 
with populations below one lakh. 
As per the DMEO, NITI Aayog evaluation report (September 2025), SBM -U 
and SBM-U 2.0 have significantly improved sanitation, dignity, and safety, 
particularly for women and vulnerable communities, with 94% of surveyed 
households reporting an end to open def ecation. The report also highlights 
major progress in solid waste management, with over 90% door -to-door 
waste collection coverage, 91% source segregation, waste processing 
increasing from 18% in 2014 to over 80% in 2025. 
Further, a two -day National Review Meeting of Swachh Bharat Mission-
Urban 2.0 was held on 19–20 May 2026 at Vigyan Bhawan, New Delhi with 
all States and UTs to review implementation progress. During the meeting 
comprehensive implementation review was taken on Institutional 
Strengthening for Improved Project Implementation, Visible Cleanliness,  
Segregation, Collection & Transportation, Organic Waste Management , 
Construction and Demolition Waste Management, Integrated Solid Waste 
Management and Financial Modelling, Legacy Waste Remediation, Access 
to Sanitation, Swachh Survekshan and Solid Waste Management Rules, 
2026. 
This was followed by a PRAGATI Review Meeting on 27
th May, 2026 to ensure 
holistic monitoring, Centre–State coordination, and facilitate the timely 
resolution of implementation challenges. 

The National Advisory and Review Committee (NARC), at the Ministry level, 
also r eviews the progress of SBM -U 2.0  & approves  action plans of 
State/UTs. 
The work done under SBM-U 2.0 is at Annexure I. 
(b): As reported by States/UTs on Swachhattam portal, door-to-door waste
