GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS 
LOK SABHA 
STARRED QUESTION NO. 276 
TO BE ANSWERED ON AUGUST 06, 2026 
 
ASSISTANCE AND INCENTIVES UNDER PM SVANIDHI SCHEME 
 
NO. 276 SHRI BIPLAB KUMAR DEB: 
   
Will the Minister of HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
(a) the details of the assistance and incentives extended to 
beneficiaries under the PM Street Vendor's AtmaNirbhar Nidhi (PM 
SVANidhi) Scheme; 
(b) the measures undertaken to improve financial inclusion and access 
to institutional credit for street vendors; 
(c) whether any assessment has been made with regard to the impact 
of the s cheme on the livelihood of street vendors, particularly in 
Tripura and if so, the details thereof; and 
(d) the initiatives undertaken to expand the outreach of the scheme?  
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS 
(SHRI MANOHAR LAL) 
 
(a) to (d): A statement is laid on the Table of the House.  

STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN THE LOK SABHA STARRED QUESTION 
NO. 27 6 (16TH POSITION) FOR ANSWER ON 06.08.2026 REGARDING 
“ASSISTANCE AND INCENTIVES UNDER PM SVANIDHI SCHEME” 
 
(a): Prime Minister Street Vendor’s AtmaNirbhar Nidhi (PM SVANidhi) 
Scheme was launched on 1
st June, 2020 with the objective of facilitating 
collateral free working capital term loans to urban street vendors. Under 
the restructured scheme which was approved by the Union Cabinet in 
August 2025,  working capital term loans are provided to the street 
vendors in three tranches of up to ₹15,000, ₹25,000, and ₹50,000 for 
repayment in 12 months, 18 months, and 36 months respectively through 
monthly instalments. As on 12th July, 2026, 76.95 lakh street vendors 
have availed 1.15 crore collateral-free loans amounting to ₹ 18,475.06 
crore under the Scheme. 
 
To incentivise regular repayment, 7% interest subsidy is provided on 
regular repayment of loans under the scheme.  
 
Under the restructured scheme, UPI -linked RuPay Credit Card has been 
introduced for beneficiaries who have repaid the second loan tranche.  
Further, to promote digital adoption, street vendor beneficiaries are 
incentivized with a cashback of up to ₹100 per month for a period of 12 
months (maximum digital incentive of ₹1200), for every tranche of loan 
provided to the street vendor. The restruct ured scheme also provisions 
for cashback of maximum ₹100 per quarter for 4 quarters (maximum 
incentive of ₹400) to street vendor beneficiaries for conducting digital 
transactions on wholesale purchases of at least ₹2,000. 
 
‘SVANidhi se Samriddhi’ component under the PM SVANidhi Scheme, was 
launched on 04 January, 2021, to build social security net for the 
beneficiaries and their family members. This facilitates linkages to eight 
selected Central Government welfare schemes. A s on 12th July 2026, 
socio economic profiling is completed for 50.63 lakh PM SVANidhi 
beneficiaries and a total of 1.56 crore scheme sanctions have been 
extended to them. 
 
(b):   Prime Minister Street Vendor's AtmaNirbhar Nidhi (PM SVANidhi) 
Scheme is implemented to improve financial inclusion and access to 
institutional credit for Street Vendors. Under the Scheme, eligible street 
vendors are provided collateral -free working capital loans in three 
progressive tranches of up to ₹15,000, ₹25,000 and ₹50,000. Street 
vendors move to the next tranche upon timely repayment, enabling them 
to avail themselves of the next higher loan tranche.  To reduce the cost 
of borrowing and encourage repayment, the Scheme provides an interest 

subsidy of 7% per annum on timely repayment of loans. Further, credit 
guarantee cover is provided to lending institutions and credit card 
issuers to mitigate credit risk, and encourage them to extend collateral-
free credit with greater confidence. 
 
UPI-linked RuPay Credit Cards have been introduced for beneficiaries 
who have repaid the second loan tranche, providing them with further 
access to credit to meet their immediate business/financial needs. 
Applications are received through the PM SVANidhi Portal and PM 
SVANidhi Mobile App. Officials of Urban Local Bodies (ULBs) and Blocks 
assist eligible street vendors in availing loans and credit cards under the 
Scheme. 
  
(c): In Tripura, since scheme inception till 12th July 2026, 6,202 street 
vendors have availed 9,517 collateral -free loans amounting to ₹15.88 
crore.  
Impact assessment studies of the PM SVANidhi S cheme were 
undertaken by Indian School of Business (ISB), Hyderabad in 2023 & 
2025. The 2023 study was conducted in 100 Urban Local Bodies (ULBs) 
across the country covering more than 5,000 beneficiaries and it found 
that PM SVANidhi was the first loan from a bank for 95% of the 
beneficiaries. The 2025 study was conducted in 99 Urban Local Bodies 
(ULBs) across the country covering more than 5,000 beneficiaries (with 
around 60% of the respondents being part of the 2023 study sample) and 
it found that the average annualized business income among SVANidhi 
borrowers grew by around 20 percent, between 2023 and 2025.  
Around 30 percent of borrowers across all cycles reported holding loans 
other than PM SVANidhi loans which underscores the scheme’s role in 
building credit histories for vendors who previously had little or no 
access to formal credit.  
The study also found the scheme’s impact extends well beyond business 
recovery. By easing credit constraints and stabilizing household cash 
flows, the scheme has enabled vendor families to improve living 
conditions, strengthen food security, enhance access to health-care, and 
support children’s education. 
(d):  The PM SVANidhi Scheme was initially implemented in statutory 
urban areas. The eligibility was also extended to street vendors from 
surrounding peri-urban areas who vend within the geographical limits of 
Urban Local Bodies (ULBs). Under the restructured PM  SVANidhi 
Scheme, the coverage of the s cheme is expanded beyond statutory 
urban areas to include census towns, peri -urban areas etc in a graded 
manner. 

To ensure wider inclusion of street vendor beneficiaries, the Ministry has 
undertaken several initiatives, including periodic awareness campaigns 
through radio jingles, television and newspaper advertisements. States 
and Union Territories are also regularl y provided with Information, 
Education and Communication (IEC) materials in local languages to 
facilitate outreach and dissemination of scheme benefits among street 
vendors. Regular reviews are also conducted with States/UTs/ULBs and 
banks /lending institutions.  
Under the scheme, MoHUA has organized various campaigns and events 
to enhance outreach to street vendors. After the approval of the 
restructured PM SVANidhi Scheme on 27th August 2025, Lok Kalyan 
Melas have been organized from time to time in ULBs across all 
States/UTs. These Melas promote awareness about the new features of 
the scheme and suppor t vendor mobilisation, loan application 
submission, faster loan disbursement, and digital onboarding of 
beneficiaries. ULBs, in collaboration with Digital Payment Aggregators 
(DPAs), also conduct regular digital literacy camps. To enhance digital 
onboarding and promote the adoption of cashless payments among 
street vendors, beneficiaries are provided cashback incentives.

STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (a) TO (c) OF STARRED 
QUESTION NO. *277 TO BE ANSWERED ON 06.08.2026 IN LOK SABHA 
REGARDING “FLOOD MANAGEMENT IN JORHAT DISTRICT OF ASSAM” 
(a) to (c) Jorhat district in Assam experiences recurring floods of varying 
magnitudes almost every year.  
Flood management, including anti-erosion schemes, and schemes for the 
supply of safe drinking water in flood affected areas are formulated and 
implemented by the concerned State Governments as per their priorities. 
Government of India supplements the efforts if the State Governments by 
providing technical guidance and promotional financial assistance. 
The Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) is being implemented, in partnership with 
the States to provide potable tap water supply of prescribed quality and on 
regular & long-term basis to every rural household in the country. The JJM 2.0 
Operational Guidelines envisage the provisions for addressing drinking water 
supply during natural calamities and disasters, and stipulates that: 
i. States/Union Territories integrate climate-resilient measures, including 
source diversification, aquifer recharge and local storage systems. Each 
scheme has an emergency continuity plan to ensure uninterrupted water 
supply during droughts, floods and other disruptions.  
ii. During emergencies and disasters, the Water Quality Monitoring and 
Surveillance framework under Jal Jeevan Mission is activated on a priority 
basis to ensure the continued safety of drinking water supplies. States and 
implementing agencies  undertake immediate risk assessment of water 
sources and infrastructure, with enhanced frequency of water quality 
testing, particularly for bacteriological contamination. Disinfection 
measures, including chlorination are ensured at all supply points and 
alternate safe water arrangements are made where contamination is 

3 
 
detected or anticipated including areas where the sources and/or supply 
systems are defunct due to disaster. Village Water and Sanitation 
Committees (VWSCs) are mobilized for community-level surveillance and 
reporting, while District and State laboratories  operate in a mission mode 
for rapid testing and response. Timely dissemination of advisories to the 
public regarding safe water handling and usage are ensured to prevent 
water-borne diseases. 
iii. States utilize National and State Disaster Response Funds to restore water 
supply infrastructure damaged by natural calamities or internal 
disturbances. 
Five flood management projects of the Government of Assam have been 
included under Flood Management and Border Areas Programme (FMBAP), in 
Jorhat district and central assistance of Rs 3,430.11 Lakh has been released. 
Further, Brahmaputra Board, under the Department of Water Resources, River 
Development and Ganga Rejuvenation has prepared Master Plans of 
Brahmaputra Main Stem, Bhogdoi, Jhanji, Dhansiri, benefiting Jorhat district, 
among others, and inter-alia, include both structural and non-structural 
measures for flood management over the short, medium and long term basis. 
The Central Water Commission also maintains 32 Flood Forecasting Stations 
(30 Level Forecast Stations and 2 Inflow Forecast Stations) in Assam, of which 
one Flood Forecasting Station, namely Neamatighat, is located on the 
Brahmaputra River in Jorhat District.

Statement referred to in reply to parts (a) to (d) of Lok Sabha Starred Question No. *278 
answered on 06.08.2026 regarding “Contaminated Drinking Water Sources” asked by Shri 
Balwant Baswant Wankhade 
 
(a) to ( d) Drinking Water being a State  subject, the responsibility of Planning, Designing, 
Approval, Implementation, Operation & Maintenance of drinking water supply schemes, including 
those under the Jal Jeevan Mission, is vested with State/UT Governments. The Government of 
India supplements the efforts of the States by providing financial, policy guidance and technical 
assistance. 
The Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) – Har Ghar Jal, was launched in August 2019, in partnership with 
States/ UTs to make provision of potable tap water supply in adequate quantity, of prescribed 
quality and on regular & long -term basis to rural households. Under JJM, as per existing 
guidelines, Bureau of Indian Standards’ BIS:10500 standards are adopted as benchmark for quality 
of water being supplied through the piped water supply schemes. 
At the start of the Mission, only 3.24 crore (16.72%) rural households were reported to have tap 
water connection in the country. As on 18.07.2026, out of 19.36 crore rural households, around 
15.89 crore (82.09%) rural households have been provided tap water connection. 
Under JJM, while planning water supply schemes to provide tap water supply to households, 
priority is given to habitations affected by chemical contaminants.  States/ UTs have been advised 
to plan and implement piped water supply schemes based on alternative safe water sources/ bulk 
water transfer for the villages with water quality issues.  Moreover, any water supply scheme 
undertaken under JJM is approved after the recommendation of Source Finding Committee of the 
respective State Government, to the effect that the identified water source planned under the 
scheme, has sufficient yield for sustaining water supply as per required norm. 
In consultation with various stakeholders 'Concise Handbook for Monitoring Water Quality of 
Piped Drinking Water Supply to Rural Households’ was released in December 2024 for guidance 
to States/ UT’s. This handbook recommended for a comprehensive testing of drinking water 
samples at various testing points such as source, treatment plant, storage and distribution points, 
and remedial action wherever necessary, to ensure that the water supplied to households is of 
prescribed quality (BIS:10500).  The recommended remedial action s include the immediate 
closure of chemically contaminated water sources,  notifying the result to the relevant authorities 
and affected communities, providing safe drinking water as per JJM guidelines (at least 8-10 lpcd) 
through a safe source or through alternate means immediately within 24 hrs till piped water supply 
is restored, implementing emergency treatment measures, actions such as cleaning of OHTs, check 
pipe line leakage, etc. within 7 days, testing all basic and area -specific chemical as well as 
bacteriological parameters, and, if found safe, restore water supply from  a safe source in case of 
chemical contaminants. On the other hand, in case of bacterial  contamination, immediate action 
(within 24 hrs) must be taken, which includes proper disinfe ction, intimate concern for authority 
and affected communities, and temporary arrangement to provide safe drinking water through 
tankers (8 -10 lpcd).

25, 2025-26 and 2026-27 are annexed. 
Ministry of Housing and Urban Af fairs (MoHUA) has informed that Atal Mission for 
Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation (AMRUT) launched in the year 2015 in selected 500 
cities and towns across the country was focused on development of basic infrastructure in the 
sectors of water supply, sewerage and septage management, etc. To expand the coverage, AMRUT

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS 
LOK SABHA 
STARRED QUESTION NO. 279 
TO BE ANSWERED ON AUGUST 06, 2026 
IMPLEMENTATION OF SMART CITIES MISSION 
 
No. 279  SMT. MALVIKA DEVI: 
 SHRI DHAIRYASHEEL SAMBHAJIRAO MANE: 
 
Will the Minister of HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government has undertaken any assessment of the 
implementation and overall performance of the Smart Cities 
Mission (SCM) across the country and if so, the details and the key 
findings thereof, city-wise; 
(b) the details of the projects sanctioned, completed, operationalised 
and under implementation under the Mission including the status 
of Integrated Command and Control Centres (ICCCs) across the 
country, city-wise; 
(c) whether the Government has taken any measures to strengthen 
monitoring, transparency, accountability and timely execution of 
projects under SCM and if so, the details thereof, city-wise; 
(d) the details of the use of digital platforms, third- party audits and 
other monitoring mechanisms for monitoring the implementation of 
projects under SCM; 
(e) the manner in which the assets and digital infrastructure created 
under the Mission are proposed to be leveraged for improving urban 
governance, citiz en-centric service delivery and long- term 
sustainability of cities; 
(f) whether any proposal is under consideration for expansion of SCM 
or related digital and urban infrastructure projects in the major 
urban areas across the country and if so, the details thereof, 
State/UT-wise; 
(g) whether the Government has any proposal or policy framework to 
replicate and extend the technological interventions and urban 
governance tools developed under the SCM to non- selected Tier-2 
and Tier-3 municipal bodies in tribal and developing regions of the 
country and if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS 
(SHRI MANOHAR LAL) 
 
(a)  to (g): A Statement is laid on the Table of the House. 

 
 
STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY OF PARTS (a) to (g) OF THE LOK 
SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. 279 (19thPOSITION) FOR ANSWER ON 
06.08.2026 REGARDING IMPLEMENTATION OF SMART CITIES MISSION 
 
(a):  Yes. NITI Aayog in its report titled ‘Evaluation of Centrally 
Sponsored Schemes in Package 4 – Urban Transformation and 
Skill Development’ published in September 2025, has concluded 
that the Smart Cities Mission (SCM) demonstrates strong 
alignment with national urban priorities and citizen needs, 
contributing significantly to multiple United Nations Sustainable 
Development Goals. As per the report, the Mission has achieved a 
high project completion rate of 93% of 8,063 projects and 100% 
completion of Integrated Command and Control Centres (ICCCs), 
leading to measurable improvements in urban livability , mobility, 
safety, and environmental outcomes. 
 
(b):  Under SCM, 8,064 projects worth ₹1,64,811 Cr were taken up 
since inception of the Mission. As reported by States/UTs as on 
31.03.2026, 7,790 projects (97%) worth ₹1,56,257 Cr have been 
completed. ICCCs have been established in all 100 Smart Cities.  
 
 State/UT-wise and City -wise status  of smart city projects  is at 
Annexure. 
 
(c) and (d): SCM has come to end on 31.03.2025. Ministry of Housing 
and Urban Affairs (MoHUA) followed multi-level review structure 
to expedite the progress of projects under the SCM. At the 
National level, implementation was  monitored by an Apex 
Committee headed by Secretary, MoHUA.  At the State level, 
Mission implementation was monitored by the State level High 
Powered Steering Committee (HPSC) chaired by the Chief 
Secretary.  At the City level, there was provision for establishing 
Smart City Advisory Forum (SCAF) for all 100 cities to advise and 
enable collaboration among various stakeholders. The monitoring 
of physical and financial progress of the projects under the 
mission was done through Geo Spatial Management Information 
System (GMIS) portal for effective monitoring and evaluation. 
 
 Further, post closure of SCM on 31.03.2025, Ministry of Housing 
and Urban Affairs (MoHUA) has issued Advisory No. 27 dated 10
th 
June, 2025 to all States/ UTs. As per the advisory, the Special 
Purpose Vehicles (SPVs) were advised to ensure the timely 
completion of SCM projects and prepare O&M plans for the assets 
created. 

 
(e): As per the Advisory No. 27 dated 10th June, 2025 issued by MoHUA, 
the SPVs were advised to leverage ICCCs as city operating 
systems and state analytical hubs, with operational control 
preferably retained by the urban development departments. SPVs 
may receive service-linked revenues for managing ICCC functions. 
States and Union Territories, through their  respective High-
Powered Steering Committees (HPSCs)  chaired by Chief 
Secretary, have been encouraged to chart out urban sector 
priorities and map areas where SPVs can continue to play a 
strategic role.  Further, MoHUA has encouraged ICCCs towards 
integration with line departments within the municipal 
governance and to render services to the Urban Local Bodies 
(ULBs).
 
  
(f): No.  
 
(g):   SCM was aimed to develop 100 cities as replicable models of 
sustainable and technology-driven urban development, serving as 
“lighthouses” for other cities. The implementation of multi -
sectoral projects has generated valuable on- ground learnings in 
integrated planning, convergence, governance, and technology 
adoption. These learnings can be leveraged by State 
Governments/UTs to handhold cities in adopting scalable and 
replicable solutions, thereby extending the impact of SCM beyond 
the selected cities and promoting broader urban transformation 
across the country.

DAMAGE TO ROADS AND FLYOVERS 
*280. SHRI CAPTAIN VIRIATO FERNANDES:            
Will the Minister of ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
सड़क परिवहन औि िाजमार्ग मंत्री 
be pleased to state: 
(a) the total number and details of National Highway (NH) road 
sections built by the Ministry that have caved in, failed or suffered 
major structural damage since 2014 due to contractor negligence; 
(b) the tot al number and details of flyovers built along National 
Highways that have collapsed or failed since 2014, State-wise; 
(c) the total number and details of contractors or firms involved in 
construction of roads penalised and/or blacklisted for failure of roa ds 
and/or flyovers along NH; 
(d) the total number and the details of cases where flooding in low 
lying areas/agricultural fields have been reported due to faulty 
construction of NH across the country since 2014, State- wise; and 
(e) the total number and de tails of land slides reported along NHs 
across the country since 2014, State-wise? 
  
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
(SHRI NITIN JAIRAM GADKARI) 
(a) to (e) A statement is laid on the Table of the House. 
  
  

STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY  TO PARTS (a) TO (e) OF LOK 
SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. 280 ANSWERED ON 06 TH AUGUST, 
2026 ASKED BY SHRI CAPTAIN VIRIATO FERNANDES REGARDING 
DAMAGE TO ROADS AND FLYOVERS 
(a) to (c) All efforts are made to ensure that the National Highways 
(NHs) are constructed as per stipulated quality standards specified in 
the Indian Roads Congress (IRC) specifications and codes. To ensure 
that highway construction adheres to stipulated quality standards, 
Consultants (Authority’s Engineer/ Independent Engineers - AE/IE) are 
appointed by the executing agencies for day -to-day supervision of 
works at site. Officials of executing agencies undertake inspections 
from time to time and ensure adherence of conformity of quality of the 
work done by the Concessionaire/ Contractors with stipul ated 
requirements. In addition, Third-Party Quality Auditors are deployed for 
independent quality audits of NH works on a case-to-case basis. 
             State / Union Territory (UT) – wise details of projects involving 
caving in, major failures or major structural damage on NHs including 
on bridges and flyovers due to various factors including negligence on 
part of Contractors and action taken against Contractors/ 
Concessionaires/ AE/IE etc. since 2014 are at Annexure -I. Action 
against defaulting agencies  has been taken as per the provisions of 
the Contract/ Concession agreement in case of deficiencies/ damages, 
such as termination of contract agreement, levying of penalties/ 
liquidated damages, debarment/ blacklisting, declaring as non -
performers etc.   
  
(d)      Drainage systems on NHs are designed keeping in mind 
expected traffic, importance and configuration of road, sources of 
water, hydrology and hydro -geologic conditions of catchment area, 
geometric characteristics of the road, presence of extreme g radients 
and cross slope, areas of excavation and landfill, existing drainage 
systems, etc.   However, localized issues in drainage systems are 

caused due to non -clearance of existing drainage system, blockage of 
the drainage outfall by unauthorized constru ction, poor maintenance 
of drainage system in some cases and unprecedented rainfall leading 
to flooding of drainage systems and low -lying areas/ agricultural fields 
near the NHs.  
State / UT – wise details of major incidents of flooding of low -
lying areas/ agricultural fields in NHs stretches reported due to faulty 
construction since 2014 and corrective actions taken are at Annexure -
II. 
(e)   Generally, incidents of extreme rainfall and landslides are 
witnessed in the Himalayan Region and Western Ghat secti ons 
causing large scale damages to infrastructure including NH sections. 
Removal of debris and necessary measures for restoration of NH 
section to traffic-worthy condition are taken on an immediate basis by 
the concerned executing agencies. Long -term Remed ial Measures of 
Landslide Prone Areas on NHs are also taken up from time -to-time 
based on details.  
State / UT – wise details of major Incidents of landslides in NHs 
stretches reported since 2014 and corrective actions taken are at 
Annexure-III. 
The Government has taken various initiatives for developing disaster 
resilient NH infrastructure in Hilly States/ UTs, such as: 
i. Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) signed with Tehri Hydro 
Development Corporation India Ltd. (THDCIL) for specialized 
landslide treatment measures for the State of Uttarakhand, 
Arunachal Pradesh and Mizoram. 
ii. Decision taken in November, 2024 for implementation of 
“Cost-effective Long-term Remedial Measures of Landslide Prone 
areas in Hilly region” as per Expert Committee Report. 
iii. Decision take n in November, 2025 through policy initiative on 
"Additional Augmented and Systematic Remedial Measures to 
Address concerns regarding Construction of National Highways 
in Hilly Regions and Amendments to the Request For Proposal 

(RFP) for Detailed Project Report (DPR)/Engineering, Procurement 
and Construction (EPC) Document thereof” in order to: 
a. improve the quality of DPRs; 
b. ensure adequate provisions of hill slope protection 
measures; 
c. improvement in construction practice in hilly terrain;  
d. ensure implementat ion of slope cutting and stabilization 
works in the first instance to be followed up by road 
construction works for NHs in Hilly/Mountainous terrain; 
e. monitoring and early warning system for potential 
landslides. 
iv. Decision taken in July, 2026 through policy initiatives on 
“Specification including mandatory Certification and Quality 
Assurance for Rockfall Mitigation Measures for National 
Highways Projects” elaborating comprehensively on necessary 
checks and balances regarding ensuring adherence to quality 
standards and obligations of contractors and field offices. 
v. MoU signed with Defence Geo -informatics Research 
Establishment (DGRE) for Technological collaboration of Geo -
hazard mitigation measures on NHs. 
vi. MoU signed with Geological Survey of India (GSI) on Geol ogical 
investigation for tunnels and sharing of data for Geohazard 
Studies.  
vii. MoU signed by NHIDCL with National Institute of Rock 
Mechanics (NIRM) for broad area of collaboration in: 
a. geotechnical Investigation scrutiny for tunnel projects, road 
projects, 
b. review/ proof check of design and drawings of tunnel during 
DPR /construction stage, 
c. checking of adequacy of instrumentation and monitoring 
devices, tunnel safety audit, 
d. formulation of scientific investigation based on rock 
mechanics and rock engineering for work package, 
e. training to officials, etc. 
viii. MoU signed with NIRM for peer review of Detailed Project Report 
for Shillong – Silchar Greenfield high speed corridor. 

ix. Research scheme taken up through Indian Institute of 
Technology (IIT) Roorkee for Development  of Guidelines for the 
Assessment of Hillslope Instability using Instrumentation & Real 
Time Monitoring.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE & FARMERS WELFARE 
DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE & FARMERS WELFARE  
 
LOK SABHA 
 UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 250 
TO BE ANSWERED ON THE 21ST JULY, 2026 
 
PROMOTION OF CLIMATE-SMART AGRICULTURE 
  250. SHRI BALABHADRA MAJHI: 
         SHRI CHAVDA VINOD LAKHAMSHI: 
 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS’ WELFARE क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण मंũी 
be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the major initiatives taken by the Government during the financial year 2026–27 to 
promote climate-resilient and climate-smart agriculture, including the current status of their 
implementation in the Nabarangpur Lok Sabha Constituency; 
(b) whether any region-specific crop diversification strategies and climate-resilient seed 
varieties have been promoted, if so, the details thereof, including the benefits extended to 
farmers in the Nabarangpur Parliamentary Constituency; and 
(c) the details of the financial and technical assistance provided to farmers for adopting 
Climate-resilient agricultural practices, including the number of beneficiary farmers and the 
assistance provided in the Nabarangpur Parliamentary Constituency? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE  
क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण राǛ मंũी (SHRI  RAM NATH THAKUR) 
 
(a) to (c): The Government through, Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) is 
implementing a project- National Innovations in Climate Resilient Agriculture (NICRA) in the 
country including the State of Odisha. The programs include studies on the impact of climate 
change on agriculture, conducting district level risk and vulnerability assessment of 
agriculture to future climate change and integrated simulation modelling studies for 
estimating the future projections of climate change.  Further, ICAR has released 2900 
varieties during last 10 years (2014-2024). Out of these 2661 varieties are tolerant to one or 
more biotic and/or abiotic stresses. 
 
Government is implementing various programmes under the National Mission for 
Sustainable Agriculture (NMSA) to ensure long-term sustainability and food security. Per 
Drop More Crop scheme to increase water use efficiency at the farm level through Micro 
Irrigation technologies i.e. drip and sprinkler irrigation systems. Rainfed Area Development 
scheme is being implemented to promote Integrated Farming System for enhancing 
productivity and minimizing risks associated with climatic variability. The Soil Health and 
Fertility scheme is implemented to assist states in promoting Integrated Nutrient 
Management through judicious use of fertilizers. Organic farming promoting through 
Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana and natural farming through National Mission on Natural 
Farming scheme. “Mission for Aatmanirbharta in Pulses”, National Mission on Edible Oils – 
Oilseeds, and National Food Security & Nutrition Mission promotes crop diversification.  
Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture, Agroforestry & National Bamboo 
Mission also promote climate resilience in agriculture. Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana 
along with weather index based Restructured Weather Based Crop Insurance Scheme 
provides a comprehensive insurance cover against failure of the crops, thereby helping 
compensate farmers for losses caused by natural calamities and climate-related risks.  

 
As reported by the Government of Odisha, during 2026–27, in the Nabarangpur 
Parliamentary Constituency, an area of 1,300 ha has been covered under the Crop 
Diversification Programme–Mega Lift Irrigation Project (CDP-MLIP), under which crop 
diversification strategies are being promoted. Under the Per Drop More Crop (PDMC) 
scheme, an area of 791.36 ha has been covered, benefiting 556 farmers, with a financial 
achievement of ₹243.46 lakh. Under the Special Horticultural Crop-Specific Scheme, an 
area of 93 ha has been covered, with a financial achievement of ₹245.91 lakh. Further, 
under the Development of Potato, Vegetable and Spices scheme, a physical progress of 
272.58 ha has been achieved, covering 2,386 beneficiaries. 
 
Further, under the Odisha Integrated Irrigation Project for Climate Resilient 
Agriculture (OIIPCRA), climate-resilient horticultural interventions such as hybrid vegetable 
cultivation, strawberry cultivation, and Low-Cost/Small-Scale Mushroom Units are being 
implemented to strengthen farmers' livelihood resilience. Climate-resilient hybrid vegetable 
varieties are also being promoted under the project. In addition, training and capacity-
building programmes on climate-resilient agricultural practices are being conducted at the 
Block and Gram Panchayat levels under the technical guidance of departmental 
officials.These interventions are aimed at promoting crop diversification, improving water-
use efficiency, enhancing horticultural production, and strengthening the resilience of 
farmers' livelihoods through sustainable and climate-resilient agricultural practices.

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 251 
 
TO BE ANSWERED ON THE 21ST JULY, 2026/ ASHADHA 30, 1948 (SAKA) 
 
NATIONAL CYBER CRIME DATA 
 
251.      SHRI ANURAG SHARMA: 
    SHRI ESWARASAMY K: 
 
Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the number of cyber -crime cases registered during the last five years, 
State-wise and year-wise along with the online scams and cyber exploitation 
during the said period; 
 
(b) the estimated financial losses suffered by citizens due to cyber fraud, the 
amount recovered or frozen, and the number of complaints resolved during 
the said period, State-wise and year-wise; 
 
(c) the measures taken by the Government to strengthen cyber -crime 
investigation through capacity building, specialised cyber police stations, 
forensic laboratories, training of investigating  agencies and coordination 
among Central and State Governments; 
 
(d) whether the Government has reviewed the timeliness and availability of 
national cyber-crime data for effective policymaking and law enforcement; 
and 
 
(e) if so, the details thereof, including the steps taken to improve real -time 
reporting and monitoring? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
(SHRI BANDI SANJAY KUMAR) 
 
 
 

 
-2- 
L.S.US.Q.NO. 251 FOR 21.07.2026  
(a) to (e) :  The National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) compiles and 
publishes the statistical data on crimes in its publication “Crime in India”. 
The latest published report is for the year 20 24.  As per the data published 
by the NCRB, State/UT wise & Crime Head-wise cases registered under cyber 
crimes (involving communication devices as medium/target) during the 
period from 2020 to 2024 is at Annexure-I & Annexure-II.  
The Ministry of Home Affairs has set up the ‘Indian Cyber Crime 
Coordination Centre’ (I4C)  as an attached office to deal with all types of 
cyber crimes in the country, in a coordinated and comprehensive manner. 
The ‘National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal’ (NCRP) 
(https://cybercrime.gov.in) has been launched, as a part of the I4C, to enable 
public to report incidents pertaining to all types of cyber crimes, with special 
focus on cyber crimes against women and children.  
The ‘Citizen Financial Cyber Fraud Reporting and Management System’ 
(CFCFRMS), under I4C, has been launched in year 2021 for immediate 
reporting of financial frauds and to stop siphoning off funds by the fraudsters. 
As per CFCFRMS operated by I4C, till 30.06.2026, financial amount of more 
than Rs. 11,158 Crore has been saved in more than 32.80 lakh complaints.  A 
toll-free Helpline number ‘1930’ has been operationalized to get assistance 
in lodging online cyber complaints. As per NCRP & CFCFRMS operated by I4C, 
from the year 2021 to 2025, the total number of financial frauds complaints  

-3- 
L.S.US.Q.NO. 251 FOR 21.07.2026  
on NCRP are more than 6589201, the total amount reported is more than ₹ 
55050 Crores, the total amount marked as Lien is more than ₹ 8189 Crores 
and the number of FIRs registered is more than 195760. 
Cyber crime incidents reported on National Cyber Crime Reporting 
Portal, their conversion into FIRs and subsequent action i.e. filing  of 
chargesheets, arrest and resolution of complaints, thereon are handled by 
the State/UT Law Enforcement Agencies concerned as per the provisions of 
the law. 
 
‘Police’ and ‘Public Order’ are State subjects under the Seventh 
Schedule to the Constitution of India. Accordingly, the States and Union 
Territories (UTs) are primarily responsible for the prevention, detection, 
investigation, and prosecution of cybercrime. The Central Government, 
through the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA), supplements the efforts  of 
States and UTs by providing policy guidance, technological support, 
capacity-building assistance, and financial resources to strengthen 
cybercrime management and enforcement capabilities. 
 
The Central Government has taken the following steps to strengthen the 
cyber crime investigation  and coordination among Central and State 
Governments : 
 

-4- 
L.S.US.Q.NO. 251 FOR 21.07.2026  
i. Samanvaya Platform has been made operational to serve as an  
Management Information System (MIS) platform, data repository and a 
coordination platform for LEAs for cybercrime data sharing and analytics. 
It provides analytics based interstate linkages of crimes and criminals, 
involved in cybercrime complaints in var ious States/UTs. The module 
‘Pratibimb’ maps locations of criminals and crime infrastructure on a map 
to give visibility to jurisdictional officers. The module also facilitates 
seeking and receiving of techno -legal assistance by Law Enforcement 
Agencies fr om I4C and other SMEs. It has lead to arrest of more than 
29,837 accused and more than 2,33,593 Cyber Investigation assistance 
request. 
ii. ‘Sahyog’ Portal has been launched to expedite the process of sending 
notices to IT intermediaries by the Appropriate Government or its agency 
under clause (b) of sub -section (3) of section 79 of the IT Act, 2000 to 
facilitate the removal or disabling of access to any information, data or 
communication link being used to commit an unlawful act. 
iii. Seven Joint Cyber Coordination Teams (JCCTs) have been constituted for 
Mewat, Jamtara, Ahmedabad, Hyderabad, Chandigarh, Vishakhapatnam, 
and Guwahati under I4C covering the whole country based upon cyber 
crime hotspots/ areas having multi jurisdictional issues by onboarding 
States/UTs to enhance the coordination framework among the Law 
Enforcement Agencies of the States/UTs. 

-5- 
L.S.US.Q.NO. 251 FOR 21.07.2026  
iv. The Massive Open Online Courses (MOOC) platform, namely ‘CyTrain’ 
portal has been developed  under I4C, for capacity building of police 
officers/judicial officers through online course on critical aspects of cyber 
crime investigation, forensics, prosecution etc. Till 30.06.2026, more than 
1,63,344 police officers/judicial officers  from States/UTs are registered 
and more than 1,61,957 Certificates issued through the portal. 
v. Cyber Commando programme was launched by the Hon'ble Home Minister 
on 10.09.2024 to establish a Special Wing of Cyber Commandos equipped 
with specialized training to counter cybersecurity threats in the country. 
The programme envisions the creation of a dedicated, skilled workforce 
capable of securing critical information infrastructure and supporting 
national cybersecurity efforts. So far, 281 cyber commandos successfully 
completed their training at premier institutions including IITs, IIITs, 
Rashtriya Raksha University (RRU), National Forensic Sciences 
University (NFSU) Gandhinagar & New Delhi, etc. 
vi. I4C, MHA is regularly organising ‘State Connect’, ‘Thana Connect’ and 
Peer learning session to share best practices, enhance capacity building, 
etc. 
vii. The state of the art  National-Digital Investigation Support Centre 
(previously known as National Cyber Forensic Laboratory (Investigation)  
{NCFL(I)}) has been established, as a part of t he I4C, at New Delhi  (on 
18.02.2019) and  at Assam (on 29.08.2025)  to provide  early stage  cyber  

-6- 
L.S.US.Q.NO. 251 FOR 21.07.2026  
forensic assistance to Investigating Officers (IOs) of State/UT Police. Till 
30.06.2026, National-Digital Investigation Support Centre, New Delhi has 
provided its services to State/UT LEAs in  more than  14,064 cases 
pertaining to cyber crimes. 
viii. The Ministry of Home Affairs has released financial assistance  to the 
tune of Rs. 132.93 crores under the ‘Cyber Crime Prevention a gainst 
Women and Children (CCPWC)’ Scheme , to the States/UTs for their 
capacity building such as setting up of cyber forensic -cum-training 
laboratories, hiring of junior cyber consultants and training of LEAs’ 
personnel, public prosecutors and judicial off icers. Cyber forensic -cum-
training laboratories have been commissioned in 33 States/UTs and more 
than 24,600 LEA personnel, judicial officers and prosecutors have been 
provided training on cyber crime awareness, investigation, forensics etc. 
ix. At present, 07  Central Forensic Science Laboratories and 2 8 State 
Forensic Science Laboratories are operational across the country' to 
assist in investigation of cybercrime cases. Assistance has been provided 
to 20 States / UTs for Strengthening of Cyber Forensic Capacities in State 
FSLs under the Nirbhaya funded scheme for Strengthening of DNA 
Analysis and Cyber Forensic Capacities in State FSLs. 
x. To further strengthen operational efficiency and ensure uniform ity in 
handling cybercrime complaints, the Ministry has issued a 
comprehensive Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) for NCRP-CFCFRMS.  

-7- 
L.S.US.Q.NO. 251 FOR 21.07.2026  
The SOP lays down a standardized framework for complaint processing, 
bank coordination, grievance redressal, removal of lien markings, and 
restoration of defrauded funds to rightful claimants based on complaints 
received through the NCRP. Money Restoration  Module for expeditious 
restoration of defrauded money to the victims and Grievance Redressal 
Module for timely attending to the grievances relating to freezing of the 
bank accounts and lien marking of the amount, have been made 
functional from April, 2026.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 253 
TO BE ANSWERED ON THE 21ST JULY, 2026 
 
FINANCIAL ASSISTANCE TO FARMER PRODUCER ORGNIZATIONS IN PUNJAB 
 
253. DR. AMAR SINGH: 
 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण मंũी 
be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the number of Farmer Producer Organisations (FPOs) formed and supported in Punjab 
under the Central Sector Scheme for Formation and Promotion of 10,000 FPOs, district-
wise; 
 
(b) the financial assistance, equity grants, credit guarantees and other support provided to 
FPOs in Punjab during the last three years, year-wise; 
 
(c) whether the Government has assessed the functioning and financial viability of FPOs in 
Punjab and, if so, the details and outcome thereof; 
 
(d) the challenges reported by FPOs in accessing institutional credit, markets and value 
addition infrastructure, and the action taken thereon; and 
 
(e) the steps taken to strengthen FPOs in Punjab to improve farmers' income, market access 
and participation of small and marginal farmers? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
 
क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण राǛ मंũी (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
 
(a):  As on date, 151 Farmer Producer Organisations (FPOs) have been formed in State 
of Punjab under the Central Sector Scheme for Formation and Promotion of 10,000 Farmer 
Producer Organisations (FPOs).  District-wise details of FPOs formed under the Scheme 
are at Annexure. 
 
(b): Year-wise details of financial assistance released to FPOs in Punjab during the last 
three years, including Equity Grant and Credit Guarantee are at Annexure. 
 
In addition, FPOs are provided continuous handholding support through Cluster 
Based Business Organizations (CBBOs) and Implementing Agencies (IAs) for business 
planning, market linkages, capacity building and facilitation in availing benefits under 
various Government schemes. 
 
  

(c):   An evaluation of the Scheme has been carried out by the Department in 2025-26 
for all States including Punjab.  The mid-term evaluation indicates that the Central Sector 
Scheme for Formation and Promotion of 10,000 Farmer Producer Organizations has 
created a substantial institutional base for farmer collectivisation. The assessment of 400 
FPOs shows strong progress on formal institutional and compliance-related indicators. 
Around 93.5% of assessed FPOs covered four or more Gram Panchayats; 92% achieved 
full license /registration compliance; 89% completed LMS modules with the CEO and 
accountant trained; and a large majority submitted audited financial statements. These 
findings indicate that the scheme has made visible progress in creating formal FPO 
structures, expanding member outreach and strengthening basic institutional readiness. 
 
(d) & (e):  FPOs formed under the Scheme including the FPOs in State of Punjab, are 
provided both financial and other support through various interventions by the Government, 
to strengthen them, improve farmers' income, enhance market access, facilitate access to 
institutional credit and promote value addition. These include: 
i. Management Cost up to ₹18 lakh per FPO over a period of three years to meet 
managerial and operational expenses. 
ii. Matching Equity Grant of up to ₹15 lakh per FPO, to strengthen the equity base 
of FPOs.  
iii. Credit Guarantee Facility for project loans of up to ₹2 crore per FPO to improve 
access to institutional credit.  
iv. Continuous handholding support for five years through Cluster Based Business 
Organizations (CBBOs) for business planning, governance, market linkages and 
capacity building.  
v. Capacity-building, training and skill development programmes for Chief Executive 
Officers (CEOs), Board of Directors (BoDs) and members of FPOs.  
vi. Facilitation in obtaining input licences and dealerships.  In Punjab, 86 FPOs have 
seed licences, 80 FPOs fertilizer licences and 69 FPOs having pesticide licenses, 
enabling them to supply agricultural inputs to their member farmers and augment 
their revenue.

CONVERSION TO VB-GRAM-G SCHEME 
 
254. Shri Rajkumar Roat: 
 
Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  the details of the works approved for conversion from Members 
of Parliament Local Area Development Scheme (MPLADS) funds 
to Viksit Bharat-Guarantee for Rojgar and Aajeevikaa Mission-
Gramin (VB-GRAM-G)  along with the rules/guidelines governing 
such conversion and the list of permissible works; 
(b)  the details of the budget sanctioned under MGNREGS/VB-G RAM-
G during the last five years; 
(c)  the details of the budget allocated and utilized, State and 
district-wise including Rajasthan; 
(d)  whether the Government proposes to make payment to 
contractors and labourers engaged under the VB-GRAM-G 
Scheme from the labour component instead of the material 
component; 
(e)  if so, the time by which it is likely to be implemented; and 
(f)  the details of the pending payments under the material 
component and the labour component in the Banswara Lok 
Sabha Constituency and the time by which such pending 
payments are likely to be cleared? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
(SHRI KAMLESH PASWAN)  
(a):     The Viksit Bharat – Guarantee for Rozgar and Aajeevika Mission 
(Gramin) (VB–G RAM G) Act, 2025 has come into force with effect 
from 1st July, 2026, and all States/UTs have commenced 
implementation of the Scheme in compliance with the provisions of 
the Act. 
  As per Paragraph 5 of Schedule I of the Act, all Central, State and 
local schemes, as may be notified by the Central Government for the 

Page 2 of 5 
 
purpose of convergence and saturation-based planning, are to be 
brought under a unified planning process anchored in the Viksit Gram 
Panchayat Plans (VGPPs). The Act further envisages that the works 
identified in the VGPPs may be implemented through convergence 
with such notified schemes.  
  In pursuance of these provisions, the Ministry of Rural 
Development has initiated consultations with the concerned 
Ministries and Departments of the Government of India, including the 
Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI), for 
operationalising the convergence framework. The framework, 
including identification of schemes eligible for convergence, 
operational modalities, and implementation guidelines, is presently 
under finalisation. 
(b):    The details of funds allocation at Budget Estimate stage, 
Revised Estimate stage, final allocation under Mahatma Gandhi 
National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme (Mahatma Gandhi 
NREGS) in the last five financial years are given below: 
   (Rs. in crore)

2023-24 60000.00 86000.00 89363.00 
2024-25 86000.00 86000.00 86000.00 
2025-26 86000.00 88000.00 88000.00 
  
(c):     Mahatma Gandhi NREGS is a demand-driven wage employment 
programme, under which funds is released by the Ministry of Rural 
Development to the States/Union Territories based on the demand for 
employment, pace of implementation and availability of funds. No 
State-wise or district-wise budget allocation was made under the 
Scheme. 
Accordingly, funds are released by the Ministry to the 
States/UTs, and no funds were directly released to the districts. 
Details of the funds released to the States/ UTs (including Rajasthan) 
during the last five financial years are given at Annexure. 
(d) & (e): Under the Viksit Bharat – Guarantee for Rozgar and 
Aajeevika Mission (Gramin) (VB–G RAM G) Act, 2025, payment of 
wages to workers engaged under the Scheme is governed by the 
provisions of the Act. 
  As per Section 22 of the Act, wages payable to unskilled, semi-
skilled and skilled workers employed under the Scheme are paid 
directly into the bank accounts of the workers through the Direct 

Page 3 of 5 
 
Benefit Transfer (DBT) mode from the wage component, in 
accordance with the provisions of the Act. 
  Further, Paragraph 21 of Schedule I of the Act expressly provides 
that no contractor shall be engaged for the execution of any work or 
component financed under the Act. All such works are required to be 
executed directly by the designated implementing agencies in 
accordance with the procedures prescribed under the Act.  
(f):    At the beginning of each financial year, admissible pending wage 
liabilities of the previous financial year, if any, are duly cleared by the 
Government of India. Accordingly, all due and admissible pending 
wage liabilities up to FY 2025–26 have been cleared for the State of 
Rajasthan, including Banswara Lok Sabha Constituency. 
  
With regard to the material component, the States/UTs are 
required to submit fund release proposals along with the prescribed 
documents to the Government of India. Funds are released to the 
States/UTs periodically, keeping in view the demand for works, 
opening balance, pace of utilization of funds, pending liabilities, 
overall performance and fulfilment of the prescribed conditions. 
Material payments are made by the respective States/UTs to the 
implementing agencies and vendors from the funds released by the 
Government of India.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF HEAVY INDUSTRIES  
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 256 
ANSWERED ON 21.07.2026 
 
DELAYED IMPLEMENTATION AND UTILISATION GAPS UNDER THE FAME-II 
ELECTRIC MOBILITY SCHEME 
 
†256. SHRI ARUN KUMAR SAGAR:  
 
Will the Minister of HEAVY INDUSTRIES be pleased to state:  
 
(a) the details of the central schemes for the development of electric vehicles in the country;  
 
(b) the details of specific provisions made under these schemes with respect to the Faster Adopti on 
and Manufacturing of (Hybrid &) Electric Vehicles (FAME -II) scheme and the establishment of 
charging stations;  
 
(c) the total number of electric vehicles sold under the aegis of these schemes so far;  
 
(d) the major challenges regarding the reach of these electric vehicle schemes; and  
 
(e) the overall impact of these schemes on enhancing electric mobility across the country? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR HEAVY INDUSTRIES 
(SHRI BHUPATHIRAJU SRINIVASA VARMA) 
 
(a) & (b):  The details of the schemes implemented by the Ministry of Heavy Industries (MHI) 
for the development of electric vehicles in the country along with provisions for charging stations 
are as under: 
 
(i) Faster Adoption and Manufacturing of (Hybrid &) Electric Vehicles in India (FAME 
India) Scheme Phase-II: The Government implemented this scheme for a period of five years 
from 01.04.2019 to 31.03.2024 with a total budgetary support of ₹11,500 crore. The scheme 
provided demand incentive for e-2Ws, e-3Ws, e-4Ws and grant for e-buses and setting up of EV 
public charging stations (EV PCS). FAME-II has supported the sale of approximately 16.72 lakh 
electric vehicles, including e-2Ws, e-3Ws, and e-4Ws. In addition, 5,197 electric buses (e -buses) 
have been deployed under the Scheme as on 30.06.2026. Further, an amount of ₹912.50 crore was 
allocated under the Scheme for the establishment of EVPCS across the country. 
 
(ii) Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme for Automobile and Auto Component 
Industry in India (PLI -Auto): The Government notified this sc heme for Automobile and Auto 
Component Industry in India, on 23.09.2021, for enhancing India's manufacturing capabilities for 
Advanced Automotive Technology (AAT) products, including EVs, with a budgetary outlay of 
₹25,938 crore.  
 
(iii) Production Linked Incent ive (PLI) Scheme for National Programme on Advanced  
Chemistry Cell (ACC) Battery Storage :  The Government on 09.06.2021 notified the PLI  
Scheme for manufacturing of ACC in the country with a budgetary outlay of ₹18,100 crore. The 
scheme aims to establis h a competitive domestic manufacturing ecosystem for 50 GWh of ACC 
batteries. 
 

 
-2- 
 
(iv) PM Electric Drive Revolution in Innovative Vehicle Enhancement (PM EDRIVE) 
Scheme: This scheme with an outlay of ₹10,900 crore has been notified on 29.09.2024. This 
scheme supports incentivization of approximately 28.30 lakh electric vehicles (EVs) including e -
2W, e-3W, e-Trucks, e-buses and e -Ambulances. Further, grant for EV public cha rging stations 
(EV PCS) and upgradation of testing agencies is also available under this scheme. An allocation 
of ₹4,391 crore has been made under the scheme for deployment of 14,028 e -buses out of which 
13,800 e-buses have been allocated in seven cities having four million plus population viz. Delhi, 
Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Mumbai, Ahmedabad, Pune and Surat. Further, 200 e -buses have been 
approved for Union Territory of Jammu & Kashmir. ₹2,000 crore has been allocated for 
deployment of EV Public Charging Station on pan India basis.   
 
(v) PM e-Bus Sewa-Payment Security Mechanism (PSM) Scheme: This Scheme notified on 
28.10.2024, has an outlay of ₹3,435.33 crore and aims to support deployment of more than 38,000 
electric buses. The objective of this scheme is to pr ovide payment security to e -bus operators in 
case of default by Public Transport Authorities (PTAs). 
 
(vi) Scheme for Promotion of Manufacturing of Electric Passenger Cars in India 
(SPMEPCI) was notified on 15 th March, 2024 to promote the manufacturing of elect ric cars in 
India. This scheme requires applicants to invest a minimum of ₹4,150 crore and to achieve a 
minimum DVA of 25% at the end of the third year and DVA of 50% at the end of the fifth year. 
 
 Further, following initiatives have also been taken up by the Government of India to 
increase the use of electric vehicles in the country:– 
i. GST on electric vehicles and chargers/ charging stations for electric vehicles has been 
reduced to 5%. 
ii. Ministry of Road Transport & Highways (MoRTH) announced that battery-operated vehicles 
will be given green license plates and be exempted from permit requirements. 
iii. MoRTH issued advisory to states to waive road tax on EVs, which in turn will help reduce

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA

DEPARTMENT OF ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
LOK SABHA 
 UNSTARRED  QUESTION No. 257 
ANSWERED ON 21st JULY , 2026 
 
ANIMAL HUSBANDRY INFRASTRUCTURE DEVELOPMENT FUND 
 
257. SHRI DUSHYANT SINGH: 
Will the Minister of FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
मत्स्यपालन, पशुपालन और डेयरी मंत्री 
 be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the steps taken by the Government under the Animal Husbandry Infrastructure 
Development Fund (AHIDF) to promote investment in modern dairy processing, cold chain, 
storage and value addition infrastructure in the country;   
 
(b) whether any specific projects or initiatives have been sanctioned under AHIDF in 
Rajasthan and if so, the details thereof, including measures taken by the Government to 
encourage participation of the private sector and dairy cooperatives;   
 
(c) the steps being taken by the Government to enhance milk processing capacity and 
farmer’s remuneration, particularly for small and marginal dairy producers; and   
 
(d) the measures taken by the Government to strengthen extension services, capacity 
building, awareness programmes and last -mile delivery mechanisms so as to ensure wider 
adoption of improved technologies and best practices in the livestock sector?  
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
(SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH ALIAS LALAN SINGH) 
 
(a) The Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying  (DAHD), GoI is implementing the 
Animal Husbandry Infrastructure Development Fund (AHIDF) to incentivize establishment of 
modern dairy processing and infrastructure for establishment of new units and strengthening 
of existing dairy processing units with quality and hygienic milk processing facilities, 

packaging facilities  and value-added dairy product manufacturing units, cold storage , 
refrigerated vans.   The Eligible Entities are Individuals, MSME, Private Companies, FPO, 
Dairy Cooperatives and Section 8 companies. 
The scheme envisages 3% interest subvention for eight years with a two-year moratorium on 
term loan up to 90% of the project cost borrowed from scheduled banks and institutions such 
as NABARD, NCDC, NDDB, and SIDBI. In addition, the Central Government has established 
a Credit Guarantee Trust to provide Credit Guarantee up to 25% of term loan to MSME and 
Dairy Cooperatives. The Trust is maintained by NABARD through its subsidiary NAB 
Sanrakshan Trustee Pvt. Ltd.  Eligible Entities can also take benefit of dovetailing with various 
Central and State Government initiatives to ensure holistic growth of the dairy ecosystem.  
(b)  A total of 13 dairy projects  have been approved with the project cost of Rs 213.07 crore 
for the State of Rajasthan with the processing capacity of 15.95 Lakh Litre Per Day (LLPD) .

(c) The DAHD, GoI is implementing National Programme for Dairy Development (NPDD) .  
Component A of NPDD focuses on creating/strengthening of infrastructure for quality milk 
testing equipment as well as primary milk chilling facilities. The Component ‘B’ of the NPDD 
scheme "Dairying through Cooperatives” aims to increase sale of milk and dairy products by 

increasing farmer’s access to organized market, upgrading dairy processing facilities and 
marketing infrastructure.  In addition, under Supporting Dairy Cooperatives and Farmer 
Producer Organizations engaged in dairy activities (SDCFPO) interest subvention on Working 
capital loans is provided to assist the Cooperative Milk Unions and Farmer Producer 
organizations engaged in dairy activities to tide over the crisis on account of severely adverse 
market conditions or natural calamities. An interest subvention of 2% per annum on the 
working capital loan is provided to the Producer Owned Institutes (POIs.). Further, for prompt 
and timely repayment of loan, an additional 2% per annum interest subvention is also payable 
at the end of the loan repayment/interest servicing period 
 The infrastructure created under the AHIDF, help in creating increased Milk processing 
capacity, market linkages for livestock farmers and thus enable livestock producers to get 
remunerative prices for their produce.  
 
(d)  The DAHD, GoI  undertakes awareness programmes, webinars, stakeholder meetings, 
training programmes and outreach activities through State Governments, implementing 
agencies and industry associations. Regular review meetings with lending institutions, State 
Nodal Agencies and other stakeholders are conducted to facilitate implementation and improve 
outreach. The DAHD, GoI t also organizes virtual awareness camps through Common Service 
Centers (CSCs) on departmental schemes, fodder development, Cattle and Dairy farming, and 
the prevention and control of livestock diseases.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA

STATUS OF MSP IMPLEMENTATION 
258. SHRI KARTI P CHIDAMBARAM 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE क ृ िष और िकसान 
कʞाण मंũी be pleased to state: 
(a) the current status of MSP implementation and procurement for the year 2026-27 
Kharif season, including the estimated payout of Rs. 2.6 lakh crore across 14 crops; 
(b) whether any disparity exists in procurement infrastructure, Mandi access and 
farmer participation, as compared among the States, if so, the details thereof, State-
wise; 
(c) the steps taken to ensure timely payment to farmers, especially in Tamil Nadu and 
other southern States; 
(d) the details of the status of pulses and oilseeds procurement under the Price 
Support Scheme (PSS) in States of Uttar Pradesh, Gujarat, Tamil Nadu and Haryana;  
(e) whether any State has reported delayed Central reimbursement affecting 
procurement operations, if so, the details thereof; 
(f) the extent of PM-AASHA scheme utilisation in this season, according to the data 
collected; and 
(g) whether any contingency measures have been prepared in view of monsoon 
variability affecting kharif sowing and procurement targets, if so, the details thereof ? 
 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE  
क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण राǛ मंũी  (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
 
(a) to (c): The Department of Food and Public Distribution (DFPD) undertakes 
Minimum Support Price (MSP) procurement of Paddy, Wheat and coarse grains, 
namely Jowar, Bajra, Maize and Ragi. MSP procurement of notified pulses - Arhar, 
Moong, Urad, Gram and Masur, oilseeds - Groundnut, Soybean, Sunflower, 
Sesamum, Nigerseed, Rapeseed/Mustard Seed and Safflower and copra is 
undertaken in Price Support Scheme (PSS) of PM-AASHA. The procurement is 
undertaken during 3 seasons in a crop year namely Kharif, Rabi and Summer, on the 
request of the respective State/UT Governments. As on date, no proposal has been 

received from any State/UT Government for procurement under PSS for the Kharif 
2026-27 season. The procurement infrastructure and mandi access varies across 
States depending on the production pattern of notified crops and the procurement 
requirements. Farmer participation under the scheme largely depends on the 
prevailing market prices. To facilitate timely payment to farmers across the country, 
including Tamil Nadu under PSS, the MSP is paid directly into the bank accounts of 
the farmers, through the Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) mechanism, thereby eliminating 
intermediaries and ensuring transparency. Government of Tamil Nadu has informed 
that to strengthen procurement operations, procurement centres under regulated 
markets are established. Warehousing Development and Regulatory Authority 
(WDRA)-accredited warehouses, Central Warehousing Corporation (CWC) 
warehouses and State Warehousing Corporation warehouses are utilised to facilitate 
procurement operations, ensure timely handling of stocks. 
 
(d): The detail of procurement of pulses and oilseeds under PSS in the States of Uttar 
Pradesh, Gujarat, Tamil Nadu and Haryana during the year 2025-26 for Kharif, Rabi 
& Summer seasons is placed at Annexure. 
 
(e) to (g): Under the PM AASHA Scheme, no instance of delayed central 
reimbursement affecting procurement operations has been reported by any State. 
Procurement under PM-AASHA is undertaken on the request of the respective 
State/UT Governments. No procurement proposal has been received under the 
scheme for Kharif 2026-27. 
 
In view of the Monsoon variability, the State Governments have been advised 
to take necessary measures including updation of District Agricultural Contingency 
Plans in consultation with the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR), the 
Central Research Institute for Dryland Agriculture (CRIDA) and State Agricultural 
Universities to ensure availability of suitable seeds, promote agronomic practises for 
moisture conservation and crop diversification, strengthen irrigation and water 
harvesting infrastructure, review water storage, and establish and activate Drought 
Monitoring Centres at the State level. The Crisis Management Plan (CMP) for 2026 
has been updated and circulated to all States and Stakeholders.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
 
LOK SABHA

TO BE ANSWERED ON 21st July, 2026 
 
 PRODUCTION AND PRODUCTIVITY OF TURMERIC 
 
 
260.  SHRI ARVIND DHARMAPURI: 
 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE   
कृ ͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण मंğी be pleased to state:  
 
(a) the details of area, production and productivity of turmeric during the last five years, 
State-wise particularly, district-wise details for Telangana including Nizamabad, 
Jagtial and Nirmal districts; 
(b) whether the Government has analysed the reasons for increase or decline in 
turmeric production in each State during the said period and if so, the details thereof, 
including factors such as rainfall, acreage shift, input cost, pest/disease incidence, 
market prices and post-harvest infrastructure; 
(c) the number of turmeric Farmer Producer Organisations, clusters, processing units, 
drying yards, storage facilities and primary processing centres, supported under 
Central schemes in Telangana; 
(d) whether the Government has assessed gaps in price realization, grading, 
processing, export quality and market linkage for turmeric farmers; and 
(e) the steps taken to enhance farmer income through value addition, scientific 
cultivation, post-harvest support and market access for turmeric growers, particularly 
in Telangana? 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
 
कृ ͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण राÏय मंğी  (SHRI RAM NATH THAKUR) 
 
(a):  The State-wise details of area, production and productivity/yield of turmeric during 
the last five years are given at Annexure-I and the district-wise details for Telangana 
State, including Nizamabad, Jagtial and Nirmal districts, are given at Annexure-II. 

(b): The area and production of turmeric in the country has shown an increasing trend 
during the recent years. Overall, favourable climatic conditions, coupled with lower 
incidence of pests and diseases, supported increase in production. In addition, the 
prevailing high market prices of turmeric encouraged farmers to bring more area under 
cultivation, leading to a corresponding increase in turmeric production. The annual 
average price of Turmeric for the last five years in major turmeric producing States is 
given below:

(c): Through the Initiatives of the Spices Board and National Turmeric Board, specific 
focus is placed on establishing infrastructure through Farmer Producer Organizations 
(FPOs). Financial assistance is extended for setting up Primary processing units, 
turmeric boilers, spices polishers, etc. through the Sustainability in Spice Sector 
through Progressive Innovative and Collaborative Interventions for Export 
Development (SPICED) Scheme. As per the information provided by the Horticulture

(d): As per the information provided by the Indian Council of Agricultural Research 
(ICAR)- Indian Institute of Spices Research (IISR), the major technology/infrastructure 
gaps identified in turmeric sector include lack of high-end value addition opportunities, 
lack of traceability systems and limited use of good manufacturing practices in 
processing, lack of cold storage facilities for long term storing of processed produce, 
absence of quality-based pricing systems for turmeric, challenges in aggregation and 
efficient functioning of cluster-based interventions, and limitations in availability and 
timeliness of export market intelligence.    
 
(e): The development of turmeric is supported by the Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers 
Welfare, Government of India through their flagship programmes like the Mission for 
Integrated Development of Horticulture (MIDH), Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana 
(RKVY), Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana (PKVY), Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchai 
Yojana (PMKSY), Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY), Natural Resource 
Management (NRM), Soil Health Card, e-National Agriculture Market (e-NAM) etc. 
Under MIDH, several production-oriented programmes are being implemented by the 
Government of India through State Horticulture Missions including Telangana, set up 
under the State Governments. MIDH has special components for creation of Marketing 
Infrastructure and Mechanization, which also extends for turmeric. 
  

 
       The Government of India established the National Turmeric Board in 2023 to 
promote turmeric production, development and value addition; enhance domestic and 
international consumption; facilitate the creation and improvement of infrastructure 
and logistics for turmeric exports; and support the overall growth of the turmeric sector. 
 
        ICAR-IISR and ICAR-All India Coordinated Research Project on Spices 
(AICRPS), based on the Central Variety Release Committee (CVRC) notifications, 
have developed the following turmeric varieties suitable for Telangana- IISR Pragati, 
Lam Swarna (LTS-2), IISR Surya, Roma, Suroma, Suguna, Sudarshana, Suvarna, 
Rashmi, Duggirala Red. These varieties have higher yield potential than the traditional 
varieties and can enhance the productivity of turmeric in Telangana. Apart from this, 
both these institutions have developed and recommended several technologies and 
varieties suitable for the state like Plant Spacing recommendation, Fertilizer 
Recommendation, adopting Drip irrigation, Nutrient Management under organic 
cultivation, Single Bud Pro-tray Propagation technology, Seed Rhizome Priming with 
Trichoprime, Good Agricultural Practices (GAP) for turmeric, Clean post-harvest 
processing and packages for biotic and abiotic stress.

functioning as Common Service Centres in Andhra Pradesh;

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
DEPARTMENT OF ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 262 
ANSWERED ON 21st JULY, 2026 
 
PROGRAMME FOR STRENGTHENING VETERINARY SERVICES 
 
262.  SHRI RADHESHYAM RATHIYA:  
SHRI NALIN SOREN:  
SHRI NABA CHARAN MAJHI:  
SHRI CHANDRA PRAKASH JOSHI:  
SHRI VIJAY KUMAR DUBEY:  
SHRI GODAM NAGESH: 
 
Will the Minister of FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
 मत्स्यपालन, पशुपालन और डेयरी मंत्री 
be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the major initiatives undertaken by the Ministry to strengthen veterinary and animal health 
services up to May 2026 in the country, including Chhattisgarh;  
(b)  the details of capacity -building programmes conducted for veterinarians and para - 
veterinary professionals in the country, including Chhattisgarh;  
(c)  the details of the proposed coverage of veterinary institutions and personnel under these 
initiatives along with the planned financial outlay for strengthening veterinary 
infrastructure and services in the country, including Chhattisgarh; and 
(d)  whether any State -specific projects, financial allocations, or action plans have been 
approved for Chhattisgarh under these initiatives and if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
(SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH ALIAS LALAN SINGH) 
 
(a) Animal Husbandry is State subject. However, the Department of Animal Husbandry & 
Dairying (DAHD), GOI provides following support to the States/ UTs including Chhattisgarh 
for strengthening veterinary and animal health services: 
i. Under Livestock Health and Disease Control Program (LHDCP) scheme, 100% central 
assistance is provided for vaccination of animals against four major diseases, namely FMD, 
Brucellosis, Peste des Petits Ruminants (PPR) and Classical Swine Fever (CSF). 
ii. Under Establishment and Strengthening of Veterinary Hospital & Dispensary (ESVHD -
MVU) of LHDCP, assistance is provided to States/UTs for operation of MVUs on sharing 

basis. Total 4019 Mobile Veterinary Units (MVUs) have been made operational in the 
Country in 29 States/UTs under the scheme. 
iii. Under Assistance to States for Control of Animal Diseases (ASCAD) support is provided 
on sharing basis for prevention and control of state prioritized livestock diseases, 
strengthening of Disease Diagnostic Laboratories etc. 
iv. ICAR-NIVEDI has developed  National Animal Disease Referral Expert System 
(NADRES_v2) which can predict the possibility of disease outbreaks at district level 2-3 
months in advance supporting better preparedness and response. 
(b) Under the ASCAD component of LHDCP, there is a provision for financial assistance on 
sharing basis for training of Veterinarians and Para -veterinarians. During 2025 -26 Rs 
971.65 lakh  has been released for all the States including Rs 7.5 lakh for the state of 
Chhattisgarh for capacity building program . Under Assistance to States for Control of 
Animal Diseases (ASCAD) support is provided on sharing basis for prevention and control 
of state prioritized livestock diseases, strengthening of Disease Diagnostic Laboratories 
etc. 
(c) The strengthening veterinary infrastructure and services is under the domain of the State 
Government. However, DAHD, GoI has formulated Guidelines for minimum Standards of 
Veterinary Infrastructure in India and communicated to States/UT for adoption and 
necessary action. 
(d) Under LHDCP scheme, total budget allocated for the state of Chhattisgarh for FY 2026-27 is 
Rs 3162 lakh.
