REVERSE MIGRATION TO AGRICULTURE 
 
†264. SHRI NEERAJ MAURYA: 
          SHRI BABU SINGH KUSHWAHA: 
          SHRI LALJI VERMA: 
           
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE be pleased to state: 
(a)  whether the data from the recently released Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) 
indicates that a large number of individuals who had migrated from rural India in search of 
employment are returning to agricultural work due to limited employment opportunities 
outside, if so, the details thereof; 
(b)  the planned steps being taken by the Government to promote sustainable and 
remunerative agricultural practices, natural farming, micro-irrigation, organic farming and 
crop diversification, in view of the increasing agricultural workforce; 
(c)  the details of the measures being taken by the Government to support individuals 
returning to agriculture, especially landless, marginal and small farmers, in terms of 
providing credit, training, modern agricultural technology and access to basic infrastructure; 
(d)  the strategy of the Government to reduce the growing pressure on the agricultural 
sector and to create alternative employment opportunities in rural areas to prevent 
overcrowding; and 
(e)  whether the Government has any data in this regard related to Uttar Pradesh, 
particularly for the Aonla-Jaunpur and Ambedkar Nagar Lok Sabha Constituencies as well 
as the Bareilly, Budaun, and Shahjahanpur districts and if so, the details thereof ? 
 
ANSWER  
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE  
कृͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण राÏय मंğी (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
 

 
(a):  The movement of workers from rural to urban and vice-versa is a common 
phenomenon due to various socio-economic reasons. As per the Periodic Labour Force 
Survey (PLFS) conducted by the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation 
(MoSPI), the percentage distribution of workers engaged in the agriculture sector (covering 
both rural and urban areas) during the last three years are 46.1% (in 2023), 44.8% (in 2024) 
and 43% (in 2025).  
 
(b) & (c):    Agriculture is a State Subject. The Government of India supports the efforts 
of States through appropriate policy measures, various schemes/programmes, budgetary 
support and price support through MSP for improving the productivity, profitability and 
sustainability in the agriculture sector. The Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare 
(DA&FW) has been implementing several Central Sector and Centrally Sponsored Schemes 
to support farmers, including marginal and small farmers, through improved access to 
institutional credit, training, modern agricultural technology and agricultural infrastructure. 
 
       Sustainable agricultural practices, including natural farming, micro-irrigation, organic 
farming and crop diversification, are being promoted through various Central Sector and 
Centrally Sponsored Schemes. The National Mission on Natural Farming (NMNF) promotes 
chemical-free and low-cost farming practices for improving soil health and reducing input 
costs.  Per Drop More Crop (PDMC) component under Pradhan Mantri Rashtriya Krishi Vikas 
Yojana (PM-RKVY) promotes efficient use of water through drip and sprinkler irrigation. It 
supports judicious use of water resources and optimize water availability during lean periods.  
Organic farming is supported through Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana (PKVY) and 
Mission Organic Value Chain Development for North Eastern Region (MOVCDNER), while 
crop diversification is encouraged under the Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana (RKVY). 
Additionally, schemes such as Soil Health & Fertility (SH&F), National Mission on Edible Oils 
(NMEO)-Oil Palm, National Mission on Edible Oils (NMEO)-Oilseeds, Mission for 
Atmanirbharta in Pulses are being implemented to encourage farmers to adopt climate-
resilient, high-value and diversified crops.  
  

 
       To improve access to institutional credit, the Government has taken several measures, 
including annual fixation of Ground Level Agricultural Credit (GLAC) targets for banks, 
prescription of Priority Sector Lending (PSL) targets, and provision of affordable short-term 
crop loans through the Kisan Credit Card (KCC) scheme and the Modified Interest 
Subvention Scheme (MISS). Capacity building and skill development of farmers are 
undertaken through Agricultural Universities (AUs), Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVKs). 
Structured training programmes are integral part of various schemes such as the Agriculture 
Technology Management Agency (ATMA), Sub-Mission on Agricultural Mechanization 
(SMAM), and other flagship programmes like, National Mission on Natural Farming (NMNF), 
National Mission for Sustainable Agriculture (NMSA), National Food Security & Nutrition 
Mission (NFSNM), Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture (MIDH), etc. of the 
Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, which are being  implemented across 
States/UTs. Further, the Government is strengthening agricultural infrastructure through 
initiatives such as the Agriculture Infrastructure Fund (AIF). The AIF provides medium and 
long-term debt financing for the development of post-harvest management infrastructure and 
community farming assets. Under the scheme, Government of India provides credit support 
through 3% per annum interest subvention. 
 
(d) & (e):   The Government of India is implementing various schemes and programmes 
aimed at making agriculture more remunerative, sustainable and employment-oriented, with 
the objective of enhancing farmers’ income, improving agricultural productivity and creating 
employment opportunities in rural areas. Under these initiatives, financial assistance and 
subsidies are provided to farmers, Farmer Producer Organisations (FPOs) and Self Help 
Groups (SHGs) to promote employment generation, entrepreneurship development and 
income enhancement in the rural areas. Further, the Government of India is also promoting 
employment opportunities and skill developments through focused interventions & measures 
in the Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs), manufacturing and services sectors. 
The Department does not maintain data relating to reverse migration or the extent of increase 
in the agricultural workforce attributable specifically to reverse migration.

265. SHRI SAPTAGIRI SANKAR ULAKA  
  
Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY (वाणिज्य एवं उद्योग मंत्री ) be 
pleased to state: 
  
(a) whether the Government has assessed the impact of the Iran –US conflict, 
possible disruptions in West Asian supply routes and the proposed India –US 
trade deal on the availability and prices of urea, DAP, MOP  and other fertilizers 
in India; 
(b) the details of India’s current import dependence on fertilizers, natural gas, 
 ammonia, phosphoric acid and potash, country-wise; 
(c) whether any contingency plan has been prepared by the Government to ensure 
 adequate fertilizer supply during Kharif and Rabi seasons through diversification 
 of imports, strategic reserves and domestic production; 
(d) whether the proposed India–US trade deal may affect fertilizer imports, subsidy 
 burden or domestic manufacturers; and 
(e) the steps taken by the Government to prevent fertilizer shortages, hoarding, 
 black marketing and ensure timely supply to farmers at subsidised prices? 
 
ANSWER 
  
वाणिज्य एवं उद्योग मंत्रालय में राज्यमंत्री (श्री णिणिन प्रसाद) 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY 
(SHRI JITIN PRASADA) 
  
(a) to (e) The Government is closely monitoring the evolving geopolitical 
developments, including the situation in West Asia, and their possible bearing on global 
supply chains and shipping routes.  
  
For ensuring adequate and timely availability of fertilizers to the farmers in the country, 
following measures are taken by the Government every season: 
  
i. Before the commencement of each cropping season, Department of Agriculture and 
Farmers Welfare (DA&FW), in consultation with all the State Governments, assesses 

2 
 
the State-wise & month-wise requirement of fertilizers. The requirement of fertilizers is 
assessed taking into account the projected gross cropped area, irrigated area, last three 
seasons’ consumption pattern and crop wise recommended dose of fertilizers as per 
soil Health fertility status etc. 
ii. On the basis of requirement projected by DA&FW, D/o Fertilizers allocates adequate 
quantities of fertilizers to States by issuing monthly suppl y plan and continuously 
monitors the availability. 
iii. The movement of all major subsidized fertilizers is monitored throughout the country 
by an on -line web-based monitoring system called integrated Fertilizer Management 
System (iFMS). 
iv. Regular Weekly Video Conference is conducted jointly by DA&FW and D/o Fertilizers 
with State Agriculture Officials and corrective actions are taken to dispatch fertilizers as 
indicated by the State Governments. 
  
v. The gap between demand and indigenous production of fe rtilizers is met through 
timely imports which are done well in advance to ensure adequate and timely availability 
of fertilizers in the country. 
vi. The distribution of fertilizers within the State at district/ block level is done by the 
concerned State Government. 
Moreover, the availability of all the fertilizers viz. Urea, DAP, MOP and NPKS, in the 
country, has also remained adequate during the ongoing Kharif 2026 season i.e. from 
01.04.2026 to 15.07.2026. The information regarding requirement, availabili ty, sales 
and closing stock of these fertilizers during the said period is as under:

In addition to this, there is also a closing stock of 22.13 LMT of indigenously produced

Further, the Government has implemented Nutrient Based Subsidy (NBS) Scheme 
w.e.f. 01.04.2010 for Phosphatic and Potassic (P&K) Fertilizers. Under the Scheme, 
P&K fertilizers are covered under Open General License (OGL) and companies are free 
to import/manufacture these fertilizers as per their business dynamics. 
To reduce dependence on imported Phosphatic fertilizers and make the country self -
reliant, the following measures have been taken by the Government: 
i. DoF Fertilizers has issued guidelines dated 18.01.2024 to ensure reasonableness of 
MRP and encourage domestic production. 
ii. Based on the requests, the new manufacturing units or increase in manufacturing 
capacity of existing units have been recognized / taken on record under the NBS 
Scheme. 
iii. The number of P&K fertilizers covered under the NBS Scheme has increased from 
22 grades in 2021 to 28 grades. 
iv. Freight Subsidy on Single Super Phosphate (SSP), wh ich is an indigenously 
manufactured fertilizer, has been approved since Kharif, 2022 to promote SSP usage 
for providing Phosphatic or 'P' nutrient to the soil. 
India and the United States (U.S.) announced a trade deal on February 02, 2026. A 
Joint Statement for the same was released on February 07, 2026. On February 07, 25% 
additional ad valorem tariffs imposed by the U.S. on certain India’s exports citing India’s 
imports of Russian oil were removed.   Pursuant to U.S. Supreme Court judgement 
dated 20th Febr uary 2026 invalidating reciprocal tariffs, the reciprocal tariffs are no 
longer in force. However, the U.S. Government has issued Executive Orders imposing 
10% tariffs on certain products from all countries under section 122 of U.S. trade Act 
1974.  The Government is studying all the developments and remains engaged with the 
U.S. Government.

IRRIGATION FACILITIES 
 
 267. SHRI SELVAGANAPATHI T.M.: 
 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS’ WELFARE क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण मंũी be 
pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has assessed that 315 districts are vulnerable to El Nino and 111 
districts in 12 States are of primary concern due to poor irrigation facilities, if so, the details thereof; 
(b) whether it is also a fact that 111 districts with irrigation coverage below 25% have been 
considered as high priority areas, if so, the details thereof; 
(c) Whether the Government has initiated contingency plans to face the challenge, if so, the details 
thereof; 
(d) Whether the deficit in rain could directly affect kharif crops; and 
(e) if so, the details thereof? 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE  
क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण राǛ मंũी (SHRI  RAM NATH THAKUR) 
 
(a) & (b): The Government through, Mahalanobis National Crop Forecast Centre (MNCFC) has 
carried out a spatial analysis to assess the possible impact of El Niño on Indian agriculture. Based 
on the analysis, 262 districts have been identified as vulnerable districts based on the following 
criteria: 
 Low Surface Irrigation Coverage (< 50%): Districts where less than 50% of the agricultural 
area is covered by surface irrigation projects, leaving them majorly dependent on monsoon rain 
 High Probability of Low Rainfall (> 30%): Districts that have a greater than 30% probability of 
receiving below-normal rainfall during the monsoon.  
 Districts having more than 20000 Hectares sown area during Kharif season 2024-25.  
 
(c):  District-level contingency plans have been prepared for the identified vulnerable 
districts by Indian Council of Agricultural Research-Central Research Institute for Dryland 
Agriculture (ICAR-CRIDA) in consultation with the States. Review meetings have already been 
held with States on the operationalization of district-level contingency measures. The Department 
is also monitoring the availability of quality seeds, maintaining National Seed Reserve of climate-
resilient and short-duration varieties, ensuring adequate availability of fertilizers, and regularly 
reviewing the implementation of contingency plans. 
 
(d) & (e): Deficit or below normal rainfall during the South-West Monsoon may affect the sowing, 
growth and productivity of Kharif crops, particularly in rainfed areas where agriculture is largely 
dependent on monsoon rainfall. The Government is monitoring the monsoon situation and crop 
progress on a continuous basis. Advisory has been issued to the States on El Nino preparedness, 
which includes seed planning, KCC and PMFBY coverage drives etc. Advisory has been issued 
to Department of Water Resources, River Development and Ganga Rejuvenation for judicious 
use of water for irrigation. Further, States have been advised to make intensive use of Viksit 
Bharat – Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission Gramin (VB-G RAM G) funds for 
rejuvenating water conservation structures, such as farm ponds, check dams, canal desilting, and 
bori bandhans, to maximize rainwater harvesting by trapping every drop of early or residual rainfall 
and enhancing water availability for agricultural purposes.

268. SHRI DARSHAN SINGH CHOUDHARY:  
Will the Minister of FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING  
मत्स्यपालन, पशुपालन और डेयरी मंत्री 
be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government is aware of the fact that the increasing number of stray and destitute cattle in the Hoshangabad-
Narsinghpur Lok Sabha Constituency causing problems for farmers, the general public and affecting road safety;  
(b) whether any proposal has been received or is under consideration of the Government establishment or development of 
a Cow Sanctuary in the said Parliamentary Constituency in collaboration with the Government of Madhya Pradesh; and  
(c) whether the Government has any proposal for providing special financial assistance for the protection, conservation, 
treatment, breed improvement and proper fodder arrangements for stray cattle and if so, the details of the proposed action 
plan, the financial assistance sanctioned and the timeframe and if not, the reasons therefor? 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
(SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH ALIAS LALAN SINGH)  
 
(a) to (c) No such information has been received from the Government of Madhya Pradesh. Further, no proposal for the 
establishment or development of a Cow Sanctuary in the Hoshangabad -Narsinghpur Lok Sabha Constituency has been 
received by the Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying from the Government of Madhya Pradesh. 
 
  Animal Husbandry and management of stray cattle including making availability of fodder for stray animals is a 
state subject. However, the Central Government is providing financial assistance to supplement the efforts of the State 
Governments through various ongoing schemes such as: 
 
(i) Rashtriya Gokul Mission (RGM):  This flagship scheme focuses on breed improvement, conservation  and 
development of indigenous breeds, and enhancing milk productivity. Under RGM, financial assistance is provided 
for setting up Gokul Grams (Integrated Cattle Development Centres) and Breed Multiplication Farms, which 
directly help to reduce the economic burden of maintaining cattle. 
 
(ii) National Livestock Mission (NLM): NLM provides subsidies for entrepreneurship development in the feed 
and fodder sector, aimed at addressing fodder scarcity across the country  and provides assistance for fodder 
production. 
 
(iii) Animal Welfare Board of India (AWBI):  The AWBI provides financial grants to recognized Non -
Governmental Organizations (NGOs) and Gaushalas for the construction of shelter houses, veterinary treatment, 
and providing food and water to stray/destitute animals.

LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 272 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 21.07.2026 
 
 
WOMEN IN TEXTILE INDUSTRY 
 
 
272.   MS. S JOTHIMANI: 
 
Will the Minister of TEXTILES वस्त्रमंत्री 
be pleased to state : 
 
(a) whether the Government is aware that a large number of women are employed in the textile 
and garment sectors in Karur and Tiruppur districts of Tamil Nadu, particularly in spinning mills, 
garment factories and home-based units and if so, the details thereof;  
(b) whether any assessment has been undertaken regarding their working conditions, wages, 
health and access to social security and if so, the key findings;  
(c) the details of central schemes or welfare measures implemented to support women workers in 
the textile sector, including maternity benefits, skill development, crèche facilities and 
occupational health provisions, if so, the details thereof;  
(d) whether the Government proposes to launch or expand targeted initiatives in these districts to 
promote labour rights, improve work standards and support women -led enterprises and if so, the 
details thereof; and 
(e) whether the Ministry is engaging with the State Government, industry associations and trade 
unions to address exploitation, wage disparity and lack of protection faced by women workers in 
the textile supply chain? 
 
 
उत्तर 
ANSWER 
वस्त्रराज्‍यमंत्री(श्री पबित्र मार्घेररटा) 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR TEXTILES  
 (SHRI PABITRA MARGHERITA) 
 
(a) Government conducts various censuses and surveys for various sectors including textiles like 
Fourth All India Handloom Census, 2019 -20, annual Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS), 
Annual Survey of Unincorporated Sector Enterprises etc. which provide estimate on employment 
including women engaged in textiles and apparel sector which also include Karur and Tiruppur. 
 
(b) The assessment of workers including women working conditions, wages, social security etc. 
on regular basis is undertaken by respective State Government and central Government agencies. 
 
(c) & (d)  The Chapter IV of the Code of Social Security, 2020 (ESIC) apply on every 
establishment in which ten or more persons are employed other than a seasonal factory which 
provides coverage on ESI benefits  viz., maternity benefits, working hours, occupational safety 
and participation of women workers across sector. Further, the Ministry has taken a 

comprehensive approach —combining industrial development, cluster strengthening, skill 
upgrading, etc. to suppo rt textiles & traditional sector which includes improvement in women’s 
participation and productivity which inter-alia include:  
1. Samarth - Women form the majority of beneficiaries in SAMARTH skill programmes —
especially in garmenting, embroidery, knitwear, handicrafts, etc. Under Samarth scheme, 
5.3 lakh beneficiaries have been successfully trained of which 88% beneficiaries are 
women 
2. Handloom Sector - Flagship scheme for Raw material supply to Handloom weavers 
(includes women Handloom weavers); RMSS provides  Transport subsidy (all types of 
yarns), 15% Price Subsidy and depot operating expenses. Further, eligible beneficiaries 
cover women handloom weavers by including individual weavers, Agencies in which 
weavers are members i.e. Self Help Groups (SHGs), Joint  Liability Groups (JLGs) and 
Cooperative Societies, Handloom Producer Company, Weavers Entrepreneurs. 
Additionally, some of the special provisions provided are: 
i. In partnership with Ministry of Textiles & Office of DC Handlooms, UN Women 
launched #Srijan, a series of workshops to nurture leadership & entrepreneurship among 
women artisans, set to reach 1000 women weavers across India within a year, 1st 
workshop held at Varanasi on 18.10.2025 
ii. Women weavers receive 100% subsidy for construction of work sheds under National 
Handloom Development Programme. More than 73% beneficiaries under Small Cluster 
Development Programme are women. 
iii. Handloom Weaver MUDRA Portal developed with Punjab National Bank for centralized 
online claim disbursement, cutting down delays in financial assistance for margin money, 
interest subvention, and credit guarantee fee 
iv. Women Day slot at Dilli Haat (1st-15th March 2026) and Panch Lakhiya weaver didi slot 
(16th-31st August 2025) organised. 
v. 30 women-led Producer Companies and 15 women-led startups across the country. 
vi. Kamladevi Chattopadhyay Award instituted since 2016 specifically for women weavers, 
with 14 awards conferred so far. 
4. Central Silk Board has developed women -friendly innovations to reduce drudgery and 
improve productivity v iz., Automatic/motorised reeling and spinning machines with women -
friendly operations, financial assistance under central schemes and promotion of women SHGs 
etc. 
(e) A formal framework to extend protections was initiated with the nationwide implementation  
of the Four Labour Codes. New Labour Codes aim to enhance welfare, maternity benefits, 
working hours, occupational safety and participation of women workers across sector including 
textile sector, where women form a substantial share of the workforce.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF PANCHAYATI RAJ 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 273 
  ANSWERED ON 21/07/2026 
  
CAPACITY BUILDING PROGRAMMES FOR WOMEN ELECTED 
REPRESENTATIVES 
  
273. SMT. SMITA UDAY WAGH:            
  
Will the Minister of PANCHAYATI RAJ be pleased to state: 
  
(a) the details and the total number of training, leadership development and governance capacity-
building programmes for Women Elected Representatives in Panchayati Raj Institutions during 
the last five years, State-wise; 
  
(b) whether the Government has assessed the prevalence of proxy representation in Panchayati 
Raj Institutions and its impact on the effective participation of women representatives, if so, the 
details thereof; 
  
(c) whether the Government maintains data on Gram Panchayats and Panchayat-level digital 
governance systems in Maharashtra, including Jalgaon that have adopted Theme-9 (Women 
Friendly Village) under the Localization of Sustainable Development Goals (LSDGs) and 
operationalised Mahila Sabhas, if so, the details thereof; and 
  
(d) whether the Government proposes to establish Panchayat Leadership and Governance 
Resource Centres for women representatives in Maharashtra, particularly in Jalgaon, if so, the 
details thereof? 
  
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF PANCHAYATI RAJ 
 
(SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH ALIAS LALAN SINGH) 
  
(a) Panchayat, being “Local Self Government”, is a State subject. However, the Ministry has 
been implementing a Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Revamped Rashtriya Gram Swaraj 
Abhiyan (RGSA) w.e.f. the financial year 2022-23 with the major objective of Capacity Building 
& Training (CB&T) of Elected Representatives, Functionaries and other stakeholders of 
Panchayats across all States/UTs for improving Panchayat Governance. Under the scheme of 
RGSA, the Ministry provides support for Capacity Building & Training of elected 
representatives, functionaries, and other stakeholders of Panchayats in different categories, viz. 
basic orientation and refresher training, thematic training, specialized training, panchayat 
development plan training, and leadership training, etc. A total of 34,14,342 Women Elected 

2 
 
Representatives were trained from FY 2022-23 to FY 2026-27 (as on 10th July 2026) under the 
scheme, including the State of Maharashtra. The State-wise details is at Annexure-I. 
In addition, on 11th March 2025, the Ministry launched a comprehensive specialised training 
module as part of “Sashakta Panchayat Netri Abhiyan” for building the capacity of Women 
Elected Representatives (WERs) of Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs) to develop their 
leadership, communication, managerial & decision-making skills for effective women-led 
governance. A total of 1,53,616 WERs have been trained on this module as on 10.07.2026. The 
state-wise detail is at Annexure-II.  
(b) Yes, Sir. On the direction of the Hon’ble Supreme Court, the Ministry of Panchayati Raj 
constituted an Advisory Committee in September 2023 to examine the issue of Women Pradhans 
being represented by the male members of their families and also to examine other issues related 
to proxy representation. The Committee submitted its Report with recommendations to the 
Ministry in February 2025, and the same has been accepted by the Ministry. 
The Advisory Committee recommended that the State Governments take necessary measures, 
including legal safeguards, capacity-building, social audits, and penal provisions, to eliminate 
proxy leadership in Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs) and ensure real empowerment, autonomy 
and accountability of elected women representatives. Owing to the importance of this matter and 
its impact on women's leadership in PRIs, this Ministry has also constituted a Task Force on 17th 
April 2025 to provide an implementation roadmap for the States/UTs to practically execute the 
recommendations put forth by the Advisory Committee on the issues of Women Pradhans. 
(c) Yes, Sir. The Ministry has conceptualized the localization of sustainable development goals 
(LSDGs) through a thematic approach to comprehend global goals into local actions through 
planning. Out of 9 themes of LSDGs, Theme 9: Women-Friendly Panchayat aims to focus on 
gender equality and women's empowerment. Panchayats are mandated to prepare a plan for 
economic development and social justice. During the preparation of the Gram Panchayat 
Development Plan, Panchayats are advised to take a Sankalp on 1-2 Themes of LSDGs to 
provide targeted interventions in various sectors of the Sankalp theme. As reported by the State 
of Maharashtra, the number of Gram Panchayats that have adopted the Sankalp on the 'Women 
Friendly Panchayat' (Theme 9) during the plan period from 2022–23 to 2025–26 in the State of 
Maharashtra and Jalgaon District is given below: 
Plan Year Maharashtra Jalgaon 
2022-23 - - 
2023-24 255 2 
2024-25 1364 62 
2025-26 1557 47 
2026-27 (As on 10.07.2026) 222 0 
 
In addition, under special initiatives of the Ministry, 744 Panchayats in the country, tentatively 
one in each district, have been selected for developing them as Model Women Friendly Gram 
Panchayats. Out of this, 34 Gram Panchayats have been selected in Maharashtra, including 1 in 
Jalgaon District.   

3 
 
Furthermore, the State has also informed that the Gram Panchayat Act of Maharashtra makes a 
mandatory provision for Gram Panchayats to hold four Gram Sabhas annually and to conduct a 
Mahila Sabha prior to each of the Gram Sabhas. Accordingly, Mahila Sabhas are conducted 
before the Gram Sabhas. 
(d) No such Panchayat Leadership and Governance Resource Centres for women representatives 
have been established in the State of Maharashtra, including Jalgaon, till date. However, under 
“Sashakta Panchayat Netri Abhiyan”, a total of 10,966 Women Elected Representatives (WERs) 
have been trained in a specialized module in Maharashtra, including 248 Women Elected 
Representatives (WERs) in Jalgaon District so far.

MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS

DEDICATED AGENCY FOR DIGITAL HARASSMENT 
 
274.      SHRI HIBI EDEN: 
 
Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government is aware of the rising cases of cyber fraud and 
digital harassment, State -wise including Kerala, particularly in Ernakulam 
district; 
 
(b) whether the Government proposes to establish a dedicated agency to 
deal with cybercrimes; 
 
(c) whether the cyber fraud cases reported and action taken, including 
blocking of SIM cards,  devices and social media accounts during the last 
three years, State/UT and district-wise data including Kerala and Ernakulam; 
and 
 
(d) whether the Government has taken any steps for public awareness, 
prevention and victim  support, including helplines and assistance 
mechanisms, to curb cyber fraud and digital harassment in Kerala? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
(SHRI BANDI SANJAY KUMAR) 
 
(a) to (d) :  The National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) compiles and 
publishes the statistical data on crimes in its publication “Crime in India”.  
The latest published report is for the year 20 24.  As per the data published 
by the NCRB, State/UT wise details of cases registered,  cases charge -
sheeted, cases  convicted,  persons  arrested, persons  charge-sheeted  and  

-2- 
L.S.US.Q.NO. 274 FOR 21.07.2026  
persons convicted under Fraud for Cyber Crimes (involving communication 
devices as medium/target) during the year 2023 & 2024 are at the Annexure-
I. As per the data published by the NCRB, District wise details of cases 
registered under Fraud for Cyber Crimes (inv olving communication devices 
as medium/target) in Kerala during the year 2023 & 2024 is at the Annexure-
II. Details regarding action taken on reported cyber fraud cases including 
blocking of SIM cards, devices and social media accounts are not maintained 
by NCRB. 
 
‘Police’ and ‘Public Order’ are State subjects under the Seventh Schedule to 
the Constitution of India. Accordingly, the States and Union Territories (UTs) 
are primarily responsible for the prevention, detection, investigation, and 
prosecution of cybercrime. The Central Government, through the Ministry of 
Home Affairs (MHA), supplements the efforts of States and UTs by providing 
policy guidance, technological support, capacity -building assistance, and 
financial resources to strengthen cybercrime management and enforcement 
capabilities.  
 
To strengthen the mechanism to deal with cyber crimes in a 
comprehensive and coordinated manner, the Central Government has taken 
steps which, inter-alia, include the following: 
 

-3- 
L.S.US.Q.NO. 274 FOR 21.07.2026  
i. The Ministry of Home Affairs has set up the ‘Indian Cyber Crime 
Coordination Centre’ (I4C) as an attached office to deal with all types of 
cyber crimes in the country, in a coordinated and comprehensive manner. 
ii. The ‘National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal’ (NCRP) 
(https://cybercrime.gov.in) has been launched, as a part of the I4C, to 
enable public to report incidents pertaining to all types of cyber crimes, 
with special focus on cyber crimes against women and childre n. Cyber 
crime incidents reported on National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal, their 
conversion into FIRs and subsequent action i.e. filing of chargesheets, 
arrest and resolution of complaints, thereon are handled by the State/UT 
Law Enforcement Agencies concerned as per the provisions of the law. 
iii. The ‘Citizen Financial Cyber Fraud Reporting and Management System’ 
(CFCFRMS), under I4C, has been launched in year 2021 for immediate 
reporting of financial frauds and to stop siphoning off funds by the 
fraudsters. As per CFCFRMS operated by I4C, till 30.06.2026, financial 
amount of more than Rs. 11,158 Crore has been saved in more than 32.80 
lakh complaints.  A toll -free Helpline number ‘1930’ has been 
operationalized to get assistance in lodging online cyber complaints. 
iv. ‘Sahyog’ Portal has been launched to expedite the process of sending 
notices to IT intermediaries by the Appropriate Government or its agency 
under   clause (b) of sub-section (3) of   section 79 of the IT Act, 2000 to  
 

-4- 
L.S.US.Q.NO. 274 FOR 21.07.2026  
facilitate the removal or disabling of access to any information, data or 
communication link being  
v. Samanvaya Platform has been made operational to serve as an 
Management Information System (MIS) platform, data repository and a 
coordination platform for LEAs for cybercrime data sharing and analytics. 
It provides analytics based interstate linkages of crimes and c riminals, 
involved in cybercrime complaints in various States/UTs. The module 
‘Pratibimb’ maps locations of criminals and crime infrastructure on a map 
to give visibility to jurisdictional officers. The module also facilitates 
seeking and receiving of tech no-legal assistance by Law Enforcement  
Agencies from I4C and other SMEs. It has lead to arrest of more than 
29,837 accused and more than 2,33,593 Cyber Investigation assistance 
request. 
vi. To further strengthen operational efficiency and ensure uniformity in 
handling cybercrime complaints, the Ministry has issued a 
comprehensive Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) for NCRP-CFCFRMS. 
The SOP lays down a standardized framework for complaint proc essing, 
bank coordination, grievance redressal, removal of lien markings, and 
restoration of defrauded funds to rightful claimants based on complaints 
received through the NCRP. Money Restoration Module for expeditious 
restoration of defrauded money to the  victims and Grievance Redressal 
Module for timely attending to the grievances relating to freezing of the  

-5- 
L.S.US.Q.NO. 274 FOR 21.07.2026  
bank accounts and lien marking of the amount, have been made 
functional from April, 2026. 
vii. To further spread awareness on cyber crime, the Central Government has 
taken steps which, inter -alia, include; caller tune campaign, 
dissemination of messages through SMS, I4C social media account i.e. X 
(formerly Twitter) (@CyberDost), Facebook(CyberDostI 4C), Instagram 
(CyberDostI4C), Telegram(cyberdosti4c), SMS campaign, TV campaign, 
Radio campaign, School Campaign, advertisement in cinema halls, 
celebrity endorsement, IPL campaign,  engaged MyGov for publicity in 
multiple mediums,  organizing Cyber Safety  and Security Awareness 
weeks in association with States/UTs, publishing of Handbook for 
Adolescents/Students, digital displays on railway stations and airports 
across, etc.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF COMMERCE & INDUSTRY 
DEPARTMENT FOR PROMOTION OF INDUSTRY AND INTERNAL TRADE 
 
LOK SABHA 
 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 275. 
      TO BE ANSWERED ON TUESDAY, THE 21ST JULY, 2026. 
 
INVESTMENT REALISATION AND EMPLOYMENT GENERATION 
 
275.  SHRI P V MIDHUN REDDY: 
 
Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY be pleased to state: 
वाणिज्य  एवं उद्योग मंत्री 
(a)  the number of investment proposals in Andhra Pradesh tracked by Department 
for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) or  Invest India that have 
converted into operational projects during the last two years, along with the total 
investment deployed and jobs created; 
 
(b)  the sector -wise investment requirements assessed by the Government for 
Andhra Pradesh in manufacturing, ports, food processing, and electronics, and 
the details of any investment roadmap prepared for the State; 
 
(c)  the number of Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) and local 
entrepreneurs in Andhra Pradesh that have benefited from centrally sanctioned 
industrial schemes during the last two years; and 
 
(d)  the measures taken to ensure equitable distribution of investment -linked 
employment across all districts? 
 
ANSWER 
 
वाणिज्य  एवं उद्योग मंत्रालय में राज्य मंत्री (श्री णिणिन प्रसाद)   
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE & INDUSTRY 
(SHRI JITIN PRASADA) 
 
(a) to (d): During the last two years, a total of 10 investment proposals, tracked by DPIIT 
and Invest India, have been grounded in Andhra Pradesh. Of these, 2 projects 
have completed the construction of their manufacturing facilities, while 8 
projects are presently under construction. The projects are being implemented 
with an estimated Investment of ₹ 6962 crore and are expec ted to generate 
employment of approx. 22,167 jobs. These cases were successfully facilitated 
by Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) and Invest 
India with support from the relevant Central Government Ministries and 
Government of Andhra Pradesh. 
Government of India is developing various Industrial Corridor Projects as part 
of National Industrial Corridor Development Programme (NICDP) designed to 
establish Greenfield Industrial Smart Cities across India, positioning the country 
as a global manufacturing hub. The National Industrial Corridor Development 

Corporation Ltd. (NICDC) is developing three major Greenfield Industrial Smart 
City nodes in Andhra Pradesh namely: Krishnapatnam, Orvakal and Kopparthy, 
located across diﬀerent indust rial corridors, reinforcing the state’s strategic 
importance in regional industrial development. These projects support the 
Make in India vision and oﬀer world -class infrastructure for industries in 
logistics, aerospace, electronics and advanced manufacturing. 
The Bulk Drug Park Scheme is being implemented with the objective of 
facilitating establishment of three Bulk Drug Parks in the states of Andhra 
Pradesh, Gujarat, Himachal Pradesh, and to reduce the cost of bulk drug 
manufacturing through the creation  of world -class common infrastructure. 
These parks provide shared facilities, including solvent recovery plants and 
common eﬄuent treatment systems, to improve efficiency and environmental 
compliance. 
11 projects under the modified Electronics Manufacturin g Clusters (EMC 2.0) 
Schemes have been approved by the Government of India across 10 states 
including Andhra Pradesh with a projected investment of over ₹ 1.46 lakh crore 
and estimated to generate employment of approx. 1.80 lakh jobs. The scheme 
supports c reation of world -class electronics manufacturing infrastructure by 
funding dedicated clusters with common facilities. 
Solar Energy Corporation of India Limited (SECI) will be developing a 1200 
MWh Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) at Nandyal, Andhra Pradesh and 
a 50 MW Hybrid Solar Project. This marks a significant milestone in 
strengthening Andhra Pradesh’s renewable energy infrastructure and 
accelerating India’s transition towards a greener, more resilient energy future. 
Government of India under the S agarmala Scheme is providing financial 
assistance to 12 projects in Andhra Pradesh including Visakhapatnam Port 
Authority for enhancing the infrastructure related to Port led Industrialization, 
Port Modernization, Port Connectivity enhancement, Coastal Com munity 
Development & Coastal Shipping and Inland Waterways. Several measures 
have been undertaken for the modernization of ports, including mechanization 
of existing berths and terminals, digitization and logistics integration, 
construction of new berths a nd terminals, development of road, rail and 
waterways connectivity. 
India’s first Drone City is being developed at Orvakal in Kurnool district, marking 
a major milestone in advancing India’s capabilities in next -generation 
aerospace and unmanned systems. Developed in collaboration with the 
Government of Andhra Pradesh, the 300 -acre Drone City is expected to 
generate over 40,0 00 jobs and will house the world’s largest common drone 
testing facility and will serve as a fully integrated ecosystem for manufacturing, 
testing, research, repairs and development, bringing key components of drone 
innovation under one unified infrastructure. 
The National Steering Committee (NSC) approved the Strategic Investment 
Plan (SIP) for the Visakhapatnam ITI Cluster in Andhra Pradesh under the 

Pradhan Mantri Skilling and Employability Transformation (PM-SETU) scheme. 
This marks the first -ever Strategic Investment Plan to be cleared under PM -
SETU and makes Andhra Pradesh the first State to operationalize an industry 
partnership under the scheme. Approval of the Visakhapatnam Cluster 
represents a significant step towards transforming Industrial Training Institutes 
into industry-managed, outcome-oriented institutions capable of responding to 
evolving workforce requirements. 
Entrepreneurship and Skill Development Programme (ESDP) is being 
implemented with the objective of motivating young and aspiring entrepreneurs 
to pursue self-employment and entrepreneurship as viable career options. The 
Scheme seeks to promote establishment of new enterprises, strengthen 
capacities of existing MSMEs and foster entrepreneurial culture across the 
country. These Training components are implemented with the help of MSME-
DFOs, premier institutes such as IIMs/IITs/ICAR/CSIR/NIT/Administrative 
Training Institutes (ATIs), post harvesting and Food Processing institutes, 
Engineering Institutes, etc. Progress of ESDP scheme in An dhra Pradesh 
during the last two years may be seen at Annexure. 
Samarth, a Central Sector Scheme is a demand -driven, placement -oriented 
skilling program aligned with the National Skills Qualifications Framework 
(NSQF). The Scheme is designed to incentivize and support industry eﬀorts in 
generating employment opportunities across the organized textile and related 
sectors and covers the entire textile value chain, excluding Spinning and 
Weaving. A total of 12 Implementing partners (IP’s) have been implementin g 
the scheme with 37 active training centres in Andhra Pradesh. 
Further, Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Schemes have been launched 
across 14 key sectors with an objective to enhance manufacturing 
competitiveness, attract investment, promote scale, and strengthen integration 
with global value chains. As of 31st March 2026, these schemes have resulted 
in actual investments of over  ₹ 2.40 lakh crore, production/sales exceeding ₹ 
22.66 lakh crore and employment generation of over 14.15 lakh persons (direct 
and indirect) in the country. These outcomes indicate contribution of the 
schemes towards expanding manufacturing capacity, increasing production, 
strengthening industrial ecosystems, and improving the competitiveness of 
participating sectors.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
DEPARTMENT OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 277

ROLE OF AGROFORESTRY IN GENERATING RURAL EMPLOYMENT 
 
277. Thiru Dr. S Jagathratchakan: 
 
Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  the role envisaged by the Government for agroforestry in 
generating rural employment, strengthening climate resilience, 
promoting sustainable land-use practices and supporting 
livelihood diversification and the factors that have constrained 
its full utilisation despite its recognised potential; 
(b)  the programmes implemented by the Government for linking 
agroforestry with rural development initiatives, livelihood 
schemes, natural resource management activities and 
community-based development interventions; 
(c)  the achievements recorded under initiatives designed to 
encourage the adoption of agroforestry practices while 
enhancing income opportunities and environmental 
sustainability in rural areas; and 
(d)  the measures proposed by the Government for expanding 
agroforestry-based livelihood opportunities, strengthening 
community engagement and improving long-term socio-
economic outcomes in rural areas in the country? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
(SHRI KAMLESH PASWAN)  
(a) to (d): As per the information furnished by Ministry of Agriculture 
& Farmers Welfare, Government of India introduced National 
Agroforestry Policy (NAP), 2014 to promote tree planting in 
agricultural landscapes, recommending establishment of a Mission 
for the organized development of agroforestry sector. In pursuance 
of the Policy, Sub-Mission on Agroforestry (SMAF) under National 
Mission for Sustainable Agriculture (NMSA) was implemented by 
Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare from 2016-17 to 2021-
22 to integrate tree planting with agricultural crops under the motto 

Page 2 of 3 
 
"Har Medh Par Ped", thereby providing farmers with an additional 
source of income and enhancing the resilience of farming systems. 
The scheme helped in generating on-farm employment, strengthening 
climate resilience and promoting sustainable land-use practices 
through integration of trees with crops/fruit trees, thus, contributed 
to improve soil health, efficient use of natural resources, carbon 
sequestration, biodiversity conservation and diversification of farm 
income through production of timber, fuelwood, fodder, fruits and 
other tree-based products.  
  Subsequently, from 2023-24, SMAF has been restructured as 
Agroforestry Component under Pradhan Mantri Rashtriya Krishi Vikas 
Yojana (PM- RKVY). The scheme aims to ensure the availability of 
Quality Planting Material (QPM), including seeds, seedlings, clones, 
hybrids and improved varieties, to promote tree-based farming and 
increase tree cover on agricultural lands. Under this component, 
assistance is being provided for establishment of nurseries, raising 
Quality Planting Material (QPM) in existing nurseries, capacity 
building, and technical support through institutions such as ICAR-
CAFRI for effective implementation of agroforestry programmes. 
  Since the start of the agroforestry scheme, a total of 1725 
agroforestry nurseries have been established, around 1,594 lakh of 
quality planting materials (QPM) (saplings) have been raised and 403 
agroforestry nurseries have been accredited under the National 
Nursery Accreditation Protocol. 
In addition, under the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural 
Employment Guarantee Scheme (Mahatma Gandhi NREGS) of the 
Ministry of Rural Development, plantation-based activities such as 
Farm Forestry on individual and community lands were permissible 
works and contributed towards natural resource management, 
climate resilience, and livelihood enhancement.  
The details of Farm Forestry works completed under Mahatma Gandhi 
NREGS during the last three financial years and the current year (up 
to 30th June, 2026) are as follows:

and the current year (up to 30th June) under Mahatma Gandhi

Consequent upon enactment of the Viksit Bharat – Guarantee 
for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) (VB–G RAM G) Act in 
December 2025 the implementation of VB- G RAM G Scheme has 
commenced in the rural areas of entire country with effect from 1st

Under the VB–G RAM G Act, 2025, plantation-based livelihood 
and climate-resilient interventions continue to receive due emphasis. 
Accordingly, "Agroforestry Block Plantation on Individual Land, 
Community Land, and Wasteland" has been included as a permissible 
work under the interim list of permissible works, replacing the earlier 
Farm Forestry category under Mahatma Gandhi NREGS. The objective 
of the intervention is to promote sustainable land use, strengthen 
climate resilience, enhance green cover, and provide long-term 
livelihood opportunities for rural households.

Cooperatives in Daman and Diu 
 
†279. Shri Patel Umeshbhai Babubhai: 
 
Will the Minister of COOPERATION (सहकारिता मंत्री) be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  the details of the Daman and Diu State Cooperative Bank Limited, Mahakaleshwar 
Fisheries Cooperative Society (Diu), and Mahasagar Fish Farming Cooperative Society (Diu) 
cooperative institutions; 
(b)   the details regarding date of last election, present management status, reason and legal 
basis for administration by an administrator/Government official, reasons for postponement of 
elections and the probable time-frame for holding the next election in these institutions; 
(c)  whether any time-bound action plan is being prepared to ensure timely democratic elections 
and if so, the details thereof; and 
(d)  the maximum period within which re -elections must be conducted after a society is 
dissolved or an administrator is appointed? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF COOPERATION 
सहकारिता मंत्री (SHRI AMIT SHAH)  
 
 (a)  As per the information provided by the Union Territory of Dadra & Nagar Haveli and 
Daman & Diu , the Daman & Diu  State Cooperative Bank Limited, Daman; Mahakaleshwar 
Fisheries Cooperative Society Ltd., Saudwadi and Shri Mahasagar Fisheries Cooperative 
Society Ltd. , Vanakbara were registered on 17.11.2015, 27.12.2010 and 10.12.1987, 
respectively. The Cooperative institutions are presently functional.   
 
(b) & (c)   The Daman & Diu State Cooperative Bank Limited, Daman has not held elections 
after its bifurcation from the Goa State Cooperative Bank Ltd. The Registrar of Cooperative 
Societies has intimated that the governing body of the bank constituted for day -to-day 
functioning of the bank, failed to hold election to elect new managing committee, was taking 
major decisions on important matters including advancement of loans and failed to quantify 
and transfer assets and liabilities from the Goa State Cooperative Bank Ltd. 
 
  Accordingly, in exercise of powers under Section 77A(1)(e)(ii) of the Maharashtra 
Cooperative Societies Act, 1960 as extended to the erstwhile Union Territory of Daman & Diu, 
the Registrar of Cooperative Societies (RCS), UT Administration of Dadra & Nagar Haveli and 

Daman & Diu (DNH&DD) appointed an Administrator in the bank vide Order dated 
03.06.2022 until further orders or till the finalization of the new managing committee 
whichever is earlier.   
  
Last elections in Mahakaleshwar Fisheries Cooperative Society Ltd., Saudwadi and in 
Shri Mahasagar Fisheries Cooperative Society Ltd., Vanakbara were held on 30.08.2019. RCS, 
DNH&DD found the Managing Committee of these societies negligent in the performance of 
its duties, as it failed to submit statutory books of accounts, did not properly maintain trading 
stock and cash book, and did not conduct meetings of the Managing Committee. Accordingly, 
RCS, in exercise of powers under Section 78 of the Maharashtra Cooperative Societies Act, 
1960 as extended to the erstwhile Union Territory of Daman & Diu, appointed an Administrator 
in these societies vide Order dated 14.10.2022 until further orders or till the finalization of the 
new managing committee whichever is earlier.   
 
(d)  In respect of the Daman & Diu State Cooperative Bank Limited, Daman, there is no 
period prescribed for the tenure of the Administrator, appointed under the provisions of Section 
77A of the Maharashtra Cooperative Societies Act, 1960, as extended to the er stwhile Union 
Territory of Daman & Diu. 
 
In respect of Mahakaleshwar Fisheries Cooperative Society Ltd., Saudwadi and Shri 
Mahasagar Fisheries Cooperative Society Ltd., Vanakbara , as per Section 78 of the 
Maharashtra Cooperative Societies Act, 1960, as extended to the erstwhile Union Territory of 
Daman & Diu, the Registrar is empowered to appoint an Administrator for a period of four 
years in aggregate.

DEPARTMENT OF FISHERIES 
 
LOK SABHA

ANSWERED ON 21ST JULY, 2026 
 
Fish Production 
 
281. Shri Dileshwar Kamait: 
 
Will the Minister of FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING  be pleased to 
state: 
(a)  the details of increase in fish production as of April 2026 since the launch of the 
scheme; 
(b)  the number of women beneficiaries and disbursement of funds under the scheme as 
of April 2026; 
(c)  whether support has been provided by the Government for cold chains, processing 
and packaging under the scheme as of April 2026; and 
(d)  if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH ALIAS LALAN SINGH 
 
(a): The Department of Fisheries, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying, 
Government of India with effect from the Financial Year 2020 -21 is implementing  the 
Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) for holistic development of fisheries and 
aquaculture sector in the country. This scheme during its implementation period of last six 
years has made vital contribution towards augmentation of fish production in the country. 
During the period of the PMMSY, the fish production in the country has increased from 
141.64 lakh tonne (2019-20) to 197.75 lakh tonne (2024-25). 
(b): The PMMSY inter-alia encompasses inclusive development by providing higher 
financial assistance of 60 percent of the unit cost for women beneficiaries under beneficiary-
oriented activities. Under the PMMSY, during the last six Financial Years (2020-21 to 2025-
26), fisheries development proposals amounting to Rs.4178.30 crore have been sanctioned 
for covering a total 1,47,654 women beneficiaries across various States and Union 
Territories.  

(c) & (d): Development of cold chain and marketing infrastructure facilities for fisheries  
and aquaculture  is one of the thrust areas of the central schemes implemented by t he 
Department of Fisher ies, Ministry of Fisheries , Animal Husbandry and Dairying.  The 
Department of Fisheries, Government of India till April, 2026 has accorded approvals to the 
proposals amounting to Rs 2,797 crore under the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana 
(PMMSY) and Fisheries and Aquaculture Infrastructure Development Fund (FIDF) for 
development of cold chain and marketing facilities in the country. The key activities 
approved includes; 775 cold storages and ice plants,  28,489 units of fish transportation 
facilities such as 1 3,718 motorcycles with ice boxes, 8,527 bicycles with ice boxes, 4,257 
auto rickshaws, 1,577 insulated trucks and 410 refrigerated trucks, 1,394 live fish vending 
units, 6,018 fish kiosks, 117 retail fish markets, 24 wholesale fish markets in all the States 
and Union Territories.

INITIATIVES TO STRENGTHEN SEED SECTOR 
 
285 .SHRI RAO RAJENDRA SINGH: 
 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE कृ ͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण 
मंğी be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the steps being taken by the Government to strengthen India's position in the 
global seed sector; 
(b) whether the Government has details on the initiatives taken to promote public-
private partnerships in the seed sector, if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether the Government proposes to address challenges posed by climate 
change and food insecurity through innovations in seed technologies and partnerships; 
and 
(d) if so, the details thereof? 
 
                                                      ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE  
कृ ͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण राÏय मंğी (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
(a): Government has taken several measures to strengthen India’s seed sector and 
enhance its global competitiveness, which include the following: 
(i) The Government, through the National Agricultural Research and Education 
System (NARES), comprising 56 ICAR Institutes, 48 State Agricultural Universities 
(SAUs), 03 Central Agricultural Universities (CAUs) and 39 centres under the All India 
Coordinated Research Project (AICRP) on Seed (Crops), is undertaking research and 
development of improved crop varieties. During the period from 2014 to 2025, a total 
of 3,236 field crop varieties have been released and notified, of which 2,996 are 
climate-resilient varieties, including 587 extreme climate-tolerant varieties 
comprising 341 drought tolerant, 89 flood tolerant, 80 salinity tolerant, 59 heat stress 
tolerant and 18 cold tolerant varieties.  
  

The crop-wise details are as under: 
S. No. Crop Group Crop Varieties Climate-resilient Varieties 
1 Cereals 1,574 1,453 
2 Oilseeds 444 397 
3 Pulses 473 446 
4 Forages 207 185 
5 Fibre 408 392 
6 Sugarcane 96 96 
7 Other Crops 34 27  Total 3,236 2,996 
(ii) The Government promotes the production and multiplication of breeder, foundation 
and certified seeds of high-yielding and climate-resilient varieties, including varieties 
tolerant to drought, heat, flood, salinity and waterlogging, to ensure timely availability 
of quality seeds suited to diverse agro-climatic conditions across the country. 
(iii) During the past three years, the Protection of Plant Varieties and Farmers’ Rights 
(PPV&FR) Authority has expedited registration of plant varieties, thereby enabling 
farmers, ICAR Institutes, State Agricultural Universities and private seed companies 
to protect the varieties developed by them. So far, 10,802 varieties of 219 crop 
species have been registered under the PPV&FR Act, out of which 5,689 varieties 
were registered during 2023–26. 
(iv) The Government has established an extensive institutional framework for 
production and distribution of quality seeds. At present, 229 Seed Hubs and 384 
Breeder Seed Production Centres are engaged in seed production. Further, 17 
State Seed Corporations and National Seeds Corporation Limited, along with national 
public sector organizations such as Bharatiya Beej Sahakari Samiti Limited (BBSSL), 
Hindustan Insecticides Limited (HIL), National Agricultural Cooperative Marketing 
Federation of India Ltd. (NAFED), National Fertilizers Limited (NFL), Krishak Bharati 
Cooperative Limited (KRIBHCO), Indian Farm Forestry Development Cooperative 
Limited (IFFDC) and private seed companies contribute significantly to the production 
and distribution of quality seeds across the country. 
  

 
(v) To strengthen quality assurance, 178 notified Seed Testing Laboratories (STLs) 
are engaged in seed testing across the country. The Government also provides 
financial assistance for strengthening Seed Testing Laboratories, including support for 
International Seed Testing Association (ISTA) membership and technical audits for 
ISTA accreditation. 
(vi) Seed quality is regulated under the Seeds Act, 1966, the Seeds Rules, 1968 and 
the Seeds (Control) Order, 1983, as amended from time to time. These statutory 
provisions empower the State Governments to regulate seed quality, undertake 
inspections, testing and enforcement, and curb the sale of sub-standard and spurious 
seeds. To support the regulatory framework, a Seed Authentication, Traceability 
and Holistic Inventory (SATHI) Portal has been deployed in phased manner to 
facilitate end-to-end digital traceability in seed production, certification, inventory 
management and distribution, thereby enhancing transparency and quality assurance 
across the seed value chain.  
(vii) To facilitate international trade and improve ease of doing business, the 
Government has simplified procedures relating to the import and export of seeds and 
planting material. Following the disbanding of the EXIM Committee in October, 2024, 
import and export approvals are being facilitated through DGFT’s digital platforms 
while continuing to ensure compliance with applicable plant quarantine and regulatory 
requirements. The Government also promotes seed exports through participation in 
the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) Seed 
Schemes, International Seed Testing Association (ISTA) framework and National 
Accreditation Board for Testing and Calibration Laboratories (NABL) accreditation of 
Seed Testing Laboratories to align India’s seed quality systems with internationally 
accepted standards.

(viii) India is a founding member of the International Treaty on Plant Genetic 
Resources for Food and Agriculture (ITPGRFA), which provides a multilateral 
framework for conservation, sustainable use and exchange of plant genetic resources 
for food and agriculture and promotes equitable sharing of benefits arising from their 
use. This provides domestic R&D sector access to global germplasm to help them in 
developing improved varieties of seeds. 
(ix) The Government also collaborates with international agricultural research 
institutions of the CGIAR system, including the International Rice Research Institute 
(IRRI), International Crops Research Institute for the Semi-Arid Tropics 
(ICRISAT), International Maize and Wheat Improvement Center (CIMMYT), 
International Center for Agricultural Research in the Dry Areas (ICARDA) and the 
Alliance of Bioversity International and the International Center for Tropical 
Agriculture (CIAT) for exchange of knowledge and identification of suitable climate-
resilient seed technologies and best practices. With Government support, the 
International Rice Research Institute established its South Asia Regional Centre 
(ISARC) at Varanasi in 2018 for collaborative rice research and capacity building. 
Further, establishment of the International Potato Center (CIP) South Asia Regional 
Centre (CSARC) at Singna, Agra, Uttar Pradesh was approved on 25.06.2025. 
(b):  Government has undertaken several initiatives to promote Public-Private 
Partnerships (PPP) in the seed sector by facilitating collaboration among ICAR 
Institutes, State Agricultural Universities (SAUs), State Seed Corporations, National 
Seeds Corporation (NSC) and private seed companies for seed multiplication, varietal 
evaluation, breeder-to-certified seed chain management, technology dissemination 
and licensing of publicly bred varieties and hybrids to private seed companies for 
large-scale multiplication and distribution, thereby leveraging private sector expertise, 
investment and outreach. 
       During the last three years (2023–24 to 2025–26), 1,317 licensing agreements 
for seeds, crop varieties and planting materials were executed by 27 ICAR Institutes 
with public and private sector organizations. 
     Further, the Agriculture Infrastructure Fund (AIF) provides financial support for 
creation of agriculture infrastructure, including seed processing facilities.  
  

       
      Government also provides financial assistance to States and implementing 
agencies for seed-related activities such as production and distribution of high-yielding 
varieties, development of seed infrastructure, seed processing, storage and testing 
facilities under various programmes including the National Food Security Nutrition 
Mission (NFSNM), National Mission on Edible Oils–Oilseeds (NMEO-Oilseeds), 
Mission for Aatmanirbharta in Pulses, Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana (RKVY), National 
Mission on High Yielding Seeds (NMHYS) and Mission for Cotton Productivity. These 
initiatives also support research and innovation in modern crop improvement 
technologies, including genome editing, molecular breeding, biofortification, 
agrobiodiversity and establishment of a Global R&D Hub for Millets. 
(c) & (d): Yes, Sir. 
        To address the challenges posed by climate change and strengthen national food 
security, the Government promotes the development and adoption of high-yielding, 
climate-resilient and bio-fortified crop varieties through the National Agricultural 
Research and Education System (NARES). ICAR Institutes and the private sector are 
using advanced crop improvement technologies such as Marker-Assisted Selection 
(MAS), Gene Editing and Speed Breeding to accelerate the development of improved 
crop varieties. 
        The Government also promotes production and dissemination of these varieties 
through the breeder, foundation and certified seed chain and collaborates with 
international agricultural research institutions of the CGIAR system for exchange of 
knowledge, germplasm, best practices and climate-resilient seed technologies. During 
the period from 2014 to 2025, 2,996 climate-resilient crop varieties have been 
developed by the National Agricultural Research and Education System (NARES), 
thereby strengthening the resilience of Indian agriculture to climate change while 
contributing to enhanced agricultural productivity and national food security.

PACS as PM Kisan Samriddhi Kendras  
†288. Dr. Sambit Patra:  
Will the Minister of COOPERATION (सहकारिता मंत्री) be pleased to state:  
(a) the total number of Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS) in the country have been 
granted permission to function as Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samridhi Kendra;  
(b) the actual number of Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS) that are currently functioning 
as PMKSK;  
(c) the States where the pilot project for PACS training was conducted by the Government including 
the number of PACS provided training under the said pilot project;  
(d) in which States the pilot project of PACS training was conducted by the Government and how 
many PACS were trained under the 'Pilot Project'; and  
(e) the key learnings from the pilot project on Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS) 
training? 
 
ANSWER  
MINISTER OF COOPERATION 
सहकारिता मंत्री (SHRI AMIT SHAH) 
 
(a) & (b)    The Government aims to operationalise PMKSKs in a phased manner, in all functional 
PACS.  PACS functioning as PMKSKs enables them to provide various quality agri -inputs like 
fertilizers, seeds, farm implements, pesticides, soil/  seed testing facilities, etc., to the farmers at 
Panchayat/village level itself, thus helping in improving the agricultural productivity. 
As per the data provided by States/ UTs, 38,974 PACS are currently operating as Pradhan Mantri 
Kisan Samriddhi Kendras (PMKSKs) in the country. 

(c) & (d)    The pilot project for PACS training was conducted in the year 2024-25 in 4 districts of 
4 states i.e. Himachal Pradesh (Una), Rajasthan (Jodhpur), Tamil Nadu (Theni) and Odisha 
(Sambalpur) in which 284 PACS were provided training by conducting 295 training programmes in 
which 85 ,219 participants were trained. Apart from the pilot project, the NCCT is conducting 
awareness programmes for PACS every year. Since inception of Ministry of Cooperation, the NCCT 
has conducted a total of 7 ,320 awareness programmes in the country for PACS through its 20 
institutes in which 6 ,00,602 participants were trained from the year 2022 -23 to June, 2026. The 
institute-wise position of number of programmes conducted and number of participants trained is 
given in Annexure.  
(e)    Key learnings from the pilot project on PACS training are as follows- 
• Training interventions have significantly reduced performance gaps and strengthened 
functional capabilities. 
• Participants have acquired new skills, particularly in DPR preparation, and gained a better 
understanding of government schemes.  
• Members are now more aware of their roles, responsibilities, and powers within 
cooperatives.  
• PACS have developed a clear understanding of converging schemes of different ministries 
to strengthen cooperative activities.  
• Members have gained a stronger sense of ownership and participation in cooperative 
institutions.  
•  Several PACS have shown interest in diversifying activities, including Common Service 
Centres, Jan Aushadhi Kendras, LPG agencies, obtaining license for providing high quality 
seeds, pesticides, etc., to farmers.

289. SHRI MAGUNTA SREENIVASULU REDDY: 
  
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE क ृ िष एवं िकसान 
कʞाण मंũी be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has conducted any study/survey regarding implementation 
of Prime Minister-Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana (PM-RKVY) across India, especially in 
Andhra Pradesh; 
(b) if so, the details regarding the status of implementation of its components pertaining 
to agricultural mechanisation, agri-based entrepreneurship and rain-fed areas development 
across Andhra Pradesh, district-wise and in Prakasam District; 
 
(c) the details regarding the total number of beneficiaries (male, female and others) of 
PM-RKVY over the last five years, year-wise, component-wise, district-wise across Andhra 
Pradesh and in Prakasam District; and 
 
(d) Whether the Government has undertaken any steps to raise awareness regarding 
the benefits of PM RKVY amongst farmers, especially the new/upgraded components, if so 
details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण राǛ मंũी (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
 
(a) & (b): Evaluation study of all Centrally Sponsored Schemes, including Pradhan 
Mantri- Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana (PM-RKVY) was conducted by Development 
Monitoring and Evaluation Office (DMEO), Niti Aayog. The Study covered 14 States across 
diverse agro climatic regions and the study was not district specific.  
 
For agricultural mechanization, the study mentioned that mechanization support 
through Customs Hiring Centres (CHCs) and machinery provisioning has shown alignment 
with smallholder needs, but not as standalone interventions. In regions where 
mechanization was integrated with input distribution and demonstration based activities, 
uptake and service utilization improved significantly. Further, it broadly recommended 
combining Custom Hiring Centres, seed delivery and farmer trainings, use of CHCs as 
integrated hubs and institutionalization of local technical facilitation teams to manage CHCs, 
monitor usage and ensure cross component coverage. With regard to Agri-entrepreneurship 
and Innovation, the study mentioned rationalizing it into value chain incubator platforms 
integrating agri processing, youth skilling, FPO support and innovating labs;, developing 

phased enterprise support frameworks that include infrastructure, branding, certification and 
market on-boarding; and suggested facilitating convergence with financial institutions and 
start up missions to ensure working capital access, book keeping support and mentorship. 
Apart from this, the study also recommended livestock development under integrated 
framing systems, bundling it with extension and backyard framing interventions.   
 
(c): The data regarding beneficiaries are maintained by the respective State 
implementing agencies. The State Government of Andhra Pradesh has informed the total 
number of beneficiaries under PM-RKVY over the last five years, component-wise, 
throughout the State and in Prakasam district, as follows:

(d): Yes. The Government of India continuously takes steps to create awareness 
regarding agricultural schemes, including PM-RKVY. These include, dissemination of 
guidelines through the Ministry‘s website to ensure transparency and accessibility for 
stakeholders. Extension services are also implemented through Krishi Vigyan Kendras 
(KVKs), State Agriculture Departments, and field-level extension workers, who educate 
farmers on various components and farmer specific interventions.  
The State Government of Andhra Pradesh has reported the following Scheme-wise 
steps taken to raise awareness regarding the benefits of PM-RKVY amongst farmers: 
i) Sub Mission on Agriculture Mechanization: Extension activities like Polam 
Pilusthondi program to reach out the farmers for creating awareness on all the 
Centrally Sponsored Schemes, especially SMAM. 
 
ii) Soil Health & Fertility: Soil samples are collected through the SHC mobile 
application and Soil Health Cards with crop wise fertilizer recommendations are 
generated in this portal. Awareness on soil health and interpretation of SHC 
results is taken up by ATMA/DRC staff, KVK Scientists and Agriculture extension 
staff. 
 
iii) Statewide "Khet Bachao Abhiyan" campaigns were organised from 1st June to 
30th June, 2026 to create awareness among the farmers about the balanced use 
of fertilisers and other agricultural inputs based on soil testing, to promote natural 
farming, to practice crop rotation, etc. 
 

iv)  Rainfed Area Development: Capacity-building training programmes on 
Integrated Farming System (IFS) activities are organized for the beneficiaries to 
facilitate effective implementation and adoption of the interventions. 
 
v) Per Drop More Crop (PDMC): Training programmes and campaigns for the 
farmers, officers and field functionaries are conducted at regular intervals in the 
farmers’ fields with the support of micro irrigation companies to create awareness 
on micro irrigation and maintenance under PDMC (Per Drop More Crop), apart 
from workshops conducted at district level and state level on automation in micro 
irrigation. 
 
vi) Agroforestry; State Government has done publicity regarding availability of forest 
species saplings (plant material) through Forest Department.

FERTILISER SHORTAGE IN KERALA 
 
292. DR. SHASHI THAROOR: 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण मंũी 
be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government is aware that during the Puncha paddy cultivation season 
(December 2025-Early 2026), farmers in Kuttanad and other parts of Alappuzha and 
Thiruvananthapuram in Kerala faced a severe shortage of fertilizers, particularly urea, 
potash, and phosphate at the critical stage of crop growth, if so, the details thereof; 
(b) whether an allocation of about 43,000 tonnes of urea for the October-December 2025 
quarter, only around 20,000 tonnes was supplied to Kerala, resulting in a substantial 
shortfall, if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether the Government has assessed the impact of this shortage on paddy productivity, 
acreage and farmer incomes in the affected districts, if so, details thereof; and 
(d) the corrective measures taken by the Government since then and the steps being 
implemented to ensure adequate and timely supply of all essential fertilizers to Kerala for 
the ongoing and forthcoming agricultural seasons? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण राǛ मंũी (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
 
 (a) to (d): State Government of Kerala has informed that farmers in Kuttanad and other 
parts of Alappuzha and Thiruvananthapuram Districts in Kerala did not experience any 
shortage of fertilizers particularly urea, potash and phosphate at the critical stage of crop 
growth during Puncha paddy cultivation season (December 2025 to Early 2026) in Kerala.  
As per Integrated Fertilizer Monitoring System (IFMS) report, against the cumulative 
requirement of 39090 MT of urea during October- December 2025 in Kerala, the availability 
(opening stock + supply) of urea was 44680 MT.  State Government of Kerala has further 
informed that since required quantity of Urea and other fertilizers were received during Rabi 
2025 cropping season, paddy productivity, acreage and farmers income were not affected. 
  
          The Government of India in order to ensure the adequate availability of quality fertilizers 
to the farmers, assess the requirement of major fertilizers, namely urea, Di-ammonium 
Phosphate (DAP), Muriate of Potash (MOP), Complexes and Single Super Phosphate (SSP) 
fertilizers, before each cropping season (viz. Rabi and Kharif) in consultations with States. 
Assessment is made based on agronomical requirement, soil health, cropping pattern, 
cropping area, previous sale etc.  Based on assessed requirement of fertilizers, Department 
of Fertilizers, Government of India supplies fertilizers to states by preparing monthly supply 
plan and ensure seamless availability of fertilizers. The movement of all major subsidized 
fertilizers is monitored through IFMS. Regular monitoring is conducted with States including 
Kerala to monitor the supply position and corrective measure is taken as per requirement.

(a)       Under the PM-KISAN Scheme, Government of India has disbursed over ₹ 4.46 
lakh Cr. to the beneficiaries through 23 installments since inception of the Scheme. As 
per the final verified data submitted by the States/UTs before each installment, the 
number of beneficiaries varies from one installment to other. Government of India has 
disbursed ₹18,895.10 Crore to more than 9.44 crore beneficiaries in the 23rd 
installment. The State/UT-wise, instalment-wise details of farmers benefitted under 
PM-KISAN since inception and amount released to them is at Annexure-1 and district-
wise details of the same in Rajasthan is at Annexure-2.  

(b)  The State/UT-wise number of women beneficiaries and amount released to 
them under PM-KISAN during the 23rd instalment and since inception is at Annexure-
3. Further, District-wise details of women farmers benefited under the Scheme in 
Rajasthan in 23rd installment and the amount transferred to women beneficiaries is at 
Annexure-4. 
 
(c) The farmers can register their complaints through CPGRAMS portal and PM 
KISAN portal. Since the inception of the Scheme, as on 14.07.2026, a total of 3,13,751 
grievances have been received on the CPGRAMS portal. The grievances are resolved 
in timely manner. As on 14.07.2026, a total of 3,12,660 have been resolved.  
In addition, on PM-KISAN portal, as on 14.07.2026, a total of 15,27,362 
grievances have been received since the inception of the Scheme. The grievances are 
resolved in timely manner. As on 14.07.2026, a total of 15,21,607 have been resolved. 
 
 
(d) In Dungarpur district, a total of 5,171 grievances have been received on PM-
KISAN portal. The grievances are resolved in timely manner. As on 14.07.2026, a total 
of 5,154 grievance have been resolved.  
 
(e) In order to ensure that the system is used only by authorized personnel and that 
no misuse or unauthorized activities occur, PM-KISAN user module has been 
revamped. Biometric authentication has been integrated into the PM-KISAN login 
process for officials at all levels. A two-layer approval system (Maker–Checker) has 
been introduced for user creation and modification. Further, Government email ID, 
unique Aadhaar, and mobile number have been made mandatory for each user.   
Further, to ensure that the benefits are provided only to the genuine eligible 
beneficiaries, land seeding, Aadhaar-based payment and e-KYC have been made 
mandatory under the scheme. Currently, the PM-KISAN database is also cross-verified 
with the PDS ration card database, UIDAI records (including deactivated Aadhaar due 
to death), and PFMS and Income Tax data for deduplication.
