GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF COMMERCE & INDUSTRY 
DEPARTMENT FOR PROMOTION OF INDUSTRY AND INTERNAL TRADE 
 
LOK SABHA 
 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 295. 
      TO BE ANSWERED ON TUESDAY, THE 21ST JULY, 2026. 
 
FEATURES OF BHAVYA 
 
295.  SHRI JASHUBHAI BHILUBHAI RATHVA: 
SHRI LAVU SRI KRISHNA DEVARAYALU: 
SHRI CAPTAIN BRIJESH CHOWTA: 
SHRI KRISHNA PRASAD TENNETI: 
 
Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY be pleased to state: 
वाणिज्य  एवं उद्योग मंत्री 
(a)  the salient features of the Bharat Audyogik Vikas Yojana  (BHAVYA) for 
developing plugand -play industrial parks across the country and the criteria 
adopted for selection of parks under the first phase; 
 
(b)  the number of proposals received from States/Union Territories so far and the 
priority sectors proposed to be covered, State-wise; 
 
(c)  the support proposed by the Government for infrastructure, technology 
adoption and common facilities within these parks; and 
 
(d)  the mechanism proposed for integrating Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises 
(MSMEs) operating in these parks into global value chains? 
 
ANSWER 
 
वाणिज्य  एवं उद्योग मंत्रालय में राज्य मंत्री (श्री णिणिन प्रसाद)   
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE & INDUSTRY 
(SHRI JITIN PRASADA) 
 
(a) to (d): Bharat Audyogik Vikas Yojana (BHAVYA) is a Central Sector Scheme notified 
on 10.04.2026 for development of investment -ready industrial parks to enable 
investors to ground investment with ease, thereby adding to the manufacturing 
capacity in the country. 
The total financial outlay for the Scheme is ₹ 33,660 crore and the duration of 
the Scheme is for a period of 6 years. 
Under the Scheme, financial assistance is to be provided for development of 
100 industrial parks. In the first phase, 50 projects are to be taken up, with one 
or more rounds of selection. 
The  mandatory  eligibility  criteria  include  minimum  contiguous  land  
area requirement of 100 acres in non -hilly States and 25 acres in hilly States, 
North Eastern Region, Union Territories and States having population below 

one crore as well as availability of 90 percent encumbrance -free land at the 
time of submission of application. 
The selection of projects is based on Challenge mode with evaluation on 
parameters such as connectivity and site suitability, quality of DPR, the demand 
for industrial land, provision of services at site, policy enablers for ensuring 
investments in the developed park, being provided by the State/UT 
Governments. 
Applications meeting the mandatory eligibility criteria would be taken up for 
evaluation and scoring in accordance with the prescribed evaluation criteria as 
prescribed under the Scheme guidelines issued on 23.05.2026. 
The scheme does not propose to develop parks in any specific sector, however, 
weightage is allowed for proposals with sector-specific thrust and infrastructure 
requirements. No proposal has been received on the portal till date. 
Financial assistance upto Rs. 1 crore per acre is provided for eligible 
components listed in the scheme guidelines. This contribution is in the form of 
equity from the Centre, with land contributed by the State/UT Government. 
The Scheme design is flexible for creation of sector specific infrastructure,  
including for encouragement of MSMEs, wherever Stat e/UT Government 
proposes for such infrastructure provision, as part of its Detailed Project Report. 
Guidelines are available on www.dpiit.gov.in .

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF COMMERCE & INDUSTRY 
DEPARTMENT FOR PROMOTION OF INDUSTRY AND INTERNAL TRADE 
 
LOK SABHA 
 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 296. 
      TO BE ANSWERED ON TUESDAY, THE 21ST JULY, 2026. 
 
ENFORCEMENT OF FDI NORMS 
 
296.  SHRI B K PARTHASARATHI: 
SHRI DAGGUMALLA PRASADA RAO: 
 
Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY be pleased to state: 
वाणिज्य  एवं उद्योग मंत्री 
(a)  the measures taken by the Government to monitor and enforce compliance with 
local sourcing requirements prescribed under the Foreign Direct Investment 
(FDI) Policy for Single  Brand Retail Trade (SBRT) and Multi Brand Retail 
Trading (MBRT); 
 
(b)  the details and the number of FDI-supported retail entities that have undertaken 
procurement from local businesses during the  last five years, year and State -
wise; 
 
(c)  the details regarding the monetary value of procurement undertaken from local 
businesses by such FDI-supported entities, State and year-wise; 
 
(d)  whether the Government maintains data regarding the number of l ocal 
businesses benefitted through such sourcing requirements, if so, the details 
thereof, State-wise; 
 
(e)  whether the Government has evaluated the effectiveness of these sourcing 
norms in  strengthening domestic value chains, generating employment and 
increasing participation of local  enterprises, if so, the details along with the 
findings thereof; and 
 
(f)  the steps taken or proposed to be taken by the Government to further 
strengthen market access and procurement opportunities for local businesses 
within the FDI framework? 
 
ANSWER 
 
वाणिज्य  एवं उद्योग मंत्रालय में राज्य मंत्री (श्री णिणिन प्रसाद)   
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE & INDUSTRY 
(SHRI JITIN PRASADA) 
 
(a): As per the FDI Policy, 100% FDI is allowed under the automatic route in Single 
Brand Retail Trading (SBRT) while 51% FDI is allowed under the Government 
route in Multi Brand Retail Trading (MBRT), subject to the stipulated conditions. 
In order to safeguard  and promote local business interests, the FDI Policy on 

SBRT mandates that in case of foreign investment beyond 51%, 30% of the 
value of goods purchased should be sourced from India, preferably from 
MSMEs, village and cottage industries, artisans and craf tsmen, in all sectors. 
Similarly, the FDI Policy on MBRT mandates that at least 30% of the value of 
procurement of manufactured/processed products purchased shall be sourced 
from Indian MSMEs, which have a total investment in plant & machinery not 
exceeding US $ 2.00 million. The sourcing from agricultural co-operatives and 
farmers co-operatives would also be considered in this category. 
As per the FDI Policy, the quantum of domestic sourcing will be self-certified by 
the company, to be subsequently checked  by statutory auditors from the duly 
certified accounts, which the company is required to maintain. Furthermore, the 
onus of compliance with the provisions of the FDI Policy is on the investee 
company. 
The reporting requirements in respect of investments in India under the Foreign 
Exchange Management (Non-Debt Instruments) Rules, 2019 are prescribed by 
the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) under the Foreign Exchange Management 
(Mode of Payment and Reporting of Non-Debt Instruments) Regulations, 2019. 
Further, FDI is a capital account transaction and any violation of FDI regulations 
is covered by the penal provisions of the Foreign Exchange Management Act 
(FEMA). The RBI administers the FEMA, and the Directorate of Enforcement 
under the Ministry of Finance is the authority for the enforcement of FEMA. The 
Directorate takes up an investigation into any contravention of FEMA. 
(b) to (e): Data on FDI-supported entities, as sought, is not available centrally. However, 
state-wise FDI equity inflow reported in Retail Trad ing, including SBRT and  
MBRT sectors, during April 2021 to March 2026 is given at the Annexure. 
(f): The FDI Policy in Retail Trading, including Single Brand and Multi Brand, is 
aimed at attracting investments in production and marketing, improving the 
availability of such goods for the consumer, encouraging increased sourcing of 
goods from India, and enhancing the competitiveness of Indian enterprises 
through access to global designs, technologies and management practices. In 
addition to the local sourc ing norms, for entities undertaking MBRT, at least 
50% of total FDI brought in the first tranche of US $ 100 million is mandated to 
be invested in 'back -end infrastructure' within three years, where ‘back -end 
infrastructure’ includes distribution, design i mprovement, quality control, 
packaging, logistics, storage, warehouse, agriculture market produce 
infrastructure etc. Subsequent investment in back -end infrastructure would be 
made by the MBRT retailer as needed, depending upon its business 
requirements. Additionally, the Government reviews FDI policy on an ongoing 
basis and makes changes from time to time in consultations with the concerned 
stakeholders.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA  
MINISTRY OF COOPERATION  
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 297 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 21st July, 2026 
 
PACS Modernization and Rural Credit 
 
297. Dr. Prabha Mallikarjun: 
Will the Minister of COOPERATION (सहकारिता मंत्री) be pleased to state: 
(a) the details of the progress made in modernization and computerization of Primary  
Agricultural Credit Societies across the country (PACS); 
(b) the details of PACS integrated with digital platforms, State-wise; 
(c) whether the Government has assessed the impact of PACS modernization on rural credit 
delivery, if so, the details thereof; 
(d) the measures being taken to improve access to affordable credit through cooperatives; and 
(e) the details of PACS modernization projects implemented in Davanagere district along with 
their present status? 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF COOPERATION 
सहकारिता मंत्री (SHRI AMIT SHAH) 
 
(a) The details of progress made in modernization and computerization of Primary 
Agricultural Credit Societies across the country(PACS) is at Annexure-‘A’. 
 
(b) The Ministry has take n steps to integrate the PACS ERP system with other State 
platforms to streamline agricultural credit and service delivery. These are as under: - 
 
i. Andhra Pradesh  – e-Governance Services, Paddy Procurement, LPG, 
MARKFED, IGRS Registration & Stamp Portal of GoAP, Public Distribution 
System (PDS), e-Crop, CCLA (Chief Commissioner of Land Administration) 
ii. Bihar:   Aadhaar enabled Public Distribution System -AePDS, e-sahkari 
iii. Chhattisgarh: Ekikrit Kisan Portal, Committee Registration Module, Khadya 
portal, MARKFED, Bhuiyan Citizen Ui, Food, Civil Supplies and Consumer 
Protection Department 
iv. Gujarat: Gujarat cooperative Portal, Any ROR( Any Record of Rights) Gujarat 
portal, 
v. Madhya Pradesh: mp bhulekh, Samagra Samajik Suraksha Mission, 
vi. Rajasthan: e-Dharti, Hosting of ERP PACS software in RSDC, SSO, ePDS, 
Jan Soochna Portal, RajSahakar Portal 
vii. Uttar Pradesh: UP Bhulekh Portal 
viii. Tamil Nadu: CAMS (Comprehensive Audit Management System) 

Alongwith the above integrations, PACS ERP system also includes integration with 
Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samriddhi Kendras (PMKSK), Common Service Centres (CSCs), 
Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Kendras (PMBJK), Kisan Rin Portal etc.

(d) Government has taken several measures to improve access to affordable credit through 
cooperatives, inter alia: 
(i) Computerization of PACS Project through common ERP-based software. 
(ii) Diversification of PACS into more than 25 economic activities through Model 
Bye-laws. 
(iii) Strengthening of PACS through convergence with various Government schemes 
like PACS working as Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samriddhi Kendra(PMKSK), Common 
Service Centre(CSC), Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Kendra(PMBJK) etc 
(iv) Integration of PACS with Kisan Rin Portal and other digital platforms. 
(v) Capacity building and training of PACS officials. 
(vi) Financial support for modernization of cooperative institutions through various 
schemes of Government of India and NABARD. 
(vii) Continuous monitoring and review of implementation with States/UTs for 
timely completion of the project. 
 
(e)   In Davangere district of Karnataka State, under Central Government initiatives, the 
modernization projects taken up by PACS and their current status is as under:-  
1. PACS Computerization:-  Out of 185 PACS in Davangere district, 176 sanctioned PACS

out of which 76 PACS are active and services such as LIC premium payment, electricity bill 
payment, crop insurance, life and vehicle insurance premium payment facility, RTC (Right and 
Tenancy Certificate), and o ther land record documents are being provided to the rural 
population.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF COOPERATION 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 298  
TO BE ANSWERED ON 21st JULY .2026 
 
Benefits of Yuva Sahakar and Swayam Shakti scheme 
298.  Shri Jai Prakash: 
Will the Minister of COOPERATION (सहकारिता मंत्री) be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government is aware of the fact that the benefits of the "Yuva Sahakar scheme 
and 'Swayam Shakti Sahakar  scheme are not reaching to all eligible youth and women's 
cooperative societies in the Hisar Lok Sabha constituency in Haryana; 
 
(b) if so, the major shortcomings and challenges noticed in the implementation of these schemes 
along with reasons therefor; 
 
(c) the number of cooperative societies, youth and women's groups that have been provided 
financial assistance or other benefits under these schemes in Hisar Lok Sabha constituency so far; 
 
(d) whether the government has formulated any special action plan to address these shortcomings, 
enhance awareness, simplify credit availability, and ensure the effective implementation of these 
schemes; and 
 
(e) if so, the details thereof along with the expected timeline for the implementation of the same ? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF COOPERATION 
(सहकारिता मंत्री) (SHRI AMIT SHAH) 
 
(a) to (c) National Cooperative Development Corporation (NCDC), a statutory organization 
under the Ministry of Cooperation, is implementing Yuva Sahakar and Swayam Shakti Shakar 
Scheme. Both the schemes are fully funded and supported by NCDC.  
Yuva Sahakar Scheme is being implemented with the aim to encourage newly formed cooperative 
societies with new and/or innovative ideas.  

The objective of Swayamshakti Sahakar Scheme is to facilitate access to affordable, cost-effective 
and reliable financial services to the poor including women Self Help Groups (SHGs) to undertake 
the common/collective socio-economic activities in order to promote sustainable livelihood.  
 
NCDC extends funding on a project basis. Under the Yuva Sahakar and Swayam Shakti Sahakar 
schemes, no cooperative from the Hisar Lok Sabha constituency in Haryana has submitted any 
proposal to NCDC. 
 
(d) & (e) NCDC through its 19 Regional Offices and 9 sub offices actively monitors the 
implementation of schemes and ensures access to timely credit flow to women cooperatives. Field 
visits/inspections are done periodically for proper monitoring of loan disbursement under the 
schemes.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO.299 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 21st July, 2026 
 
 Support for Women Farmers  
 
299. SMT. POONAMBEN HEMATBHAI MAADAM: 
  
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE कृ ͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण 
मंğी be pleased to state: 
 
a. the details of the estimated percentage of women engaged in agricultural activities 
across the country; 
b. whether specific schemes exist to support women farmers to access credit, inputs, 
training and market linkages; 
c. if so, the details thereof; 
d. whether training and capacity-building programmes have been implemented to 
enhance the technical and entrepreneurial skills of women engaged in agriculture; 
and 
e. if so, details thereof? 
ANSWER 
  
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
कृ ͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण राÏय मंğी                                                (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
 
(a)  As per the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) conducted by the National Statistics 
Office (NSO), Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI), females 
constituted 59.8 percent of the total workforce engaged in the agricultural activities during 
2025 (January-December) across the country. 
 
(b) to (e) The Government is implementing a number of schemes to support farmers to 
access credit, inputs, training and marketing linkages. The benefits under the scheme 
can be availed by women farmers.  
 
 Under Modified Interest Subvention Scheme (MISS) concessional interest rates on 
short-term agricultural loans are provided to farmers through Kisan Credit Cards (KCC). 
Farmers (including women farmers) can avail Kisan Credit Card (KCC) loans at a 
subsidized interest rate of 7% for their working capital requirement. Additionally, farmers 
who repay their loans promptly receive a 3% Prompt Repayment Incentive (PRI), 
effectively reducing the interest rate to 4% per annum. Number of female account holders 
who have benefited from Agricultural credit subsidy under the Kisan Credit Card linked 
Modified Interest Subvention Scheme (MISS) for meeting working capital requirements 
are around 22% of 5.4 crores beneficiaries in financial year 2024-25. 
 
 
 

Under Integrated Scheme for Agricultural Marketing (ISAM), subsidy is provided 
for storage infrastructure, and marketing infrastructure other than storage, to the eligible 
beneficiaries including individuals, Group of farmers/growers, Self Help Group (SHG), 
Cooperative Marketing Federation etc. In order to promote women farmers and 
entrepreneurs including women Self Help Groups (SHGs), assistance in the form of 
subsidy is provided to all the women beneficiaries at a higher rate i.e. @33.33% instead 
of 25%.  
 
Under the formation and promotion of 10,000 Farmers Producer Organization 
(FPOs) scheme, special provisions have been made to empower women by providing 
special focus to include women farmers/women Self Help Groups (SHGs) as members 
to make FPOs more effective and inclusive. Out of these, 914 FPOs are 100 percent 
women share holders FPOs.  
 
Under Sub Mission on Agricultural Mechanization (SMAM) scheme, in order to 
make farm machinery more accessible and affordable to farmers, financial assistance @ 
40-50% of the cost of machinery depending on the category of farmers is provided for 
purchase of agricultural machines. For women farmers the financial assistance is @ 50% 
of the cost of machinery. The Farm Machinery Training and Testing Institutes (FMTTIs) 
imparts training to women farmers/ Technicians/ Engineers/ Unemployed youths/ 
Machinery manufacturers, etc. on latest technology of farm mechanization. 
 
Agriculture Technology Management Agency (ATMA) Scheme supports State 
Government's efforts and introduces latest agricultural technologies and good agricultural 
practices in different thematic areas of agriculture and allied sectors to farmers including 
women farmers through different extension activities viz; farmers training, 
demonstrations, exposure visits, kisan mela, mobilization of famers groups and 
organizing Farm Schools. As per ATMA Guidelines, minimum 30% of resources meant 
for programs and activities are required to be allocated to women farmers and women 
extension functionaries. 
 
The PM-KISAN provides ₹6,000 per year to all eligible farmers through direct 
benefit transfer without gender discrimination, and has significantly benefited women 
farmers as   ensuring transparent and direct financial support to strengthen their income 
and participation in agriculture. A total of 2,18,66,774 women beneficiaries received 
benefits under the 23rd instalment of PM-KISAN Scheme.  
 
The Government is implementing Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVKs) scheme to 
promote adoption of new technologies of agriculture and allied sectors through 
technology assessment, demonstration and capacity development among the extension 
functionaries of state governments and farmers including women farmers.  
 
Indian Council of Agricultural Research-Central Institute for Women in Agriculture 
(ICAR-CIWA), Bhubaneswar provides latest technologies to increase status of livelihood 
of women farmers. It organises various extension activities like field days, exhibitions, 
exposure visits, demonstration, transfer of technologies through mass media etc. to 
acquaint the women farmers with latest technologies. 
 
 
  
 

Mahila Kisan Sashaktikaran Pariyojana (MKSP) is implemented by the Ministry of 
Rural Development as a sub-scheme of Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana-National Rural 
Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM). The objective of the sub-scheme is to empower 
women Self Help Group (SHG) members as Mahila Kisan and train them on adoption of 
agro ecological practices, enhanced livestock practices and scientific 
cultivation/collection of Non-Timber Forest Products (NTFPs). To provide market access, 
the Mahila Kisans are supported to mobilized into Producer Collectives. The SHG 
members are facilitated to get credit access through the capitalization support given to 
Cluster Level Federation (CLF) and SHG credit linkage program.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING  
DEPARTMENT OF ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING  
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION No. 301 
 ANSWERED ON 21st JULY, 2026 
 
NATIONAL DIGITAL LIVESTOCK MISSION 
 
301.  SMT. BHARTI PARDHI: 
SHRI NARESH GANPAT MHASKE: 
DR. SHRIKANT EKNATH SHINDE: 
SHRI SHRIRANG APPA CHANDU BARNE: 
SHRI RAVINDRA DATTARAM WAIKAR:  
Will the Minister of FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
मत्स्यपालन, पशुपालन और डेयरी मंत्री 
be pleased to state: 
 
(a) Whether the Government has operationalised the integrated National Digital Livestock 
Mission digital infrastructure across all states to enforce centralized health mapping and digital 
tracking for dairy herds, if so, the details thereof; 
 (b) the details of the advanced data encryption standards and blockchain -backed protocols 
deployed to protect livestock identity data from unauthorized database manipulation; 
(c)  the structural checks established within the unified portal to ensure seamless, real-time data 
synchronization across remote block-level mobile veterinary units; 
(d)  the criteria used to grant Application Programming Interfaces  (API) integration rights to 
scheduled commercial banks to automate collateral-free working capital loans for smallholder 
farmers; 
(e) the measures taken by the Gov ernment to host localized outbreak prediction models 
directly on the interface to assist field veterinary officers in active monitoring; and  
(f) the projected reduction in processing timelines for formal micro -credit applications 
following the nationwide deployment of this infrastructure? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
(SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH ALIAS LALAN SINGH) 
 
(a) The Government has operationalized the Integrated National Digital Livestock Mission 
(NDLM) digital infrastructure across all States and Union Territories (UTs). Under this system, 

every registered animal is assigned a unique 12 -digit Tag ID, which serves as a permanent 
identifier for recording and tracking all animal -related activities, including vaccination, 
artificial insemination, deworming, treatment, and other veterinary interventions. The Tag ID, 
along with the complete history of activities undertaken on the animal, is maintained in the 
NDLM database and is accessible to authorized stakeholders for reference, monitoring, 
planning, and service delivery. 
(b) To protect livestock identity data AES-256 (Advanced Encryption Standard, 256-bit key) 
is used for ‘data at rest’  and ‘data in transit’ is secured using Transport Layer Security  (TLS) 
with RSA 2048 -bit certificates. This ensures end -to-end encryption using industry -standard, 
government-grade security. 
 
(c) Currently, Mobile Veterinary Units (MVUs) are not integrated with NDLM - Bharat 
Pashudhan Portal. 
 
(d) Department has received no request from any bank for Application Programme Interface 
(API) integration till date. 
 
(e) The National Animal Disease Referral Expert System (NADRES_v2) of Indian Council 
of Agricultural Research  - National Institute of Veterinary Epidemiology and Disease 
Informatics (ICAR-NIVEDI) can be accessed on the designated portal from anywhere anytime 
for advance preparedness and response. However, this module has not been integrated with 
NDLM – Bharat Pashudhan Portal. 
 
(f) As of now, there is no micro-credit provision under any scheme of this Department.

RURAL CREDIT AND DEVELOPMENT SCHEMES 
 
302. Shri Pushpendra Saroj: 
 
Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  whether the Union Government has assessed the impact of 
tightening banking liquidity conditions on the flow of 
institutional credit to rural development programmes and self-
help groups, if so, the details thereof, particularly for Uttar 
Pradesh; 
(b)  the extent to which banks implementing rural development 
schemes have increased reliance on short-term market 
borrowings, such as Certificates of Deposit, State and district-
wise specifically for Uttar Pradesh; 
(c)  whether any review has been conducted regarding delays in 
credit-linked rural livelihood and infrastructure projects due to 
tightening liquidity conditions, if so, the details thereof; 
(d)  the number of instances where financing support to rural 
development programmes faced delays due to banking sector 
liquidity pressures, State and district-wise specifically for Uttar 
Pradesh; and 
(e)  the corrective steps proposed by the Union Government to 
ensure uninterrupted credit flow for rural development 
initiatives despite emerging stress in banking liquidity? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
(DR. CHANDRA SEKHAR PEMMASANI) 
  
(a): The Ministry facilitates access to institutional credit for women 
Self Help Groups (SHGs) under its flagship programme, Deendayal 
Antyodaya Yojana – National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM). 
Under the programme, women SHGs are supported to avail collateral-
free loans from Scheduled Commercial Banks and Cooperative Banks 
in accordance with guidelines of the Reserve Bank of India and the 

Page 2 of 3 
 
National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD). The 
details of the institutional credit accessed by women SHGs in the 
country and in the State of Uttar Pradesh are as under:- 
  
(Amount  in Rs. Cr.) 
Sr. No. Year All India  Uttar Pradesh  
1 2024-25 2,00,937.94 2,931.16 
2 2025-26 2,27,389.95 3,301.13 
  
As reported by State Level Bankers’ Committee, Uttar Pradesh (SLBC, 
UP), no adverse impact of banking liquidity conditions on the flow of 
institutional credit to rural development programmes or Self-Help 
Groups has been reported in the State of Uttar Pradesh.  
(b): Liquidity management, including reliance on short-term market 
borrowings such as Certificates of Deposit, is an internal treasury 
function of individual banks and is managed at their respective Head 
Office level.  
(c): The progress of credit linkage under Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana 
– National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM) is reviewed 
periodically at various levels in coordination with Banks and State 
Governments. These review meetings are conducted to monitor the 
progress of institutional credit to women Self Help Groups, identify 
and address bottlenecks causing delays in credit linkage, and 
facilitate timely sanction and disbursement of loans. Further, for 
continuous monitoring, SHG-bank linkage portal is used.    
(d): No such instances have been reported to this Ministry.  
(e): To ensure uninterrupted and timely flow of institutional credit to 
women Self Help Groups under Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana – 
National Rural Livelihoods Mission, the Government has put in place 
the following measures: 
i. The Ministry engages with financial regulators to facilitate the 
issuance of guidelines for SHG credit linkage. The Reserve Bank 
of India issues an annual Master Circular on Financing of 
Women Self Help Groups for Scheduled Commercial Banks, 
Private Sector Banks and Small Finance Banks. The Master 
Circular prescribes the operational framework for SHG 
financing, including eligibility criteria, loan quantum, lending 
norms and other procedural requirements. Similarly, NABARD 
issues circular for Regional Rural Banks and Cooperative Banks 

Page 3 of 3 
 
to ensure uniform implementation of the SHG-Bank Linkage 
Programme. 
ii. Bank-wise and State-wise annual credit targets are fixed by the 
Ministry in consultation with banks, based on the credit 
potential, performance and the scope for credit expansion. 
Based on the target, States prepare district, block, and branch 
wise targets. 
iii. A Central Level Coordination Committee (CLCC) meeting, 
chaired by the Secretary, Department of Rural Development, is 
convened annually with senior representatives of RBI, NABARD, 
the Department of Financial Services, Indian Banks' Association 
(IBA), Banks, and State Government to review the progress of 
SHG credit linkage, and to address bottlenecks and facilitate 
timely credit flow. 
iv. Periodic consultation and review meetings are held at various 
levels with Public Sector Banks, Private Sector Banks, Regional 
Rural Banks, Cooperative Banks and SRLMs to monitor credit 
disbursement, resolve operational issues and improve credit 
delivery. 
v. Regular training, orientation and sensitisation programmes are 
conducted for bankers/functionaries to enhance their capacity 
and promote timely sanction and disbursement of credit to 
eligible women SHGs.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 308 
 
TO BE ANSWERED ON THE 21ST JULY, 2026/ ASHADHA 30, 1948 (SAKA) 
 
MECHANISM TO TRACK FIR REGISTRATION 
 
308.      SHRI MADDILA GURUMOORTHY: 
 
Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the number of Andhra Pradesh police officers who received dedicated 
training from the Bureau of Police Research and Development on sensitive 
handling of SC/ST atrocity cases,  including FIR registration, victim 
protection, and witness support, during 2024-25 and 2025-26; 
 
(b) whether the Government maintains a real-time monitoring mechanism to 
track FIR registration, charge-sheeting, and trial progress in SC/ST atrocity 
cases State-wise, including Andhra Pradesh's during the said period; and 
 
(c) whether the Central Government proposes to deploy Special Central 
Monitoring Teams or issue specific advisories to Andhra Pradesh given the 
persistent concerns regarding trial pendency and low conviction rates under 
the SC/ST Prevention of Atrocities Act and if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
(SHRI BANDI SANJAY KUMAR) 
 
(a) to (c): Police’ and ‘Public Order’ are ‘State’ subjects under the Seventh Schedule 
of the Constitution of India. State Governments/ UT Administrations are primarily 
responsible for the prevention, detection, investigation and prosecution of crimes 
through their Law Enforcement Agencies (LEAs).  
 
 
 

 
-2- 
L.S.US.Q.NO. 308 FOR 21.07.2026  
Bureau of Police Research & Development (BPR&D) conducted a total of 118 
training courses on various topics in which 1120 police personnel of Andhra Pradesh 
were trained during the years 2024-25 to 2026-27. 
 
The Ministry of Home Affairs has taken a number of steps on issues relating 
to FIR registration, victim protection, witn ess support, charge -sheeting and trial. 
Steps taken are briefly mentioned as under:- 
(i) The Crime and Criminal Tracking Network and Systems (CCTNS) application is 
used by State/UTs police to track FIR registration, chargesheeting and trial 
progress of cas es including SC/ST atrocity cases. This system is implemented in 
Andhra Pradesh also. Digital platforms under CCTNS and State Police systems 
facilitate monitoring and tracking of FIR registration, charge -sheeting and trial 
progress of cases by the respective states including Andhra Pradesh.  
(ii) Under Section 173 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023 e-FIR 
and Zero FIR provisions enable timely and accessible registration of cases.  
 (iii)  The Ministry of Home Affairs issue advisories to State s/UTs, from time to 
time, for effective implementation of the provisions of the SC/ST (Prevention of 
Atrocities) Act  and the Rules framed thereunder, including expeditious 
investigation and prosecution of cases, establishment and functioning of Exclusive 
Special Courts/Special Courts for trial of SC/ST Cases, appointment of Special 
Public Prosecutors, and timely relief and rehabilitation of victims from SCs/STs. 
State Governments /UT Administrations are also advised to hold regular meetings 
of the State  and  District  Level  Vigilance  and Monitoring  Committees  to  review 

 
-3- 
L.S.US.Q.NO. 308 FOR 21.07.2026  
implementation of the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act,  and address issues 
relating to pendency of investigation and trial. All these advisories are available in 
MHA website www.mha.gov.in

309.  Dr. Kalanidhi Veeraswamy: 
 
Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  the total budget allocation, funds sanctioned, and expenditure 
incurred under the Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana – National Rural 
Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM), State-wise including Tamil 
Nadu; 
(b)  the total number of Self-Help Groups (SHGs) formed and the 
number of rural households benefitted under the Mission; 
(c)  whether the Government has assessed the impact of the 
Mission on women’s empowerment, income generation, and 
poverty alleviation, if so, the details thereof; 
(d)  the measures taken by the Government to ensure timely fund 
release, capacity building, and technical support for SHGs and 
community institutions; 
(e)  whether there are challenges in implementation, such as lack of 
awareness, administrative delays, or inadequate training, if so, 
the details thereof; and 
(f)  the steps taken to strengthen market linkages, sustainable 
livelihoods and skill development for rural communities under 
DAY-NRLM? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
(DR. CHANDRA SEKHAR PEMMASANI) 
(a):  The total budget allocation, funds sanctioned, and expenditure 
incurred under the Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana – National Rural 
Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM), State-wise including Tamil Nadu 
during FY 2026-27 are given at Annexure-I. 
 
(b):  Under Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana – National Rural Livelihoods 
Mission (DAY-NRLM), 10.05 crore rural households have been 
organised into 92 lakh SHGs in the country.  

Page 2 of 5 
 
(c):  Under the Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana–National Rural 
Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM), the Ministry of Rural Development 
has adopted a multipronged strategy for the social, economic, and 
institutional empowerment of rural women. The positive outcomes of 
these interventions have been validated through independent impact 
evaluation studies commissioned by the Ministry. The 3ie Impact 
Evaluation Study (2025), based on two rounds of data collection 
conducted in 2019 and 2024 across 9 States, covering about 23,000 
households, found that household incomes increased by 9.5% in 
NRLM blocks, while income gains in mature community institution 
clusters ranged from 12% to 33%. The study also reported an 
increase of 6–11% in per capita household consumption, along with 
improvements in women’s empowerment, livelihood diversification, 
and overall household welfare.  
 
Further, NITI Aayog’s Evaluation of Centrally Sponsored 
Schemes in the Rural Development Sector (2025) assessed DAY-
NRLM as a highly relevant and impactful programme, noting its 
contribution to increased incomes, diversified livelihood 
opportunities, enhanced financial inclusion and literacy, greater self-
confidence among women, and improved social inclusion through 
strong community institutions and convergence with other 
development initiatives. These findings underscore the significant 
role of DAY-NRLM in advancing women’s empowerment and 
improving the socio-economic well-being of rural households.  
 
(d):  The Ministry has put in place a robust mechanism to ensure 
timely fund release, capacity building, and technical support for SHGs 
and community institutions under DAY-NRLM. Funds are released to 
States/UTs in a timely manner based on approved allocations and 
utilization requirements. To strengthen financial management, 
expenditure monitoring, and transparency, the Ministry has 
developed the e-Financial Management and Accounting System (e-
FMAS/GramNidhi), which is integrated with LokOS and the Public 
Financial Management System (PFMS) for real-time tracking and 
efficient fund flow. 
 
Capacity building is a core strategy of DAY-NRLM aimed at 
strengthening the knowledge, skills, leadership, and institutional 
capacities of SHGs, their federations, community cadres, and mission 
staff.  Experienced SHG members are nurtured as Community 
Resource Persons (CRPs) and para-professionals to provide local 
mentoring and technical guidance, while 619 Community Managed 
Training Centres (CMTCs) function as decentralized training hubs at 
the block level. Capacity-building interventions cover institution 

Page 3 of 5 
 
building, financial management, livelihoods, governance, social 
inclusion, digital literacy, and entrepreneurship. The Mission also 
leverages digital platforms such as LokOS for data-driven monitoring, 
performance tracking, and informed decision-making, thereby 
strengthening the effectiveness and sustainability of SHGs and 
community institutions. 
  
(e): The implementation of DAY-NRLM is carried out through a well-
defined institutional architecture supported by regular capacity-
building, continuous handholding, robust monitoring mechanisms, 
and digital platforms for fund flow and programme management. The 
Mission places significant emphasis on awareness generation, 
training of SHG members and community cadres, and strengthening 
of community institutions through Community Resource Persons 
(CRPs), Community Managed Training Centres (CMTCs), and 
dedicated support structures at the National, State, District, and 
Block levels. To ensure smooth implementation, the Ministry 
continuously reviews programme progress with States/UTs, provides 
technical guidance and capacity-building support, and leverages 
digital platforms such as LokOS for effective monitoring and 
transparency.  
  
(f): The Ministry of Rural Development has undertaken several 
initiatives to strengthen the branding and marketing ecosystem for 
products made by Self-Help Group (SHG) members, including 
promotion of the Saras, Saras Aajeevika and Aajeevika brands and 
development of State-level brands. Every year, the Ministry organizes 
two National-level Saras Melas, one Saras Food Festival, and more 
than 50 State-level Saras Melas and Food Festivals, providing SHG 
members with opportunities to showcase and sell their products in 
urban markets. The Ministry also operates the Saras Aajeevika 
Gallery in New Delhi and has established the eSaras e-commerce 
platform, besides partnering with GeM, ONDC, Amazon, Flipkart, 
Meesho and JioMart to enhance market access and sales 
opportunities for SHG products. 
  
   Further, to strengthen sustainable livelihoods under DAY-NRLM, 
regular training and capacity-building programmes are conducted for 
SHG members and community cadres on financial literacy, livelihood 
promotion and enterprise development. In the farm sector, women 
are supported through agro-ecological farming, livestock-based 
livelihoods, Integrated Farming Clusters and dedicated Community 
Resource Persons such as Krishi Sakhi, Pashu Sakhi, Van Sakhi and 
Matshya Sakhi and in Non farm sector Start-up Village 

Page 4 of 5 
 
Entrepreneurship Programme (SVEP) supports rural non-farm 
enterprises.  
  
Under Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana - National Rural Livelihoods 
Mission (DAY-NRLM), this Ministry implements Deen Dayal 
Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana (DDU-GKY) and Rural Self 
Employment Training Institutes (RSETI) programmes for skill 
development of rural poor youth through their employment to 
eradicate poverty in the country.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 310 
TO BE ANSWERED ON THE 21st   July, 2026 
 
EVALUATION OF VOLUNTARY PREMIUM-PAYING MODEL UNDER PMFBY 
310. SHRI Y.S. AVINASH REDDY: 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण 
मंũी be pleased to state:  
(a) whether the Government has evaluated if Andhra Pradesh's transition to a voluntary, 
premium-paying Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) model from Rabi 2024-
25 has caused a sharp drop in farmer enrolment, increasing climate vulnerability and 
farm-sector suicides; 
(b) whether the State Government is required to update the Pradhan Mantri Kisan 
Samman Nidhi (PM-PM KISAN) beneficiary database, and if so, the total number of 
eligible beneficiaries in Andhra Pradesh as of May 2026; and 
(c) the market intervention mechanisms being deployed to prevent price crashes that 
trigger suicides among farmers in Andhra Pradesh? 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE  
 
क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण राǛ मंũी  (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
 
(a) :    Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) being implemented since 2016 is 
demand driven and voluntary for States/UTs as well as farmers. After implementing the 
scheme initially from Kharif 2016, Andhra Pradesh Government did not implement the 
scheme from Kharif 2020 till Rabi 2021-22.  Andhra Pradesh re-joined the scheme from 
Kharif 2022 season as a free crop insurance scheme, wherein farmers share of premium 
was also borne by the State Government.  However, after implementing the free crop 
insurance scheme till Kharif 2024, State Government decided to transit to voluntary model 
from Rabi 2024-25 wherein farmer has to enrol in the scheme by paying his/ her share of 
premium.  The participation of farmers under the scheme has decreased in Andhra Pradesh 
as compared to the original implementation by the State.   
 Further, the State Government has informed that no study has been brought to the 
notice of the Government establishing any relationship between the decline in enrollment 
and climate vulnerability or farmer suicides. 
 
(b): As per the PM-KISAN scheme guidelines, farmers who acquired land as of 01.02.2019 
(except for succession due to death) are eligible to get the scheme benefit.  The total number 
of beneficiaries in the Andhra Pradesh State under the scheme as of May, 2026 is 41.26 
lakhs. 
 

(c):  Government fixes Minimum Support Prices (MSPs) for 22 mandated agriculture crops 
on the basis of the recommendations of the Commission for Agricultural Costs & Prices 
(CACP), after considering the views of concerned State Governments and Central 
Ministries/Departments. While recommending MSPs, CACP considers important factors like 
cost of production, overall demand-supply conditions; domestic and international prices, 
inter-crop price parity, terms of trade between agricultural and non-agricultural sectors, the 
likely effect on the rest of the economy, besides ensuring rational utilization of land, water 
and other production resources and a minimum of 50 percent as the margin over cost of 
production. 
 The Union Budget for 2018-19 had announced the pre-determined principle to keep 
MSPs at levels of one and half times of the cost of production.  Accordingly, Government 
had increased MSP for all mandated Kharif, Rabi and other Commercial crops with a 
minimum return of 50 percent over all India weighted average cost of production from year 
2018-19 onwards. 
To realize the objective of MSP policy, Government procures cereals and coarse 
cereals through Food Corporation of India (FCI) and other designated state agencies to 
provide price support to farmers. Cotton and Jute are procured by Govt. at MSP through 
Cotton Corporation of India (CCI) and Jute Corporation of India (JCI), respectively.  
Further, Market Intervention Scheme (MIS) under the integrated Scheme of Pradhan 
Mantri Annadata Aay Sanrakshan Abhiyan (PM-AASHA) for the procurement of agricultural 
and horticultural commodities which are perishable in nature and are not covered under the 
MSP regime is also implemented by the Government. The objective of intervention is to 
protect the growers of these commodities from making distress sale in the event of a bumper 
crop during the peak arrival period when the prices tend to fall below economic levels and 
the cost of production. There should be at least a 10 percent decrease in the ruling market 
prices over the previous normal year. The scheme is implemented at the request of a 
State/UT government, which is ready to bear 50 percent of the loss (25 percent in case of 
North-Eastern States), if any, incurred on its implementation. The extent of total amount of 
loss to be shared on a 50:50 basis between the Central Government and the State 
Government is restricted up to 25 percent of the total procurement value based on Market 
Intervention Price (MIP) which includes cost of the commodity procured plus permitted 
overhead expenses. The total procurement value will be the cost of procured quantity at 
Market Intervention Price (MIP) determined by MIS Committee plus permitted overheads 
expenses, which is  generally of 25% of MIP. Under this scheme, the procurement is carried 
out by State designated agency upto 25% of estimated state production of the particular 
crop at fixed MIP. However, States/UTs have also an option to make the differential payment 
between the MIP & Sale Price to the farmers.  
Procurement agencies under PM-AASHA scheme are National Agriculture 
Cooperative Marketing Federation of India Ltd. (NAFED) and National Cooperative 
Consumers Federation of India Ltd. (NCCF).  
Further, in special cases, where there is a price difference of TOP crops (Tomato, 
Onion and Potato) between the producing and consuming States, in the interest of the 
farmers, the operational costs incurred by Central Nodal Agencies (CNAs) like NAFED and 
NCCF and State designated agencies in storing and transporting crops from producing state 
to other consuming states will be reimbursed.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF COMMERCE & INDUSTRY 
DEPARTMENT FOR PROMOTION OF INDUSTRY AND INTERNAL TRADE 
 
LOK SABHA 
 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 311. 
      TO BE ANSWERED ON TUESDAY, THE 21ST JULY, 2026. 
 
ONE DISTRICT ONE PRODUCT 
 
311.  SHRI PRABHAKAR REDDY VEMIREDDY: 
DR. C M RAMESH: 
 
Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY be pleased to state: 
वाणिज्य  एवं उद्योग मंत्री 
(a)  whether it is true that the State of Andhra Pradesh has identified about 100 
products under One District One Product; 
 
(b)  whether it is true that Udayagiri Wooden Cutlery and Paturu Cotton silk Sarees 
have been identified from Nellore district of Andhra Pradesh under ODOP; 
 
(c)  whether it is true that Etikoppaka toys, Palm Leaf and Payakaraopet Silk Sarees 
have been identified as p rimary, secondary and tertiary respectively from 
Anakapalli district of Andhra Pradesh; 
 
(d)  the details of revenue generated and employment created through production, 
marketing and sale of above products since identification under ODOP; 
 
(e)  the details of support extended/going to be extended to push marketing and 
export of above products; and 
 
(f)  whether there are demands for inclusion of more products under ODOP and if 
so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
 
वाणिज्य  एवं उद्योग मंत्रालय में राज्य मंत्री (श्री णिणिन प्रसाद)   
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE & INDUSTRY 
(SHRI JITIN PRASADA) 
 
(a) to (c): One District One Product (ODOP) is an initiative by the Department for 
Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) with the aim of selecting, 
branding, and promoting at least one product from each district of the country 
to enable holistic growth across all regions. The selection of ODOP products is 
undertaken by the res pective State/UT Governments. The Government of 
Andhra Pradesh has identified 99 products (26 Primary, 26 Secondary, 21 
Tertiary, and 26 category products) from 26 districts. Udayagiri Wooden Cutlery 
(primary) and Paturu Cotton silk Sarees (secondary) ODOP  product has been 
identified for SPSR Nellore district and Etikoppaka Lacquerware/ Wooden Toys 
(primary), Palm  Leaf (secondary) and Payakaraopet Silk Sarees (tertiary) 
ODOP product has been identified for Anakapalli district. 

(d): As per the information received from the Government of Andhra Pradesh: 
i. About 100 handloom weavers are engaged in the weaving of 
Payakaraopeta Silk Sarees. Since its identification under ODOP, a 
production value of ₹10.08 crore has been reported under the Handlooms 
and Textiles Department. 
ii. The A.P. Handicrafts Development Corporation Limited organizes district -
level and State-level exhibitions and conducts training programmes for the 
promotion and marketing of ODOP products. 
iii. According to the Marine Products Export Development Authority (MPEDA), 
exports of marine products through Visakhapatnam Port accounted for 
US$2.19 billion out of India's total seafood exports of US$7.38 billion during 
FY 2024. The corresponding share was 50.87% in FY 2025 and 48.89% in 
FY 2026. 
 
(e): Several steps have been undertaken to promote and enhance the visibility of 
products identified under the ODOP initiative, including the products identified 
from Andhra Pradesh. These steps include facilitating participation in domestic 
and international exhibition s, capacity building initiatives in collaboration with 
various agencies, e -commerce onboarding drives for the Government e -
Marketplace (GeM) - ODOP Bazaar, which showcases and stocks India’s best 
ODOP products. For promoting ODOP at the international level , engagement 
with MEA and Indian Missions abroad, virtual buyer -seller meets, and 
participation in international exhibitions have been undertaken. Also, various 
ODOP Products have been included in gifting at multilateral and bilateral 
meetings in India to popularize them internationally. 
Further, the Government of Andhra Pradesh has informed that National 
Handloom Expos (NHEs) and State Level Handloom Expos (SHEs) are 
conducted to provide marketing facilities to sell their products under the 
Handloom Marketing Assistance (HMA) component of the National Handloom 
Development Programme (NHDP). The Handlooms and Textiles Department 
has collaborated with the Handloom Export Promotion Council (HEPC) to 
identify exportable Handloom Products in the State. The SHAPHA RI 
Certification Scheme of the Marine Products Export Development Authority 
(MPEDA) aims to ensure the production of quality, antibiotic -free aquaculture 
products for export markets. Under the Scheme, SHAPHARI certification has 
been granted to eligible aqu aculture hatcheries and feed manufacturing units 
in the State. Further, the Fisheries Department has undertaken measures to 
support the fisheries sector by providing fishing boats and nets to traditional 
fishermen under the PMMSY sub-component, "Replacement of Boats and Nets 
to Traditional Fishermen", and by promoting seaweed cultivation through the 
establishment of seaweed culture units for the empowerment of Self -Help 
Groups (SHGs). 
(f): No proposal has been received from the Andhra Pradesh Government for  the 
inclusion of more products under ODOP.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE & FARMERS’ WELFARE 
DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE & FARMERS’ WELFARE  
 
LOK SABHA 
 UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 312 
TO BE ANSWERED ON THE 21st JULY, 2026 
 
INCOME GENERATION BY FARMERS THROUGH CARBON CREDIT 
 
 312. SHRI UMMEDA RAM BENIWAL: 
 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS’ WELFARE क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण 
मंũी be pleased to state: 
 
(a) Whether any policy, framework or scheme exists to facilitate participation of farmers in 
carbon credit and carbon trading mechanisms and if so, the details thereof; 
(b) Whether any assessment has been conducted regarding the potential for income 
generation by farmers through carbon credit mechanisms and if so, the details thereof; 
(c) Whether any pilot projects or programmes relating to carbon credit generation in the 
agriculture sector are being implemented in the country and if so, the details thereof; and 
(d) the steps taken by the Government to facilitate participation of small and marginal 
farmers in carbon credit initiatives? 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE  
क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण राǛ मंũी                                       (SHRI  RAM NATH THAKUR) 
 
(a) & (b) The Government has notified the Carbon Credit Trading Scheme (CCTS), 2023, 
under the Energy Conservation Act, 2001, which provides the overarching framework for 
the development of the domestic carbon market. As reported by the Bureau of Energy 
Efficiency, Ministry of Power, under the Offset Mechanism of the Carbon Credit Trading 
Scheme (CCTS), two methodologies have been approved for the agriculture sector, 
namely: (i) Methane Recovery from Livestock and Manure Management at Households 
and Small Farms; and (ii) Emission Reduction through Improved Management Practices 
in Rice Cultivation. These methodologies, along with the 'Detailed Procedure for Offset 
Mechanism', provide a framework for participation in the generation of carbon credits. The 
detailed procedure and approved methodologies are available on the Indian Carbon 
Market Portal (https://indiancarbonmarket.gov.in/offset-mechanism/MzI=). However, no 
such assessment has been conducted so far regarding the potential for income generation 
by farmers through carbon credit mechanisms. 

(c) & (d) The Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare (DA&FW) is supporting 11 pilot 
projects on the Voluntary Carbon Market (VCM) for carbon credit generation in the 
agriculture sector through seven Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) institutes 
and four State Agricultural Universities (SAUs). These projects aim to facilitate technical 
support and capacity building of the participating institutions, including the development of 
methodologies for carbon credit generation from various regenerative agriculture 
practices. 
Government has published the draft Detailed Procedure for Programme of Activities (PoA) 
under the Offset Mechanism of the Carbon Credit Trading Scheme (CCTS). The PoA 
framework is to facilitate the participation of small and marginal farmers by enabling 
Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs), Non-Governmental Organizations (NGOs) and 
project developers to aggregate multiple small-scale farm-level activities under a common 
framework for carbon credit generation based on approved methodologies.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
DEPARTMENT OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 313 
  ANSWERED ON 21/07/2026 
 
DIGITAL MONITORING OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT SCHEMES 
 
313.  Shri Ashish Dubey: 
Dr. Hemant Vishnu Savara: 
 
Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  the key initiatives undertaken by the Ministry for strengthening 
digital monitoring of rural development schemes in the country, 
State-wise including Palghar district in Maharashtra; 
(b)  whether an integrated digital monitoring framework has been 
developed, including the use of geo-tagging, GIS-based 
monitoring and real-time project tracking and if so, the details 
thereof, State-wise; 
(c)  the details of schemes covered under the framework and the 
current status of their integration with digital platforms; 
(d)  whether the framework provides outcome-based evaluation and 
evidence-based planning for rural development schemes, if so, 
the details thereof; and 
(e)  the details of the digital monitoring of rural development 
schemes in the country and the current status of their 
integration with digital platforms including in Palghar district of 
Maharashtra? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
(SHRI KAMLESH PASWAN) 
 
(a): The Department of Rural Development has undertaken several 
digital initiatives to strengthen transparency, accountability and 
eﬃciency through real-time monitoring the implementation of all the 
rural development schemes across the country. The key initiatives 
include: 

Page 2 of 8 
 
 
 End-to-end digital implementation of all rural development schemes 
through dedicated Management Information Systems (MIS) and 
platforms. 
 
 Digital monitoring of beneﬁciary identiﬁcation, project planning, 
execution, fund flow and asset creation. 
 
 
 Geo-tagging and Geo-referencing of public assets for transparent 
monitoring. 
 
 GIS based planning and monitoring to facilitate better planning and 
prevent duplication of works. 
 
 
 Aadhaar-enabled Direct Beneﬁt Transfer (DBT) for timely and 
transparent transfer of benefits to eligible beneficiaries. 
 
 Digital fund management through the SNA SPARSH platform. 
These initiatives are implemented across all the States and Union 
Territories, including Palghar district of Maharashtra. The details of 
all Management Information System (MIS) and the platforms of 
Department of Rural Development is placed at Annexure I. 
(b): The Department of Rural Development has developed and 
operationalized scheme-specific digital monitoring systems 
incorporating geo-tagging, geo-referencing, GIS-enabled planning 
and real-time monitoring of Projects.  
Geo-spatial technologies are extensively used for planning, 
monitoring and verification of assets, thereby minimizing duplication 
of works and improving the quality of implementation. Geo-tagged 
photographs and GIS-enabled applications facilitate real-time 
tracking of the progress in the projects. List of Schemes and their 
GIS based monitoring link is placed at Annexure II. 
While robust digital platforms are operational for individual 
schemes, the Department is continuously strengthening 
interoperability among these platforms and is working towards a 

Page 3 of 8 
 
 
more comprehensive integrated digital monitoring framework to 
enable seamless monitoring of assets, finances and programme 
outcomes across rural development schemes. 
Under the framework, each asset under PMGSY and PMAY-G is 
assigned a geo-spatial identification number linked to a QR code. 
This identity is displayed on signboards and backed by a digital 
record containing its location, classification, and asset details. In 
effect, every asset becomes a traceable, searchable entity in a 
national inventory and is available for citizen. 
(c): The details of the major rural development schemes and their 
corresponding digital platforms is placed at Annexure III.  
(d): The digital monitoring framework supports outcome-based 
monitoring and evidence-based planning by providing real-time 
information on physical and financial progress, geo-tagged assets, 
beneficiary details and fund utilization. 
The availability of digital data enables continuous monitoring, 
informed policy decisions, eﬃcient resource allocation and improved 
programme implementation, hand holding of States/Districts which 
are poor performing, identiﬁcations of pending issues or hindrances 
in implementation district-wise or work wise so that intended 
outcomes is achieved in time across the regions.  
(e): All the digital platforms are operational across all States and 
Union Territories, including Palghar district of Maharashtra, the 
speciﬁc schemes wise link for Palghar district is placed at Annexure 
IV.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 314 
 
TO BE ANSWERED ON THE 21ST JULY, 2026/ ASHADHA 30, 1948 (SAKA) 
 
RESETTLEMENT OF PEOPLE DISPLACED BY EROSION 
 
314.     SHRI GAURAV GOGOI: 
 
Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be pleased to state:  
 
(a) whether the Rs. 1,000 crore earmarked by the 15th Finance Commission 
within NDRF specifically for "resettlement of people displaced by erosion" 
has been operationalised through a dedicated scheme; 
 
(b) the quantum of funds released and earmarked from 2021 -22 to till date, 
State-wise including Assam; 
 
(c) the criteria applied by the Government in determining which erosion -
displaced communities qualify for this fund; and 
 
(d) whether the funds under this head have not been released to Assam, if so, 
the reasons therefor and the alternate funding mechanism, if any, used for 
erosion resettlement? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
(SHRI NITYANAND RAI) 
 
(a) For resettlement of displaced people affected by erosion, 15 th Finance 
Commission had recommended that both the Union and State Governments 
develop a policy to deal with the extensive displacement of people caused by 
coastal and river erosion. To implement such policy, 15th Finance Commission 
had recommended an allocation of Rs.1,000 Crore at the national level under  
 
 

 
-2- 
L.S.US.Q.NO. 314 FOR 21.07.2026 
 
the Recovery & Reconstruction Funding Window of National Disaster 
Response Fund (NDRF). The Union Government had formulated the policy on 
“Resettlement of People affected by Erosion” under NDRF. Under the policy 
State Governments were required to submit Detai led Project Reports for 
seeking funds from the NDRF. 
 
(b) to (d) The communities impacted by coastal and river erosion are 
covered under this policy. So far, no State (except Assam) has sent project 
proposal under this policy and no funds have been released from NDRF to any 
State. The government of Assam had submitted a proposal for rehabilitation 
and resettlement of families affected by river erosion which was examined 
by National Disaster Management Authority  (NDMA) and the proposal had 
been returned to t he State Government by NDMA to revise the proposal in 
conformity with the Policy. Also, States can execute such projects under their 
own schemes.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 315 
 
TO BE ANSWERED ON THE 21ST JULY, 2026/ ASHADHA 30, 1948 (SAKA) 
 
TRAFFICKING OF NARCOTICS 
 
†315.     SHRI DILIP SAIKIA: 
     SHRI ZIA UR REHMAN: 
 
Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be pleased to state:  
 
(a) whether the Government has taken note of drug trafficking and narcotics 
menace in the country; 
 
(b) if so, the specific steps taken by the Government to check and prevent 
the illicit trafficking of narcotics along with the action taken under NDPS Act; 
and 
 
(c) the plan devised by the Government to strengthen and coordinate 
Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB) to effectively counter the growing menace 
and threats of narcotics including the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
(SHRI NITYANAND RAI) 
 
(a) & (b) Government has taken various steps to check and prevent the 
illicit trafficking of narcotics. The important steps are as under: - 
 
(i) Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB), Drug Law Enforcement Agencies 
(DLEAs) and State Police, are actively engaged in enforcement activity 
under the Narcotics Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act, 
1985. These concerted efforts have resulted in significan t 
achievements in term of drug seizures, registration of cases, arrests,  

 
-2- 
L.S.US.Q.NO. 315 FOR 21.07.2026 
 
disposal of seized drugs, destruction of illicit cultivation, financial 
investigations and preventive detention under Prevention of Illicit 
Traffic in Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (PITNDPS) Act, 
1988. 
(ii) To address the challenge of illicit drug trafficking & abuse of drugs, 
Vision Document on Narcotics Control (2026 -2029) has been released 
on 26.06.2026, which lays down a 3 -year road map with clear priorities 
and time bound targets to be achieved by various stakeholders to 
control drugs with ‘whole-of-government’ & ‘whole-of-society’ approach. 
(iii) Established a 4-tier Narco-Coordination Centre (NCORD) mechanism for 
ensuring be tter coordination between Central & State Drug Law 
Enforcement Agencies and other stake holders in the field of controlling 
drug trafficking and drug abuse in India.  
(iv) To monitor the investigation of significant and important drug cases 
including cases  of narco -terrorism, a Joint Coordination Committee 
(JCC) with DG, NCB as its Chairman has been set up. 
(v) All DGPs of States/UTs have been requested  for sensitization of beat 
constables, field officers and SHOs regarding Red Flag Indicators (RFI) 
and emerging threats relating to clandestine manufacturing of synthetic 
drugs, particularly Mephedrone and ATS. 
 

 
-3- 
L.S.US.Q.NO. 315 FOR 21.07.2026 
 
(vi) Financial investigations and effective implementation of the PITNDPS is 
being regularly emphasized at forums viz. NCORD, JCC, Regional 
Conference for dismantling and weakening of organized synthetic drug 
trafficking networks.   
(vii) Comprehensive guidelin e on financial investigation, facilitating 
systematic identification, tracing and attachment of proceeds of crime 
have been issued. 
(viii) For the capacity building of Drug Law Enforcement Officers and 
Agencies, NCB organizes workshops/ seminars/ training programmes. 
NCB is regularly conducting specialised training programmes on 
investigation of clandestine laboratories and precursor chemical 
diversion in collaboration with the US-DEA, with participation of officers 
from Central Agencies and State DLEAs. 
(ix) India holds regular Director General (DG) Level/Bilateral talks on drug 
related matters with countries such as Myanmar, Nepal, Thailand, Sri 
Lanka, Indonesia, Singapore, United States of America (USA). 
(x) NCB has strengthened international cooperation in drug control through 
bilateral agreements with 27 countries and MoUs with 19 countries.  
 
 
 

 
-4- 
L.S.US.Q.NO. 315 FOR 21.07.2026 
 
(c) To strengthen NCB, the following steps have been taken:-  
 
i. Regional offices have been increased  from 03 to 07 by addition of 04 
Regional offices at Amritsar, Guwahati, Chennai and Ahmedabad. 
ii. Zonal offices have been increased from 13 to 30, across the Country by 
addition of 05 new Zonal offices at Gorakhpur (Uttar Pradesh), Siliguri 
(West Bengal), Agartala (Tripura), Itanagar (Arunachal Pradesh) and Raipur 
(Chhattisgarh) and by upgradation of 12 existing Sub-zones as Zones.  
iii. Approval has been accorded recently for establishment of Six (06) new 
Zonal Offices at Port Blair (Andaman & Nicobar Islands), D imapur 
(Nagaland), Aizawl (Mizoram), Shimla (Himachal Pradesh), Shillong 
(Meghalaya) and Gangtok (Sikkim). 
iv. In addition, 10 Field offices have been approved and operationalized. 
v. 568 new posts have been created in the sanctioned strength of NCB. 
vi. In-principle approval for the establishment of a dedicated Directorate of 
Prosecution within the Narcotics Control Bureau has been accorded. 
Additionally, 36 prosecutors have been engaged at Regional and Zonal 
offices to add value to the effective prosecution efforts.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE & FARMERS WELFARE 
DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE & FARMERS WELFARE  
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 316 
TO BE ANSWERED ON THE 21ST JULY 2026, 
 
LACK OF MODERN AGRICULTURAL FACILITIES 
316.  SHRI RAM SHIROMANI VERMA: 
 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण मंũी 
be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government is aware that farmers in aspirational and flood affected 
districts like Shravasti and Balrampur in Uttar Pradesh are facing lack of irrigation and 
storage, cold storage, agricultural mechanization and modern agricultural facilities and if 
so, the steps taken for development of the said facilities: 
(b) whether special benefits have been provided to the farmers of the said districts under 
the Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchai Yojana, Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana, and other 
schemes and if so, the district-wise details during the last three years, 
(c)whether any special action plan has been formulated by the Government to ensure 
timely availability of certified seeds, fertilizers, DAP manure and agricultural machinery to 
the farmers and if so, the details thereof; and 
(d) whether the Government is considering the implementation of any new scheme to 
expand cooperative societies, agricultural processing, value addition, storage, and 
agricultural marketing to increase the income of farmers? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE  
क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण राǛ मंũी (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
(a) & (b): The Aspirational Districts Programme (ADP) of the Government aims to 
quickly and effectively transform 112 most under-developed districts across the country 
including Shravasti and Balrampur districts of Uttar Pradesh through convergence, 
collaboration and competition strategies. Agriculture and water being a State subject, 
development of irrigation and agricultural infrastructure is primarily the responsibility of the 
State Governments. However, the Government of India supplements the efforts of the 
States through various Centrally Sponsored and Central Sector Schemes these include, 
Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana (PMKSY), PM- Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana 
(RKVY), Sub-Mission on Agricultural Mechanization (SMAM), Mission for Integrated 
Development of Horticulture (MIDH), Agriculture Infrastructure Fund (AIF), National 
Agriculture Market (e-NAM), Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana (PKVY), National Food 
Security Mission (NFSM), Integrated Scheme for Agricultural Marketing (ISAM) etc.  
Farmers in aspirational districts, including Shravasti and Balrampur in Uttar 
Pradesh, are eligible for assistance under various schemes being implemented based on 
the Annual Action Plans prepared by States for holistic and sustainable development of 
agriculture. Under Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana (PMKSY), the Saryu Nahar 
Pariyojana has been completed under the Accelerated Irrigation Benefits Programme 
(AIBP) in December, 2023, creating an irrigation potential of 11.72 lakh hectares benefiting 
different districts of Uttar Pradesh including Shravasti and Balrampur. Under Per Drop 
More Crop (PDMC) scheme, 820 hectares have been covered under micro-irrigation in 
Balrampur and 322 hectares in Shravasti during last three years. Further, under 
Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana (PKVY), organic farming has been promoted in 

Balrampur and Shravasti districts benefitting 628 and 940 farmers till date, respectively. In 
addition, under the National Mission on Natural Farming (NMNF), 23 clusters covering 
1,150 hectares with 2,875 beneficiary farmers have been taken up in Balrampur, whereas 
20 clusters covering 1,000 hectares with 2,500 beneficiary farmers have been taken up in 
Shravasti, along with establishment of one Bio-Input Resource Centre (BRC) in each 
district to facilitate supply of natural inputs and promote adoption of natural farming 
practices. 
(c): The Government has taken several measures to ensure timely availability of quality 
agricultural inputs, including certified seeds, fertilizers and agricultural machinery. For 
effective fertiliser availability, advance assessment and allocation of fertilizers, Nutrient 
based subsidy, Urea subsidy, Neem coating of urea, Point of Sale (PoS), provision of 
‘other costs’, in coordination with fertiliser manufacturers, importers and State 
Governments are undertaken by Department of Fertilisers. For Quality seed availability, 
the Sub-Mission on Seeds and Planting Material (SMSP) now subsumed under National 
Food Security and Nutrition Mission (NFSM), SATHI portal etc. is implemented by Central 
Government. Further, financial assistance is provided for purchase of agricultural 
machinery and equipment under the Sub-Mission on Agricultural Mechanization (SMAM) 
and performance testing of machinery and equipment’s is mandated for the schemes 
through Farm Machinery Training and Testing Institutes (FMTTI’s). For effective inputs 
management regular review meetings with State Governments and stakeholders are held 
to ensure timely availability of agricultural inputs. 
 
As per the information from State Government timely availability of certified seeds, 
DAP, and agricultural machinery are ensured. Certified seeds are distributed to farmers 
selected via an e-lottery process following their booking on the designated portal. During 
the 2024-25 financial year, a total of 62,521.23 quintals and in the 2025-26 financial year 
67,264.2 quintals of seed were distributed (combining Rabi and Kharif seasons) was 
distributed to farmers in Shravasti District. The distribution of Kharif fertilizers is being 
carried out based on the farmer registry. Fertilizers are being distributed to farmers at the 
government-prescribed rates of 7 bags of Urea and 5 bags of DAP per hectare in the 
Shravasti District. In the 2024-25, 8,991 MT and in the financial year 2025-26, 10,291 MT 
of material were distributed. Under SMAM, farmers are selected via an e-lottery system 
for registered farmers. A total of 404 farmers have benefited from the scheme over the 
past three financial years. 
 
(d):   The Government is implementing several initiatives to strengthen farmer institutions 
with aim for quality input provisioning, post-harvest management and agricultural value 
chains, storage of agricultural produce and capacity building by applying principle of 
Economies of scale for increasing income of farmers. These include Formation and 
promotion of Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs) under the Central Sector Scheme 
for Formation and Promotion of 10,000 FPOs, Agriculture Infrastructure Fund (AIF) for 
financing warehouses, cold storages, primary processing centres and other post-harvest 
infrastructure, Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture (MIDH) for production 
and post-harvest management and cold chain infrastructure and Integrated Scheme for 
Agricultural Marketing (ISAM) and e-NAM for improving agricultural marketing. These 
interventions are aimed at improving market access, reducing post-harvest losses, 
enhancing value addition and increasing farmers' income.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF COMMERCE & INDUSTRY 
DEPARTMENT FOR PROMOTION OF INDUSTRY AND INTERNAL TRADE 
 
LOK SABHA 
 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 317. 
      TO BE ANSWERED ON TUESDAY, THE 21ST JULY, 2026. 
 
NATIONAL SINGLE WINDOW SYSTEM 
 
317.  DR. BHOLA SINGH: 
 
Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY be pleased to state: 
वाणिज्य  एवं उद्योग मंत्री 
(a)  the present status of implementation of the National Single Window System; 
 
(b)  the number of Ministries, States and services integrated with the platform; 
 
(c)  whether the Government has assessed its impact on reducing approval 
timelines; and 
 
(d)  if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
 
वाणिज्य  एवं उद्योग मंत्रालय में राज्य मंत्री (श्री णिणिन प्रसाद)   
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE & INDUSTRY 
(SHRI JITIN PRASADA) 
 
(a) & (b):  National Single Window System (NSWS), accessible through nsws.gov.in, is 
a one -stop digital platform for facilitating Government to Business (G2B) 
approvals and investor -related clearances for industry in a streamlined 
manner with transparency and accountability. At present, NSWS is 
integrated with 32 Central Ministries/De partments and 34 States/UTs, 
providing seamless access to 325 Central G2B approvals and 2215 State 
G2B approvals through a single platform. 
(c) & (d):  NSWS provides a single -window platform for businesses to apply for 
registrations, approvals and licenses . All eﬀorts are made to provide a 
seamless experience, however, the timelines for grant of approvals depend 
upon the existing business processes, service delivery mechanisms and 
statutory requirements of the concerned Ministries and Departments. While 
no separate study has been done on reduction of approval timelines, NSWS 
has features of dashboards and alerts to Ministries and Departments for 
monitoring the processing of applications, thus increasing transparency and 
enabling timely action.
