GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF COOPERATION 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 318 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 21st July, 2026 
 
Bharat Taxi Service 
318: Shri P C Mohan: 
Will the Minister of COOPERATION (सहकारिता मंत्री) be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the present status of the  Bharat Taxi scheme, including the number of drivers and vehicles 
registered nationally and the cities where it is currently operational; 
 
(b) the other cities and States identified for expansion of the scheme, along with the expected 
timeline; 
 
(c) whether the Be ngaluru, being a major IT and start -up hub with an extremely high daily 
commuting population and acute traffic congestion, has been accorded priority in the expansion 
plan, and if so, the details thereof; 
 
(d) whether the Government of Karnataka and local tran sport authorities will be consulted to 
streamline permits and registrations for Bengaluru; and if so, the details thereof; and 
 
(e) the steps being taken for driver onboarding and commuter awareness in the city ? 
 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF COOPERATION 
सहकारिता मंत्री (SHRI AMIT SHAH) 
(a) Bharat Taxi is a cooperative -based ride-hailing platform being operated by Sahakar Taxi 
Cooperative Limited to provide a transparent, driver -owned mobility service under the 
cooperative model. The platform comprising of Sarathi ( Driver) App lication, Passenger 
Application, and Backend Management System. Sahkar Taxi Cooperative Limited is undertaking 
the phased rollout of the platform across the country including  Sarathi ( driver) onboarding, 
customer registration, document verification, training and expansion of services. 
Presently the Bharat Taxi is operational in cities of Delhi-NCR and Gujrat. 7.76 lakh Sarathis 
(drivers) and 40.84 lakh customers have been registered on the platform..  
b)  Sahkar Taxi Cooperative Limited is expanding Bharat Taxi in a phased manner. The 
rollout of services in additional cities and States is sub ject to operational requirements and 
approvals. Expansion in depends on factors such as operational preparedness, availability of 

Sarathis, completion of stat utory requirements, and coordination with the concerned State 
Governments, cooperative institutions and other stakeholders.  
c) Yes. Sahkar Taxi Cooperative Limited undertakes the rollout of Bharat Taxi services only 
after ensuring operational preparedness and completion of the applicable  statutory requirements, 
obtaining the necessary approvals and fulfilling other administrative requirements, in accordance 
with its overall implementation plan. 
d)  Prior to the rollout of Bharat Taxi services in any  of the  States, Sahkar Taxi Cooperative 
Limited undertakes consultations, as required,  with the concerned departments of State 
Government including the Transport Department, Urban Local Bodies/Municipal Authorities and 
the Department of Cooperation. The necessary licences, registrations, permissions and other 
statutory approvals are obtained by Sahkar Taxi Cooperative Limited in accordance with the 
applicable legal and regulatory framework. Operations are commenced only after completion of 
the requisite statutory and administrative formalities. 
e)  As part of its implementation process, Sahkar Taxi Cooperative Limited undertakes d river 
onboarding and public awareness activities prior to the rollout of Bharat Taxi services in a city. 
Such activities may include dissemination of information through the official social media 
platforms of Bharat Taxi, engagement with the concerned department of the State Government 
and local authorities, and other outreach initiatives, as considered necessary. Bharat Taxi 
maintains an active presence across major social media platforms to facilitate public awareness 
and dissemination of information regarding its services.

321. THIRU ARUN NEHRU: 
 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण मंũी 
be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government has conducted any studies on the problems faced by maize, 
cotton, paddy and other major crops in Perambalur Parliamentary Constituency; 
(b) if so, the key findings thereof; and 
(c) the steps taken to improve access to quality inputs, credit, extension services and 
assured markets? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE  
क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण राǛ मंũी (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
 
(a) & (b): The Government of Tamil Nadu/ Tamil Nadu Agricultural University (TNAU) has 
undertaken several research studies to address the major production constraints affecting 
maize, cotton, paddy and other crops in Perambalur constituency. 
The Department of Agriculture, State Government of Tamil Nadu has informed that 
maize hybrids [VGIH(M) 2, COH(M) 11 & COH(M) 12] suitable for drought-affected rainfed 
cultivation and improved new rice varieties (CO 58 & CO 59) have also been developed 
and released for cultivation in Perambalur constituency. Further, drought tolerant rainfed 
cotton varieties (VPT 2 & VPT 3) have been developed and released. Improved agronomic 
practices, including broad bed and furrow, mulching, moisture conservation, protective 
irrigation, foliar nutrient application, Alternate Wetting and Drying (AWD), System of Rice 
Intensification (SRI), and Direct Seeded Rice (DSR), etc. have been validated for 
enhancing drought resilience. Crop-specific nutrient formulations, namely “Cotton Plus" 
nutrient and growth regulator technology has been developed to reduce square and flower 
shedding and improve drought tolerance. "Maize Maxim" nutrient formulation has been 
developed to improve crop performance under moisture stress. 
(c): The Department of Agriculture, State Government of Tamil Nadu has informed that 
the Perambalur constituency has 10 Integrated Agricultural Extension Centres at block 
level and 8 Sub Agricultural Extension Centres at firka level operated by the Government 
of Tamil Nadu promoting various Centre-State shared schemes. Uzhavar mobile 
application provides farmers with real time information and access to Government 
Services through single platform. The application provides information on agricultural 
schemes, benefit registration, seed stock, pest and disease diagnosis, e-market etc. 
Further, trainings are conducted on various Good Agricultural Practices from land 
preparation to marketing for the predominant crops cultivated in the constituency. 
The Department of Agriculture, State Government of Tamil Nadu has also informed 
that during 2025-26, 579 Metric Tonnes of seeds were distributed in the Perambalur 
Constituency comprising 363 Metric Tonnes of Paddy, 41 Metric Tonnes of Millets, 52 
Metric Tonnes of Pulses, 48 Metric Tonnes of Oilseeds & 75 Metric Tonnes of Green 
Manure Seeds. In addition, inputs like 32 Metric Tonnes of Biofertilzers, 49 Metric Tonnes 
of Fertilizers, 1546 Numbers of Machineries & Implements, 92 Metric Tonnes of 
Micronutrient mixtures, 6 Metric Tonnes of Organic Fertilizers, 27 Metric Tonnes Organic 

Inputs, 27 Metric Tonnes of Bio-Pesticides and 3 Metric Tonnes of Traditional Seeds have 
been distributed during 2025-26. Further, seeds, fertilizers and other agriculture inputs are 
distributed through 287 Primary Agricultural Co-operative Credit Societies (PACCS) at 
village level. 
The Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare (DA&FW), Government of 
India is implementing the National Food Security & Nutrition Mission (NFSNM) in 28 States 
(including Tamil Nadu) and 2 Union Territories with the objective to increase production of 
Shree Anna, Coarse Cereals (Maize & Barley), Rice, Wheat and Commercial Crops (Jute 
& Sugarcane) through area expansion and productivity enhancement. An amount of 
Rs.9422.155 lakh has been approved in the Annual Action Plan for the state of Tamil Nadu 
under NFSNM during 2026-27. Flexibility has been given to States / UTs to identify districts 
for implementation of different components of the Mission prioritizing districts with low 
productivity but high potential. 
The Component-I (B) of the Mission for Cotton Productivity (KAPAS KANTI) is being 
implemented by Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Government of India in 14 
States including Tamil Nadu from 2026-27, with an objective to enhance cotton production 
& productivity through Upscaling technologies viz., High Density Planting System (HDPS) 
and Closer Spacing (CS), Promoting Extra Long Staple (ELS) cotton &good management 
practices and Capacity building of farmers through trainings. During 2026-27, an allocation 
of Rs. 2621.25 lakhs (Central Share + State Share) has been approved for implementing 
in various districts (including Perambalur and Tiruchirappalli) of the state of Tamil Nadu. 
The Government of India is implementing a 100% centrally funded Central Sector 
Scheme known as the Modified Interest Subvention Scheme (MISS) across various States 
and UTs to provide concessional interest rates on short-term agricultural loans obtained 
by farmers through Kisan Credit Cards (KCC) for their working capital requirements.  
The Department of Agriculture, State Government of Tamil Nadu has also informed 
that there are two regulated markets functioning in Perambalur with necessary 
infrastructure facilities including two storage warehouses with a capacity of 3000 Metric 
Tonnes each, one transaction shed and one drying yard. Perambalur Regulated Market 
has also been integrated with the National Agriculture Market (e-NAM), allowing local 
farmers (especially of maize and small onions/shallots) to bid their produce to a wider 
network of traders. Further, direct procurement centres for paddy and maize are set up by 
the state government during harvest seasons to ensure Minimum Support Prices (MSP), 
along with state incentives. For maize, the major maize-producing (surplus) districts have 
been mapped with nearby grain-based distilleries and poultry feed manufacturing units to 
strengthen market linkages and facilitate efficient procurement.

Will the Minister of PANCHAYATI RAJ be pleased to state: 
  
(a)  the number of villages in Uttar Pradesh where survey and mapping work, including 
mapping under the "Survey of Villages and Mapping with Improvised Technology in Village 
Areas (SVAMITVA)" scheme, has been completed;  
  
(b)  the percentage of households in the said areas to whom property cards have been 
distributed under the said scheme;  
  
(c)  the timeline fixed for achieving cent percent mapping of all land parcels and areas under 
the said scheme; and  
  
(d)  the provisions made to resolve potential disputes arising out of anomalies or

(SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH ALIAS LALAN SINGH)

      TO BE ANSWERED ON TUESDAY, THE 21ST JULY, 2026. 
 
STARTUP INDIA SEED FUND SCHEME 
 
323.  SHRI BRIJMOHAN AGRAWAL: 
 
Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY be pleased to state: 
वाणिज्य  एवं उद्योग मंत्री 
(a)  the total funds allocated and utilized under the Startup India Seed Fund 
Scheme (SISFS) as of June 2026, including the count of operational incubators; 
 
(b)  whether the Government is aware of implementation friction caused by the 
decentralized ‘incubator-mediated’ disbursement model, specifically the 
operational delays in milestone -based fund releases due to inadequate due -
diligence capacity in empanelled incubators; 
 
(c)  the data regarding SISFS fund utilization, particularly the disparity between 
startups in aspirational districts versus urban hubs and the operational overlap 
with the State’s ‘Seed Fund Assistance’ policy, State-wise and distrcit-wise for 
Chhattisgarh; 
 
(d)  the corrective measures or capacity -building mechanisms being implemented 
to eliminate  disbursement stagnancy and ensure equitable regional capital 
distribution; and 
 
(e)  the list of all the successful startups bo rn out  of this scheme since the 
implementation of the scheme? 
 
ANSWER 
 
वाणिज्य  एवं उद्योग मंत्रालय में राज्य मंत्री (श्री णिणिन प्रसाद)   
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE & INDUSTRY 
(SHRI JITIN PRASADA) 
 
(a): The Startup India Seed Fund Scheme (SISFS) was launched to enable financial 
assistance for eligible early-stage startups through incubators across India. As 
on 30th June 2026, 219 operational incubators have been selected under the 
Scheme with a total approved funding of Rs. 945 crore, of which Rs. 650 crore 
has been disbursed to the incubators. 
(b): Under the Startup India Seed Fund Scheme (SISFS), funds are released  by 
selected incubators to startups in milestone -based instalments in accordance  
with the guidelines for the Scheme. To ensure timely implementation of the 
Scheme and disbursement of funds, an institutional mechanism comprising the 
Experts Advisory Committ ee (EAC) and Incubator Seed Management 
Committees (ISMCs) has been established. 

The EAC oversees the implementation and monitoring of the Scheme including 
selection of incubators for allocation of funds, while the ISMCs evaluate eligible 
startups and determine the nature and quantum of seed support in accordance 
with the Scheme Guidelines. 
Regular review meetings and webinars are also conducted with incubators to 
review the progress of fund disbursement, identify implementation bottlenecks 
and facilitate th eir timely resolution. Further, advisories and training modules  
have been shared with incubators to facilitate timely processing of funds. 
Further, given the milestone -based nature of disbursement and the time 
required by incubators and startups to utilize  sanctioned funds eﬀectively, the 
Scheme has recently been provided an extension to facilitate disbursement of 
committed funds and to enable incubators and startups to complete approved 
activities. 
(c): SISFS enables financial assistance for eligible early -stage startups across 
State/Union Territories (UTs), cities, towns, rural areas, and aspirational 
districts. The State/UT -wise details of funds approved and disbursed to 
incubators selected under the SISFS as on 30th June 2026 are placed as  
Annexure-I. Th e State/UT -wise details of funds approved and disbursed to 
startups by selected incubators under the SISFS as on 30th June 2026 are 
placed as  Annexure-II. The district -wise details of funds approved and 
disbursed to startups in the State of Chhattisgarh by selected incubators under 
the SISFS as on 30th June 2026 are placed as Annexure-III. 
Under SISFS, eligible startups can receive up to Rs. 20 lakh as grant for 
validation of Proof of Concept, or prototype development, or product trials and 
up to Rs. 50 Lakhs of investment for market entry, commercialization, or scaling 
up through convertible debentures or debt or debt -linked instruments. As per 
the Chhattisgarh Innovation and Startup Promotion Policy 2025 -2030, under 
Chhattisgarh Seed Fund Assistance (CGSF), eligible startups shall be provided 
seed funding of up to Rs. 10 lakh for the development of a Minimum Viable 
Product (MVP). 
Further, under SISFS, the startup should not have received more than Rs 10 
lakh of monetary support under any other Central or St ate Government 
scheme, and under the CGSF, the startup should not have received seed 
funding for the development of a Minimum Viable Product (MVP) under any 
other Scheme of the State or Central Government. 
(d): To strengthen implementation of the Scheme, build the capacity of incubators 
and facilitate timely disbursement of funds across regions, the Government has 
undertaken several measures. 
These include capacity -building workshops and handholding support for 
incubators to promote eﬀective implementation of the Scheme. Eﬀorts are also 
undertaken to assist incubators and startups, particularly from non-metropolitan 
regions, in navigating the application process. 
The Government has also developed a dedicated digital portal for end -to-end 
implementation of SI SFS, providing a common online platform for application 

processing, fund management and monitoring across the country. Benefits 
under the Scheme are further disseminated through various outreach and 
social media initiatives. 
In addition, specific initiatives for regional awareness and outreach of benefits 
under Startup India initiative including SISFS are undertaken through the 
States' Startup Ranking exercise, Innovation Week and TEJAS (Transforming 
Entrepreneurial Journeys Across States & Districts). 
(e): The regular businesses are often measured by success or failure in a specific 
number of years of operation, whereas the startups are measured in particular 
phase of business making it difficult to put together a statistic covering success 
or survival rate of startups. Therefore, the information with respect to survival 
rate of startup is not centrally maintained by the Government. 
However, the total number of startups selected and the total number of 
startups that are categorized as closed (i.e., dissolved/struck-oﬀ) as per the 
Ministry of Corporate Aﬀairs (MCA) data [basis data shared on 10th July 2026], 
under the Startup India Seed Fund Scheme (SISFS) are as follows:

मत्स्यपालन, पशुपालन और डेयरी मंत्री 
be pleased to state:

Financial Year 2025-26;  
(b) whether any scheme-level assessment has been undertaken by the Government and if so, the

THE MINISTER OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING

327.  SHRI SUDHAKAR SINGH: 
 
Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY be pleased to state: 
वाणिज्य  एवं उद्योग मंत्री 
(a)  the number of industrial units accorded approval in Bihar under various 
industrial incentive  and manufacturing promotion schemes of the Union 
Government during the last three years; 
 
(b)  the number of units out of them which have been established and have 
commenced production, year and sector-wise during the last three years; 
 
(c)  whether the Government has made a holistic assessment of the major 
structural bottlenecks affecting industrial growth in Bihar such as lack of 
industrial infrastructure, limited  availability of credit from financial institutions 
and logistic and transport challenges and if so, the main findings thereof; and 
 
(d)  the concrete steps being taken by the Government to promote labour-intensive 
industries, Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) clusters and agro -
based value -added industries,  to enhance employment generation and to 
reduce regional industrial imbalance in the State? 
 
ANSWER 
 
वाणिज्य  एवं उद्योग मंत्रालय में राज्य मंत्री (श्री णिणिन प्रसाद)   
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE & INDUSTRY 
(SHRI JITIN PRASADA) 
 
(a) & (b): The primary responsibility for developing the industrial sector rests with the 
State Governments, which adopt different policy measures to promote 
industrial development. The Union Government supplements the efforts of the 
State/UT Governments through various schemes,  programmes, and policy 
initiatives for the overall development and promotion of industry across the 
country, including in Bihar. These initiatives include the Scheme for Investment 
Promotion, Ease of Doing Business (EoDB) and initiatives aimed at reducing  
compliance burden, the Industrial Infrastructure Upgradation Scheme, the 
Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme, Integrated Manufacturing Clusters 
(IMCs) under the National Industrial Corridors, Startup India, Make in India, PM 
Gati Shakti, National Inf rastructure Pipeline (NIP), National Single Window 
System (NSWS), India Industrial Land Bank (IILB), reforms in Foreign Direct 
Investment (FDI), Project Monitoring Group (PMG). Some of the initiatives 

specific to the Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME) sector are Prime 
Minister's Employment Generation Programme, Credit Guarantee Scheme for 
Micro and Small Enterprises, Micro and Small Enterprises –Cluster 
Development Programme, Raising and Accelerating MSME Performance, Self 
Reliant India Fund, etc. Be nefits under these schemes are available to all 
eligible MSMEs throughout the country, subject to meeting the guidelines and 
the eligibility criteria. 
Govt. of Bihar has informed that  under the Bihar Industrial Investment 
Promotion Policy (BIIPP) 2024-27, implemented in coordination with the State 
Government, a total of 932 industrial investment proposals have received 
Stage-I clearance during the last three years (FY 2024 -25 to FY 2026 -27), 
entailing a cumulative proposed investment of approximately Rs. 48 ,160.80 
crore. Year-wise details of Stage-I clearances are given below:

(c) & (d):  Need based assessments are made under various Government initiatives. 
Such assessments are conducted to meet the sectoral requirement of the 
scheme or initiative. 
 
For example, the Logistics Ease Across Different States (LEADS) Report, the 
Ease of Doing Business (EoDB) assessment framework, of the Department for 
Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) are aimed at encouraging the 
States, including the State of Bihar, to undertake reforms,  infrastructure 
strengthening and other initiatives aimed at improving the industrial ecosystem 
and doing business environment in the State. 
 

These assessments  indicate that progress has been made across various 
parameters but also highlight the need for continued strengthening of 
multimodal connectivity, industrial infrastructure, ease of doing business, and 
investment facilitation to support sustainable industrial growth. 
 
To address these challenges, the Union Government has undertaken several 
initiatives that benefit Bihar, including PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan for 
integrated infrastructure planning, the National Infrastructure Pipeline, National 
Industrial Corridor Development Programme, Production Linked Incentive (PLI) 
Schemes. 
 
For promoting labour -intensive industries, MSMEs and agro -based value 
addition, the Union Government implements schemes such as the Prime 
Minister's Employment Generation Pr ogramme (PMEGP), Prime Minister 
Formalisation of Micro Food Processing Enterprises (PMFME) Scheme, Micro 
and Small Enterprises –Cluster Development Programme (MSE -CDP), Credit 
Guarantee Scheme for Micro and Small Enterprises (CGTMSE), Raising and 
Accelerating MSME Performance (RAMP), Self Reliant India (SRI) Fund, PM 
Kisan SAMPADA Yojana, and the National Handloom Development 
Programme.  
 
These interventions facilitate enterprise creation, cluster development, 
technology upgradation, credit access, value add ition, market linkages and 
employment generation across the country, including in Bihar.

329. THIRU THANGA TAMILSELVAN: 
 
Will the Minister of STEEL be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is true that an industrial accident at the Visakhapatnam Steel Plant (VSP) 
that claimed the lives of nine workers and left five others seriously injured; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether the Union Government has appointed any enquiry commission to find out 
the cause of such accident and poor management of the steel plant; 
(d) whether the Union Government has initiated any disciplinary action against officials 
linked to production and quality control operations of the plant; and 
(e) if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE          (SHRI BHUPATHIRAJU SRINIVASA VARMA) 
MINISTRY OF STEEL 
 
(a)to(e):   An accident occurred at Steel Melting Shop (SMS-2) of Steel Plant of 
Rashtriya Ispat Nigam Ltd., Vishakhapatnam on 08th June, 2026, resulting in spillage 
of molten steel. In this accident, ten (10) workers comprising of five (5) Regular 
Employees and five (5) Contractual Workers lost their lives and four (4) Regular 
Workers sustained injuries. 
A high Level Enquiry Committee chaired by Director-in-Charge of Bokaro Steel 
Plant of Steel Authority of India Limited(SAIL) 
 along with outside Experts, was constituted by Ministry of Steel. The report of 
Enquiry Committee has been received and appropriate action has been initiated.

Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE कृ ͪष और ͩकसान कãयाण 
मंğी be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government is aware that onion growers in the country, especially in 
Ahilyanagar and Nashik of Maharashtra State, have reached on the verge of severe 
economic ruin and suicide due to not getting profitable prices; 
(b) the year-wise data on decline in the share of Indian onion in the global market due 
to restrictions imposed on onion exports and uncertain trade policies; 
(c) whether the Government proposes to provide legal guarantee for the Minimum 
Support Price (MSP) of onion based on the cost of production, so as to protect farmers 
from exploitation by middlemen; 
(d) whether the Government will provide any direct financial assistance to farmers to 
mitigate the unexpected increase in storage and transportation costs of onions; and 
(e) what is the effective plan to permanently streamline onion export arrangements 
and provide immediate relief to farmers through Price Stabilization Fund (PSF)? 
 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE  
कृ ͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण राÏय मंğी (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
 
(a) to (e): As per the second advance estimates for 2025–26, the total onion production 
in the country is 307.37 lakh metric tonnes (LMT) out of which 151.10 LMT is produced in 
Maharashtra. The average market price in Maharashtra during the period from March to 
May 2026 ranged from Rs 900 to Rs 1150 per quintal.  
 
      To provide remunerative price to the farmers for agricultural and horticultural 
commodities including onion which are perishable in nature and are not covered under the 
Minimum Support Price regime, the Government under Pradhan Mantri Annadata Aay 
Sanrakshan Abhiyan implements Market Intervention Scheme (MIS) across the 
country. The objective of the Scheme is to protect the farmers from distress sale in the 
event of a bumper crop during the peak arrival, when the prices tend to fall below economic 

levels and the cost of production. There should be at least a 10% decrease in the ruling 
market prices over the previous normal year. The scheme is implemented at the request 
of a State/UT Government, which is ready to bear 50% of the loss (25% in case of North-
Eastern States), if any, incurred on its implementation. The maximum quantity of 
procurement is allowed upto 25% of estimated production of the State for particular crop in 
a particular season. Total amount of loss is shared on a 50:50 basis between the Central 
Government and the State Government (75:25 for North East States). 
       A new component of Price Differential Payment (PDP) with an option to make direct 
payment of the price difference between the Market Intervention Price (MIP) and the selling 
price to the farmers for the crops traded in the Agricultural Produce Market Committee 
(APMC) Mandis has also been added. Additionally, reimbursement for transportation and 
storage cost of TOP crops (Tomato, Onion and Potato) to Central Nodal Agencies & State 
Designated Agencies for storing and transporting TOP crops from producing state to 
consuming state is allowed.  
      To control extreme volatility of prices in essential commodities, under Price Stabilisation 
Fund (PSF) scheme, the Government creates an annual buffer stock of onions, with the 
buffer target decided each year. Onions are procured from producing States through 
Implementing Agencies (NAFED and NCCF) at market price linked, Minimum Assured 
Procurement Price (MAPP) on the basis of Maximum and Modal prices prevailing during 
previous 3 trading days. The quantity procured in 2025-26 was 2.87 Lakh MT. Under the 
Price Stabilisation Fund (PSF) scheme, Department of Consumer Affairs has approved the 
procurement target of 2 Lakh MT for the year 2026-27, out of which 0.37 LMT procured.

TO BE ANSWERED ON THE 21st JULY, 2026 
 
PROMOTION OF COLD STORAGE INFRASTRUCTURE 
 
334. SHRI RAJESH NARANBHAI CHUDASAMA:  
   
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE  क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण मंũी 
be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has taken steps to bring about more awareness for promoting 
cold storage infrastructure in the country;  
(b) if so, the quantum of assistance extended to the entrepreneurs, attracting more 
entrepreneurs in this field;  
(c) whether the Government will pay special attention to this area as popularising the 
technology among the youth, would not only bring down the commodity value uniformly 
throughout the year but also bring manifold employment opportunities to the youth; and  
(d) whether the Government provides support by extending loans to the entrepreneurs 
more freely and also interest free loans for setting up cold storage infrastructure? 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
 
क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण राǛ मंũी (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
 
(a) & (b): To create awareness on the various scheme for subsidy including cold storage 
among the farming community, the Mass Media Support under Agriculture Extension scheme 
is implemented since 2004 with the objective of creating awareness among farming 
communities and other stakeholders about the schemes, programmes, missions and new 
initiatives of the Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare (DA&FW), as well as crop 
advisories, weather information, market information and modern, region-specific agricultural 
technologies. The scheme is implemented through Doordarshan, DD Kisan and All India 
Radio (AIR) for the telecast and broadcast of agriculture and allied sector programmes 
sponsored by DA&FW. Under the scheme, a 30-minute programme, ‘Krishi Darshan’, is 
telecast through 19 Regional Doordarshan Kendras. In addition, three programmes, namely 
‘Krishi Darshan’, ‘Adhunik aur Satat Krishi Ki Ore’ and ‘Krishi Chaupal’ are telecast on DD 
Kisan.  
 
Through All India Radio (AIR), the ‘Kisanvani’ programme is broadcasted through 232 
AIR FM, FM-Gold and Rainbow stations across the country to create awareness among the 
farming community. In addition, agriculture-related programmes are also broadcast through 
29 Vividh Bharati stations. Publicity and awareness activities are also undertaken through 
outdoor publicity and print advertisements in leading newspapers across the country. 

 
Further, in view of the increasing penetration of mobile phones and internet services, 
including in rural areas, social media platforms such as Facebook, X (formerly Twitter), 
Instagram, YouTube and WhatsApp Channels are also being utilised for disseminating 
information and creating awareness about the initiatives, schemes and programmes of 
DA&FW. 
 
Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare is implementing Mission for Integrated 
Development of Horticulture (MIDH) for holistic development of horticulture in the country to 
reducing the post-harvest losses through increasing cold storage infrastructure. Under MIDH 
scheme financial assistance is provided for various horticulture activities including 
Construction/Expansion/ Modernization of cold storages of capacity up to 5000 MT in the 
country on the basis of Annual Action Plan (AAP) received from States/UTs. The component 
of Cold Storage is demand/entrepreneur driven for which Government assistance in the form 
of credit linked back ended subsidy is available at the rate of 35% of the project cost in general 
areas and 50% of the project cost in case of NE & Himalayan State, Scheduled areas, vibrant 
villages, Andaman & Nicobar and Lakshadweep Islands through respective State Horticulture 
Missions. Under the Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture (MIDH), awareness 
is generated through capacity-building programmes, workshops, seminars, exhibitions, and 
exposure visits aimed at farmers, entrepreneurs, and other stakeholders. 
 
Besides, National Horticulture Board (NHB) is implementing a scheme namely “Capital 
Investment Subsidy for Construction/Expansion /Modernization of Cold Storages and 
Storages for Horticulture Products”. Under the scheme, credit linked back-ended subsidy at 
the rate of 35% of the capital cost of the project in general areas and 50% in case of North 
East, hilly & scheduled areas for construction/expansion/modernization of cold storage and 
Controlled Atmosphere (CA) storage of capacity above 5000 MT and up to 20000 MT is 
available. 
 
As per the records, Rs.175.89 crore and Rs. 37.63 crore have been approved for 
establishment of 122 numbers and 16 numbers of cold storages under National Horticulture 
Board and Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture respectively during 2025-26.  
 
  

Ministry of Food Processing Industries (MoFPI) implements a Scheme for Integrated 
Cold Chain, Food Processing and Preservation Infrastructure as one of the components of 
Pradhan Mantri Kisan Sampada Yojana (PMKSY) with the objective of reducing post-harvest 
losses of horticulture and non-horticulture produce and providing remunerative price to 
farmers for their produce. Under the scheme, Ministry provides financial assistance in the 
form of grant-in-aid at the rate of 35% for general areas and 50% for North East and 
Himalayan States, Integrated Tribal Development Programme (ITDP) areas and Islands for 
storage and transport infrastructure and at the rate of 50% and 75% respectively for value 
addition and processing infrastructure subject to a maximum grant-in-aid of Rs. 10.00 crore 
per project for setting up of integrated cold chain projects including irradiation facility. 
Standalone cold storages are not covered under the Scheme. 
 
(c): The Government is promoting the adoption of modern and advanced technologies 
such as protected cultivation, high-density planting, precision irrigation, quality planting 
material, mechanization, post-harvest management infrastructure, cold chain, and other 
technology-driven interventions in the horticulture sector through various schemes and 
programmes, including the Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture (MIDH).  
 
        Apart from this, MIDH and NHB have recently introduced solar-based micro cold 
storage, bio-mass based cold storage under the new technology interventions and can be 
availed under the component of farm gate pack house, integrated pack house and collection 
aggregation center. These new technologies promote use of renewal energy and are climate 
friendly. To spread awareness among youth, FPOs growers and young entrepreneurs 10 
training workshops along with State horticulture departments have been organized for 
highlighting the use and importance of latest technologies in horticulture sector.  
 
(d): To facilitates institutional credit and strengthen agriculture infrastructure in the country, 
Government has launched Agriculture Infrastructure Funds (AIF) of Rs. 1.00 lakh crore. 
Under AIF, there is provision for collateral free term loan upto Rs. 2.00 crore and interest 
subvention of 3% on the term loan availed for creation of post-harvest infrastructure including 
establishment of cold storages. These initiatives significantly reduce the cost of credit and 
make it more accessible for entrepreneurs investing in cold storage facilities. As per report 
uploaded on the AIF website, a total 3079 number of cold storage/cold chain projects have 
been sanctioned with total financial assistance of Rs. 10901.54 crore under Agriculture 
Infrastructure Fund Scheme.

SECTOR-WISE PROGRESS OF PLI SCHEME 
 
335.  MR PATHAN YUSUF: 
 
Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY be pleased to state: 
वाणिज्य  एवं उद्योग मंत्री 
(a)  the progress of the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme in attracting 
investments and generating employment, sector-wise; 
 
(b)  the value of exports achieved under the scheme during the last three years; 
 
(c)  whether any review has been undertaken to address implementation 
challenges, if so, the details thereof; and 
 
(d)  the corrective measures proposed by the Government to improve the 
effectiveness of the scheme? 
 
ANSWER 
 
वाणिज्य  एवं उद्योग मंत्रालय में राज्य मंत्री (श्री णिणिन प्रसाद)   
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE & INDUSTRY 
(SHRI JITIN PRASADA) 
(a): The Government has launched Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Schemes for 
14 key sectors with an approved financial outlay of ₹1.91 lakh crore to enhance 
India's manufacturing capabilities, attract investments, increase exports, 
generate employment a nd improve India's global competitiveness. The 
Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) acts as the 
nodal Department for overall coordination and monitoring of the PLI Schemes, 
while the respective Administrative Ministries/Departments are responsible for 
implementation of their respective Schemes. 
As on 31.03.2026, under the PLI Schemes, resulted actual investment of over 
₹2.40 lakh crore  and employment generation of over 14.15 lakh (direct and 
indirect). The sector -wise details of investments and employment generated 
are at Annexure-I. 
The sectoral impact of the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Schemes across 
various sectors is as under: 
 The PLI Schemes have collectively enabled exports of over ₹15.2 lakh crore 
since their inception, reflecting India's growing integration with global value 
chains. 

 In the Large Scale Electronics Manufacturing sector, mobile phone production 
has increased by around 2.4 times since the launch of the Scheme. Mobile 
phone i mports have declined by about 77%, and around 99.2% of mobile 
phones used in India are now manufactured domestically. 
 The Pharmaceuticals sector has recorded cumulative sales of over ₹3.64 lakh 
crore under the Scheme. It has also enabled the domestic manufacture of 1,931 
pharmaceutical products, including 191 bulk drugs  manufactured in India for 
the first time, thereby strengthening domestic manufacturing capabilities. 
 In the Bulk Drugs sector, manufacturing capacity of about 55,000 MT has been 
established across 26 critical Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients (APIs) , 
significantly enhancing domestic production capacity and reducing import 
dependence for products such as Paracetamol, Levofloxacin and Norfloxacin. 
 The PLI Scheme for Manufacturing of Medical Devices has facilitated domestic 
manufacturing of advanced medical equipment such as CT Scanners, MRI 
Systems, Cath Labs and Ultrasonography equipment . 22 applicants  have 
commenced operations and 55 unique medical devices  have been 
commissioned. 
 In the Telecom & Networking Products sector, the Scheme has supported the 
development of indigenous 4G technology  and domestic manufacturing 
capability for 5G telecom equipment , strengthening India's telecom 
manufacturing ecosystem. 
 The PLI Scheme for White Goods has contributed to a significant expansion in 
domestic manufacturing. Compressor manufacturing capacity has increased 
from 1 million units in 2021 to 10 million units in 2025 -26, while localisation of 
key components such as PCBAs and Cross Flow Fans  has improved 
substantially, leading to domestic manufacturing of several critical air -
conditioner components. 
(b): The cumulative exports reported under the Sectors of PLI Schemes have 
shown a steady increase over the last three years. The cumulative expo rts 
reported as on 31.03.2024 were ₹4 lakh crore, which increased to ₹15.2 lakh 
crore as on 31.03.2026. The year-wise details are given at Annexure-II. 
(c): The implementation of the PLI Schemes is reviewed periodically by the 
Empowered Group of Secretarie s (EGoS), chaired by the Cabinet Secretary, 
as well as by the respective Administrative Ministries/Departments. Based on 
stakeholder feedback and implementation experience, modifications have been 
carried out in certain Schemes, wherever required, to addre ss implementation 
challenges and facilitate effective implementation. 
(d): The Government has undertaken several measures to improve the 
effectiveness of the PLI Schemes. These include periodic review of Scheme 
implementation, rationalisation of Scheme guidelines, relaxation of certain 
eligibility conditions, strengthening of pro ject monitoring mechanisms, regular 

stakeholder consultations, and timely resolution of implementation issues in 
coordination with the concerned Ministries/Departments through the 
Empowered Group of Secretaries (EGoS). These measures are aimed at 
improving Scheme uptake, accelerating investments, enhancing production 
and exports, generating employment and strengthening domestic 
manufacturing ecosystems.

FREE TRADE AGREEMENTS 
  
337. MS. PRANITI SUSHILKUMAR SHINDE: 
  
 Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY  (वाणिज्य एवं उद्योग मंत्री) be 
pleased to state: 
  
(a) whether the Government has undertaken steps to diversify India’s export markets 
in light of global geopolitical and economic uncertainties; 
(b) the details of recent and ongoing Free Trade Agreements (FTAs) and their 
expected impact on India’s cross-border trade; 
(c) the measures taken by the Government to address non -tariff barriers and 
improve market access for Indian exporters in key regions such as the European 
Union, Africa and Southeast Asia; and 
(d) the steps being take n by the Government to promote ease of cross -border e-
commerce exports, including regulatory simplification and support for small 
exporters? 
  
ANSWER 
 
वाणिज्य एवं उद्योग मंत्रालय में राज्यमंत्री (श्री णिणिन प्रसाद) 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY 
(SHRI JITIN PRASADA) 
(a) & (b) Government has undertaken several initiatives to diversify export markets in 
light of evolving global geopolitical and economic developments. These include 
expanding network of Free Trade Agreements (FTA s) and Comprehensive Economic 
Partnership/Cooperation Agreements (CEPAs/CECAs); pursuing trade negotiations 
with major economies and regions to secure preferential market access for exporters; 
undertaking focused export promotion activities through Export Promotion Mission, 
Indian Missions overseas, Export Promotion Councils (EPCs), industry associations 
and other stakeholders; implementing district and sector -specific export promotion 
initiatives under the Districts as Export Hubs (DEH) initiative; and cap acity-building 
programmes.  
A list of trade agreements signed in the past few years is at Annexure I.  Further, 
a list of ongoing FTAs is at Annexure II.   

2 
 
            Free Trade Agreements (FTAs) are entered into with the concerned trading 
partner countries primarily with the aim of increasing bilateral trade through enlarging 
the scope of market access and building on the trade complementarities for increas ing 
trade and investment, thereby providing enhanced export potential, creating benefits for 
industry and farmers and enhancing job opportunities. The FTAs facilitate preferential 
market access for labour intensive sector products to boost growth and emplo yment 
opportunities in sectors like textile, apparel and leather goods. FTAs endeavor to deliver 
a comprehensive, balanced, broad based and equitable agreement based on the 
principle of fairness and reciprocity and overall benefit to all the stakeholders.  
(c)        The FTAs include provisions on Technical Barriers to Trade to promote mutual 
understanding of each sides’ standards, technical regulations, and measures to 
enhance transparency. These provisions facilitate smoother and more effective access 
to export markets for Indian goods. Government engages with its trading partners 
through bilateral, regional and multilateral mechanisms to address non -tariff barriers 
(NTBs) and improve market access for Indian exports. These includes holding regular 
meetings and direct talks with partners through Joint Committees and Working Groups 
established under trade agreements to solve specific export problems to align with 
emerging global requirements, consultations with partner countries to resolve market 
access issues, technical discussions on sanitary and phytosanitary (SPS) measures, 
technical barriers to trade (TBT), standards, conformity assessment procedures and 
regulatory requirements and continuous engagement with stakeholders to identify and 
address market ac cess concerns in key export destinations, including the European 
Union, Africa and Southeast Asia. 
(d)       Government has undertaken various policy and facilitation measures to promote 
cross-border e-commerce exports, particularly for Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises 
(MSMEs), startups, artisans and other small exporters. Key initiatives include: 
(i) Export Promotion Mission (EPM): The Export Promotion Mission (EPM) was 
launched in 2025 to strengthen India’s export competitiveness with a total outlay of  
₹25,060 crore for the period FY 2025 –26 to FY 2030 –31. The EPM shall operate 
through two integrated sub-schemes: 
• NIRYAT PROTHSAHAN, focused on improving access to trade finance through 
instruments such as interest subvention, export factoring, collateral guarantees 
for export credit, credit guarantee for e -commerce exporters, and credit 
enhancement support; and 
• NIRYAT DISHA, focused on other trade enablers such as export quality and 
compliance support, international branding and packaging, market access 
initiatives, export logistics & warehousing, and trade intelligence. 
(ii) Implementation of the E-Commerce Export Hub (ECEH) initiative on a pilot basis to 
create an integrated ecosystem for e -commerce exports by facilitating logistics, 
customs clearances and other export-related services. 

3 
 
(iii) The District Export Hub (DEH) Initiative provides the district -level framework for 
decentralised export promotion. In each district, the effort is to identify and prioritise 3–
5 products/services with viable export potential for targeted interventions. 
(iv) Reforms to simplify exports through courier mode and reduce compliance burden: 
• The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has relaxed export reconciliation requirements 
for small-value exports up to ₹10 lakh by permitting closure of export transactions 
in the Export Data Processing and Monitoring System (EDPMS) on the basis of 
declarations furnished by exporters and reconciliation undertaken by banks. 
• The per-consignment value limit of ₹10 lakh for exports through courier mode 
has been removed vide DGFT Notification No. 67/2025 –26 dated March 27, 
2026 and CBIC Notification No. 34/2026 dated March 31, 2026. 
• CBIC Notification No. 33/2026 dated March 31, 2026 has simplified reverse 
logistics by facilitating the re -import of export rejects and returned goods in 
respect of cross-border e-commerce exports. 
(v)  PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan (NMP) was launched to facilitate data -based 
decisions related to integrated planning of multimodal infrastructure, thereby reducing 
logistics cost. 
(vi) Refund of Duties and Taxes on Exported Products (RoDTEP) Scheme aims to 
refund currently un-refunded duties/taxes/levies borne on the export product, including 
prior stage cumulative indirect taxes on goods and services used in production of th e 
exported products. 
(vii) The Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises has established 65 Export 
Facilitation Centers (EFCs) in its field offices across the country with the aim of providing 
requisite mentoring and handholding support to MSMEs in exporting their products and 
services. 
(viii) International Cooperation (IC) Scheme of Ministry of MSME aims to build capacity 
of MSMEs by facilitating their participation in international 
exhibitions/fairs/conferences/seminar/buyer-seller meets abroad as w ell as 
reimbursement of various costs.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
DEPARTMENT OF ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 339 
ANSWERED ON 21st JULY, 2026 
 
STRAY DOG MENACE 
 
339. SHRI M K RAGHAVAN:  
Will the Minister of FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING  
मत्स्यपालन, पशुपालन और डेयरी मंत्री 
be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has assessed the financial and administrative preparedness of Urban 
Local Bodies, Gram Panchayats and other Local Self -Government Institutions to effectively 
implement sterilisation, anti -rabies vaccination, animal birth control and stray dog management 
programmes in view of the increasing incidents of dog attacks in the country;  
 
(b) the details of funds allocated, released and utilised by the Union Government for supporting Local 
Self-Government Institutions in tackling the stray dog menace, including establishment of Animal 
Birth Control (ABC) centres, shelters, veterinary infras tructure and awareness programmes, during 
the last five years, State-wise; and  
 
(c) whether the Government has received requests from States seeking enhanced financial assistance 
for stray dog management due to inadequate resources available with local bodies and, if so, the 
details thereof along with the action taken in this regard? 
 
ANSWER  
THE MINISTER OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
(SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH ALIAS LALAN SINGH)  
 
(a) to (b) The Government of India has notified Animal Birth Control Rules, 2023 for implementation 
of Animal Birth Control (ABC) Programme for Dog population management through Sterilization. 
The Local Bodies are implementing the Animal Birth Control Programme through sterilization. The 
Hon’ble Supreme Court, in the matter of Suo -moto W.P.5 of 2025 has upheld animal birth control 
rules and issued detailed direction s and guidelines to the State Government s vide order dated 
19.05.2026. The arrangement of fund is the mandate of the State Government. However, the 
Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying, Government of India (GoI) is implementing Special 
Assistance to States for Capital Investment (SASCI) during 2026-27. The State Government can avail 
incentives under the scheme after taking various reform measures. Sterilisation and vaccination of 
dogs are included as an important reform measures under SASCI. The State Governments can 
establish dog shelter, animal shelter and animal birth control centres under the scheme.  
The Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying, GoI has made provision for registration of street 
dogs and animal birth control centers in National Digital Livestock Mission (NDLM) portal to 
improve monitoring of sterilization and anti -rabies vaccination programmes, and strengthen 
implementation of the Animal Birth Control Programme 
(c) No Sir.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
DEPARTMENT OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 341 
  ANSWERED ON 21/07/2026 
 
HOUSES SANCTIONED UNDER PMAY-G 
 
341.  Shri Govind Makthappa Karjol: 
 
Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  the details of houses sanctioned, completed and pending under 
the Pradhan Mantri Awaas Yojana–Gramin (PMAY-G) during each 
of the last five years, State and district-wise particularly in 
Karnataka; 
(b)  the details of funds allocated, released and utilized under PMAY-
G during the said period, State and district-wise particularly in 
Karnataka; 
(c)  the number of beneficiaries identified through the SECC-2011 
Permanent Wait List and Awaas+ Survey, the number approved, 
sanctioned and still awaiting sanction under PMAY-G, district-
wise in Karnataka; 
(d)  the details of financial assistance provided per beneficiary 
under PMAY-G, including convergence support for toilets, LPG, 
electricity and drinking water; 
(e)  whether the Government proposes to revise the unit assistance 
in view of rising construction costs, if so the details thereof; and 
(f)  the steps taken to expedite completion of pending houses, 
ensure timely release and utilization of funds and achieve 
saturation of eligible beneficiaries particularly in rural and 
backward districts of Karnataka? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
(DR. CHANDRA SEKHAR PEMMASANI) 
(a): The Ministry of Rural Development is implementing Pradhan 
Mantri Awaas Yojana- Gramin (PMAY-G) with effect from 1st April 
2016 to achieve the objective of "Housing for All" in rural areas by 
providing assistance to 4.95 crore eligible rural households with 
basic amenities by March 2029. As on 16.07.2026, a cumulative 
target of 4.18 crore houses has been allotted to States/UT, out of 

Page 2 of 6 
 
which, 3.92 crore houses have been sanctioned, and 3.10 crore 
houses have been constructed. In the last five years (2021-2022 – 
2025-26), 1.99 crore houses have been sanctioned, 1.61 crore houses 
have been completed. The State-wise and year-wise details are at 
Annexure A. 
In the State of Karnataka, in the last five years, 4,12,283 houses 
were sanctioned and 80,786 houses were completed. The District 
level data of all States/UTs related to houses allocated and 
completed is available in public domain on the programme website at 
www.pmayg.dord.gov.in.  
(b): Under PMAY-G, during the last five years, Rs. 1,31,102.84 crore 
was released as central share of funds to States/UTs, and Rs. 
2,17,856.01 crore (including State share) was utilized . The State-
wise and year-wise details are at Annexure B.  
In the State of Karnataka, Rs. 661.71 crore was released as 
central share of funds, and Rs. 1525.84 crore was utilised during the 
last five years. The Central Assistance under PMAY-G is released 
directly to the State/Union Territory (UT) considering the State/UT as 
a unit. Further release of these funds to beneficiaries is done by the 
respective State/UT Governments. The District-level data related to 
funds released & utilised Financial Year wise is available in public 
domain on the programme website at www.pmayg.dord.gov.in 
(c): A total of 10.85 lakh households were identified and included in 
PWL from SECC, 2011 and Awaas+ data in the State of Karnataka, out 
of which 5.69 lakh houses have been sanctioned.  In the State of 
Karnataka, equivalent targets have already been allocated. The 
district-wise PWL in the State is provided in Annexure C.  
(d): Under the Pradhan Mantri Awaas Yojana–Gramin (PMAY-G), 
financial assistance of ₹1.20 lakh per house is provided in plain areas 
and ₹1.30 lakh per house in hilly States, including the Union 
Territories of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh.  In addition to the unit 
assistance provided under the scheme, financial assistance of 
₹12,000 is extended for the construction of toilets through 
convergence with the Swachh Bharat Mission–Gramin (SBM-G). 
Further, there is a provision for providing prescribed person-days of 
unskilled wage employment within the approved scheme parameters, 
at prevailing wage rates to each PMAY-G beneficiary for the 

Page 3 of 6 
 
construction of their houses through convergence with MGNREGS/VB 
G-RAM G. 
PMAY-G households are also provided with piped drinking water 
through convergence with the Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) and Har Ghar 
Nal Se Jal (HGNSJ) of the Department of Drinking Water and 
Sanitation, Ministry of Jal Shakti, or other similar schemes. In 
addition, beneficiaries are supported with electricity connections 
through relevant schemes implemented by the Ministry of Power, 
State Governments, or UT Administrations, and are provided 
Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) connections under the Pradhan Mantri 
Ujjwala Yojana (PMUY) of the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas 
or other relevant schemes. 
Convergence under PMAY-G also includes the inclusion of 
women members of beneficiary households in Self-Help Groups 
(SHGs), thereby promoting their social and economic empowerment. 
At the national level, as on 16.07.2026, a total of 3.08 crore 
houses have been provided with toilets, 2.43 crore with water 
connections, 3.07 crore with electricity connections, 2.9 crore with 
LPG connections, and 1.35 crore beneficiary households have been 
associated with Self-Help Groups (SHGs). 
(e): The Government has approved the continuation of PMAY-G till 
March, 2029 as per the existing unit assistance for construction of 2 
crore more houses.  
(f): The Ministry has taken several steps towards enhancing the 
pace of sanction and completion of houses and ensuring timely 
release and utilization of funds under the scheme. These include 
timely allocation of targets to the States/UTs, monitoring and 
supervision of the scheme through an analytic dashboard, using 
latest IT tools and technologies, organization of Workshops/ Review 
Meetings at the national and regional level for review of physical and 
financial progress, timely release of funds as per requirements of 
States/UTs and regular follow ups with the State to ensure release of 
central and state share of funds.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS’ WELFARE 
DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS’ WELFARE 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 342 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 21st July, 2026 
 
FINANCIAL ASSISTANCE FOR NATURAL FARMING 
 
342. Dr. Anand Kumar: 
 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण 
मंũी be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government is aware of the fact that in the first one to two years of 
switching over to natural/organic farming, the yield of many farmers temporarily 
reduced, due to which they become dependent on chemical fertilizers again; 
(b) whether the Government has made any assessment of the impact on the income 
and production of farmers adopting natural farming in the initial years; 
(c) whether the Government proposes to provide special incentives, direct financial 
assistance or any other support to such farmers during the first two years of the 
transition period; and 
(d) if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor? 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण राǛ मंũी                                        (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
 
(a) & (b) : Indian Council of Agricultural Research has initiated study from 2020-21 
through All India Network Programme on Natural Farming (previously AINP-Organic 
Farming) with 20 cooperating centres covering 16 States to evaluate 8 major cropping 
systems and develop package of practices under Natural farming besides evaluation 
of cropping systems under organic farming. The scheme involves 11 State Agricultural 
Universities, 8 ICAR institutes/centres and 1 deemed to be university. 

Studies on the benefits of natural farming have shown that if natural farming is adopted 
with the right techniques and in a balanced manner, yields improve. The experiences 
of many farmers have also proven that improving soil health in the initial years 
improves crop quality, taste, and long-term yield. Furthermore, reducing chemical 
costs increases farmers' net profits. Mulching in natural farming helps maintain soil 
moisture, control weeds, and increase organic matter in the soil. This also increases 
the activity of soil microorganisms and improves soil health. Multi-cropping increases 
biodiversity in the field, reduces the incidence of pests and diseases, and improves 
nutrient utilization. The finding is as below; 
(i) Under the network research, crop system-based natural farming packages 
have been developed for various states, such as groundnut + sesame – fennel 
+ cabbage (Rajasthan and Gujarat), soybean + maize – wheat + mustard 
(Chhattisgarh and Madhya Pradesh), and cassava (Kerala).  
(ii) In Bajaura (Himachal Pradesh), Almora (Uttarakhand) and Gangtok (Sikkim), 
the average system productivity (soybean equivalent) of 6475 kg/ha/year was 
recorded in the soybean + maize – vegetable pea + coriander (green leaf) crop 
system (in 5 years) under completely natural farming, which was about 5 
percent higher than organic farming/integrated crop management.  
(iii)  In Bhopal and Jabalpur (Madhya Pradesh) and Raipur (Chhattisgarh), the 
average system productivity (soybean equivalent) of 3346 kg/ha/year was 
recorded in the soybean + maize – wheat + mustard crop system (in 5 years), 
which was found to be equivalent to integrated crop management and organic 
farming. 
(iv) S.K. In Nagar (Gujarat), Ajmer, and Udaipur (Rajasthan), the average system 
productivity (cowpea equivalent) of 9209 kg/ha/year was recorded in the 
cowpea + maize/peanut + sesame – fennel + cauliflower/cabbage cropping 
system (in 5 years) under complete natural farming. This was found to be 
comparable to integrated crop management. 
(v) Natural farming (NF) management has shown a clear improvement in soil 
health indicators. Soil organic carbon (SOC) levels increased in natural farming 
fields over a period of 2–3 years. For example, in trials conducted in the 
Himalayan regions, SOC increased from approximately 0.90% to 1.15%. The 
number and diversity index of microorganisms in natural farming soils was 
found to be higher than in soils cultivated with chemical fertilizers. The 
abundance and balanced distribution of beneficial bacteria, fungi, and 

actinomycetes were observed, indicating the development of a healthy soil 
ecosystem over time. This increase in organic matter and microorganisms in 
the soil under natural farming improves nutrient cycling and soil structure, laying 
a strong foundation for long-term soil fertility and crop production sustainability. 
           Further, NITI Aayog Assessment Report states that approximately 91.2% of 
farmers adopting natural farming experience, increased crop productivity and 
significantly improved soil health. 90.1% of farmers reported that adopting natural 
farming has reduced input costs (production costs). 
 
(c) & (d) : Under the Mission, there is a provision for an Output Based Incentive of 
₹4000/- per acre, per year to a farmer for 2 years (up to 1 acre per farmer). The 
incentive support is for farmers to practice Natural Farming, to train more farmers, 
upkeep of livestock, preparation of natural farming inputs including purchase of mixing 
& storage containers or purchase of inputs from Bio-input Resource Centers (BRCs) 
etc.

PROTECTION OF PLANT VARIETIES AND FARMERS' RIGHTS  
 
343. SHRI ANURAG SINGH THAKUR:  
 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण मंũी 
be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the details of activities undertaken under the Protection of Plant Varieties and Farmers' 
Rights (PPV&FR) Act in Himachal Pradesh, including awareness programmes, 
registration facilitation and benefit-sharing measures for farmers;  
(b) the details of plants, seed varieties registered or protected by the PPV&FR Authority 
in the State during the last three years including varieties developed by ICAR institutions 
and agricultural universities, crop-wise;  
(c) the details of work being undertaken by ICAR institutes and Krishi Vigyan Kendras 
(KVKs) in Himachal Pradesh for varietal development, seed multiplication, farmer training 
and technology dissemination in hill agriculture during the above period;  
(d) the quantum of funds allocated, released and utilised for PPV&FR-related, ICAR-
related and KVK activities in the State during the above period; and  
(e) the steps being taken to promote farmers' rights, conservation of traditional varieties 
and incentivisation of innovation in the hill agriculture ecosystems of the country? 
 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण राǛ मंũी (SHRI RAM NATH THAKUR) 
(a): The Protection of Plant Varieties and Farmers' Rights (PPV&FR) Authority has been 
conducting several activities including capacity building, fairs & exhibitions in Himachal 
Pradesh to create awareness about registration of traditional varieties as well as about 
farmers’ rights under Protection of Plant Varieties and Farmers' Rights Act, 2001. To 
facilitate registration, the PPV&FR Authority has also established its branch office at 
Palampur in Himachal Pradesh. The details of activities conducted in the State of 
Himachal Pradesh during last three years is given in Annexure-I.  
The PPV&FR Authority also confers awards, rewards and accord recognition to 
farmer(s) and farming communities who have contributed in conservation and 
preservation of plant genetic resources of economic importance. A list of farmer(s) and 
farming communities who have been conferred with Plant Genome Saviour Community 
Award, Plant Genome Saviour Farmer Reward or Plant Genome Saviour Farmer 
Recognition is given in Annexure-II.   
(b):  The crop-wise detail of plants, seed varieties registered by the PPV&FR Authority 
in the State during last three years (01.01.2023 to 01.07.2026), including varieties 
developed by agricultural universities, is as under:

Further, no variety of ICAR Institutions has been registered with the PPV&FR 
Authority in Himachal Pradesh during last three years. 
(c): Indian Council of Agricultural Research - All India Coordinated Research Project 
(ICAR-AICRP) on Seed (Crops) has a participating centre at Ch. Sarwan Kumar Himachal 
Pradesh Krishi Vishvavidyalaya (CSKHPKV), Palampur, which undertakes breeder seed 
production and quality seed production of improved crop varieties suitable for hill 
agriculture. 
During last three years, the Centre produced 1,957.20 quintals of breeder seed and 
17,512 quintals of quality seed, thereby contributing to the availability of quality seed in 
the Himachal Pradesh. As a part of technology dissemination, improved varieties of finger 
millet, barnyard millet, amaranth, maize, lentil, garlic and French bean were demonstrated 
in Himachal Pradesh during the last three years. Also, Black Soybean VL Bhat has been 
released and notified for the State of Himachal Pradesh. 
Further, 13 Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVKs) are functioning in the State of Himachal 
Pradesh. These KVKs are engaged in the dissemination of outcomes of agricultural 
research among farmers through technology assessment, demonstration and capacity 
development of extension functionaries of the State Government and farmers. 
During the last three years, the details of activities undertaken by these KVKs are as 
under: 
i. 23,960 demonstrations on improved agricultural technologies were organized; 
ii. 0.93 lakh individuals including farmers, farm women, rural youth, extension 
personnel were trained through various training programmes; 
iii. About two lakh stakeholders were made aware of various technologies related to 
agriculture and allied sectors through different extension activities; 
iv. In order to promote adoption of improved crop varieties, the KVKs produced 
5567.35 quintals of quality seed of field crops and 18.27 lakh planting materials of 
horticultural crops. 
(d): During last three years, the details of funds released and utilized for PPV&FR-
related, ICAR-related and KVK activities in the State are as under: 
i. PPV&FRA: Rs. 2.94 crore has been released for activities related to PPV&FRA 
including conducting various training, seminars etc. and fund given to DUS test 
centres in the State.  

ii. ICAR: Rs. 5.31 crore was released to the Centre for implementation of the AICRP 
on Seed (Crops) activities. 
iii. KVKs: Rs. 10.33 crore was released and utilized by the KVKs of Himachal Pradesh 
for carrying out their mandated activities. 
(e): The Government is implementing several measures to promote farmers' rights, 
conserve traditional crop varieties, and foster innovation across the country, including in 
hill agriculture ecosystems. The major initiatives are as follows: 
i. Statutory recognition of farmers as breeders under the PPV&FR Act, 2001, 
enabling registration of farmers' varieties free of cost and protection of their right to 
save, use, exchange and sell seed of registered varieties, other than branded seed; 
ii. National Gene Fund has been established under the PPV&FR Act, 2001, with the 
aim of promoting conservation and sustainable use of plant genetic resources, 
including traditional varieties. It seeks to reward and incentivize farmers and 
communities engaged in conservation, improvement, and preservation of plant 
genetic resources through benefit-sharing, awards, and recognition schemes, while 
also supporting capacity building activities to safeguard agro-biodiversity. 
iii. Government is implementing an intervention titled "Boosting Seed Production of 
Traditional Varieties" under the Seeds component of the National Food Security & 
Nutrition Mission (NFSNM), aimed at promoting traditional varieties of crops. Under 
this intervention, financial assistance is extended for seed distribution, seed 
production, capacity building, and the creation/development of seed banks for 
traditional varieties, in accordance with prescribed cost norms. 
iv. Strengthening of ICAR institutions and Krishi Vigyan Kendras in hill and mountain 
States for location-specific varietal development suited to fragile hill ecosystems; 
v. Promotion of climate-resilient, bio-fortified and region-specific crop varieties to 
strengthen the resilience and sustainability of hill agriculture. 
vi. Government provides financial assistance to the States/UTs and implementing 
agencies for seed related activities including production and distribution of high 
yielding varieties, Seed infrastructure facilities through various Crop Development 
Programmes viz. National Food Security and Nutrition Mission, National Mission on 
Edible Oils–Oilseeds (NMEO-Oilseeds), Mission for Aatmanirbharta in Pulses, 
Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana and National Mission on High Yielding Seeds 
(NMHYS). 
vii. Government is implementing “Innovation and Agri-Entrepreneurship Development” 
programme under Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana (RKVY) and also set up a fund 
namely AgriSURE (Agri Fund for Start Ups & Rural Enterprises) with an objective 
to promote innovation and agri-entrepreneurship by providing financial support to 
startups working in agriculture sector and nurturing an incubation ecosystem in the 
country including in hill agriculture ecosystem.  
viii. Under the Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture (MIDH), Government 
provides support for setting up of Centres of Excellence (CoEs) across the country 
including in hill ecosystem with the objective of promoting excellence in horticultural 
practices, enhancing productivity, and ensuring sustainable development in the 
sector.

Insurance and Credit Schemes for Small Scale and Marginal Fishermen 
 
344. Shri Bapi Haldar:  
 
Will the Minister of FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING be pleased to state: 
(a)  whether the Government has launched or proposes to launch any targeted insurance 
and credit schemes for small-scale and marginal fishermen in the Sundarbans delta;  
(b)  if so, the total number of beneficiaries covered during the last three years, district-wise;  
(c)  whether the Government has received any representations seeking mobile fish 
procurement and cold-chain infrastructure to support remote fishing communities;  
(d)  whether any budget has been earmarked under Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada 
Yojana (PMMSY ) or other schemes for fisher community development in the 
Sundarbans; and  
(e)  if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH ALIAS LALAN SINGH 
 
(a) and (b): The Department of Fisheries, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and 
Dairying. Government of India is implementing the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana 
(PMMSY) with a total investment of Rs. 20,990.79 crore from the financial year 2020-21 to till 
date for development of fisheries in all States/Union Territories  including Sundarbans delta 
region of West Bengal .  The scheme inter-alia provides social security measure to fishers, 
fish workers through group accidental insurance coverage to both  marine and inland fishers 
and allied fish workers wherein the entire insurance premium amount is shared between the 
Centre  and State in the ratio of 60:40, 90:10 for the Himalayan & North Eastern States and 
in the case of the Union Territories, the entire premium amount is paid by the Centre.  The 
insurance coverage provided under the PMMSY includes (i) Rs.5,00,000/ - against death or 
permanent total disability, (ii) Rs.2,50,000/ - for permanent partial disability and (iii) 
hospitalization expenses in the event of accident for a sum of Rs. 25,000/.  West Bengal did 
not participate in Group Accidental Insurance Scheme (GAIS) during last three years under 
the aforesaid scheme. Hence, no beneficiaries from West Bengal including Sundarbans areas 
have been provided insurance coverage. 
 
The Government of India from the financial year 2018-19, has extended the Kisan Credit Card 
(KCC) facility to fishers and fish famers to help them to meet their working capital requirement. 
1,498 Kisan Credit Cards have been sanctioned to fishers and fish farmers from West Bengal. 
The district wise details are at Annexure. 

 
 
 
 
(c) to (e) As reported by the Government of west Bengal, no specific representation seeking 
mobile fish procurement and cold -chain infrastructure exclusively for the remote fishing 
communities of the Sundarbans has been received. However, a dministrative approval of 
Rs.10 crore has been accorded under the Central  Sector Component of PMMSY during 
2024-25 for the development of five identified fishing villages in West Bengal as Climate 
Resilient Coastal Fishermen Villages  (2 crores per village) including  the villages of 
Akshayanagar and Madanganj in South 24 Parganas district situated in the Sunderbans delta 
region. In addition, Fish Transport Vehicles, insulated boxes with weighing Machines and 
allied facilities have been included under the economic activities of the Climate Resilient 
Coastal Fishermen Villages Project.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA

Registered Fishermen Families 
345. Shri Murasoli S:  
Will the Minister of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying  be pleased to 
state: 
(a)  the number of registered fishermen families in Thanjavur district in Tamil Nadu 
and the assistance disbursed under the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana 
(PMMSY) during the last three years; 
(b)  whether the Government is aware of the fact that inland fishermen dependent on 
the Cauvery river system have reported declining catch due to reduced water flow and 
also the steps taken by the Government to rectify the same; and 
(c)  the steps taken by the Government to promote inland aquaculture as an 
alternative livelihood in delta districts? 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
(SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH ALIAS LALAN SINGH) 
(a) As per the information received from Go vernment of Tamil Nadu, a total number of 
1,480 inland fish farmers are registered with the District Fish Farmers Development 
Agency (DFFDA) and a total number of 1,234 inland fishermen  are registered in inland 
fishermen cooperative societies in Thanjavur district of Tamil Nadu. Funds to the tune of  
Rs. 196.30 Lakhs have been disbursed under the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada 
Yojana (PMMSY), during the last three years (2021 -22 to 20 23-24) for the 
implementation of the projects namely construction of fresh water finfish hatchery (2 
units), construction of seed rearing ponds (07 ha), construction of new grow out ponds 
and input assistance (25 ha), input subsidy assistance for grow out ponds (25 ha), 
establishment of small Biofloc  units (09 units)  and establishment of re -circulatory 
aquaculture system (01 unit). 
(b) As informed by the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) the Central Inland 
Fisheries Research Institute (CIFRI) has conducted a study in the Cauvery River stretch 
in Thanjavur Dis trict, Tamil Nadu. The study revealed that extensive diversion of  river 
water for agricultural purposes through a well -developed canal network has resulted in 
reduced flow in this stretch for most of the year. The river stretch receives water mainly 
during the monsoon season and through regulated releases from upstream reservoirs. 
Consequently, riverine capture fisheries in the Thanjavur stretch remain seasonal,  with 
limited intensity.  

Under the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY)  implemented by the 
Department of Fisheries , Government of India  (DoF, GoI) , the River Ranching 
Programme was implemented in Tamil Nadu, under which 176 lakh advanced fingerlings 
were released in river stretches across the State (including 59.76 lakh in Cauvery riverine 
system) to enhance fishery resources and conserve native fish biodiversity, enhance fish 
catches and protect the livelihood of inland fishers . This stocking is anticipated to 
increase the fish production to 220 tonnes in the Cauvery river system thereby enhancing 
inland fish production and supporting the livelihood of inland fishers.  
(c) The DoF, GoI since 2015, has substantially stepped-up investment in fisheries sector 
through various schemes for holistic development of fisheries, inland aquaculture and 
welfare of fishermen in the country including delta districts of Tamil Nadu (Thanjavur, 
Tiruvarur, Nagapattinam, Mayiladuthurai and Cuddalore). The Government of Tamil 
Nadu has implemented several activities under the PMMSY and the state schemes to 
enhance the fish production, area expansion  under aquaculture, promotion of 
sustainable livelihoods and intensive aquaculture  by adopting  technologies such as 
Biofloc Systems and Recirculating Aquaculture Systems (RAS). In addition, subsidy 
assistance is provided under the PMMSY for fishing gear to reduce the operational costs 
of inland fishers. 
The Government of Tamil Nadu  has informed that subsidy assistance under PMMSY 
has been provided to 355 beneficiaries from Delta districts for activities su ch as input 
assistance and construction of freshwater finfish hatcheries, new seed rearing ponds, 
grow out ponds, establishment of Biofloc units, RAS, ornamental units, and purchase of
