TEXTILE EXPORT TARGET AND POLICY SUPPORT 
 
374.   THIRU DAYANIDHI MARAN: 
 
 
Will the Minister of TEXTILES वस्त्रमंत्री 
be pleased to state : 
 
(a) the details regarding roadmap prepared by the Union Government to enable Tamil Nadu to 
achieve its assigned textile export target of US$21 billion by 2030, including Tiruppur's target of 
US$11.5 billion, and the financial and policy support proposed therefor;  
(b) the details regarding present status of the PM -MITRA Mega Textile Park at Virudhunagar, 
including land acquisition, infrastructure creation, funds sanctioned & released, industries 
allotted & the timeline for commencement of operations;  
(c) the details of the proposed scheme for modernisation of textile machinery, including financial 
assistance for Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) in textile clusters such as 
Tiruppur, Coimbatore, Erode & Karur;  
(d) whether the Government proposes to support the establishment of hostels for women workers 
& new textile clusters in Tamil Nadu and the details thereof; and  
(e) if so, the details and steps taken to ensure that the transition towards man -made fibres & 
sustainable textiles does not adversely affect cotton -based Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises 
(MSMEs) and employment in Tamil Nadu? 
 
उत्तर 
ANSWER 
वस्त्रराज्‍ यमंत्री(श्री‍पबित्र‍मार्घेररटा) 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR TEXTILES  
 (SHRI PABITRA MARGHERITA) 
 
(a):      Tamil Nadu’s exports of textile and apparel including Handicrafts stood at Rs. 68791.7 
Crore in 2025 -26, exhibiting a growth of 1.4% compared to Rs. 67863.4 Crore in 2024 -25. 
Tiruppur’s exports of textile and apparel including handicrafts stood a t Rs. 38676.5 Crore in 
2025-26, exhibiting a growth of 3.0% compared to Rs. 37563.6 Crore in 2024 -25. Tiruppur is 
Tamil Nadu's leading textile and apparel export district and is globally recognized as the 
Knitwear Capital of India. The district functions a s a fully integrated manufacturing hub 
covering spinning, knitting, dyeing, processing, and garmenting, along with strong backward 
linkages in yarn and fabric and forward linkages in exports and logistics.  Tiruppur has the 
potential to solidify its positio n as India's premier textile and apparel export powerhouse by 
2030. Its production -centric cluster model, supported by a robust base of over 90,000 MSME 
units and strategic proximity to major ports like Chennai, Tuticorin, and Cochin, provides a 
unique competitive advantage in large-scale, compliance-driven global supply chains.  
 

The Ministry of Textiles successfully conducted the Textiles Summit 2026 in June 2026 
which brought together representatives from State Governments including Tamilnadu, industry, 
and academia to foster collaborative dialogue on the growth and roadmap of the textile sector. 
Discussions focused on strategies to enhance competitiveness, strengthen the textile value chain, 
and achieve the vision of increasing India’s textile and appare l exports to USD 100 billion by 
2030.  
The Government is implementing various schemes and initiatives to boost the Indian 
textile and apparel sector including Tamilnadu and enhance its competitiveness. The major 
schemes/initiatives include PM Mega Integrat ed Textile Regions and Apparel (PM MITRA) 
Parks Scheme; Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme; National Technical Textiles Mission; 
SAMARTH – Scheme for Capacity Building in Textile Sector; Silk Samagra -2; National 
Handloom Development Programme; Nation al Handicrafts Development Programme; 
Comprehensive Handicrafts Cluster Development Scheme; Rebate of State and Central Taxes 
and Levies (RoSCTL) Scheme; Remission of Duties and Taxes on Exported Products (RoDTEP) 
Scheme; Export Promotion Mission (EPM), co mprising Niryat Protsahan and Niryat Disha; and 
Credit Guarantee Scheme for Exporters (CGSE). 
(b):       As per present status of PM MITRA Park at Virudhunagar, it  has achieved 100% land 
acquisition, and has received Environmental Clearance. Joint Venture  agreement is signed 
between central and state government  and land has been transferred in name of SPV. A DPR 
worth Rs. 1,894 Cr. for PM MITRA Park, Tamil Nadu has been approved . The Park has been 
appraised in 98th NPG meeting held on 12.08.2025. The core  infrastructure EPC package has 
been awarded to a construction Company. The 1st installment of Development Capital Support 
(DCS) amounting to ₹50 crore has been released to the project. 
 
(c to  e) :  In the Union Budget 2026 -27, the Government had announced  an Integrated 
Programme for the Textile Sector comprising five sub -components, including the Textile 
Expansion and Employment Scheme, which envisages modernization of traditional textile 
clusters through capital support for machinery, technology upgradati on and establishment of 
common testing and certification centres.  
 
            The Government is promoting balanced growth of the textile sector through initiatives 
relating to man -made fibres (MMF), technical textiles, sustainability, technology upgradat ion, 
machinery modernisation, skill development and value addition across the textile value chain. 
These initiatives are aimed at promoting sustainable growth, employment generation and 
enhancing the global competitiveness of the Indian textile industry. The Government of India has 
adopted a balanced approach by temporarily exempting customs duties on cotton imports from 
1st June till 31st October 2026 to augment availability of cotton.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 375 
TO BE ANSWERED ON THE 21ST  JULY, 2026 
 
DIGITAL AGRICULTURE MISSION 
 
 
375.  SHRI THARANIVENTHAN M S: 
 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE (कृ ͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण मंğी) 
be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government will furnish the details of initiatives, pilots and projects 
implemented under the Digital Agriculture Mission, including the timeline of its approval, 
rollout and current status across States, State-wise including Arani constituency of Tamil 
Nadu and year-wise; 
(b) the details of funds allocated, released and utilised under the Mission during the last 
five years, along with the components covered such as digital land records, farmer registry, 
crop mapping, soil health data, advisory services and use of AI/remote sensing technologies 
(c) whether the Government has assessed the impact of the Mission on improving farm 
productivity, price discovery, risk management and access to credit and insurance, and if 
so, the findings thereof; and 
(d) the steps taken to ensure inclusive digital access for small and marginal farmers, 
particularly in Tamil Nadu, and to safeguard data privacy and interoperability of agricultural 
databases? 
 
ANSWER 
 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
कृ ͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण राÏय मंğी (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
 
(a): The Government approved the Digital Agriculture Mission in September 2024. The 
Mission envisages the creation of a Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) for Agriculture, such 
as AgriStack, Krishi Decision Support System, a Comprehensive Soil Fertility & Profile Map 
and other IT initiatives undertaken by the Central Government/State Government to enable 
a robust digital agriculture ecosystem in the country as a single source of truth for information 
on farmers, crops, livestock and fisheries and farmer centric digital solutions. The main 
features and their outcomes of the above initiatives are as follows: 
  

 
I. The AgriStack DPI consists of three foundational registries or databases 
associated with the agriculture sector, i.e., Farmer Registry, Geo-Reference 
Village Maps and the Crop Sown Registry, all created and maintained by the 
State Governments/ Union Territories. As of 16th July, 2026, more than 10.15 
Crore Farmer IDs have been created. Out of these, 2,20,602 Farmers' IDs have 
been created in Tiruvannamalai district of Tamil Nadu, which includes 
Arani Constituency. During Rabi 2025-26, the Digital Crop Survey (DCS) was 
conducted in 648 Districts covering more than 31.3 crore plots across the 
country, including Tiruvannamalai district. The current status of Farmer IDs 
and year-wise DCS data (since inception) across the nation is given in 
Annexures I, IIA, IIB, IIC and IID. 
II. Krishi Decision Support System DPI has been developed, which is a geo-spatial 
platform that integrates satellite imagery, weather, soil, and crop data using 
Geographic Information System (GIS) to support agricultural planning and 
decision-making.  
III. A Nationwide Soil Resource Mapping project has been initiated by the Soil and 
Land Use Survey of India (SLUSI), for reserve inventory soils at a village level 
on a 1:10,000 scale using high-resolution satellite and ground data. As of June, 
2026, a soil survey of 52.38 million hectares has been carried out across the 
country.  
IV. Digital General Crop Estimation System (DGCES) is a robust crop production 
estimation system that requires truthful and reliable data on area and yield. 
While the Digital Crop Survey provides crop sown area in near real-time, the 
new Digital General Crop Estimation System (DGCES) provides accurate and 
timely crop yield data for evidence-based crop production estimates. Across the 
country, Digitized Crop Cutting Experiments have been conducted in 43,105 
villages during 2025-26.  
  

 
(b) The yearly funds released under the Digital Agriculture Mission (since inception) for 
various components, including the Farmer Registry, Digital Crop Survey (DCS), Digital 
Geospatial Crop Estimation System (DGCES), Soil Profile, and other activities at both the 
Central and State levels, are provided in Annexure–III.   
 
(c) The government consistently evaluates the outcomes of the mission. States are using 
Farmer IDs to ease the lives of farmers. Farmer ID has enabled the integration of Direct 
Benefit Transfer (DBT) schemes such as registrations under Pradhan Mantri Kisan 
Samman Nidhi Yojna (PM Kisan), Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojna (PMFBY), Minimum 
Support Price (MSP) based procurement, access to credit delivery, input distribution, 
and disaster relief.  
 
 
(d) Although internet penetration has increased in rural areas of the country, including 
Tamil Nadu, additional steps have been taken to ensure the digital inclusion of farmers, 
including small & marginal farmers. They can use existing support structures like Farmer-
Producer Organisations (FPOs), Krishi Sakhis, and Common Service Centres (CSCs) to 
get them registered on AgriStack and access services and benefits. Further, the States 
are organizing camps to create a Farmer’s Registry so that no farmer is left out of getting 
the benefits of AgriStack. 
 
Further, the State Farmer Registry is built in a federated architecture, which means 
the ownership of the data is with the respective States. The Ministry of Agriculture and 
Farmers Welfare has developed the Agri Stack in accordance with the Digital Personal 
Data Protection Act, 2023 and the Digital Personal Data Protection Rules 2025, to ensure 
the complete privacy of farmers' data.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
DEPARTMENT OF ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 377 
ANSWERED ON 21st JULY , 2026 
 
SELF-RELIANT GAUSHALAS 
 
377. SHRI ANUP SANJAY DHOTRE:  
Will the Minister of FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING  
मत्स्यपालन, पशुपालन और डेयरी मंत्री 
be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has formulated or is in the process of formulating any comprehensive 
strategy to make Gaushalas self-reliant through activities such as compost fertilizer production, milk 
and ghee processing, and bio -gas/based power generation u nder the Cow/Progeny Development 
Scheme and if so, the details thereof;  
 
(b) the steps taken by the Government to enhance public –private partnerships in the management 
and operation of Gaushalas and to promote the production of medicines and other useful products 
derived from cow-based resources; and  
 
(c) whether any financial or technical assistance is being provided by the Government to such 
Gaushalas for capacity building and value addition and if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
(SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH ALIAS LALAN SINGH)  
 
(a) Animal Husbandry and management of stray cattle including making availability of fodder 
for stray animals is a state subject.  
 
However, t he Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying , Government of India  is 
implementing the Animal Husbandry Infrastructure Development Fund (AHIDF) to incentivize 
establishment of dairy processing and value addition infrastructure. This scheme also provides 
assistance for establishment of infrastructure for animal waste to wealth management (agri -waste 
management). Under this component the eligible e ntities can establish bio -gas/based power 
generation and compost fertilizer  (Phosphate Rich Organic Manure). The eligible e ntities are 
Individuals, MSME, Private Companies, FPO, Dairy Cooperatives and Section 8 companies.  
 
The scheme envisages 3% interest subvention for eight years with a two-year moratorium on term 
loan up to 90% of the project cost borrowed from scheduled banks and institutions such as 
NABARD, NCDC, NDDB, and SIDBI. In addition, the Central Government has established a 
Credit Guarantee Trust to provide Credit Guarantee up to 25% of term loan to MSME and Dairy 
Cooperatives. Eligible entities can also take benefit of dovetailing with various central and state 
government initiatives to ensure holistic development of the dairy ecosystem. 
 

The Ministry of New and Renewable Energy is promoting the installation of small biogas, medium 
size biogas plants. Under GOBARdhan (Galvanizing Organic Bio-Agro Resources Dhan) scheme 
implemented by Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, assistance is provided for setting up of 
community/ cluster-based bio-gas plant. 
 
(b) & (c) Since the establishment of gaushala is State subject, the policy of running of gaushala is 
determined by the respective state government. States, if required, can frame policy for running of 
gaushala through Public P rivate Partnership model. The Animal Welfare Board of India promotes 
scientific Gaushala management through awareness and capacity-building programmes. The Board 
has developed a Gaushala Management Training Module and organizes training programmes, 
workshops and seminars on scientific management of Gaushalas, Panchgavya, utilization of cattle 
bio-resources (cow dung and cow urine), and production of Panchgavya and other value -added 
products, with the objective of promoting sustainable and self-reliant Gaushalas

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF COMMERCE & INDUSTRY 
DEPARTMENT FOR PROMOTION OF INDUSTRY AND INTERNAL TRADE

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 378. 
      TO BE ANSWERED ON TUESDAY, THE 21ST JULY, 2026. 
 
INDUSTRIAL PARKS 
 
378.  SHRI SANJAY DINA PATIL: 
PROF. VARSHA EKNATH GAIKWAD: 
 
Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY be pleased to state: 
वाणिज्य  एवं उद्योग मंत्री 
(a)  whether the Government has launched the Bharat Audyogik Vikas Yojana 
(BHAVYA) to promote the competitive development of industrial  parks in the 
country and if so, the details thereof, State-wise; 
 
(b)  whether any industrial parks in Mumbai in Maharashtra have been identified, 
approved or  proposed for support under the Scheme and, if so, the details 
thereof; 
 
(c)  the criteria adopte d for selection and evaluation of industrial parks under the 
Scheme and whether industrial parks in Mumbai meet the prescribed criteria; 
 
(d)  the details of financial assistance, infrastructure support and capacity -building 
measures proposed for eligible industrial parks in Mumbai; 
 
(e)  whether the yojana is expected to attract additional domestic and foreign 
investment into Mumbai; and 
 
(f)  the projected benefits of the Scheme in terms of industrial development, 
employment generation, ease of doing business and strengthening Mumbai's 
position as a leading industrial and investment destination? 
 
ANSWER 
 
वाणिज्य  एवं उद्योग मंत्रालय में राज्य मंत्री (श्री णिणिन प्रसाद)   
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE & INDUSTRY 
(SHRI JITIN PRASADA) 
 
(a) to (f): Bharat Audyogik Vikas Yojana (BHAVYA) is a Central Sector Scheme notified 
on 10.04.2026 for development of investment -ready industrial parks to enable 
investors to ground investment with ease, thereby adding to the manufacturing 
capacity in the country. 
The total financial outlay for the Scheme is ₹ 33,660 crore and the duration of 
the Scheme is for a period of 6 years. 

Under the Scheme, financial assistance is to be provided for development of 
100 industrial parks. In the first phase, 50 projects are to be taken up, with one 
or more rounds of selection. 
The mandatory eligibility criteria include minimum contiguous land area of 100 
acres in non -hilly States and 25 acres in hilly States, North Eastern Region, 
Union Territories and States having population below one crore as well as 
availability of 90 percent encumbrance -free land at the time of submission of 
application. 
The selection of projects is based on Challenge mode with evaluation on 
parameters such as  connectivity and site suitability, quality of DPR, the 
demand for industrial land provision of services at site, and policy enablers for 
ensuring investments in the developed park, being provided by the State/UT 
Governments. 
Applications meeting the mandatory eligibility criteria would be evaluated and 
scored in accordance with the evaluation criteria prescribed under the Scheme 
guidelines issued on 23.05.2026. No proposal has been received on the portal 
till date. 
Financial assistance upto Rs. 1 crore per acre is allowed for eligible 
components listed in the scheme guidelines. This contribution is in the form of 
equity from the Centre, with land contributed by the State/UT Government. 
The Scheme is designed to further the objective of transforming the country into 
a globally competitive manufacturing hub by providing supportive indus trial 
ecosystem with proximity to cities, connectivity to multi-modal logistics facilities 
and industrial hubs.

investments in drought-risk reduction measures such as irrigation, watershed 
development, groundwater recharge and climate-resilient agriculture; 
 
(b) whether the Government has assessed the investment in drought preparedness 
measures to reduce farmers' dependence on crop insurance and drought relief 
assistance and in view of the projected El Nino conditions and the increasing 
frequency of erratic monsoons, if so, the details thereof; 
 
(c) whether the Government has prepared district-specific drought preparedness plans 
for the 315 monsoon-vulnerable districts, particularly the 111 districts identified as 
having poor irrigation facilities, including those in Andhra Pradesh and if so, the details

(d) the details of investments made in Andhra Pradesh under drought-risk reduction

क ृ िष एवं ᳰकसान क᭨याण रा᭔य मंᮢी  (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR)

Further, 16th Finance Commission has recommended a total allocation of 
Rs.1,63,521 crore under SDRF to the States for the period 2026-27 to 2030-31, of 
which Central Govt. share is Rs.1,24,732.65 crore. 
 
For watershed development, under Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana 
(PMKSY), during the period 2021–22 to 2025–26, a total of ₹ 6,260.86 crore has been 
released. Further, the Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare is implementing 
Centrally Sponsored Scheme, namely Per Drop More Crop (PDMC) in the country 
from 2015-16 including Andhra Pradesh. During the year 2015-16 to 2021-22, the 
PDMC was implemented as a component of PMKSY and from 2022-23, it is being 
implemented under the Pradhan Mantri Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana (PM-RKVY). 
PDMC focuses on enhancing water use efficiency at farm level through Micro Irrigation 
namely Drip and Sprinkler Irrigation Systems. During last five years (2021-22 to 2025-
26), 4.31 lakh ha area has been covered under Micro Irrigation through PDMC scheme 
in Andhra Pradesh with release of Central Assistance of Rs. 1162.93 crore. 
 
In addition, Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare is implementing 
Rainfed Area Development (RAD) scheme since 2014-15 which focuses on Integrated 
Farming System (IFS) for enhancing productivity and minimising risks associated with 
climatic variability, mitigating impacts of drought, flood or other extreme weather 
events. Since its inception, a total of Rs. 2,251.98 Cr has been released under RAD 
and 9.53 lakh hectares have been brought under IFS, benefitting around 15.7 lakh 
farmers.  
 
State Government of Andhra Pradesh has also informed that an amount of Rs. 
790.73 crores was spent in the last five years on drought relief assistance towards 
input subsidy to affected farmers. 
  

(b) & (c):  The Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare is continuously monitoring 
the evolving monsoon situation and the possible impact of El Niño conditions on 
agriculture in close coordination with the India Meteorological Department (IMD), 
various Indian Council of Agriculture Research (ICAR) institutions, ICAR- Central 
Research Institute for Dryland Agriculture (CRIDA), Central Water Commission 
(CWC), Central Ground Water Board (CGWB), Mahalanobis National Crop Forecast 
Centre (MNCFC), the Department of Food and Public Distribution (DFPD), the 
Department of Fertilisers (DoF) and State Governments.  
 
In this regard, District Agriculture Contingency Plans (DACPs) have been 
updated for 14 States including Andhra Pradesh, covering 342 districts which are likely 
to receive below normal rainfall by the ICAR’s Central Research Institute for Dryland 
Agriculture (ICAR-CRIDA). 
 
Weekly meeting of the Crop Weather Watch Group (CWWG) is being held with 
the representatives of India Meteorological Department (IMD), Central Water 
Commission (CWC), Central Ground Water Board (CGWB), Mahalanobis National 
Crop Forecast Centre (MNCFC), Indian Council of Agriculture Research - Central 
Research Institute for Dryland Agriculture (ICAR - CRIDA), Department of Fertilizers, 
Department of Food & Public Distribution and the State Governments to review rainfall 
situation, reservoir storage, groundwater levels, crop sowing, input availability, market 
situation and pest/ disease incidence for timely intervention. 
 
Adequate availability of seeds has been ensured for the ensuing season. 
Against the demand of 172.80 lakh quintals from the States, availability of 192.25 lakh 
quintals of Kharif crop seeds has been assessed.  States have maintained 1% seeds 
i.e. 1.73 lakh quintals as National Seed Reserve. 
 
Special emphasis has been laid on promoting crop diversification, promotion of 
short-duration and drought-tolerant crop varieties, balanced use of fertilizers, water 
conservation practices, micro-irrigation, mulching, inter-cropping and practices of 
other climate-resilient technologies. 
 
Further, a nationwide Khet Bachao Abhiyaan was organised by Government of 
India during 1st – 30th June, 2026 in which 80,67,300 farmers participated in 1,14,567 
programmes which were organised to promote water conservation, introduce efficient 
irrigation and climate-resilient farming practices. Simultaneously, an intensive Kisan 
Credit Card (KCC) saturation drive and awareness campaign under Pradhan Mantri 
Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) is being implemented in the vulnerable districts. 
 
The Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) is implementing a project- 
National Innovations in Climate Resilient Agriculture (NICRA) that studies the 
challenges posed by climate change on agriculture and conducts district level risk & 
vulnerability assessment due to climate change.  
  

 
For enhancing the resilience and adaptive capacity of farmers to climate 
variability, location-specific climate resilient technologies such as system of rice 
intensification, aerobic rice, direct seeding of rice, cultivation of climate resilient 
varieties tolerant to extreme weather conditions such as drought and heat etc. have 
been demonstrated under the project through KVKs in 151 districts covering 448 
Climate Resilient Villages.  Capacity building for establishing village level seed banks 
and community nurseries is undertaken under NICRA to enable availability of seed in 
the adopted villages.  
 
Drought and flood tolerant climate-resilient varieties of rice, wheat, soybean, 
mustard, chickpea, sorghum, gram, and foxtail millet were demonstrated in several 
NICRA villages. Besides, training programmes are conducted under Agricultural 
Technology Management Agency (ATMA) on various issues of agricultural practices. 
Under NICRA, technical assistance for small and marginal farmers is extended to 
additional vulnerable districts beyond the 151 currently covered districts, to promote 
adoption of climate-resilient practices.   
 
During 2014-25 a total of 341 drought tolerant varieties have been released by 
Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) out of which 200 are of Cereals, 25 are 
of Oilseeds, 43 are of Pulses, 18 are of Fibre, 16 are of Forage crops, 36 are of 
Sugarcane, 3 are of other crops. During the same period a total of 59 heat stress 
tolerant varieties have been released out of which 43 are of Cereals, 7 are of Oilseeds, 
7 are of Pulses, 2 of Mung bean and 2 are Fibre crops. 
 
State Government of Andhra Pradesh has informed that in view of the likely El 
Niño conditions and increasing monsoon variability, the State Government has 
reviewed drought preparedness measures, including promotion of Pre-Monsoon Dry 
Sowings (PMDS), climate-resilient cropping systems, soil moisture conservation, and 
increased green cover to reduce long-term drought vulnerability.  
 
The Central Water Commission and State Governments have been advised to 
undertake advance planning for optimum utilization of reservoir water and promote 
efficient irrigation practices. Assistance to farmers is available through ongoing 
schemes such as Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana: Per Drop More Crop 
(PDMC) with a focus on enhancing water-use efficiency at the farm level through 
installation of Micro-Irrigation systems. Department of Rural Development is utilising 
Viksit Bharat – Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) (VB G Ram G) 
funds for rejuvenating water structures – such as farm ponds, check dams, canal 
desilting, and bori bandhans – to trap every drop of early or residual rainfall.  
 
(d): State Government has also informed that District-level drought contingency 
plans have been prepared for vulnerable districts in Andhra Pradesh, covering crop 
contingency measures, seed reserves, irrigation management, and crop advisories. 
The State is also giving special focus to Kurnool, Anantapur, and Sri Sathya Sai 
districts. 
 
  

The State of Andhra Pradesh has invested Rs. 67.47 crore towards supply of 
contingency seed under drought-risk reduction measures during last five years i.e. 
2021-22 to 2025-26. Further, for the monsoon-vulnerable districts identified as having 
poor irrigation facilities in Andhra Pradesh, i.e. Anantapur, Sri Sathya Sai, Kurnool, the 
state agriculture and water resources departments have prioritized the following 
localized interventions:  
 
(a) Pivoting Crop Choices: Enforcing a structural shift away from water-intensive 
paddy toward low-water millets (Shree Anna), pulses, and oilseeds. 
(b) Groundwater & Tank Management: Accelerated desilting of local minor irrigation 
tanks and the optimization of agricultural pump usage.  
(c) The "Jaladhara–Jala Harathi" mission flagship water conservation and climate 
resilience program launched by the Government. The program was initiated as a 
100-day time-bound mission (April 6 to July 14, 2026) to systematically address 
summer drought, protect minor irrigation infrastructures, and boost the rural 
economy. 
(d) Check Dams and Percolation Tanks: Constructed to slow down rainwater runoff, 
giving it time to sink into the ground and recharge local bore wells. 
(e) Beyond local farm planning, the state relies on Lift Irrigation Schemes and River 
Interlinking.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING

 ANSWERED ON 21ST JULY, 2026 
Coastal Fishing Village 
 
380.    Shri Balashowry Vallabhaneni: 
 
Will the Minister of FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING: be 
pleased to state:  
 
(a)  whether the Government is providing support to development of integrated 
modern coastal fishing villages in the country, including Andhra Pradesh; 
(b) whether it is also true that Sorlag ondhi and Gullalamodha villages in Krishna 
district of Andhra Pradesh has been identified for development; 
(c) if so, the details of initiatives such as fish drying yards, processing centers, fish 
markets, fishing jetty, ice plant, cold storage and emergen cy rescue facilities, etc. 
undertaken to make this village a model and economically vibrant fishermen village; 
and 
(d) whether it is also true that the scheme has been extended till March, 2026 and if 
so, the details thereof? 
 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
 
(SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH ALIAS LALAN SINGH) 
 
 
(a) to (c): The PMMSY, implemented from 2020-21, provides for developing Integrated 
Modern Coastal Villages at a unit cost of ₹750 lakh to enhance economic and social 
gains for coastal fishers through sustainable practices. The initiative strengthens 
livelihoods and parti cipation across the fisheries value chain by supporting modern 
infrastructure, disaster -resilient housing, cyclone and tsunami shelters, and post -
harvest amenities tailored to local needs. It is a non -beneficiary-oriented intervention 
implemented jointly w ith coastal State Governments on a 60:40 cost -sharing basis. 
The scheme leverages the inherent strengths of coastal communities to promote 
sustainable economic growth. The Government of Andhra Pradesh has not availed 
this activity under the PMMSY.  

 
The Department of Fisheries, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying, 
recognizing the importance of developing the coastal communities, has also taken up 
another transformative initiative under the Pradhan Mantri Matya Sampada Yojana 
(PMMSY) to develop the existing 100 fishermen villages situated close to the coastline 
in various States and Union Territories (UTs), including Andhra Pradesh, into Climate 
Resilient Coastal Fishermen Villages (CRCFV), to make them economically vibrant 
fishermen villages. The development of CRCFV has been taken up under the Central 
Sector scheme component of the PMMSY with a unit cost of Rs 200 lakh per fishing 
village, and the entire cost (100%) is borne by the Government of India.  
The Department of Fisheries, Ministr y of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying, 
in consultation with the Government of Andhra Pradesh, has identified 15 villages in 
the state  for development as CRCFV , including Sorlagondhi and Gullalamodha in 
Krishna district  of Andhra Pradesh . The propos als of the Government of Andhra 
Pradesh to develop the identified 15 villages as CRCFV at a total cost of Rs. 30 crore 
have been approved based on the Detailed Project Report ( DPR) submitted by the 
State, and so far, Rs. 15.0 Crore has been released to the  Government of Andhra 
Pradesh for implementation of the approved projects of CRCFV based on the 
utilisation. The approved interventions for Sorlagondhi and Gullalamodha villages 
include fish -drying platforms, solar fish -drying units, multipurpose fisheries  center, 
common fish market, high-mast solar lights, and jetty extension for safe boat mooring. 
Livelihood and climate-resilient activities comprise seaweed culture farms, sea -cage 
culture, colour GPS units, life -saving appliances, iceboxes, and other prod uctivity-
enhancing assets. The details of the interventions in both villages are provided in 
Annexure I.  
(d): The PMMSY scheme is extended up to 30 September 2026.

BAREFOOT TECHNICIANS 
383.  Adv Dean Kuriakose: 
 
Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  whether the Government is aware that there are a total of 114 
Barefoot technicians across six districts in the State of Kerala 
who have received three month technicians training from the 
Ministry and have been working for the last nine years; 
(b)  if so, the details thereof; 
(c)  whether the Ministry has issued any notification directing the 
State Governments to put on hold the services of these Barefoot 
Technicians and if so, the details thereof; 
(d)  whether the Government has taken any steps to ensure that the 
honorarium paid to these technicians are continued and they are 
not terminated from service; and 
(e)  if so, the details thereof? 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
(SHRI KAMLESH PASWAN) 
  
(a) & (b): Out of a total of 157 candidates trained through National 
Institute of Rural Development and Panchayati Raj (NIRDPR) under 
the Barefoot Technicians initiative, 143 were deployed in the field 
in  Kerala and 111 BFTs have been reported by the State Government 
to be currently  deployed in 103 Gram Panchayat across the State.

Kerala regarding the continuation of BFTs, the  Ministry vide 
communication dated 08.07.2026, clarified that section 37(3) of the

Act 2025  provides that all appointments, engagements, 
authorisations, approvals and administrative arrangements made 
under the repealed Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment

appointed date shall, unless inconsistent with the provisions of the 
Act, continue to remain valid and in force until altered, superseded or 
withdrawn under the provisions of the Act.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED D. QUESTION NO. 384 
 
TO BE ANSWERED ON THE 21ST JULY, 2026 
 
AGRICULTURAL CENSUS (2021-22) 
 
384. SHRI SHAFI PARAMBIL: 
 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the present status of the 11th Agriculture Census (2021-22), including the stages of 
work completed and the progress made since its commencement in 2022; 
(b) the reasons, if any, for the delay in completing the Census and publishing its 
findings, along with the revised timeline for its completion and release; 
(c) the number of villages and agricultural households selected or covered under the 
Census, indicating the sampling methodology adopted, wherever applicable, State/UT-
wise; and 
(d) whether the Government proposes to use the findings of the census for formulating 
polices relating to agricultural production, land holdings, crop diversification and farmers’ 
welfare, if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
 
कृͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण राÏय मंğी  (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
(a) to (d):  Agriculture Census in India is conducted after every five years in collaboration 
with the States and Union Territories. The field work of Agriculture Census is carried out 
in three distinct phases. The ongoing 11th Agriculture Census with the reference year 
2021-22 has been commenced in 2022 and so far, field work & data collection for three 
phases have been completed within time frame.         
  

 
 
Further, in phase-I, data on primary characteristics of agricultural holdings and area 
operated are collected on complete enumeration basis. In Phase-II, data on characteristics 
of holdings like cropping pattern, irrigation status etc. are collected from randomly selected 
20% of sample villages in each Tehsil. In phase III, data on input use pattern of operational 
holdings are collected from randomly selected 7% of sample villages in each Tehsil.  
Agriculture Census provides reliable data base on socio-economic aspects of 
operational holders in the country which is used for making agricultural policies. It provides 
information on the number, size and distribution of operational holdings by classes 
(marginal, small, semi-medium, medium and large), tenancy, consolidation of holdings, 
land distribution etc. which is used for efficient planning for utilization of land, irrigation 
facilities, crop diversification, mechanization and other agricultural inputs. It provides data 
on woman-operated land holdings to support gender-based agricultural interventions. 
Census data also enables Government in efficient allocation of subsidies, credit facilities, 
targeting rural development programs, and establishing national and regional agricultural 
priorities. Further, it serves as a key data source in agriculture sector for researchers, 
planners, and other stakeholders.

Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE क ृ िष एवं िकसान

(a) whether the States have submitted annual action plans under Sub-Mission 
on Agricultural Mechanization (SMAM); 
(b) if so, the number of beneficiaries mentioned under the “Financial assistance 
to farmers for procurement of farm machinery and equipments on individual 
ownership basis” component of the scheme during the last five years, year-wise, 
State/UT-wise and particularly district-wise for the State of Andhra Pradesh; 
(c) whether any audit mechanisms have been conducted by State/Union

(d) if so, the number of beneficiaries who have been benefited under the 
scheme during the last five years, year-wise, State/UT-wise and particularly district-

(e) if not, whether any audit will be conducted to measure the impact of the

ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE  
 
क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण राǛ मंũी  (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
 
                        
(a), (b) & (d): States have submitted single consolidated Annual Action Plans 
(AAPs) covering all relevant schemes of the Department of Agriculture & Farmers 
Welfare (DA&FW), including the Sub-Mission on Agricultural Mechanization 
(SMAM).  
  

       The State-wise and year-wise number of beneficiaries during last five years 
under “Financial assistance to farmers for procurement of farm machinery and 
equipments on individual ownership basis” component of SMAM are indicated in 
Annexure-I. The district-wise allocation are decided at the State level and as per 
the information provided by the Department of Agriculture, Government of Andhra 
Pradesh, the district-wise details of beneficiaries of Andhra Pradesh are indicated 
in Annexure-II.  
 
(c) & (e): Impact evaluation study of schemes is a standard, systematic 
process used to determine the long-term, direct, and indirect effects of policies, 
programs, or projects. The impact evaluation of SMAM was carried out as a part of 
study ‘Evaluation of CSS Schemes in Package 1 – Agriculture & Allied Sector’ 
under the aegis of the Development Monitoring and Evaluation Office (DMEO), NITI 
Aayog.   
 
        The study report released in 2025, provides an integrated assessment of 
various schemes including SMAM based on primary fieldwork across diverse agro-
climatic zones, quantitative surveys with beneficiaries, extensive stakeholder 
consultations at the central, state, district, and block levels, and secondary data 
analysis from official records and scheme Management Information System (MIS). 
The study report indicated that the SMAM has showed enhanced alignment with 
smallholder needs, particularly through the availability of rental machinery. 
Agricultural mechanization has been viewed as a critical intervention for improving 
farm productivity and reducing labour constraints.  As informed by Indian Council 
of Agricultural Research (ICAR), the farm power availability of India increased from 
0.372 kW/ha in 1971-72 to 3.045 kW/ha in 2021-22.

PERFORMANCE OF MGNREGS IN WARANGAL DISTRICT 
 
386. Dr. Kadiyam Kavya: 
 
Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  the performance of the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural 
Employment Guarantee Scheme (MGNREGS) in Warangal 
district, Telangana, during the last two years, including the 
average number of person-days of employment provided per 
household in each year; 
(b)  whether any wage payments under the Scheme are pending in 
Warangal district, if so, the details thereof, including the amount 
and duration of such pendency; and 
(c)  the steps taken by the Government to ensure timely payment of 
wages to the beneficiaries? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
(SHRI KAMLESH PASWAN) 
  
(a):    During the last two financial years 2024–25 and 2025–26, 99.99% 
and 99.97% respectively, of the eligible rural households in Warangal 
district of Telangana were offered employment against the demand 
under the scheme. It is also stated that the average number of days 
of employment provided per household was 41.12 in 2024–25 and 
27.89 in 2025–26.  
  
(b) & (c): Under Mahatma Gandhi NREGS, the wage payments are 
directly credited by the Central Government to the accounts of the 
beneficiaries through Direct Benefit Transfer protocol.  At the 
beginning of each financial year, admissible pending liabilities of the 
previous years, if any, are duly reimbursed by the Government of 
India. Accordingly, all due and admissible pending wage liabilities 
upto FY 2025-26 have already been cleared.

Will the Minister of TEXTILES वस्त्र मंत्री 
be pleased to state : 
 
(a) the details of textile parks and integrated textile projects approved in Telangana;  
(b) the details regarding Central assistance extended for handloom and powerloom sectors;  
(c) the details regarding measures taken to enhance exports from Telangana; and  
(d) whether any new textile clusters are under consideration? 
 
 
उत्तर 
ANSWER 
वस्त्रराज्‍यमंत्री(श्री पबित्र मार्घेररटा) 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR TEXTILES  
 (SHRI PABITRA MARGHERITA) 
 
(a):  Ministry of Textiles is implementing two scheme namely Scheme for Integrated Textiles 
Park (SITP) & PM Mega Integrated Textile Regions and Apparel Park (PM MITRA) Scheme for 
establishing textile parks across various locations in the country including Telan gana. Under the 
SITP Scheme; 2 textile parks have been established in Telangana. Furthermore, 1 Brownfield 
project has been sanctioned under the PMMITRA Park Scheme. This park has recently been 
inaugurated in May 2026. Currently with the grounded investmen t of Rs. 3862 cr, approximately 
24,500 jobs have been generated. Details of these projects is as per Annexure-A. 
 
(b)   The Ministry of Textiles is implementing the following schemes to promote handloom 
sector and welfare of handloom workers across the country including Telangana: 
 
1. National Handloom Development Programme; 
2. Raw Material Supply Scheme; 
 
Under the above schemes, financial assistance is provided to eligible handloom agencies/workers 
for raw materials, procurement of upgraded looms &  accessories, solar lighting units, 
construction of workshed, skilling, product diversification & design innovation, technical and 
common infrastructure, publicity and brand development through India Handloom Brand (IHB), 
Handloom Mark (HLM) and GI tag , e-commerce facilities, marketing of handloom products in 

domestic/overseas markets, concessional loans under weavers’ MUDRA scheme and social 
security etc.  
Further, on receipt of proposals from Government of Telangana, financial assistance of 
Rs.1223.97 lakh has been provided for 26 Small Cluster Development Programme (SCDPs) 
covering 4971 beneficiaries during the FY 2021-22 to 2025-26. 
Further, the details regarding Central assistance extended for handloom and Powerloom sectors 
is as per Annexure-B. 
(c)  The Government has implemented various duty -exemption, duty -remission and export -
promotion schemes for the benefit of all exporters, including those from Telangana. These 
include RoSCTL, RoDTEP, Advance Authorisation, EPCG, Duty Drawback and the Export 
Promotion Mission. Exporters also benefit from preferential market access under the 16 Free 
Trade Agreements currently in force, which helps reduce costs and improve export 
competitiveness. 
Further, for export promotion of handlooms, financial assistance are provided for participation of 
handloom exporters/weavers from across the country in various International marketing 
events/fairs i.e International Trade Fair, Buyer Seller Meet, Reverse Buyer Seller Meet, Big 
Ticket events, Bharat Tex, are organized thro ugh Handloom Export Promotion Council (HEPC). 
In consultation with stakeholders, as part of the ‘Textile Summit’ organized by the Ministry, the 
Govt. of Telangana has formalized ‘State Export Action Plan’ to boost exports in the sector. 
(d)  The Government  has announced an integrated program in the Union Budget 2026 -27, 
featuring the Textile Expansion and Employment Scheme  to modernise traditional clusters 
with capital support for machinery, technology upgradation and common testing and certification 
centres.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF PANCHAYATI RAJ 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO.389 
ANSWERED ON 21.07.2026 
FIFTEENTH FINANCE COMMISSION UNTIED GRANTS 
  
389.     SHRI KALYAN BANERJEE: 
  
Will the Minister of PANCHAYATI RAJ be pleased to state: 
  
(a) whether the Government has sanctioned and released the fifteenth finance commission untied 
grants of over Five Hundred Ninety-Two Crore rupees to Panchayati Raj Institutions and Rural 
Local Bodies during June and July of 2026; 
  
(b) if so, the details of amount released for West Bengal State; and 
  
(c) the detail of central budget allocations and sanctions towards MGNREGA, now VB-GRAM-
G scheme, pending since last four financial years and regularise the payments of beneficiaries 
therefor? 
  
ANSWER 
  
THE MINISTER OF PANCHAYATI RAJ 
 
(SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH ALIAS LALAN SINGH) 
  
(a) No, Sir. The award period of the Fifteenth Finance Commission (XV FC) concluded on 31st 
March, 2026. Consequently, no grants under the XV Finance Commission for Rural Local 
Bodies/Panchayati Raj Institutions were sanctioned or released during June and July, 2026. 
(b) Does not arise in view of (a) above. 
(c) As informed by the Ministry of Rural Development, under the erstwhile Mahatma Gandhi 
National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme (Mahatma Gandhi NREGS), which remained in 
force up to 30.06.2026, employment was provided to every rural household whose adult 
members demanded unskilled manual work, in accordance with the provisions of the Act. With 
effect from 01.07.2026, the Viksit Bharat-Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) 
(VB-G RAM G) Act, 2025 has come into force, replacing the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural 
Employment Guarantee Act, 2005.  
  
The details of funds allocation at Budget Estimate stage, Revised Estimate stage, final 
allocation and fund released under Mahatma Gandhi NREGS in the last four financial years are 
given below:

Under the Scheme, the wage payments are directly credited by the Central Government to 
the accounts of the beneficiaries through Direct Benefit Transfer protocol. At the beginning of 
each financial year, admissible pending liabilities of the previous years, if any, are duly 
reimbursed by the Government of India. Accordingly, all due and admissible pending wage 
liabilities upto FY 2025-26 have already been cleared (except in case of State of West Bengal).  
  
In the case of West Bengal, the pending liabilities towards wage component an amount of 
Rs. 1457.22 crore. The admissibility of this liability is subject to verification by the Central 
Government.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF SOCIAL JUSTICE & EMPOWERMENT 
DEPARTMENT OF EMPOWERMENT OF PERSONS WITH DISABILITIES 
(DIVYANGJAN) 
  
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO-391 
TO BE ANSWERED ON- 21/07/2026 
  
ORGANISING A DISTRIBUTION CAMP UNDER ADIP SCHEME 
  
391. Shri Bajrang Manohar Sonwane: 
  
Will the Minister of SOCIAL JUSTICE AND EMPOWERMENT be pleased to state: 
  
(a) whether the Government has received a proposal for organising a distribution camp in Beed 
District, Maharashtra, under the Assistance to Disabled Persons (ADIP) Scheme and 
the Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana (RVY) for free distribution of aids and assistive devices to 
eligible Divyangjans and Senior Citizens; 
 
(b) if so, the present status of the proposal and the reasons for the delay, if any, in organising the 
distribution camp; 
 
(c) whether assessment camps were conducted in all eleven talukas of Beed District and if so, the 
number of beneficiaries identified under both the schemes along with the estimated value of aids 
and assistive devices; 
 
(d) whether the Government proposes to accord administrative approval and organise 
the distribution camp at the earliest; and 
 
(e) the timeline fixed for distribution of aids and assistive devices to all eligible 
beneficiaries under the ADIP and RVY Schemes in Beed District? 
  
  
  
ANSWER 
  
MINISTER OF STATE FOR SOCIAL JUSTICE AND EMPOWERMENT 
(SHRI B. L. VERMA) 
  
(a) and (b) No proposal for organising a camp in Beed District, Maharashtra has been received 
from any Implementing Agency under the Assistance to Persons with Disabilities for 
Purchase/Fitting of Aids and Appliances (ADIP) Scheme. However, a request from Shri Bajrang 
Manohar Sonwane, Hon'ble Member of Parliament (Lok Sabha) has been received for organising 

a Camp in Beed District, Maharashtra under the ADIP Scheme and the Rashtriya Vayoshri 
Yojana (RVY). 
(c) Assessment camps under the ADIP Scheme and RVY were conducted by Artificial Limbs 
Manufacturing Corporation of India (ALIMCO) across all eleven talukas of Beed District, 
Maharashtra. Based on the assessments conducted, 1816 eligible beneficiaries were identified 
under the ADIP Scheme and 1419 eligible beneficiaries under the RVY, involving an estimated 
cost of ₹188.09 lakh and ₹117.43 lakh, respectively. 
(d) and (e) ALIMCO has requested the District Magistrate, Beed, to confirm the necessary local 
arrangements and coordination for organising the distribution camp.

ANSWERED ON 21.07.2026 
 
TECHNOLOGICAL AND FINANCIAL SUPPORT 
 
392. SHRI ATUL GARG:  
 
Will the Minister of HEAVY INDUSTRIES be pleased to state:  
 
(a) whether the Government has extended targeted technological and financial support to the 
heavy engineering units operating in the Ghaziabad Constituency;  
 
(b) if so, the details thereof;  
 
(c) whether the Government has facilitated the up -skilling of the local in dustrial workforce to 
handle automated manufacturing processes and advanced robotics;  
 
(d) the specific measures taken to protect these local machinery manufacturers from the dumping 
of cheap, sub-standard industrial imports; and  
 
(e) the future initiatives planned to establish a dedicated industrial technology park in the region 
to foster innovation and support the holistic growth of the regional heavy manufacturing sector? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR HEAVY INDUSTRIES 
(SHRI BHUPATHIRAJU SRINIVASA VARMA) 
 
(a) to (e): Ministry of Heavy Industries has notified the Scheme for Enhancement of 
Competitiveness in the Indian Capital Goods Sector. Under the Scheme, project named Robotic 
Laser Cladding Technology for Hydro Power Industry by Industrial Process ors & Metallizers 
Pvt. Ltd at Ghaziabad has been sanctioned with budgetary support of Rs. 1.24 crore and total 
project cost of Rs. 4.97 crore.  
 
Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship under its Pradhan Mantri Kaushal 
Vikas Yojana 4.0 has train ed/oriented 312 candidates in Industrial Automation PMKVY 4.0 in 
Ghaziabad as of 30.06.2026.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 393 
TO BE ANSWERED ON THE 21ST JULY , 2026 
 
ACTION PLAN FOR DROUGHT MITIGATION 
393.  SHRI MANSUKHBHAI DHANJIBHAI VASAVA:  
 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण मंũी 
be pleased to state:  
 
(a) whether the Government propose to formulate concrete plan to tackle the drought 
situation in the country in the near future; and 
(b) if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण राǛ मंũी (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
(a) & (b): As per the National Policy on Disaster Management (NPDM), the State 
Government is primarily responsible for providing necessary relief measures on ground 
level in the wake of notified calamities including drought. The State Governments 
undertake relief measures in the wake of natural calamities from funds available in the 
form of the State Disaster Response Fund (SDRF) in accordance with the Government of 
India approved items and norms. Additional financial assistance, over and above SDRF, 
is considered from the National Disaster Response Fund (NDRF), as per laid down 
procedure, in case of disaster of ‘severe nature’, which includes an assessment based on 
the visit of an Inter-Ministerial Central Team (IMCT) and a memorandum for assistance 
under NDRF submitted by the State/ UT Government.  
The details of the fund allocated and released under SDRF/NDRF to the States are 
available on Disaster Management, MHA's website i.e. https://ndmindia.mha.gov.in . 
 
Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare is mandated to monitor and 
coordinate relief measures in the wake of drought in the country. Monitoring and 
management of drought is carried out as per the Manual for drought management which 
clearly delineates the roles and responsibilities of different agencies and guides 
coordination against them. The Manual covers institutional structure, key variables for 
monitoring drought, declaration of drought, drought response, relief and mitigation. 
 
To promote the use of modern technology, the Manual was revised / updated in 
2020. The revised Drought Manual provides for use of modern technology in 
monitoring/determination of drought. New scientific indices and parameters was 
incorporated for a more accurate assessment and monitoring of drought.  
 
District Agriculture Contingency plan (DACPs) is prepared by ICAR-CRIDA for 651 
districts in the Country which provides for contingency measures to cope with drought for 
rainfed and irrigated (ground water irrigated, tankfed and canal command areas), farming 
situations on account of delayed onset of monsoon ( 2/4/6/8 weeks delays) and (early/mid 
season/ terminal drought) for field and horticulture crops. The contingency measures 
include alternate crops/ crop varieties/agronomic practices/ other management options 
appropriate for drought scenarios. 

Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) along with weather index based 
Restructured Weather Based Crop Insurance Scheme (RWBCIS) provide a 
comprehensive insurance cover against failure of the crop  to farmers suffering crop 
loss/damage arising out of unforeseen natural calamities. PMFBY covers risks from 
prevented sowing to post harvest losses.    
Per Drop More Crop (PDMC) scheme improves water use efficiency through Micro 
Irrigation technologies i.e. drip and sprinkler irrigation systems.  
The focus of Rainfed Area Development (RAD) scheme is on Integrated Farming 
System (IFS) to enhance productivity and minimise risks associated with climatic 
variability. Under RAD, crops/ cropping system is integrated with activities like horticulture, 
livestock, fishery, agro-forestry, apiculture etc. to enable farmers, not only in maximize 
farm returns for sustainable livelihood but also to mitigate the impacts of drought, flood or 
other extreme weather events.  Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture (MIDH), 
Agroforestry & National Bamboo Mission also aim to increase climate resilience in 
agriculture. 
National Innovations in Climate Resilient Agriculture (NICRA) project implemented 
by the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) has developed and promoted 
climate resilient technologies in agriculture for vulnerable areas of the country. The outputs 
of the project help the regions to cope with extreme weather conditions like droughts, 
floods, frost, heat waves, etc. For enhancing the resilience and adaptive capacity of 
farmers to climate variability, the Concept of “Climate Resilient Villages” (CRVs) was 
initiated under NICRA. Location-specific climate resilient technologies are demonstrated 
in climatically vulnerable districts for adoption by farmers. Capacity building programmes 
are conducted to educate the farmers on various aspects of climate change for wider 
adoption of climate resilient technologies.

CROP DAMAGE DUE TO ELECTRICAL SHORT CIRCUITS 
394. Shri Manoj Kumar: 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE कृ ͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण मंğी 
be pleased to state:  
 
(a) whether the Government is aware that in areas like Shivsagar and Karhagarh in Rohtas 
(Sasaram), crops are frequently damaged due to short circuits in old and damaged electric 
wires; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; and 
(c) the policy and steps taken by the Government to compensate affected farmers and 
coordinate with the electricity department to prevent such incidents  
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE  
कृ ͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण राÏय मंğी    (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
 
(a) & (b) : As informed by the State Government, some incidences of crop damage due to 
short circuits in old and damaged electric wires has been reported in Shivsagar Block 
covering damage of about 21 acre in wheat crop.  
 
(c) The State of Bihar does not implement Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana. Further, 
losses due to fire on account of short circuit is not covered under the scheme.  
 
However, as informed by the State Government of Bihar, Department of Disaster 
Management has policy to compensate crop loss of more than 33% for natural disaster as 
well as loss due to fire incidence as per SDRF norms. On the report of District Magistrate 
of the concerned district, the compensation amount is released. Department of Energy, 
Government of Bihar regularly monitors the maintenance of loose wire as well as electric 
transformers.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF PANCHAYATI RAJ 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 395 
                                          ANSWERED ON 21.07.2026 
  
DRONE-BASED LAND SURVEYS AND DIGITISATION OF PROPERTY RECORDS 
  
395. DR. PRASHANT YADAORAO PADOLE:      
  
Will the Minister of PANCHAYATI RAJ be pleased to state:  
  
(a) whether the Ministry has assessed the impact of drone-based land surveys and digital 
property records on dispute reduction and transparent land governance;  
(b) if so, the details thereof and the number of land disputes resolved before and after 
implementation along with coverage of drone surveys and digitized records; state and district 
wise; and  
(c) the details of time reduction in land record verification and registration. 
  
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF PANCHAYATI RAJ 
 
(SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH ALIAS LALAN SINGH) 
  
(a), (b) and (c) The main objective of the SVAMITVA Scheme is to provide Record of Rights to 
property owners in rural inhabited areas. Under the Scheme, rural inhabited land is demarcated 
using drone survey and Continuously Operating Reference Stations (CORS) technology to create 
high accuracy maps of abadi areas of villages. These highly accurate maps help reduce property-
related disputes by clearly demarcating property boundaries and creating Record of Rights. The 
Scheme provides for ground verification and resolution of objections/disputes by the competent 
State authorities before issuance of Property Cards, ensuring transparency and fair demarcation 
of properties.  
  
No such assessment has been undertaken on the reduction of property-related disputes, time 
taken for land record verification and registration, or improvement in land administration before 
and after implementation of the SVAMITVA Scheme. However, the Ministry of Panchayati Raj 
has conducted an impact evaluation of the Scheme through IIM Ahmedabad to assess the impact 
on bank loan uptake and Gram Panchayat’s own sources of revenue. The study found substantial 
increase in bank loan amounts availed against property cards and increase in Gram Panchayat’s 
property tax and other local taxes after implementation of SVAMITVA Scheme. The Ministry 
does not maintain data on the number of land disputes resolved before and after implementation 
of the Scheme. As on date, drone survey has been completed in 3.30 lakh villages, and 3.24 crore 
Property Cards have been prepared for 1.97 lakh villages. State and district-wise details are at 
Annexure.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 396 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 21st  JULY, 2026 
 
INCOME OF MUSTARD AND BAJRA PRODUCING FARMERS  
 
396. SHRI BHAJAN LAL JATAV: 
 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE कृ ͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण 
मंğी be pleased to state: 
(a) the details of the schemes being implemented by the Union Government to 
increase the income of mustard and bajra producing farmers;  
(b) the extent to which the farmers of Rajasthan have benefited from these schemes;  
(c) the assistance made available for the development of value addition, storage and 
marketing infrastructure; and  
(d) whether any special scheme is under consideration to promote agro-processing in 
the Karauli-Dholpur region? 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE  
कृ ͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण राÏय मंğी  (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
(a) & (b): The Government of India is implementing a comprehensive range of 
Central Sector and Centrally Sponsored Schemes across the country, including 
Rajasthan, aimed at increasing the income of farmers including those growing mustard 
and bajra. These interventions aim to improve production & productivity, reducing 
whole cultivation costs, mitigating production risks and enhancing farmers’ income. 
Details at Annexure 1. The National Mission on Edible Oils-Oilseeds (NMEO-OS) 
aims at enhancing domestic edible oil production including mustard & rapeseed to 
achieve self-reliance (Atmanirbhar Bharat) in edible oils.  Under the Mission in 
Rajasthan, an expenditure amounting to Rs. 74.90 crores has been incurred during 
FY 2025-26. 
  

 
       The Sub-Mission on Shree Anna under the National Food Security & Nutrition 
Mission (NFSNM) is being implemented to increase the production and productivity of 
millets, including Bajra, in the 28 States and 2 Union Territories, including Rajasthan. 
Under the programme, assistance is provided for demonstration of improved 
production and protection technologies, distribution of certified seeds, integrated 
nutrient and pest management, and other interventions aimed at enhancing 
productivity. Under the Mission in Rajasthan, an expenditure amounting to Rs. 127.53 
crores has been incurred during FY 2025-26. 
(c) & (d): The Government of India supports the development of agricultural value 
addition, post-harvest management, storage and marketing infrastructure through 
various schemes and programmes such as Agriculture Infrastructure Fund 
(AIF), Integrated Scheme for Agricultural Marketing (ISAM), Mission for Integrated 
Development of Horticulture (MIDH) etc.  In addition, under the Pradhan Mantri 
Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana (PM-RKVY), financial assistance is available to States 
for undertaking State-specific projects aimed at strengthening agricultural value 
chains, post-harvest management, processing, storage and market linkages, based 
on local priorities and requirements. 
       Under AIF, loans worth ₹4,895.13 crore have been sanctioned for 6,544 projects 
with a total project cost of ₹8,123.67 crore. In Karauli district, loans worth ₹14.39 crore 
have been sanctioned for 20 projects with a total project cost of ₹25.19 crore. In 
Dholpur district, loans worth ₹25.11 crore have been sanctioned for 25 projects with a 
total project cost of ₹52.22 crore.  
      Under ISAM, 1,934 storage infrastructure projects of storage capacity of 39.53 lakh 
MT have been assisted with subsidy release of Rs. 151.49 crore up to 30.06.2026. In 
addition to storage infrastructure, 610 Marketing Infrastructure (other than storage) 
projects have also been assisted with subsidy release of ₹ 106.94 crore. Karauli and 
Dholpur district have 1 project each with a storage capacity of 5,000 MT each, for 
which a subsidy of ₹37.50 lakh and ₹25.00 lakh has been released respectively. 
     No special scheme is under consideration for promotion of agro-processing in the 
Karauli–Dholpur region.  

ANNEXURE I 
 
The list of the schemes implemented by the Government to support States in 
agriculture 
 
1. Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi (PM-KISAN)  
2. Pradhan Mantri Annadata Aay SanraksHan Abhiyan (PM-AASHA) 
3. Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY)/Restructured Weather Based 
Crop  Insurance Scheme (RWBCIS) 
4. Modified Interest Subvention Scheme (MISS)  
5. National Mission on Edible Oils (NMEO)-Oilseeds 
6. National Mission on Natural Farming (NMNF) 
7. National Food Security and Nutrition Mission (NFSNM) 
8. Sub-Mission on Agriculture Mechanization (SMAM) 
9. Sub-Mission on Agriculture Extension (SMAE) 
10. Soil Health & Fertility (SH&F) 
11. Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana (PKVY) 
12. Per Drop More Crop (PDMC) 
13. Crop Diversification Programme (CDP) 
14. Rainfed Area Development (RAD) 
15. Agriculture Infrastructure Fund (AIF) 
16. Formation and Promotion of 10k new Farmer Producers Organizations (FPOs)  
17. Integrated Scheme for Agriculture Marketing (ISAM)  
18. Digital Agriculture Mission

(a) & (b): Agriculture is a State subject. Government of India supports State 
Governments/Union Territories through a range of Central Sector and Centrally 
Sponsored schemes. These schemes encompass entire spectrum of agriculture 
including credit, insurance, income support, infrastructure, crops including horticulture, 
seeds, mechanization, marketing, organic and natural farming, farmer collectives, 
irrigation, extension, procurement of crops and digital agriculture. 
Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) and weather index based 
Restructured Weather Based Crop Insurance Scheme (RWBCIS) provide financial 
support to farmers at the time of losses due to natural calamities. The adoption of the 
schemes is voluntary for States/Union Territories as well as farmers. The UT of Delhi is 
not implementing the scheme. 
The Kisan Credit Card (KCC) Scheme is being implemented in Delhi. Till date, a 
total of 1,821 Kisan Credit Cards have been issued to farmers in Delhi. 
No proposal/demand has been received from the State Implementing Agency of 
the Government of NCT of Delhi for allocation under PM-KUSUM, being implemented 
by Ministry of New and Renewable Energy. 
Under Pradhan Mantri Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana (PM-RKVY) and Krishonnati 
Yojana (KY), financial assistance is released to States/UTs for implementation of 
approved projects and interventions under the respective scheme components. The 
Government of NCT of Delhi has been provided assistance under these schemes based 
on approved Annual Action Plans.  In the last three years,  action plans of ₹5.77 crore 

and ₹1.10 crore have been approved by Government of India for implementation of 
projects under PM-RKVY and KY respectively based on the proposal received from 
Government of Delhi. For the current Financial Year 2026–27, Annual Action Plan (AAP) 
for KY has been approved with an outlay of ₹10.00 lakh under the Digital Agriculture 
Mission, ₹130.43 lakh under Agriculture Extension, and ₹140.43 lakh under the Mission 
for Atmanirbharta in Pulses.  Further, an amount of ₹339.00 lakh has been approved 
under the Crop Residue Management (CRM) component of PM-RKVY, while ₹36.49 
lakh has been approved under the National Mission on Natural Farming (NMNF). 
(c) to (e): As per the Agriculture Census (2015–16), Delhi had a total of 20,842 
operational holdings, defined as land wholly or partly used for agricultural production. 
The low coverage is primarily attributable to the prevalence of marginal 
landholdings, relatively small number of farmers engaged in agriculture and allied 
activities, and the fact that a significant proportion of farmers cultivate leased agricultural 
land. 
Saturation of beneficiaries under various scheme is a continuous process and 
depends upon identification of eligible beneficiaries, participation of the State/UT 
Government and fulfillment of the prescribed eligibility conditions.

DECLINE IN SUGARCANE PRODUCTION 
 
400.  SHRI MOHITE PATIL DHAIRYASHEEL RAJSINH: 
      SHRI BALWANT BASWANT WANKHADE: 
      SMT. SUPRIYA SULE: 
 
Will the Minister of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare/ कृͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण मंğी 
be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government has taken note of the decline in sugarcane production 
in Maharashtra due to crop diseases such as red rot, erratic weather conditions 
including El Niño-induced drought and unseasonal rains, and the increasing shift of 
farmers towards alternative crops because of rising labour and cultivation costs; 
(b) whether the Government has assessed impact on sugar recovery, farmer 
incomes, and the functioning of cooperative sugar mills in Maharashtra, district-
wise; 
(c) whether any special financial assistance, disease-resistant sugarcane varieties, 
climate-resilient farming practices, and irrigation support are proposed for 
sugarcane-growing regions in the State; and 
(d) the steps being taken to strengthen research, disease surveillance and extension 
services to safeguard Maharashtra’s sugar economy and protect the livelihoods of 
sugarcane farmers? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE & FARMERS WELFARE 
कृͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण राÏयमंğी (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
 
(a):  The production of Sugarcane has increased from 1,099.70 lakh tonnes during 
2024-25 to 1,316.49 lakh tonnes during 2025-26 (3rd Advance Estimates) in the State 
of Maharashtra (Annexure I).  
Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare (DA&FW), through its 
Regional and Central Integrated Pest management Centers at Nagpur and Nashik 
regularly conducts pest surveillance and disseminates Integrated Pest Management 
(IPM) knowledge through training programmes like Farmers Field Schools, Season 
Long Training Programme and Orientation Programme.  

Surveys were conducted in various districts of Maharashtra and infestation of 
red rot disease in sugarcane above Economic Threshold Level (ETL) was observed in 
34 Ha only out of 4295 Ha surveyed during 2024-2025. Similarly, infestation above 
ETL was observed in 5 Ha only out 1450 Ha surveyed in 2025-2026. Accordingly, 
advisories were issued to farmers. Details of trainings conducted and advisories 
issues are at Annexure II. 
(b):  As per inputs received from Department of Food and Public Distribution, the 
State Government systematically assesses estimation of area and productivity of 
sugarcane. Sugar recovery depends closely on the specific crop variety, soil 
conditions, weather parameters, and several other regional agro-climatic factors. As 
per recent concluded crushing season, the average sugar recovery rate  was recorded 
at 11.26% across Maharashtra. There were a total of 210 operational sugar mills (of 
both cooperative and private crushing entities) during current sugar season across the 
state. In terms of impact on farmer incomes, the implementation of regulatory payout 
mechanisms remains highly effective, with approximately 99.6% of Fair and 
Remunerative Price (FRP) payments successfully disbursed to growers during current 
sugar season. 
 To build long-term economic resilience, the State Government continuously 
encourages mills to diversify their revenue streams, including the setting up and 
technical upgradation of co-generation power plants and ethanol distillation units 
under the National Ethanol Blending Programme (EBP), thereby enabling mills to 
optimize cash flows and become less dependent on sugar market price volatility alone.  
Further, the Central Government has increased the Fair and Remunerative 
Price (FRP) of sugarcane for the ensuing Sugar Season 2026–27 to Rs. 365 per 
quintal, up from Rs. 355 per quintal in the current Sugar Season 2025–26, based on 
a sugar recovery rate of 10.25% 
(c) & (d):   During 2014-25, a total of 341 Drought tolerant Varieties have been 
released by Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR), out of which 36 are of 
Sugarcane.  
As informed by the State Government, the State of Maharashtra has been 
implementing the Centrally Sponsored Scheme National Food and Nutrition Security 
Mission (NFNSM) – Commercial crop: Sugarcane Development Programme since 
2014-15. Under NFNSM, emphasis has been given on transfer of technology through 
demonstrations and training in order to extend benefits to the farmers.  
  

Under the programme, the following components are being implemented: (a) 
demonstration on inter-cropping and single bud chip technology with sugarcane, (b) 
assistance for breeder seed production, (c) tissue culture plantlets, (d) State level 
training for 2 days, (e) Distribution of plant protection and bio agents; (f) Local 
initiatives Raton and Trash Management distribution and Supercane nursery. 
Rs. 415.02 lakhs has been allocated to Maharashtra for implementation of the 
activities of NFSNM-Sugarcane during 2026-27. 
Further, the Department of Agricultural Research and Education (DARE) 
through the ongoing All India Coordinated Research Project (AICRP) on Sugarcane 
and AICRP on Biological Control, undertakes breeding of sugarcane varieties with 
resistance to diseases and pests, surveillance of disease of sugarcane and training 
programmes for farmers on sugarcane production.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
 LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 404 
TO BE ANSWERED ON THE 21ST JULY, 2026 
SELECTION METHODOLOGY UNDER PM-DDKY 
404. SHRI G KUMAR NAIK: 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण मंũी 
be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government has prepared district-wise scores and rankings based on the 
criteria of agricultural productivity, cropping intensity and credit disbursement for selection 
under Pradhan Mantri Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana (PMDDKY); 
(b) if so, the details and the criterion-wise scores and rankings of all districts considered for 
inclusion under the scheme; 
(c) whether the Government will place the methodology, weightage assigned to each 
parameter and cut-off values used for selection in the public domain; 
(d) whether any districts were excluded despite meeting one or more of the prescribed 
criteria and if so, the details thereof; and 
(e) whether the Government has undertaken any independent assessment or validation of 
the selection methodology and if so, the details and findings thereof? 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण राǛ मंũी (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
(a) & (b): The 100 districts under Prime Minister Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana (DDKY) have 
been selected based on three indicators of low productivity, low cropping intensity and less 
agriculture credit disbursement.   
The number of districts for each State is based on net cropped area and number of 
operational holdings, ensuring balanced regional development and fostering agricultural 
growth where it is most needed. 
(c) & (d): The methodology used published data, which is already in public domain, of above 
mentioned three indicators. Each State was covered under DDKY, with at least 1 district, 
based on net cropped area and number of operational holdings, hence question of exclusion 
does not arise. Further, if States identify additional districts that require similar focused 
attention, they may adopt and replicate the same framework and approach in those districts 
using their existing administrative mechanisms and available scheme resources. 
(e): Since scheme is in 1st year, no independent assessment has been commissioned.
