GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE & FARMERS WELFARE 
DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE & FARMERS WELFARE  
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 405 
TO BE ANSWERED ON THE 21st JULY 2026, 
 
IMPACT OF GROUNDWATER CRISIS ON AGRICULTURE 
405.  SHRI DHARAMBIR SINGH: 
 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण मंũी be 
pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government has conducted any study regarding the economic losses suffered 
by farmers in Bhiwani-Mahendergarh Lok Sabha Constituency due to declining groundwater 
availability and increasing irrigation costs, if so, the details thereof; 
(b) whether any district-wise assessment has been made regarding the suitability of climate-
resilient and low-water-consuming crops for the region, if so, the details thereof; 
(c)whether the Government proposes to introduce a special pilot programme for millet, olive, 
medicinal plants and arid horticulture cultivation in the constituency, if so, the details thereof; 
(d) whether any proposal is under consideration for establishment of a Dryland Agriculture 
Research and Demonstration Centre in South Haryana; and 
(e)if so, the details thereof along with the expected benefits to farmers of Bhiwani and 
Mahendergarh districts? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE  
क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण राǛ मंũी (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
 
(a):  Government has not conducted any study regarding the economic losses to farmers 
in Bhiwani-Mahendergarh Lok Sabha Constituency due to declining groundwater. However, 
Central Ground Water Board jointly with the State Ground Water Departments, carries out 
annual assessment of dynamic groundwater resources at the block level. The assessment 
provides updated estimates of annual groundwater recharge, annual extractable groundwater 
resource, annual groundwater extraction and stage of groundwater extraction, and categorizes 
assessment units as Safe, Semi-Critical, Critical and Over-Exploited based on stage of 
groundwater extraction. Out of 19 groundwater assessment units in Bhiwani, Charkhi Dadri and 
Mahendragarh districts 14 units fall under over-exploited, critical and semi-critical units. 
 
(b): Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) - Central Research Institute for 
Dryland Agriculture has prepared District Agriculture Contingency Plans (DACPs) for all districts 
of the country, which identify district-specific climate-resilient and low-water-requiring crops and 
suitable varieties based on local agro-climatic conditions. For Bhiwani and Mahendragarh 
districts of Haryana, the recommended crops include pearl millet, greengram, mothbean, 
clusterbean, cowpea, castor, sesame, mustard, and chickpea. 
 
(c) to (e):  As per the information received from the Government of Haryana, the Centre 
of Excellence for Semi-Arid Horticulture Crops, Gignow, Bhiwani and the Integrated Horticulture 
Development Centre, Sundrah, Narnaul are operational in the constituency to promote semi-
arid horticulture cultivation. The Centres demonstrate improved varieties of semi-arid 
horticultural crops along with modern technologies such as micro-irrigation, automation and 
protected cultivation. They also serve as centres for production of quality planting material and 
hybrid vegetable seedlings and impart training to farmers on improved horticultural practices 

and efficient water management. Government assistance is also being provided for area 
expansion of horticultural crops through financial support for establishment of new orchards and 
cultivation of vegetables, spices, flowers and aromatic plants to promote crop diversification. To 
promote diversification towards horticulture, Government assistance is being provided to 
farmers for the area expansion of fruit crops such as ber, aonla, citrus (kinnow), guava, and 
strawberry, as well as for the cultivation of vegetables, spices, flowers and aromatic plants. 
During the year 2026–27, in District Bhiwani and Narnaul a target of approximately 2,360 acres 
with a total financial outlay of Rs. 3.18 crore has been earmarked for the area expansion of 
horticultural crops. Government assistance at the rate of 40% to 50% is being provided to 
farmers for establishment of new orchards and for the cultivation of vegetables, spices, flowers, 
and aromatic plants.

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY         
(SHRI JITIN PRASADA) 
 
(a) to (c) The Union Cabinet approved the Export Promotion Mission (EPM) on 12 
November 2025 with an outlay of ₹25,060 crore for the period FY 2025–26 to FY 
2030–31. The Mission aims to enhance India's export competitiveness, with                    
a special focus on MSMEs, first-time exporters and labour-intensive sectors, through an 
integrated approach combining trade finance support with measures to improve market 
access and export readiness. 
 

 
2 
 
Districts as Export Hubs (DEH) initiative provides the district-level framework for 
decentralised export promotion duly engaging all stakeholders and is aided by Export 
Promotion Mission at grassroots level. 
 
 
The institutional infrastructure under DEH comprises State Level Export Promotion 
Committees (SEPCs) and District Export Promotion Committees (DEPCs). 
 
The State/UT and district-wise list of products/services identified under the DEH 
initiative including districts of Bihar is placed at 
https://content.dgft.gov.in/Website/dgftprod/a667478a-d204-4d95-a71c-
a58452e1c6d9/Note%20-%20Districts%20as%20Export%20Hubs%20Initiative.pdf. 
 
In Bihar, District Export Action Plans (DEAPs) have been prepared and adopted for 
all 38 districts. Micro-enterprises and clusters are engaged through district-level 
outreach, capacity-building and market-linkage activities. 
 
(d) The operational details of interventions under the Niryat Protsahan sub 
scheme are as under: 
i. Support for Interest Subvention aims to bridge the interest-rate gap and ensure 
liquidity for MSME exporters at globally competitive rates against items notified. 
ii. Support for Collateral for Export Credit aims to bridge existing collateral gap 
and enable access to export credit for MSMEs. 
iii. Support for Alternative Trade Instruments provides alternate export financing 
mechanism by subventing export factoring interest rates for MSMEs. 
iv. Credit Guarantee Facility for E-Commerce Exporters supports MSME e-
commerce exporters selling via courier, postal or fulfilment warehouses through credit 
guarantee and interest subvention support on revolving working capital. 
v. Support for Emerging Export Opportunities enables MSMEs to expand into 
new/high-risk markets through access to shared-risk and credit-enhancement 
instruments. 
 
( e ) Available to all MSMEs, the Niryat Disha sub-scheme is focused on trade 
enablers such as export quality and compliance support, international branding and 
packaging, market access initiatives, logistics cost support to low export intensity 
regions, warehousing, e-commerce export hubs, trade intelligence and capacity 
building. eCommerce exporters in tier-two and tier-three are eligible to avail support 
under relevant interventions of Niryat Protsahan and Niryat Disha Sub-Schemes of 
EPM.

DATA BASE OF CHILD SEX OFFENDERS 
 
407.      SMT. PRIYANKA GANDHI VADRA: 
 
Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government proposes to make the data base of child sex 
offenders accessible to the public and if so, the details thereof; 
 
(b) whether the Government proposes to undertake real time monitoring of 
child sex offenders  and if so, the details thereof, along with the any pilot 
projects taken up; 
 
(c) whether measures are being taken to strengthen background verification 
and screening of individuals employed in child-care, educational institutions, 
sports institutions and other  establishments that grant easy access to 
minors and if so, the details thereof; 
 
(d) whether the mandatory verification of criminal records and availability of 
child sex offender data to such institutions and if so, the details thereof; and 
 
(e) the action being taken to ensure the protection of minors from convicted 
sex offenders and  the reporting mechanisms established for the same 
particularly in child-care and educational institutions? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
(SHRI BANDI SANJAY KUMAR) 
 
(a) & (b): Police’ and ‘Public Order’ are ‘State’ subjects under the Seventh Schedule 
of the  Constitution of India. State  Governments/ UT  Administrations  are primarily  
 

 
-2- 
L.S.US.Q.NO. 407 FOR 21.07.2026  
responsible for the prevention, detection, investigation and prosecution of crimes 
through their Law Enforcement Agencies (LEAs).  
 
The National Database on Sexual Offenders (NDSO), is a centralized database 
established by NCRB in 2018 under the Ministry of Home Affairs. It is designed to 
assist law enforcement agencies in the investigation, detection and prevention of 
sexual offences, including offences under the Protection of Chi ldren from Sexual 
Offences (POCSO) Act, by maintaining records of sexual offenders. The database 
serves as an investigative tool to facilitate the identification of accused and repeat 
offenders, verify criminal antecedents, during investigation of sexual o ffences. 
Access to NDSO is restricted to authorized law enforcement agencies, ensuring that  
information is used for official investigative purposes.  
 (c) to (e): National Crime Records Check (NCRC) portal developed by NCRB is used 
by government agencies for the preliminary verification of employees and 
personnel. It facilitates preliminary crime record check using CCTNS/ Inter-operable 
Criminal Justice System (ICJS) database.  
States/UTs have launched citizen portal over CCTNS application facilitating 
verification request by individuals/ organizations. Educational institutions, child 
care homes, and other establishments may request for verification of individuals 
through CCTNS citizen portals. States/UTs police can use NCRC for verifying crime 
records of an individual during the verification process.  
 
 
 

 
-3- 
L.S.US.Q.NO. 407 FOR 21.07.2026  
The Ministry of Home Affairs has also launched the online Cyber Crime 
Reporting Portal for reporting incidents of online child sexual exploitation and other 
cyber-crimes, and the National Cyber Crime Reporting Helpline (1930) provides 
assistance in reporting cyber related offences.

ONE DISTRICT ONE PRODUCT FOR KARBI ANGLONG 
 
408.  SHRI AMARSING TISSO: 
 
Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY be pleased to state: 
वाणिज्य  एवं उद्योग मंत्री 
(a)  whether Karbi Anglong and Dima Hasao districts of Assam have been identified 
under the  One District One Product (ODOP) initiative and, if so, the details 
thereof; 
 
(b)  the products identified under the initiative in the said districts; 
 
(c)  the details of financial, technical and marketing assistance, including support 
for branding and exports, provided under the initiative in the said districts; and 
 
(d)  whether the Government proposes to establish dedicated ODOP export hubs 
or common facilitation centres in Karbi Anglong and Dima Hasao and, if so, the 
details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
 
वाणिज्य  एवं उद्योग मंत्रालय में राज्य मंत्री (श्री णिणिन प्रसाद)   
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE & INDUSTRY 
(SHRI JITIN PRASADA) 
 
(a) to (d):  One District One Product (ODOP) is an initiative by the Department for 
Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) with the aim of selecting, 
branding, and promoting at least one product from each district of the country 
to enable holistic growth across all regions. The selection of ODOP products is 
undertaken by the respective State/UT Governments. The Government of 
Assam has identified Ginger as an ODOP product for Karbi Anglong and Dima 
Hasao districts. 
The implementation of ODOP is primarily throug h convergence with the 
schemes/programmes of the Central Ministries/Departments and the State 
Governments. No district-specific financial allocation is made under the ODOP 
initiative. 
Several steps have been undertaken to promote and enhance the visibility  of 
products identified under the ODOP initiative, including those identified from 
Assam. These steps include facilitating participation in domestic and 
international exhibitions; capacity -building initiatives in collaboration with 

various agencies; and e -commerce onboarding drives for the Government e -
Marketplace (GeM)-ODOP Bazaar, which showcases and stocks India’s best 
ODOP products. 
The ODOP initiative has previously collaborated with key institutions such as 
the Indian Institutes of Technology (IIT Bom bay, Roorkee, Kharagpur, and 
Bhubaneswar), and National Institute of Design (NID Ahmedabad), along with 
the Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT) and Press Information Bureau 
(PIB), to undertake capacity-building initiatives focused on product innova tion, 
diversification, quality enhancement, and market readiness, thereby supporting 
local industries including agriculture-based products from Assam. 
For promoting ODOP at the international level, engagement with MEA and 
Indian Missions abroad, virtual buyer -seller meets, and participation in 
international exhibitions have been undertaken. Also, various ODOP Products 
have been included in gifting at mul tilateral and bilateral meetings in India to 
popularize them internationally. 
Further, the Government of Assam has informed that the PM Formalization of  
Micro Food Processing Enterprises (PMFME) Scheme provides financial 
assistance for setting up ODOP unit s, along with branding and marketing 
support for food processing units. Under the Scheme, financial assistance has 
been extended to 7 ODOP units in Karbi Anglong and 8 ODOP units in 
Dima Hasao. District Export Promotion Committees have been constituted in 
all districts to promote ODOP products. The State Government has constructed 
the Unity Mall in Guwahati, which has stalls showcasing ODOP products, 
including those from Karbi Anglong and Dima Hasao.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE & FARMERS’ WELFARE 
DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE & FARMERS’ WELFARE  
 
LOK SABHA 
 UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 409 
TO BE ANSWERED ON THE 21st JULY, 2026 
 
AGRICULTURE DISTRESS DUE TO EXTREME CLIMATE 
 
 409. ADV GOWAAL KAGADA PADAVI: 
 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण मंũी 
be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has taken note of the increasing agricultural distress caused 
by unpredictable rainfall, extreme heatwaves, falling groundwater levels, and climate 
change-related crop losses, particularly in drought-prone and tribal regions of the 
country; 
(b) the details of the measures being taken to support farmers facing rising fertilizer, diesel 
and irrigation costs; 
(c) whether any district-specific assessment has been conducted regarding the impact of 
climate variability on crop productivity and farmer incomes in vulnerable regions; and 
(d) the steps being taken by the Government to strengthen climate-resilient agriculture, 
improve water conservation and protect small and marginal farmers from recurring crop 
losses? 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE  
क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण राǛ मंũी (SHRI  RAM NATH THAKUR) 
 
(a) & (b) The Government is taking various measures to promote sustainable agricultural 
practices and effectively address the climate change-related challenges. The Government 
supports farmers by ensuring the availability of key fertilizers at affordable prices through 
price regulation and subsidy mechanisms. Government has also implemented Nutrient 
Based Subsidy (NBS) Scheme w.e.f. 01.04.2010 for Phosphatic and Potassic (P&K) 
Fertilizers. Under NBS policy, MRP of P&K fertilizers are decontrolled and companies are 
free to fix MRP as per their business dynamics at a reasonable level. Further, under Urea 
Subsidy Scheme, Govt ensures affordable urea availability to farmers by providing 
government subsidies covering production and freight costs, with urea sold at a fixed 
Maximum Retail Price (MRP). In addition, under the Soil Health & Fertility Scheme, 
assistance is provided to States for promoting Integrated Nutrient Management through the 
judicious use of fertilizers, thereby improving fertilizer use efficiency and promoting 
balanced nutrient application. Since the inception of the scheme (2014-15), 26.18 crore 
Soil Health Cards have been generated. Fertigation is being promoted through micro-
irrigation systems under the Per Drop More Crop (PDMC) Scheme. Fertigation enables the 
application of water-soluble fertilizers directly to the root zone through micro irrigation 
systems, ensuring precise and uniform nutrient delivery. This improves fertilizer use 
efficiency, reduces nutrient losses, and promotes judicious use of fertilizers. Since the 
inception of the scheme (2014-15), an area of 114.60 lakh hectares has been brought under 
micro-irrigation, benefitting about 100 lakh farmers. Further, as of the pre-monsoon 2026 
assessment, the groundwater situation remains largely stable across the country. Out of 
9,085 monitoring wells, 87.8% (7,977 wells) fall under the normal category.  Ministry of New 
and Renewable Energy (MNRE) is implementing Pradhan Mantri Kisan Urja Suraksha 

evam Utthaan Mahabhiyan (PM-KUSUM) under which financial assistance is provided for 
the installation of standalone solar agricultural pumps, including the replacement of existing 
diesel agricultural pumps in off-grid areas where grid supply is not available. Against the 
sanctioned capacity of 13.07 lakh solar pumps, around 11.5 lakh solar pumps have been 
installed, benefiting an equivalent number of farmers. These installations have resulted in 
annual savings of around 793 million litres of diesel and reducing the cost of irrigation. All 
these measures help in reducing the cost of production.      
 
(c) & (d): The Government, through Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) is 
implementing a project- National Innovations in Climate Resilient Agriculture (NICRA) that 
studies the impact of climate change on agriculture, conducts district level risk and 
vulnerability assessment of agriculture. Under the project, risk and vulnerability assessment 
of agriculture to climate change has been carried out at district-level for 651 predominantly 
agricultural districts as per Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) protocols. 
310 districts were identified as vulnerable out of which 109 districts have been categorized 
as ‘very high’ and 201 districts as ‘highly’ vulnerable. District Agriculture Contingency Plans 
(DACPs) for these 651 districts have also been prepared to address weather aberrations 
and recommending location specific climate resilient crops and varieties and management 
practices. To enhance resilience to climate variability, location-specific climate-resilient 
technologies, including the System of Rice Intensification (SRI), aerobic rice, direct-seeded 
rice, zero-till wheat, climate-resilient crop varieties, and in-situ crop residue management, 
are being demonstrated for adoption by farmers. Under NICRA, climate-resilient 
technologies are being demonstrated in 448 Climate Resilient Villages across 151 
vulnerable districts in 28 States/UTs, supported by village-level seed banks and community 
nurseries to enhance farmers' resilience and ensure timely availability of quality seeds. 
Technical assistance is provided to small and marginal farmers to promote climate-resilient 
practices through Village Climate Risk Management Committees (VCRMCs), while 
capacity-building and training programmes are conducted under the Agricultural 
Technology Management Agency (ATMA). Further, to address the challenges of climate 
change, ICAR has released 2900 varieties during last 10 years (2014-2024), out of which 
2661 varieties are tolerant to one or more biotic and/or abiotic stresses. In anticipation of 
El Niño conditions and their potential impact on the southwest monsoon, Mahalanobis 
National Crop Forecast Centre (MNCFC) has identified 262 vulnerable districts and States 
have updated the District Agriculture Contingency Plans (DACPs) in coordination with 
ICAR-Central Research Institute for Dryland Agriculture (ICAR-CRIDA). 
 
Further, the Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY), along with the 
Restructured Weather Based Crop Insurance Scheme (RWBCIS), provides comprehensive 
insurance coverage against crop losses arising from natural calamities and adverse 
weather events, thereby mitigating climate-related risks faced by farmers. As on 
30.06.2026, a total of 92.68 crore farmer applications have been enrolled under the 
Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) and the Restructured Weather Based Crop 
Insurance Scheme (RWBCIS). Further, since the inception of the schemes in 2016, 86% 
of the total unique farmer applications enrolled under PMFBY and RWBCIS have been from 
small and marginal farmers.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF COOPERATION 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 411 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 21th July, 2026 
 
National Cooperative Policy 2025 
411. Dr. C M Ramesh: 
Will the Minister of COOPERATION (सहकारिता मंत्री) be pleased to state: 
a) whether the National Cooperative Policy, 2025 envisages expansion of cooperatives into 
new sectors such as food processing, renewable energy, logistics, exports and digital 
commerce;  
b) whether the Government has identified sector -wise opportunities for promoting 
cooperative enterprises in Andhra Pradesh, particularly in fisheries, horticulture, dairy, 
tribal products, women-led enterprises and handloom sectors; 
c) whether any proposals have been received from the State Government of Andhra Pradesh 
for financial or technical assistance under the Policy; and 
d) if so, the details thereof, district -wise, including the likely employment generation and 
increase in farmers' income expected from such initiatives? 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF COOPERATION 
सहकारिता मंत्री (SHRI AMIT SHAH) 
(a) Yes, Sir. The expansion of cooperatives into new sectors such as food processing, 
renewable energy, logistics, exports and digital commerce is enunciated in the National 
Cooperation Policy, 2025. Some of which are as follows: 
“4.2.5 Promote exports of cooperative sector products to international markets and 
enhance the share of the cooperative sector in the total export of the country;  
4.2.9. Promote the enhancement of existing processing capacities, including the 
manufacturing of value -added products through capital infusion, to increase 
members' incomes;  
5.1.3. Promote cooperatives to leverage e-commerce platforms, such as the Government e -
Marketplace (GeM) and the Open Network for Digital Commerce (ONDC), to access 
a large customer base and achieve better pricing;  
7.1.2. Promote the entry and strengthening of cooperatives in new and emerging sectors, in 
both urban and rural space, such as micro -insurance, renewable energy, water 

Page 2 of 3 
 
distribution, health, education, waste management, transportation, biogas production, 
mobile application -based aggregator services (for example – cooperative of taxi 
drivers, individuals providing household services (like plumber, electrician, etc.)), 
etc., to enhance diversification and increase member income.” 
(b) Yes, Sir. The Central Government has identified opportunities for promoting 
cooperative societies in Andhra Pradesh in the dairy sector under the White Revolution 2.0. 
Under the said initiative, it has been envisaged to set up 7042 new dairy cooperative societies 
(DCS) and to strengthen 2107 existing DCS. To date, 1078 new DCS have been formed, and 
807 existing DCS have been strengthened.  
Moreover, the National Cooperative Development Corporation (NCDC), a statutory 
organization under the Ministry of Cooperation, is implementing the “Yuva Sahakar” and 
“Swayam Shakti Sahakar” Schemes. Both the schemes are fully funded and supported by 
NCDC. Yuva Sahakar Scheme is implemented with the aim of encouraging newly formed 
cooperative societies with new and/or innovative ideas. The objective of the “Swayam Shakti 
Sahakar” Scheme is to facilitate access to affordable, cost -effective, and reliable financial 
services to the poor, including women ’s Self-Help Groups (SHGs), to undertake 
common/collective socio - economic activities to promote sustainable livelihoods. NCDC 
extends funding on a project basis. 
(c) & (d): No, Sir. No proposal has been received from the Government of Andhra Pradesh 
for financial or technical assistance under the National Cooperation Policy, 2025.  
However, NCDC has been mandated to promote economic development through cooperative 
institutions. The primary objective of this Corporation is to promote, strengthen, and develop 
farmer cooperatives with a view to enhancing production, productivity , and the creation of 
post-harvest infrastructure. To this end, NCDC extends financial assistance to cooperatives in 
diverse sectors such as agricultural marketing and inputs, processing, storage, marketing of 
agricultural produce, and supply of seeds, fertilizers , and other agricultural inputs. Since its 
inception, NCDC has been providing financial assistance under its Corporation -sponsored 
schemes as well as Central Sector Schemes of various Ministries, covering a wide spectrum 
of notified commodities and services. As of 30.06.2026, NCDC has cumulatively disbursed 
₹73,454.93 crore for the development of cooperative institutions in the state of Andhra 
Pradesh. Activity-wise disbursement in Andhra Pradesh during the last five years is placed at 
Annexure-I.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
 MINISTRY OF PANCHAYATI RAJ 
LOK SABHA 
 UNSTARRED QUESTION 412 
ANSWERED ON 21.07.2026 
  
E-GRAM SWARAJ PORTAL IN SCHEDULED TRIBE-DOMINATED AREAS 
  
412. DR. FAGGAN SINGH KULASTE: 
  
Will the Minister of PANCHAYATI RAJ be pleased to State:   
(a)  whether the Government is aware that the utilization of e-Gram Swaraj and Audit Online 
portals by Gram Panchayats in Scheduled Areas and tribal-dominated areas is lower than the 
national average in these regions; 
  
(b)  if so, the details thereof, State-wise; 
  
(c)  the current status of the preparation of Gram Panchayat Development Plans (GPDP) in 
alignment with the provisions of the Panchayats (Extension to the Scheduled Areas) Act (PESA), 
1996, and the subsequent uploading of these plans on the e-Gram Swaraj portal in these areas; 
  
(d)  the major challenges identified regarding digital infrastructure, internet bumbling, 
connectivity, electricity supply, and technical capacity, along with the steps taken by the 
Government to mitigate them; and 
  
(e) whether the Government has conducted special training and capacity building programmes 
for elected representatives and panchayat officials in tribal areas formulated a specific action 
plan to strengthen digital governance in these regions of Panchayats, if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
  
THE MINISTER OF PANCHAYATI RAJ 
 
(SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH ALIAS LALAN SINGH)  
  
(a) to (b)  The Parliament enacted the Provisions of the Panchayats (Extension to the 
Scheduled Areas) Act, 1996 (PESA) under Article 243M(4)(b) of the Constitution to extend the 
provisions of Part IX of the Constitution to the Fifth Schedule Areas with certain exceptions and 
modifications. Panchayats, being "Local Government", are a State subject and operate through 
the respective State Panchayati Raj Acts. Accordingly, implementation of PESA, including the 
adoption and utilisation of digital governance applications such as eGramSwaraj and 
AuditOnline in Scheduled Areas, falls within the purview of the respective State Governments. 
The Ministry of Panchayati Raj facilitates digital governance through the e-Panchayat 
Mission Mode Project (MMP), including eGramSwaraj and AuditOnline, and periodically 
reviews their implementation with the States through review meetings and other monitoring 

2 
 
mechanisms. The Ministry has also developed 10 PESA Indicators to facilitate assessment of 
PESA implementation by the States, one of which relates to the uploading of Gram Panchayat 
Development Plans (GPDPs) of PESA Gram Sabhas on the eGramSwaraj portal. 
The State-wise details of utilisation of eGramSwaraj/ status of GPDP uploads in PESA areas, are 
placed below. 
S.No. State Name Total PESA Panchayat Total Villages Approved PESA Main Plan 
1 Andhra Pradesh 609 1613 609 
2 Chhattisgarh 5552 9891 5532 
3 Gujarat 2889 4701 2755 
4 Himachal Pradesh 178 1533 164 
5 Jharkhand 2066 17240 2066 
6 Madhya Pradesh 5197 7710 5173 
7 Maharashtra 2918 4317 2907 
8 Odisha 1390 11668 1390 
9 Rajasthan 1608 5690 1604 
10 Telangana 1314 1321 1314 
Total 23,721 65,684 23,514 
  
(c)  The Ministry of Panchayati Raj has initiated Gram Panchayat Development Plan (GPDP) 
integration of PESA within the GPDP framework to enable the preparation of PESA-specific 
Village Development Plans. A dedicated PESA-GPDP Portal has been launched by the Ministry 
to facilitate the preparation, implementation, and monitoring of Gram Panchayat Development 
Plans (GPDPs) in Scheduled Areas under the provisions of the PESA Act. 
Further, in Plan Year 2026-27, PESA has been included as a separate theme in 
eGramSwaraj Portal with 42 activities. It has also been made mandatory for Gram Sabhas in 
Fifth Schedule Areas to take up at least one activity under PESA theme while preparing their 
GPDP plan. 
(d)  In certain rural and tribal areas, challenges such as inadequate digital infrastructure, 
intermittent internet connectivity, and limited technical capacity have been experienced, 
affecting the adoption of digital governance applications. To address these challenges, the 
Ministry of Panchayati Raj, in coordination with the State Governments, provides continuous 
technical support, undertakes periodic reviews of the implementation of the e-Panchayat 
applications, and upgrades the applications based on feedback received from the stakeholders. 
Further, internet connectivity to Gram Panchayats is being strengthened through the BharatNet 
project being implemented by the Department of Telecommunications to provide broadband 
connectivity to Gram Panchayats across the country. 
(e)  Yes, sir.  Panchayat, being “Local Self Government”, is a State subject and part of the 
State list of the Seventh Schedule of the Constitution of India. However, the Ministry of 
Panchayati Raj is implementing the Centrally Sponsored Scheme of revamped Rashtriya Gram 
Swaraj Abhiyan (RGSA) since the financial year 2022-23 in States/ UTs, including tribal/PESA 

3 
 
areas with the objectives to strengthen the capacity of Panchayati Raj institutions (PRIs) by 
imparting training to Elected Representatives (ERs), Panchayat Functionaries and other 
stakeholders to develop their governance capabilities for leadership roles, enabling the Gram 
Panchayats to function effectively across all States/UTs.  
Under the scheme, the Ministry provides support for Capacity Building & Training 
(CB&T) of Panchayat representatives and Officials in different categories, including various 
digital trainings as per the priority of the States/UTs. Since, 2022-23 to 2026-27 (as on 
10.07.2026), 1,87,238 Panchayat representatives and officials have been trained in PESA States 
to strengthen digital governance and other digital platforms.

EXPAND SUGARCANE FARMING 
 
413.  SHRI HARENDRA SINGH MALIK: 
 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण 
मंũी be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government is providing any special Budgetary incentives for expanding 
the scope of sugarcane farming from sugar to Bio-energy in Muzaffarnagar and Bijnor 
district with an aim to make these districts Bio-energy subs, if so, the details thereof;  
 (b) whether the Government proposes to provide any additional subsidy on solar pumps 
for irrigation to sugarcane farmers in Muzaffarnagar and Bijnor districts under the PM-
KUSUM Scheme;  
(c) whether the Government is contempleting upon amending the FRP formula in order 
to ensure that farmers are able to receive their share directly from the income generated 
from the production of electricity and ethonol as by products in sugar mills, if so, the details 
thereof; and  
 (d) the details of the target fixed for Muzaffarnagar regarding the promotion of drip 
irrigation under Per Drop More Crop Scheme keeping in view the depleting ground water 
table in the district? 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
 
क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण राǛ  मंũी                                       (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
 
(a)  Sugarcane is one of the important commercial crops in India, cultivated over an 
average area of 54.20 lakh hectares with an average production of 448.62 million tonnes 
during the period 2020-21 to 2024-25. Besides meeting the domestic requirement of 
sugar, sugarcane serves as a feedstock for a range of value-added products such as 
jaggery, khandsari, ethanol, etc. Further, its by-products, viz., molasses, bagasse and 
press mud, are utilized for the production of ethanol, renewable electricity, organic 
manure and compressed biogas. 
 

The Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution and Ministry of New and 
Renewable Energy implement various schemes throughout the country which includes 
support for sugar mills for Bio-energy. The Department of Food & Public Distribution 
implemented the 'Scheme for extending financial Assistance to sugar mills/distilleries for 
enhancement and augmentation of the Ethanol Production capacity' with a view to 
increase production of ethanol and its supply under Ethanol Blended with Petrol (EBP) 
Programme, especially in the sugar surplus seasons. The scheme also aimed to improve 
the liquidity position of the sugar mills enabling them to clear cane price arrears of the 
farmers. Under the scheme, the Government extended financial assistance in the form 
of interest subvention for five years including a one-year moratorium against the loan 
availed by project proponents from banks @ 6% per annum or 50% of the rate of interest 
charged by banks, whichever is lower, for setting up of new distilleries or expansion of 
existing distilleries or converting molasses-based distilleries to dual feed stocks. Various 
windows for application were opened under the scheme from 2018 to 2022 and a 
separate scheme window of 6 months for Cooperative Sugar Mills was notified on 
06.03.2025. Currently no window is open for receiving applications under the ethanol 
interest subvention scheme. 
The Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE) under its National Bioenergy 
Programme has been providing Central Financial Assistance for installation of waste-to-
energy plants, biomass-based power projects, biomass based Briquette/Pellet 
manufacturing projects, including Muzaffarnagar and Bijnor districts of Uttar Pradesh. 
The Scheme was valid till 31.03.2026, for issue of sanctions under the National 
Bioenergy Programme. However, there is no separate budgetary incentives for 
expanding the scope of sugarcane farming from sugar to Bio-energy in Muzaffarnagar 
and Bijnor District of Uttar Pradesh with an aim to make these districts Bio-energy hubs, 
under their National Bioenergy Programme. 
(b) The Government of Uttar Pradesh under Component-B of the PM-KUSUM Scheme 
provides a subsidy of 60% to farmers across all districts of the State for the installation 
of solar pumps ranging from 2 HP to 7.5 HP. Further, the subsidy applicable for 7.5 HP 
solar pumps is being extended to 10 HP solar pumps. No additional subsidy is being 
provided exclusively to sugarcane farmers in the Muzaffarnagar and Bijnor Lok Sabha 
constituencies. 
(c) The Central Government fixes the Fair and Remunerative Price (FRP) of sugarcane 
for Sugar Season (October-September) on the recommendations of the Commission for 
Agricultural Costs and Prices (CACP) in consultation with the State Governments and 
other stakeholders, in accordance with the factors mentioned in clause 3(1) of the 
Sugarcane (Control) Order, 1966. There is no proposal of amending the FRP formula. 
(d) The Horticulture Department, Government of Uttar Pradesh had set a target of 1,500 
hectares for the installation of drip irrigation systems in sugarcane under Muzaffarnagar 
district during 2025–26, against which an area of 1,208 hectares has been covered.

414.  SHRI AMAR SHARADRAO KALE: 
 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE कृषि और ककसान कल्याण 
मंत्री be pleased to state: 
(a)  whether the Government proposes to launch any new scheme to promote cotton 
research, value addition and the export of cotton and cotton-based products in the Wardha Lok 
Sabha constituency of Maharashtra; 
(b)  if so, the details of the said scheme, the proposed budgetary provision and the timeline 
for the implementation thereof; 
(c)  whether the Government proposes to establish a cotton research centre, modern ginning 
and processing facilities in textile and value addition cluster, and an export facilitation centre in 
the Wardha Lok Sabha constituency; 
(d)  if so, the details thereof; and 
(e)  if not, the reasons therefor? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
कृषि और ककसान कल्याण राज्य मंत्री (SHRI BHAGIRATH CHOUDHARY) 
 
(a) & (b): Yes, the Govt of India has approved the “Mission for Cotton Productivity (Kapas 
Kanti)” to enhance cotton productivity and production through strategic interventions including 
research and extension activities in 14 cotton growing districts of the country including Wardha 
Lok Sabha constituency. Mission also seeks to augment supply of superior quality Indian cotton 
through improved processing capabilities, robust branding, strengthened value chain linkages 
and promote cotton export.  
 
 The Mission has been approved by the Govt. of India for the entire country on 5th May, 
2026 with an outlay of ₹5659.22 crore for a period of five years (2026-27 to 2030-31). 
 
 

2 
 
 
 
 
(c) to (e):  There is no proposal to establish a cotton research center , modern ginning and 
processing facilities, a textile and value addition cluster, and an export facilitation center in 
Wardha. ICAR - Central Institute for Cotton Research (CICR), Nagpur and All India Coordinated 
Research Project (AICRP) on Cotton  centres in Dr Panjabrao Deshmukh Krishi Vidyapeeth, 
Akola; Vasantrao Naik Marathwada Krishi Vidyapeeth, Parbhani and Mahatma Phule Krishi 
Vidyapeeth, Rahuri are operating in Maharashtra to enhance cotton production and productivity 
in different cotton -growing zones including Wardha  through development of high -yielding, 
climate-resilient and disease resistant varieties, and their production and protection 
technologies.

DEPARTMENT OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT

  ANSWERED ON 21/07/2026 
 
LOANS TO SELF-HELP GROUPS 
 
415.  Shri Chandan Chauhan: 
 
Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  whether the Government is aware that Micro Finance 
Companies frequently extend loans to Self Help Groups (SHGs) 
in rural areas at exorbitantly high rates of interest, forcing these 
SHGs to provide loans to their members at interest rates ranging 
from 30 to 40 per cent or even higher; 
(b)  if so, the details thereof and whether complaints regarding such 
high rates of interest have been received; 
(c)  the steps taken by the Government to rectify this situation so 
that members can access credit at fair and equitable rates of 
interest; and 
(d)  whether the Government plans to implement any regulations or 
rules for the loan processes of Self Help Groups to protect the 
interests of members and ensure the availability of loan at 
affordable rates? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
(DR. CHANDRA SEKHAR PEMMASANI) 
 
(a) to (c): The Ministry facilitates access to institutional credit for 
women Self Help Groups under Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana – 
National Rural Livelihood Mission (DAY-NRLM) through Scheduled 
Commercial Banks and Cooperative Banks. Under the programme, 
women SHGs are supported to avail collateral-free loans from these 
banks in accordance with the guidelines issued by the Reserve Bank 
of India and NABARD. The Ministry does not facilitate or promote 
borrowing by SHGs from Microfinance Companies. 
 

Page 2 of 2 
 
(d): To ensure the availability of loan to women Self Help Groups at 
affordable rates and to safeguard their interests, the Government has 
put in place a policy framework under Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana – 
National Rural Livelihood Mission (DAY-NRLM). The programme 
provides Interest Subvention on loans availed by eligible women 
SHGs from Scheduled Commercial Banks and Cooperative Banks.

be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government has assessed the decreasing profitability of agriculture 
in the Moradabad district of Uttar Pradesh owing to costs escalation in farming, erratic 
rains, depletion in the groundwater level and the increasing instances of pests and 
diseases; 
(b) the details of the assistance provided to the district under the Pradhan Mantri 
Krishi Sinchai Yojana National Mission for Sustainable Agriculture (NMSA), Soil Health 
Card Schemes and other Central Scheme during the last three years; 
(c) whether the Government has conducted any study regarding crop diversification, 
micro irrigation and climate-friendly agricultural practices for the benefits of farmers of the 
district; 
(d) the arrangement made for the effective implementation of the soil Schemes and 
monitoring of their impacts on income of farmers; and 
(e) the other measures proposed by the Government to improve irrigation efficiency, 
reduce costs and increase the income of farmers of Moradabad district? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE  
क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण राǛ मंũी  (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
 
(a) : No study has been commissioned to assess the decreasing profitability of 
agriculture in Moradabad district of Uttar Pradesh. 
 
(b) to (e): Pradhan Manti Krishi Sinchayee Yojana (PMKSY) is an umbrella scheme, 
consisting of three components -  Accelerated Irrigation Benefit Programme (AIBP) and Har 
Khet Ko Pani (HKKP) being implemented by the Department of Water Resources, River 
Development & Ganga Rejuvenation (DoWR,RD&GR), Ministry of Jal Shakti,  and 
Watershed Development Component (WDC) being implemented by Department of Land 
Resources, Ministry of Rural Development.   
 Under Accelerated Irrigation Benefits Programme (AIBP) and Har Khet Ko Paani (HKKP) 
components of PMKSY, total irrigation potential created in Uttar Pradesh since 2016 is 
777.02 thousand hectares. Of this, the Madhya Ganga Canal Project, which benefits 
Moradabad district of Uttar Pradesh, has created an irrigation potential of 76.68 thousand 
hectares. Rs. 63.81 crore central assistance has been provided to this project under 
PMKSY.  
 
In Moradabad district, one watershed development project was sanctioned during 
2021-22 under WDC–PMKSY 2.0, covering 5,042 ha with a project cost of ₹11.09 Crore.   
 

 The Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare implements Soil Health & Fertility 
(SH&F) scheme to provide Soil Health Cards (SHCs) for all farm holdings, to promote 
balanced and integrated nutrient management for improving productivity and soil fertility. 
The activities like, Testing of Soil Samples to issue/generate the Soil Health Card, Training 
and Demonstration, setting up/ strengthening of Soil Testing, Fertilizers/ Bio-Fertilizers & 
Organic Fertilizers Quality Control Labs, Promotion of Micro-nutrients. 28800 Soil Health 
Card have been generated through the scheme in Moradabad district during the last 
three years. Under the Per Drop More Crop (PDMC)  Scheme, Central Assistance of Rs. 
596.57 crore has been provided to the State of Uttar Pradesh during the last three years. 
An area of 2.55 lakh ha has been covered under micro irrigation in the State which includes 
1823 ha area in Moradabad District during this period. The SH&F and PDMC schemes are 
implemented based on the Annual Action Plan prepared by the State.

(a) :  The Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY)  envisages coverage of all food 
crops  (cereals, millets and pulses), oilseeds and commercial/horticultural crops subject 
to availability of past yield data of requisite number of years based on Crop Cutting 
Experiments  (CCEs)  as well as capacity of the State Government to conduct requisite 
number of CCEs or adopt YES-TECH (Yield Estimation System Based on Technology) 
to assess the yield of the crop to calculate claims.   However, specific crop is notified by 
the concerned State Government keeping in view the aforesaid provision.    
For the crops not meeting the aforesaid conditions, the concerned State 
Government is free to notify them for coverage under Restructured Weather Based Crop 
Insurance Scheme  (RWBCIS)  under which claims payment are being structured on the 
basis of weather index parameters. 
  

State-wise details of crops being notified by the State Governments under the 
scheme are given in Annexure-I.  
(b):  At present, in addition to all the 5 Public Sector General Insurance Companies, 15 
private general insurance companies have also been empaneled for implementation of 
Crop Insurance schemes in the country.  The company for implementation of the scheme 
is selected by the concerned State Government from the empaneled list of companies 
through tender process. The insurance companies currently empaneled for 
implementation of PMFBY are as under:

1. Agriculture Insurance Company of India Ltd. 
2. National Insurance Company Ltd. 
3. New India Assurance Company Ltd.

Central)

General Insurance Company Ltd.)

(c) to (d):  Year and State-wise details of premium collected from farmers and claims paid 
to farmers during last five years under the scheme from 2021-22 to 2025-26 are given in 
Annexure-II.  Insurance company-wise, year-wise details of farmers’ share of premium 
and claims paid to farmers in respect of all States/UTs and insurance company-wise 
details of farmers share of premium and claims paid in Maharashtra during 2021-22 to 
2025-26 are given in Annexure-III & Annexure-IV respectively. 
 
(e):  Under PMFBY, actuarial/ bidded premium rates are charged by implementing 
insurance companies.   
The scheme is mainly implemented on ‘Area Approach’ basis. Actual yield is 
arrived at by the concerned State Government on the basis of Crop Cutting Experiments 
(CCE) as well as technology-based yield estimation under YES-TECH (wherever 
applicable), subsequent to which season end claims are worked out based on the shortfall 
in actual yield vis-à-vis threshold yield on the National Crop Insurance Portal (NCIP) as 
per the formula in the Operational Guidelines of the scheme.  Enrolled farmer has no 
need to file the claims.   
 
However, losses due to localized risks of hailstorm, landslide, inundation, cloud 
burst & natural fire and post-harvest losses due to cyclone, cyclonic/unseasonal rains & 
hailstorms are calculated on individual insured farm basis.    The extent of loss and  claims 
in such case are assessed by a joint committee comprising representatives of State 
Government and concerned insurance company within stipulated time frame under the 
Operational Guidelines of the scheme.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
 MINISTRY OF PANCHAYATI RAJ 
LOK SABHA 
 UNSTARRED QUESTION 419 
ANSWERED ON 21.07.2026 
  
DIGITAL GOVERNANCE 
  
419. SHRI BUNTY VIVEK SAHU: 
  
Will the Minister of PANCHAYATI RAJ be pleased to State:   
(a)  the major progress made to empower Gram Panchayats and enhance transparency 
through the 'Gram Swaraj Abhiyan' and digital governance via the 'e-Gram Swaraj, portal in the 
country during the last two years; 
  
(b)  the specific budgetary assistance provided by the Government to strengthen the three-tier 
Panchayati Raj system and develop rural infrastructure in Madhya Pradesh; and 
  
(c)  whether the Government is providing any special financial package or technical 
assistance to address the lack of basic amenities such as modernization of Panchayat Bhawans 
and computer/internet connectivity in the remote and tribal-dominated Gram Panchayats of 
Chhindwara district, if so, the details thereof? 
  
ANSWER 
  
THE MINISTER OF PANCHAYATI RAJ 
 
(SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH ALIAS LALAN SINGH)  
  
(a)  The Ministry of Panchayati Raj is implementing the e-Panchayat Mission Mode Project 
(MMP) under the Rashtriya Gram Swaraj Abhiyan (RGSA) with the objective of strengthening 
transparency, efficiency, and accountability in the functioning of Panchayati Raj Institutions 
(PRIs) through digital enablement across all States. eGramSwaraj application developed under 
the e-Panchayat MMP is being implemented across Gram Panchayats throughout the country to 
strengthen transparency, accountability and digital governance in Panchayati Raj Institutions. 
eGramSwaraj facilitates planning, budgeting, accounting, progress reporting and asset 
management. 
As on date, during the FY 2025–26, out of a total of 2,58,730 Gram Panchayats and equivalent 
across the States/UTs, 2,55,251 Gram Panchayats and equivalent (98.65%), have uploaded their 
Gram Panchayat Development Plans (GPDPs) on e-Gram Swaraj and 2,45,839 Gram Panchayats 
and equivalents (95%) have made payments amounting to ₹57,337 crore through the e-
GramSwaraj–PFMS interface.  
The State-wise status of implementation of eGramSwaraj during last two years, is placed at 
Annexure.  

2 
 
(b)  Ministry of Panchayati Raj has been implementing the Centrally Sponsored Scheme of 
Rashtriya Gram Swaraj Abhiyan (RGSA) since the financial year 2022-23 in States/ UTs. The 
main objective of the scheme is to build the capacity of Panchayati Raj institutions (PRIs) by 
creating a learning ecosystem, especially through training for the Elected Representatives (ERs), 
functionaries, and other stakeholders to develop their governance capabilities to function 
effectively, and also by supporting exposure visits, development of training modules and 
materials, etc.  
Rural Local Bodies, including Gram Panchayats in Madhya Pradesh, receive Finance 
Commission Grants released by the Ministry of Finance for providing basic services and creation 
and maintenance of community assets and civic infrastructure in rural areas. The year wise 
details of funds released to the State of Madhya Pradesh under the Fifteenth Finance 
Commission Grants during the period from 2022–23 to 2026–27 are as under: 
(Rs. in crore) 
2021-22 2022-23 2023-24 2024-25 2025-26 
2944 3050 3080 3262.75 3150.35 
  
(c)  No, Sir. The Ministry of Panchayati Raj does not provide any separate special financial 
package specifically for the Chhindwara district. 
Panchayat, being “Local Government”, is a State subject and part of the State list of the Seventh 
Schedule of the Constitution of India. Thus, the primary responsibility of providing dedicated 
office infrastructure for Gram Panchayats and computer/internet connectivity in Panchayats lies 
with States/UTs. However, under the Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Rashtriya Gram Swaraj 
Abhiyan (RGSA), the Ministry supplements the efforts of States/UTs in building Panchayat 
infrastructure and Computers and peripherals, at a limited scale, with particular focus on the 
North Eastern States. Accordingly, since the inception of Revamped RGSA i.e. 2022-23, the 
Ministry has approved the procurement of 289 computers and the construction of 50 Panchayat 
Bhawans for the State of Madhya Pradesh. District-wise information is not maintained centrally.  
Further, the Ministry has developed digital applications such as eGramSwaraj, AuditOnline and 
mActionSoft to facilitate digital planning, accounting, audit and monitoring of Panchayat assets. 
The Ministry also extends technical support and capacity-building for effective adoption of these 
applications. Internet connectivity to Gram Panchayats is being improved through initiatives of 
the Department of Telecommunications, including the BharatNet project. 
*****

O.I.H. 
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
DEPARTMENT OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 420 
  ANSWERED ON 21/07/2026 
 
PROGRESS OF RURAL HOUSING UNDER PMAY-G 
 
420.  Shri Bhumare Sandipanrao Asaram: 
Dr. Shivaji Bandappa Kalge: 
 
Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has formulated any fast-track action 
plan or special strategy to achieve the targets ahead of the 
stipulated timeline in view of the current progress of rural 
housing under construction in various States under the Pradhan 
Mantri Awas Yojana-Gramin (PMAY-G); 
(b)  if so, the details thereof, State-wise including Maharashtra; 
(c)  whether the Government is undertaking coordinated efforts with 
the States to streamline provisions relating to acceleration of 
construction, availability of materials, payment processes and 
land verification; and 
(d)  if so, the details thereof, State-wise including Maharashtra? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
(DR. CHANDRA SEKHAR PEMMASANI)  
(a) to (d):  The Ministry of Rural Development is implementing the 
Pradhan Mantri Awaas Yojana- Gramin (PMAY-G) w.e.f. 1st April 2016 
to provide assistance to eligible rural households for the construction 
of Pucca houses with basic amenities to achieve the objective of 
"Housing For All" in rural areas. The scheme seeks to provide 
assistance for the construction of 4.95 crore houses by 31.03.2029.  
  
As of 16.07.2026, a cumulative target of 4.18 crore houses have been 
allocated under the PMAY-G to the States and Union Territories (UTs) 
against which 3.92 crore houses have been sanctioned, 3.10 crore 

Page 2 of 4 
 
houses completed and 1.08 crore houses are remaining to be 
completed against allocated targets. The progress under the PMAY-
G, State/UT wise, including the State of Maharashtra is given in 
Annexure.  
  
A number of steps have been taken by the Government to accelerate 
construction of houses in all States/UTs including Maharashtra, to 
achieve the targets under PMAY-G. These include timely allocation of 
targets and release of adequate funds to the States/UTs, Regular 
review of progress, Monitoring and supervision of the scheme on a 
Dashboard, Regular Workshops by the Ministry with the States/UTs, 
Rural Mason Training program, etc. 
  
The following steps have been taken to ensure availability of 
materials for construction of houses under PMAY-G: 
  
(i) The beneficiaries are assisted in house construction by 
States/UTs with a bouquet of suitable house design typologies;  
(ii) The States/ UTs have also taken necessary steps to ensure the 
sustained availability of good quality construction materials; 
(iii) Awaas SAKHI (Support Application for Knowledge, Help and 
Innovation) mobile application has been developed by Ministry to 
enhance access to PMAY-G by bringing essential information and 
resources in one place. Through the application, the information on 
available house design typologies, locally available BIS certified 
materials and trained rural masons is made available to the 
beneficiaries;  
(iv) The State/UT may tap into Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) 
funding / funding from bilateral/multilateral agencies to promote 
environment friendly green construction designs, technologies and 
materials; and 
(v) Further, Self-Help Groups (SHG) can undertake production of 
quality building materials for supplying the same to the 
beneficiaries of PMAY-G at reasonable rates.  

Page 3 of 4 
 
  
Under the PMAY-G, release of payment of progress linked 
installments of assistance to the beneficiaries is using Aadhaar 
Payments Bridge. From FY 2025-26 onwards, the SNA SPARSH 
framework is being implemented under the PMAY-G for Real time 
System of Integrated Quick Transfers for scheme funds through an 
integrated framework of the Public Financial Management System 
(PFMS), State IFMIS and e-Kuber platform of Reserve Bank of India 
(RBI) in a progressive manner. This ensures more efficient cash 
management and achieving the goal of “Just–in–time” fund flow from 
both the Centre and State Consolidated Funds.  
  
Land is a State subject and hence under the PMAY-G, the States and 
UTs are responsible for land verification of the beneficiary 
households. 
*****

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 421 
 
TO BE ANSWERED ON THE 21ST JULY, 2026/ ASHADHA 30, 1948 (SAKA) 
 
NARCOTICS ENFORCEMENT FOR DRUG TRAFFICKING 
 
421.     SHRI SHREYAS M PATEL: 
 
Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be pleased to state:  
 
(a) whether the Government is aware of the increasing incidence of drug 
trafficking and substance abuse in Hassan district of Karnataka; 
 
(b) the details of cases registered under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic 
Substances (NDPS) Act during the last five years, including the quantity of 
narcotic drugs and psychotropic  substances seized, persons arrested, 
chargesheets filed and convictions secured, year-wise; 
 
(c) whether the Government has provided financial or technical assistance to 
the Government of Karnataka for strengthening anti -narcotics enforcement, 
intelligence gathering, forensic  facilities and capacity building in Hassan 
district and if so, the details thereof; 
 
(d) the measures taken to  prevent drug abuse among youth through 
awareness campaigns,  educational institution outreach, de -addiction 
services and community-based interventions; and 
 
(e) whether the Government proposes to strengthen coordination among 
Central agencies,  the State Po lice, educational institutions and local 
authorities to effectively curb drug trafficking and substance abuse in Hassan 
district and the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
(SHRI NITYANAND RAI) 
 
(a) & (b) As per latest data published by National Crime Records Bureau 
(NCRB) pertaining to the year 2024; the details of district-wise (including  
 

 
-2- 
L.S.US.Q.NO. 421 FOR 21.07.2026 
 
Hassan district) cases registered under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic 
Substances (NDPS) Act, 1985 during 2020-2024 is at Annexure-I. The quantity 
of narcotics drugs and psychotropic substances seized and year -wise cases 
registered (CR), cases charges heeted (CCS), cases convicted (CON) and 
persons arrested (PAR) in the State of Karnataka during 2020 -2024 is at 
Annexure-II and Annexure-III respectively.  
 
(c) Ministry of Home Affairs is providing assistance to States/ UTs under 
the Assistance to States/ UTs Scheme for strengthening anti -narcotics 
enforcement capacity and related infrastructure. Though, no direct district -
level funding has been released to Hassan District, Government of Karnataka 
has been provided financial assistance under the scheme as detailed below: 
 
Year Released amount in Rs. 
2022-23 1,73,15,589/- 
2024-25 2,59,73,383/- 
2025-26 5,19,46,766/- 
Source: NCB 
 
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment has formulated and is 
implementing National Action Plan for Drug Demand Reduction (NAPDDR), a 
centrally sponsored scheme to tackle the issue of substance use. Under the 
scheme, financial assistance is provided to State Governments/ UTs as per  
 

 
-3- 
L.S.US.Q.NO. 421 FOR 21.07.2026 
 
their State Action Plan for Preventive Education and Awareness Generation, 
Capacity Building, Programmes for Drug Demand reduction by States/ UTs 
etc. In this component, funds are released to the State of Karnataka and not 
to any specific district. In financial year 2024 -25, Rs. 2.96 crore were 
allocated and in financial year 2025-26, Rs. 3.25 crore were allocated by the 
Ministry to the State of Karnataka for the State Action Plan. 
 
(d) Government has taken various initiatives to prevent drug abuse among 
youth through awareness campaigns, educational institution outreach, de -
addiction services and community -based interventions  in Karnataka 
(including Hassan  district), some of which are as under: - 
 
(i) On 17.02.2026, NCB Bengaluru Zonal Unit, in collaboration with Rajiv 
Gandhi University of Health Sciences (RGUHS) and the Dishabodh 
Foundation, organised an intensive anti -drug awareness campaign in 
Hassan district. The programme included dist ribution of drug 
awareness pamphlets, publicity of the MANAS Helpline and a 2-km anti-
drug walkathon with participation of public representatives, district 
administration, students and members of the public to promote 
awareness against drug abuse. 
 
 

 
-4- 
L.S.US.Q.NO. 421 FOR 21.07.2026 
 
(ii) During 2025, NCB Bengaluru Zonal Unit conducted 59 awareness 
programmes in schools, colleges, corporate offices and public spaces, 
including walkathons and cyclothons, with participation of 
approximately 17,000 persons, predominantly students. Further, during 
2026 (till 15.04.2026), 11 awareness programmes have already been 
conducted under the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan in coordination with 
the Government of Karnataka, Rajiv Gandhi University of Health 
Sciences (RGUHS) and other stakeholders, with participation of around 
37,450 students across various districts of Karnataka. 
 
(iii) Department of School Education & Literacy (DoSEL) has developed a 
comprehensive Three-Year Nasha Mukt Vidyalaya  Action Plan (2026 –
2029) to create safe, healthy, tobacco and drug -free school 
environments across India through awareness, prevention, capacity 
building, and community participation. The action plan aims to achieve 
these objectives through the following: - 
 
a) A self-declaration Nasha Mukt Vidyalaya Portal for monitoring the 
implementation of Drug -Free Zone/ Tobacco-Free Educational 
Institutions (ToFEI) compliance. 
b) Declaration of a 500 -meter radius around all school campuses as a 
Drug-Free Zone, with mandatory signage boards outside schools. 

 
-5- 
L.S.US.Q.NO. 421 FOR 21.07.2026 
 
c) Integration of age -appropriate curriculum on substance abuse 
prevention into the life skills and health education. 
d) Development of standardized training and IEC materials on tobacco, 
drugs, and substance abuse. 
 
(iv) Government under National Action Plan for Drug Demand Reduction 
(NAPDDR) scheme by Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment 
(MoSJ&E) is providing support to 30 (01 in Hassan district) Integrated 
Rehabilitation Centres fo r Addicts (IRCAs), 04 District De -Addiction 
Centres (DDACs)  and 01 Addiction Treatment Facilities (ATFs) in 
Karnataka. 
 
(e) Government has taken various measures to strengthen coordination 
among Central agencies, the State Police, educational institutions and local 
authorities to effectively curb drug trafficking and substance abuse, some of 
which are as under: - 
 
(i) Established a 4-tier Narco-Coordination Centre (NCORD) mechanism for 
ensuring better coordination between Central & State Drug Law 
Enforcement Agencies and other stake holders in the field of controlling 
drug trafficking and drug abuse in India. An NCORD portal has been 
developed by NCB. It is an all in one portal for information related to  
 

-6- 
L.S.US.Q.NO. 421 FOR 21.07.2026 
 
drug law enforcement. Topics like NCORD, Training & Capacity Building, 
Narco-offenders data, legal information, exemplary initiatives taken by 
states etc are covered on the NCORD portal. 
 
(ii) At the district level, an NCORD committee has been constituted under 
the chairmanship of Deputy Commissioner, with the Superintendent of 
Police as the member secretary, involving different State and Central 
Government departments like Education, Excise, Agriculture, Tourism, 
Forest, Intelligence and Railways for addressing the various aspects of 
drug trafficking and abuse.  During 2025, 08 District -Level NCORD 
Meetings were conducted in Hassan & 04 such meetings have been held 
in 2026 (till 30.06.2026, as per data uploaded in NCORD portal). 
 
(iii) Joint Coordination Committee (JCC) meetings are held regularly in 
which all relevant Central and State agencies participate, to discuss 
investigation of important narcotics cases in the State. During 2026, 01 
State Level Joint Coordination Sub Committee meeting for the State of 
Karnataka was held on 10.04.2026. 
 
(iv) A dedicated Anti-Narcotics Task Force (ANTF)  headed by Additional 
Director General/ Inspector General level Police Officer is established 
in each State/UT to function as the NCORD Secretariat for the State/UT 
and follow-up on compliance of decisions taken in NCORD meetings at 
different levels. 

 
-7- 
L.S.US.Q.NO. 421 FOR 21.07.2026 
 
(v) Department of School Education & Literacy  undertakes sustained 
awareness, sensitization, and capacity -building initiatives to promote 
tobacco and drug free school campuses.  The Department is proactively 
working in close collaboration with States/UTs to strengthen preventive 
education awareness campaigns, capacity -building programmes and 
Information, Education and Communication (IEC) materials for schools, 
teachers, students, parents and the wider community. These initiatives 
aim to enhance awareness about the harmful effects of tobacco, drugs 
and all forms of substance abuse, to build capacity of teachers to 
implement preventive interventions, encourage active participation of 
parents and communities and to create a safe, healthy, and supportive 
learning environment for all students. 
*****

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 422 
 
TO BE ANSWERED ON THE 21ST JULY, 2026/ ASHADHA 30, 1948 (SAKA) 
 
SUICIDES BY CHILDREN 
 
422.     SHRI K C VENUGOPAL: 
   ADV DEAN KURIAKOSE: 
 
Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be pleased to state:  
 
(a) the number of suicides committed by children below the age of 18 years 
during the last five years, State-wise; 
 
(b) whether there is a continuous year -on-year percentage increase in the 
suicide rate among minors, and if so, the details thereof, State-wise; 
 
(c) whether the Government has conducted any comprehensive study to 
identify the primary systemic causes driving this surge among the youth; and 
 
(d) the concrete measures, specialized helpline  infrastructure, or national 
crisis-intervention frameworks implemented by the Government specifically 
to address and prevent the growing mental health crisis among children and 
adolescents? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
(SHRI NITYANAND RAI) 
 
(a) & (b): National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) compiles and publishes 
information on deaths due to suicides, received from States/Union Territories, 
in its publication “Accidental Deaths & Suicides in India”. Published reports 
are available till the year 2024. State/UT-wise details of suicides committed 
by Children (Below 18 years) during 2021-2024 are available on NCRB website 
(http://ncrb.gov.in). The Bureau started publishing such data since 2021. 

 
-2- 
L.S.US.Q.NO. 422 FOR 21.07.2026 
 
(c) & (d): Ministry of Health & Family Welfare, Government of India has taken 
the following measures to prevent the growing Mental Health crisis among 
Children and Adolescents: 
i. The National Suicide Prevention Strategy was released in November, 
2022. It provides a framework for multiple stakeholders to implement 
activities for prevention of suicides in India. This national strategy aims 
to reduce suicide mortality by 10% in the country by 2030. It also 
includes an action framework with proposed actions with key 
stakeholders, implementation framework and mechanism, thus 
providing a path forward for preventing suicides.  
 
ii. A 15 -Member National Task Force constituted by the Anti -Ragging 
committee of the National Medical Commission (NMC) in February 2024 
on Mental Health and Well-being of Medical Students.  
 
iii. A "National Tele Mental Health Programme" was launched on 10 th 
October, 2022 to further improve access to quality mental health 
counselling and care services in the country. 
 
iv. Tele MANAS Mobile Application was launched on the occasion of World 
Mental Health Day on October 10, 2024 to provide support for mental 
health issues ranging from well being to mental disorders. A video 
 

 
-3- 
L.S.US.Q.NO. 422 FOR 21.07.2026 
 
 consultation facility has been introduced under Tele -MANAS, as an 
upgrade to the existing audio calling service. 
 
v. The National Mental Health Programme (NMHP) has been launched  to 
address the burden of mental disorders, in the country. The District 
Mental Health Programme (DMHP) component of the NMHP has been 
sanctioned for implementation in 767 districts for which support is 
provided to States/UTs through the National Health Mission. 
 
vi. To strengthen mental healthcare services at primary healthcare level, 
more than 1.83 lakh Sub Health Centres (SHCs) and Primary Health 
Centres (PHCs) have been upgraded to Ayushman Arogya Mandirs. 
Mental health services have been added in the packa ges of services 
under Comprehensive Primary Health Care provided at these Ayushman 
Arogya Mandirs. 
 
vii. There are 47 Government run mental hospitals in the country, including 
3 Central Mental Health Institutions, viz. National Institute of Mental 
Health and Ne uro Sciences, Bengaluru, Lokopriya Gopinath Bordoloi 
Regional Institute of Mental Health, Tezpur, Assam and Central 
Institute of Psychiatry, Ranchi. Mental Health Services are also 
provisioned in all AIIMS. 
 

 
-4- 
L.S.US.Q.NO. 422 FOR 21.07.2026 
 
Further, the Ministry of Education, Government of India, also circulated, in 
July 2023, a broad framework for emotional and mental well-being of students 
in Higher Education Institutions (HEIs) with direction to all Centrally Funded 
Institutions to develop institutional mechanism to address the emotional and 
mental wellbeing of students in HEIs.

NATIONAL SOYBEAN RESEARCH CENTRE 
 
423.  SHRI OMPRAKASH BHUPALSINH ALIAS PAVAN RAJENIMBALKAR: 
SHRI SANJAY HARIBHAU JADHAV: 
 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE कृषि और ककसान 
कल्याण मंत्री be pleased to state: 
(a)  whether the Government is considering to establish a National Soybean Research 
Centre in the Dharashiv and Parbhani districts of Maharashtra; 
 
(b)  whether the Dharashiv and Parbhani districts are major soybean-producing districts of 
Maharashtra and whether there is a need for a national -level research centre there for 
soybean production, quality improvement, seed development, pest and disease management 
and providing technical guidance to farmers; 
 
(c)  if so, the details of the action taken so far in this regard and if not, the reasons therefor; 
and 
 
(d)  whether the Government proposes to conduct a feasibility study or take necessary 
steps in coordination with the State Government for the establishment of a National Soybean 
Research Centre in Dharashiv and Parbhani districts, if so, the details thereof? 
 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
कृषि और ककसान कल्याण राज्य मंत्री (SHRI BHAGIRATH CHOUDHARY) 
 
(a) to (c): No, there is no proposal to establish a National Soybean Research Centre in 
the Dharashiv and Parbhani districts of Maharashtra.  
 
 Dharashiv (4.54 lakh ha) and Parbhani (2.76 lakh ha) districts of Maharashtra account 
for about 14.39% of total soybean area of the state (50.72 lakhs ha). In order to enhance 
soybean production, quality improvement, seed development, pest and disease management 
and providing technical guidance to farmers of different agro-ecologies of the state, the ICAR 
is implementing the All India Coordinated Research Project (AICRP) on Soybean in 
collaboration with two State Agricultural Universities viz., Vasantrao Naik Marathwada Krishi 

2 
 
Vidyapeeth, Parbhani; and Dr Panjabrao Deshmukh Krishi Vidyapeeth, Akola; and one 
autonomous institute viz., Agharkar Research Institute, Pune.  Consequently, a total of 48 
climate resilient high yielding varieties of soybean have been notified for the sta te during 
2014–2025 along with matching crop management technologies for the Soybean farmers.  
 
 During 2023-24 to 2025-26, against the indents of 12202 quintals of soybean breeder 
seed, 36252 quintals breeder seed was supplied to the state by the AICRP on Seed centres. 
To augment the local availability of the quality seed of latest varieties of Soybe an, the 
Government of India had established two Seed Hubs of Soybean in 2018-19 at Parbhani and 
Akola. Additionally, one more seed Hub on Soybean has been established at Rahuri under 
the National Mission on Edible Oil-Oilseeds (NMEO-OS) during 2024-25. 
 
 To create awareness and demonstrate the new varieties and technologies, 1300 
frontline demonstrations were conducted at farmers’ fields during the last past five years. 
  
 Hence, there is no need for establishment of a national level research centre in 
Dharashiv and Parbhani districts of Maharashtra. 
 
(d)  No Sir.

(b) whether timelines announced for concluding India –U.K. trade deals have been

वाणिज्य एवं उद्योग मंत्रालय में राज्यमंत्री (श्री णिणिन प्रसाद)

(a) to (c)   India and UK signed the Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) 
on 24 th July 2025 after the conclusion of negotiations on 6 th May 2025. The Agreement 
entered into force on 15th July 2026. 
(d) In order to ensure that the CETA is aligned with India’s priorities and protects 
domestic sensitivities on Agriculture detailed and thorough consultations were held with 
various stakeholders including line ministries, industries, relevant organizations and  export 
promotion bodies. Based on these consultations, India's priorities and sensitivities were 
identified and these were taken into account during the negotiations. As a result, the final 

2 
 
Agreement has protected our sensitivities in Agriculture while si multaneously opening up 
vast opportunities for our farmers and agriculture exports in the UK market.   
(e) Tariff reductions are already effective with the entry into force of the India UK CETA 
on 15 th July 2026. The tariff line wise concession by UK to In dia is published at 
" https://www.commerce.gov.in/?target_lang=en#/international-trade/trade-
agreements/india-united-kingdom-comprehensive-economic-and-trade-agreement". The 
tariff concessions will provide Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises ( MSMEs) with 
competitive advantage and will thereby help in increasing the exports by Indian MSMEs  to 
the UK in sectors such as textiles, leather, jewellery, footwear, home decor, agriculture and 
processed food products. In addition to trade facilitation obligations in the Agreement, a 
separate chapter on MSMEs with provisions related to transparency and cooperation will 
also help in facilitating exports from MSMEs.

ONION EXPORT POLICY 
425. SHRI RAJABHAU PARAG PRAKASH WAJE: 
         Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY (okf.kT; ,oa m|ksx ea=h) be 
pleased to state: 
 
(a)      whether the Government is aware that onion farmers of Maharashtra, particularly 
from Nashik district, have suffered severe financial distress due to Centre’s 
frequent and unpredictable interventions in onion export policy, if so, the details 
thereof; 
(b)   whether it is a fact that these policy decisions resulted in a sharp decline in 
domestic onion prices, forcing farmers in Nashik, Lasalgaon and the other major 
onion-producing regions to sell onions below their cost of production, while 
consumers did not receive commensurate benefits, if so, the details  thereof; 
(c)  whether the Government acknowledges that the repeated use of export 
restrictions has undermined India’s credibility in the international onion market 
and adversely affected farmers’ income security, if so, the details thereof; and 
(d)    whether the Government proposes to formulate a stable long-term export policy, 
provide legal price protection for onion farmers and establish a compensation 
mechanism for losses arising from sudden export restrictions  and if so, the 
details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor? 
 
ANSWER 
okf.kT; ,oa m|ksx ea=ky; esa jkT;ea=h ¼Jh ftfru izlkn½ 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY 
(SHRI JITIN PRASADA) 
 
(a) to (d) The Government continuously monitors the availability, market arrivals, 
wholesale and retail prices, buffer stock position and export trends of onion across the 
country, including in Maharashtra and the Nashik region.  
Onion prices are influenced by several factors, including inter alia, crop area, weather 
conditions, seasonality, production and productivity, arrivals, storage losses, domestic 

2 
 
demand and international prices. Therefore, variations in mandi prices cannot be 
attributed solely to changes in the export policy. 
The existing policy framework provides for market intervention, buffer procurement 
and calibrated trade-policy measures. Whenever domestic supplies show stress, 
calibrated and temporary measures, such as minimum export price (MEP), export 
duties, or temporary restrictions, are imposed in the public interest to ensure food 
security, and withdrawn once the supply situation eases.  
The export policy of onion is accordingly calibrated from time to time, based on the 
prevailing domestic availability and price situation, with the objective of balancing the 
interests of farmers and domestic consumers. The flexible export regime based on the 
dynamics of domestic availability and prices gives Government the ability to respond 
promptly to exceptional supply and price situations.
